source_spec: `{implementation_artifacts}/spec-9-11-replay-v2-tagged-body-scenario-re-gate-replay-ux-browser-playback-perspective.md`
reason: The v4 replay header embeds a `rulesetHash` (and the player exposes `RulesetHash`), but playback re-gates ONLY the scenario hash — a replay recorded under different ruleset/effect-graph caps than the current build passes the scenario gate and plays, silently desyncing at the first ruleset-sensitive effect, the exact silent-desync class this story eliminates for scenario drift. — Evidence: `MatchLifecycleController.TryLoadReplay` computes only `CanonicalModelHash.Compute` for the loaded scenario and passes it with `player.ScenarioHash` to `ReplayPlayer.ScenarioGateBlockReason` (scenario-only); the embedded `rulesetHash` is read into the header and never compared, whereas the live MP `MatchAgreementHash` mixes BOTH scenario and ruleset hashes. The intent scoped the re-gate to the scenario hash, so this is a latent gap beyond the story's contract rather than a spec deviation. Closure = fold a `RulesetHash.Compute()` vs `player.RulesetHash` check into the fail-closed re-gate (mirroring `MatchAgreementHash`), or document why replay tolerates ruleset drift that live MP does not.
status: done 2026-08-04
resolution: closed by workflow burn-down bundle `replay-lifecycle-hardening` (commit acbab1e) - added a pure fail-closed `ReplayPlayer.RulesetGateBlockReason` mirroring the scenario gate and MatchAgreementHash (which mixes BOTH hashes); it blocks on 0 or on mismatch, since RulesetHash.Compute() is sentinel-guarded nonzero so 0 is always corrupt. Wired into MatchLifecycleController.TryLoadReplay after the scenario gate with its own "REPLAY REFUSED (ruleset mismatch)" surfacing. Covered by new Godot-free ruleset-gate matrix tests including a real-build fingerprint self-gate. Caveat: the TryLoadReplay call site is Godot-coupled and compile-verified only - a candidate for the Epic 10 live-verification batch. Gate: dotnet build 0 errors; suite 4119/0/1 (baseline 4111 + the bundle's 8 tests). No golden/CanonicalModelHash/StartStateHash movement.

### DW-433: The server's merged-tick fan-in (`MergedTickBuilder.TryBuild`) waits for ALL Expected slots to submit tick T with…
origin: migrated from flat appender bullet, 2026-07-30 (A1-E11)
source_spec: `{implementation_artifacts}/spec-9-13-per-client-command-rate-throttle-anti-spam-on-the-dedicated-server.md`
location: MergedTickBuilder.cs:186
reason: The server's merged-tick fan-in (`MergedTickBuilder.TryBuild`) waits for ALL Expected slots to submit tick T with no timeout or force-advance, so any slot whose tick-T packet never arrives — a mis-set throttle cap, a silent app-level drop, or an uncooperative client — stalls every client on that tick with no recovery short of a transport disconnect (which triggers freeze-and-continue). — Evidence: `MergedTickBuilder.cs:186` returns false and buffers whenever any slot has not arrived; the only silent-recovery path (`DropController`/`FrozenSlotInjector`) fires exclusively on a transport disconnect, never on a still-connected slot with a missing tick. Pre-existing property of the Story 9.3/9.6 backbone (not introduced by 9.13, and not reachable by 9.13 under legitimate play — the [2,12] input-delay pipeline bounds a lockstep client's in-flight backlog far below the 60/window cap). Latent robustness gap worth hardening for the 4-player e2e work (9.15): e.g. a bounded force-advance / missing-slot watchdog so a never-arriving slot degrades to freeze rather than an indefinite stall.
status: open
seen-again: 2026-08-03 (workflow burn-down bundle dw-minority-halt-quorum-rebase — ESCALATION, not just a re-sighting: this entry judged the still-connected-slot stall "not reachable under legitimate play", but a DESYNC SELF-HALT reaches it. LockstepManager turns a DesyncAlert into a terminal RaiseHalt while the peer stays CONNECTED, so it stops submitting TickCommands and MergedTickBuilder.TryBuild (godot/src/Multiplayer/Server/MergedTickBuilder.cs:185-186) never completes again; DedicatedServer.cs:412-434 only reaches NotifyDrop/freeze from a transport disconnect, so survivors stall until ENet finally times the halted peer out or the human closes the halt overlay. DW-237's fix rebased the CHECKSUM quorum so the survivors' desync guard survives an N>=3 minority halt, but with the command stream stalled they produce no new checksums to compare, so the command half must close for the guard to be useful. Closing it means firing a DropController DropDirective + all-survivor ACK dance from the desync path in the Godot-coupled DedicatedServer — unverifiable by the Godot-free Tier-1 gate, hence deliberately out of that bundle's scope)

### DW-200: Host-side (ENet DedicatedServer) StartGame identity enforcement + deterministic in-match deployment of the attested online hero

origin: named follow-up from spec-9-12-server-validated-online-hero-persistence-rail (bmad-loop-resolve decision, Alec, 2026-07-24)
location: godot/src/Multiplayer/DedicatedServer.cs (StartGame path / HandleReady) + godot/src/Multiplayer/NakamaService.cs (MatchFoundInfo, endpoint-only) + godot/src/Multiplayer/Server/AssignedRoster.cs (TryFreeze) + godot/src/Core/Bootstrap/Phases/MatchLifecycleController.cs (OnMatchStart mints no hero) + StartStateHash fold
severity: medium
reason: Story 9.12 shipped the server-authoritative storage + validating RPC rail and a live, fail-closed CLIENT launch/Ready attestation gate (`OnlineHeroLaunchGate` over `NakamaService.AttestHeroProfileAsync`), but deliberately did NOT (a) enforce the attestation host-side, nor (b) deploy the attested hero into the lockstep match. Both are blocked on the SAME missing plumbing: the Nakama→ENet handoff (`MatchFoundInfo`) is endpoint-only and the `DedicatedServer` knows peers by transport slot alone — no Nakama userId/token reaches it, and no peer's profile reaches the other peers. Two remaining holes: (1) a friend who patches the game binary to skip the client-side gate (the decisive defense is already the server-owned No-Client-Write storage object + validating RPC — a client cannot forge the stored profile — but the host does not verify the gate ran); (2) minting one peer's hero would diverge `HeroStore` across peers → `StartStateHash` disagreement → online matches would fail to start, so deterministic cross-peer deployment needs a start-state fold this story's `Never`/`Block If` clauses forbid. Fix (post-1.0 fast-follow): add (a) a client→server attestation packet carrying a Nakama-issued credential; (b) server-side Nakama trust so the `DedicatedServer` can verify it; (c) a userId→slot bind in `AssignedRoster.TryFreeze` + a fail-closed gate in `HandleReady`; and (d) server distribution of every peer's attested profile so all peers mint an identical multi-hero `HeroStore` (a deterministic fold, re-baselining `StartStateHash`). 9.12 leaves the `DedicatedServer` StartGame path byte-unchanged and mints no hero into the online match.
status: open
goldens: none — an unbuilt feature moves no existing golden, because no recorded scenario exercises it. Story 15.14; does NOT wait on a re-baseline batch.
decision: 2026-07-30 Build the full rail — Client→server credential packet, server-side trust, userId→slot bind in TryFreeze, fail-closed HandleReady gate, and server distribution of all peers' profiles minting an identical multi-hero HeroStore (StartStateHash re-baseline)
seen-again: 2026-08-07 (bmad-dev-auto 15-14 HALTED `blocked` at planning — needs a human, not unattended dev-auto; same class as Story 15.1). Investigation confirmed the wall: (1) component (b) "server-side Nakama trust" has NO foundation — `DedicatedServer.cs` has zero Nakama surface and knows peers as transport-slot ints only (`HandleConnect(int slot)`); `MatchFoundInfo` is endpoint-only (no userId/token crosses into ENet); Nakama is not hosted (local docker-compose recipe, gitignored+unbuilt TS module). The trust MECHANISM is an unmade architecture decision — live server→Nakama token validation OR a signed-JWT shared-secret scheme — and BOTH force the "deploy/host+configure Nakama" infra commitment spec-9-12 explicitly deferred. (2) The enforcement behavior is unverifiable unattended: it only means anything across TWO peers with distinct real credentials, but the in-engine bridge is single-client and no Nakama is hosted (cf. DW-435). (3) The determinism half (e) alone bumps StartStateHash.AlgoVersion and re-baselines the hero start-state golden (+ up to ~33 goldens if the per-tick fold shifts) — an isolated re-baseline story, and shipping it without the enforcement it serves is the dormant-half-feature anti-pattern 9-12's review rejected. Decisions needed from Alec before re-dispatch: trust mechanism? host Nakama for real? full rail vs. split off the Tier-1 determinism/packet/bind/gate-predicate foundation as its own story with live host-enforcement as a human-run follow-up? Full finding: `bmad-dev-auto-result-15-14-host-side-hero-identity-enforcement-attested-deployment-dw-200.md`.

### DW-435: The live online hero rail may be unreachable end-to-end — a first-time online player can only obtain an attested…

reason: The live online hero rail may be unreachable end-to-end — a first-time online player can only obtain an attested hero via the picker's Save, which is enabled only when `TryResolvePrimaryHero` finds a placeable hero in the online lobby's scenario; whether a real matchmaking lobby actually presents such a scenario before Ready is unverified, and if it does not, the fail-closed Ready gate soft-locks every player out of every online match. — Evidence: `HeroPickerOverlay.UpdateButtonStates` gates `_saveBtn` on `TryResolvePrimaryHero(...)` (a placed hero for the local faction in `_scenario`), and `LobbyUi.EnsureOnlinePicker` sources that scenario from `ScenarioProvider?.Invoke()` (wired by `HeroPickerPhase` to `_ctx.Scenario`). Online Ready is fail-closed on `_onlineHeroAttested`, set only after a successful Save+attest. All four review layers flagged the reachability risk. It is genuinely runtime-dependent (needs a live two-client Nakama match, which the spec's Boundaries explicitly exclude — "Do not deploy/host Nakama") so it could not be verified in the review sandbox. Closure = a live-Nakama manual verification that a fresh online player can create+attest a hero and Ready, plus (if the pre-match lobby has no placeable-hero scenario) an online-first hero-creation/selection path that does not depend on an in-scenario placed unit.

### DW-436: The TS server validator runs O(n^2) duplicate-key/duplicate-slot scans over `values`/`inventory` BEFORE any size…
origin: migrated from flat appender bullet, 2026-07-30 (A1-E11)
source_spec: `{implementation_artifacts}/spec-9-12-server-validated-online-hero-persistence-rail.md`
reason: The TS server validator runs O(n^2) duplicate-key/duplicate-slot scans over `values`/`inventory` BEFORE any size cap bites (the `MAX_STORED_PROFILE_BYTES` check is applied only after `validateHeroProfile` on the write path, and not at all on the attest read path), so a single large in-range payload can drive a per-request CPU spike on Nakama's single-threaded goja runtime. — Evidence: `docs/server-deploy/nakama-modules/src/main.ts` `handleWriteHeroProfile` calls `validateHeroProfile(profile)` before the `JSON.stringify(sanitized).length > MAX_STORED_PROFILE_BYTES` guard; `validation.ts` `validateHeroProfile` does nested O(n^2) dup scans. `handleAttestHeroProfile` re-validates a stored object with no size cap at all (reachable via a first-time raw client write of an oversized object, since permissionWrite=0 only protects an already-stored object). Low real priority for a self-hosted trusted-friends EA server and likely partly mitigated by Nakama's own RPC request-size limits, but a genuine hardening gap in new code. Closure = a raw-payload / element-count guard at the top of both handlers (handler-only, goja-safe with `String.length`, no impact on the shared C#<->TS parity fixture), and/or O(n) dup detection via a Set.
status: done 2026-08-03
resolution: closed by workflow burn-down bundle `nakama-validator-guards` (commit 0fbd288) - verified still-open first via a baseline probe (a 40KB junk-blob payload was WRITTEN ok:true and a rule-valid oversized planted storage object ATTESTED true), then fixed with handler-only guards in docs/server-deploy/nakama-modules/src/main.ts: MAX_RAW_PAYLOAD_BYTES (32768, goja-safe String.length) checked before JSON.parse on BOTH rpc_write_hero_profile and rpc_attest_hero_profile; MAX_PROFILE_ELEMENTS (512) checked before validateHeroProfile's O(n^2) dup scans; and a new stored-object size+count guard on the attest read path (previously no cap at all). validation.ts and the shared C#<->TS parity fixture untouched, and the 512 cap provably cannot flip any verdict the 8192-byte stored cap allowed. 6 new vitest regression tests each fail behaviorally on the pre-fix baseline (vitest 44/44, tsc --noEmit clean, esbuild bundle ok). Zero goldens moved; no SimChecksum/CanonicalModelHash/StartStateHash surface touched. npm-audit devDependency residual filed as DW-569.

### DW-442: Scenario team authoring has no validation — a scenario putting all active slots on one team (combat then excludes…
origin: migrated from flat appender bullet, 2026-07-30 (A1-E11)
source_spec: `{implementation_artifacts}/spec-9-14-teams-alliances-lobby-teams-wired-into-the-sim-alliance-model.md`
location: godot/src/Core/Definitions/ScenarioValidator.cs
reason: Scenario team authoring has no validation — a scenario putting all active slots on one team (combat then excludes everyone → no acquisition/eliminations → degenerate/hung match), a duplicated `.Slot` (order-dependent canonical team id), an out-of-range team member (silently dropped, no log), and an inert team-of-one all ship without author-facing feedback. — Evidence: `godot/src/Core/Definitions/ScenarioValidator.cs` (player-slots loop ~230-264) validates `Slot`/ore/coords/uniqueness but never `Team`; `godot/src/Core/AllianceSeeder.cs` `ComputeTeamIds` (~706-731) drops `faction >= FACTION_COUNT` silently (unlike `ScenarioApplier`'s warning) and is last-write-wins on duplicate `.Slot`. These layouts became authorable only with this story's new `Team` field. Closure = add `ScenarioValidator` team checks (>=2 distinct live teams among active slots; reject/warn on duplicate `.Slot` and inert team-of-one) and a diagnostic in `AllianceSeeder` for out-of-range team members.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: workflow burn-down bundle scenario-team-validation (2026-08-05) - verified STILL OPEN at run-base 4c7a2259 before any change: ScenarioValidator's player-slots loop (cs:283-314) validated slot / engine-ceiling / uniqueness / ore / coords / blocked-cell and never read `Team` at all (zero `Team` hits in the whole file), and AllianceSeeder.ComputeTeamIds still dropped an out-of-range member with no diagnostic and was still last-write-wins on a duplicated `.Slot`. No decisions.json entry exists for DW-442, so this entry's own `reason:` text governed scope. One of the four cases was ALREADY closed and was not re-done: a duplicated `.Slot` is hard-rejected by the pre-existing uniqueness check (`!declared.Add(s.Slot)`), pinned now by DuplicateSlot_IsStillHardRejectedByTheLoadGate; the seeder diagnostic added here covers only the models that never pass through Validate (LobbyUi.RebuildSlotGrid calls ComputeTeamIds directly on an unvalidated model). The fix is SPLIT by how certain the defect is, which is the load-bearing judgement in this bundle. HARD, fail-closed in Validate: a NEGATIVE `team` is now a located rejection - ComputeTeamIds treats `team <= 0` as UNASSIGNED, so -1 silently means FFA while the JSON claims a team, and because Team folds into MatchAgreementHash two peers whose files differ only in WHICH negative ordinal they carry fail the start handshake over alliance masks that are byte-identical (pinned by NegativeTeam_IsRejected_EvenThoughTheSeederWouldTreatItAsFfa); `team == 0`, the omit-when-default value every shipped scenario carries (checked: no scenario JSON contains a "team" key at all), still passes. POSITIVE ordinals were deliberately NOT hard-capped and the all-on-one-team layout deliberately NOT hard-rejected, even though SkirmishSetupValidator rule 7 makes the same all-allied check a blocking error for the lobby. Two reasons, both checked in code: (1) ordinals are documented arbitrary authoring labels that never reach a sim store (AllianceSeederTests pins ordinals 5/9 seeding canonical ids 1/3), and a slots.Length-relative cap would reject a legitimate FFA map left with teams 3,4 after two slots were deleted; (2) trigger factions are gated by CheckFactionSlot, NOT by `declared`, so a co-op map whose enemies arrive from spawn_unit triggers on an UNDECLARED faction slot is legitimately all-allied among its declared slots and a hard fail would make that map unloadable. The lobby can be strict because there the active set IS the whole match. SOFT, non-fatal in CollectAdvisories (appended LAST so existing advisories keep their indices - an existing test asserts advisories[0]): the all-on-one-side verdict plus the seeder's own diagnostics, under a `scenario.` prefix. The sides verdict runs through AllianceSeeder.ComputeTeamIds - the same mapping the sim seeds and the agreement hash folds - so the warning can never disagree with the alliances the match actually gets, and it counts distinct FACTIONS rather than entries so a duplicated `.Slot` cannot inflate the active count and mask the verdict; an FFA map produces nothing new (each faction is its own side), which is why CreateBlank and the existing MapWithSlots advisory tests stay Assert.Empty. NEW read-only API AllianceSeeder.CollectDiagnostics(ScenarioData?) is the seeder's own account of what the mapping silently did - out-of-range member dropped, duplicate-.Slot last-write-wins, inert team-of-one; it is never called from Seed or ComputeTeamIds so the mapping is untouched, and it is null-element safe unlike the mapping itself (filed as DW-814). DETERMINISM: nothing folded into SimChecksum, CanonicalModelHash, MatchAgreementHash or StartStateHash changed - the only additions are a load-gate rejection of a value no shipped map carries plus two pure read-only reporting paths; no golden was re-recorded and none moved, and the full suite including every golden is green. COVERAGE: 21 Godot-free, integer-only tests in godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Definitions/ScenarioTeamValidationTests.cs. Red-test proof done properly - with the three new behaviours neutered in place (negative-team branch disabled, advisory call bypassed, CollectDiagnostics returning pre-fix silence) 9 defect tests went RED and the 12 non-regression guards stayed green; probes reverted and grep-confirmed absent before committing. Two test premises that were wrong on the first pass were caught and corrected rather than weakened: the order-dependence case needs the duplicated slot to be a NON-lowest faction (a duplicate on slot 0 is order-INDEPENDENT because the canonical id is a min that always includes the entry itself), and the out-of-range drop is best proven by asserting the resulting mask is byte-identical to FFA. GATE: `dotnet build godot/godot.csproj` = 0 errors (6 pre-existing warnings); `dotnet test godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/...` = 5898 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped, i.e. the 5877 baseline plus exactly the 21 new tests - no flake exception needed, CanonicalModelHashPerfTests passed in the full run. Follow-on filed as DW-814.

The AUDIT half was ALREADY SATISFIED: every match-start / peer-agreement path in godot/src was walked and both live gates already compare the agreement value — LobbyUi.cs:421 sends TickCommandPacket.MakeReady(PROTOCOL_VERSION, MatchAgreementHash) and LobbyUi.cs:649 passes MatchAgreementHash into ReadyPacketRouting.Route (-> HandshakeGate.CheckStart), while DedicatedServer.cs:604-629 feeds ServerLobbyPolicy.CheckStartStateAgreement the _readyHash it parsed off the Ready wire; the only other MakeReady producer is LoopbackDesyncSelfTest's fixed AGREE constant (a debug loopback smoke, no scenario involved). So no production change was warranted and NONE was made. The COVERAGE half was genuinely open: every existing test of those gates (HandshakeGateTests, ReadyPacketRoutingTests, StartStateAgreementTests, StartStateAgreementSlotMapTests) uses synthetic hash literals, and MatchAgreementHashTests pins only that the VALUE moves on a team change — nothing tied the two together, so rewiring a gate to CanonicalModelHash would have shipped with a fully green suite. Added godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Multiplayer/StartPathTeamAgreementTests.cs (14 Godot-free integer-only tests) in three layers: (1) the premise — two models differing ONLY in ScenarioPlayerSlot.Team hash IDENTICALLY under CanonicalModelHash (64-bit and the 32-bit ToWire fold) while AllianceSeeder.ComputeTeamIds genuinely diverges, and differ under MatchAgreementHash; (2) both live gates driven with the REAL agreement hashes over real MakeReady bytes — the P2P route and HandshakeGate directly, the server gate on both the dense and the DW-397 slot-map overload, contiguous and gapped/non-contiguous rosters — each paired with an agreed-layout control AND the counterfactual asserting the identical call ALLOWS when fed model-hash values, so the rejection provably comes from the agreement hash and not the fixture; (3) an "EVERY start path" source audit over godot/src/** that comment/literal-strips each file, extracts the balanced argument list of every CheckStart / CheckStartStateAgreement / ReadyPacketRouting.Route / TickCommandPacket.MakeReady call site and fails if any is fed a CanonicalModelHash / ScenarioHash / StartStateHash / ContentHash / RulesetHash / ToWire-derived value, plus positive pins on the two Godot-coupled production sites Tier-1 cannot execute — that scan is how the entry's "EVERY start path" clause is enforced for a gate added later. Proved load-bearing by mutation (each reverted immediately, no git stash used): rewiring LobbyUi's Route to CanonicalModelHash.ToWire(ScenarioHash) turned 2 red; neutralizing the team fold in MatchAgreementHash.Compute turned 7 red; perturbing DedicatedServer's _readyHash assignment turned 1 red. Determinism: no production code touched, so no golden, SimChecksum, CanonicalModelHash or StartStateHash value moves and nothing was re-recorded. The REPLAY playback re-gate has the same Team-blindness and is deliberately out of scope (DW-443's closure clause is scoped to peer start paths, and the v4 replay header would need a new field plus a format bump) — filed as DW-827. Gate: dotnet build godot/godot.csproj 0 errors; dotnet test full suite 5891 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped — exactly the 5877/0/1 baseline plus the 14 new tests, no flake, no isolation re-run needed.

### DW-444: Projectile primary/direct-hit damage is not alliance-rechecked at impact (only `ApplySplash` is), so if a primary…
origin: migrated from flat appender bullet, 2026-07-30 (A1-E11)
source_spec: `{implementation_artifacts}/spec-9-14-teams-alliances-lobby-teams-wired-into-the-sim-alliance-model.md`
location: godot/src/Combat/ProjectileSystem.cs
reason: Projectile primary/direct-hit damage is not alliance-rechecked at impact (only `ApplySplash` is), so if a primary target's entity id is recycled into an allied entity between projectile spawn and impact, the projectile still damages the now-ally — asymmetric with the splash guard. — Evidence: `godot/src/Combat/ProjectileSystem.cs` `ApplySplash` (~169) skips `AreAllied(owner, victim)` but the primary-target delivery path re-checks only `IsAlive`, not alliance; `CombatSystem`'s force-fire comment flags id-recycle as reachable. Obscure edge (target acquisition already excludes allies at spawn time) and a pre-existing damage-delivery class. Closure = recheck `!AreAllied(owner, FactionOf[primaryTarget])` at impact for symmetry, or document the site as out of scope with the recycle reasoning.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: closed by workflow burn-down bundle `combat-alliance-idrecycle` (merge ed39026f, dev cc1f71ac), alongside DW-446 - verified STILL OPEN at run-base 6c509c57 (ProjectileSystem.Tick computed `targetAlive = world.IsAlive(targetId)` with no faction/alliance re-check, so a slot recycled into the shooter's own or an allied faction was damaged anyway). The primary/direct-hit path now validates at the site the entry names (`targetAlive`, ~cs:96) rather than only at the impact branch: a friendly occupant makes the target GONE, so the shell stops tracking it, coasts to its last known position and drops harmlessly - no damage, no impact event, no splash - which is byte-for-byte what a target dying WITHOUT a recycle already does. Both halves of an impact now share one `IsFriendlyToOwner(world, owner, victim)` helper with ApplySplash (whose two guard lines were folded into it, semantics unchanged) so primary and splash can never disagree about who is friendly. Neutral stays a legal target on every path (AreAllied(Player, Neutral) == false), and a slot recycled into a still-HOSTILE faction is still engaged - the pre-existing ABA behaviour the entry scopes out, now pinned by tests so the guard cannot silently widen (filed as DW-775; the building-target path's equivalent gap as DW-774). 9 new Godot-free Fixed-only tests in Combat/EntityIdRecycleTargetGuardTests.cs, each driving the recycle explicitly; with both source files reverted the 5 defect tests went RED and the 4 non-regression tests stayed green. No golden, SimChecksum, CanonicalModelHash or StartStateHash moved - the new terms are unreachable in every recorded scenario and nothing was re-recorded. Gate: build 0 errors; suite 5597/0/1 = the 5588 baseline plus 9.

Per the decision's "allied-skip is the FLOOR" clause, the picker also de-prioritizes a hostile structure a TEAMMATE is already force-attacking - a preference, never a filter, so it cannot reintroduce a no-target stall. ### DW-446: A HELD auto-acquired unit `AttackTarget` is not alliance/faction-rechecked while retained —…
origin: migrated from flat appender bullet, 2026-07-30 (A1-E11)
source_spec: `{implementation_artifacts}/spec-9-14-teams-alliances-lobby-teams-wired-into-the-sim-alliance-model.md`
location: godot/src/Combat/CombatSystem.cs
reason: A HELD auto-acquired unit `AttackTarget` is not alliance/faction-rechecked while retained — `CombatSystem.ValidateOrClearTarget` clears only on the target's death — so if that target's entity id is recycled into an allied (or same-faction) unit between ticks, the attacker fires on the now-ally for a tick, violating "an ally is never auto-attacked." — Evidence: `godot/src/Combat/CombatSystem.cs` `ValidateOrClearTarget` (~554-563) drops a held `AttackTarget` only when `!IsAlive`; Story 9.14 added allied-exclusion only at acquisition (`FindNearestEnemy*`, threaded `_alliances`) and on the per-tick forced paths (force-fire ~900, `TickAttackBuildingCombat` re-checks alliance every tick). Entity slots are shared across factions in one `EntityWorld`, so a teammate training a unit into a freed enemy slot in a 2v2 is reachable. Distinct from the existing projectile-primary-recycle defer (that entry is `ProjectileSystem.ApplySplash`/primary impact; this is the CombatSystem held unit-target path). The underlying recycle-into-friendly gap also pre-exists for same-faction (the force-fire comment at ~274-276 acknowledges it), so a holistic fix should cover both same-faction and allied. Obscure edge (one-tick window on a same-tick slot recycle). Closure = make `ValidateOrClearTarget` an instance method that also clears when `_alliances.AreAllied(FactionOf[id], FactionOf[target])` (and, for the pre-existing class, same-faction), mirroring the per-tick forced-path guards.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: closed by workflow burn-down bundle `combat-alliance-idrecycle` (merge ed39026f, dev cc1f71ac), alongside DW-444 - verified STILL OPEN at run-base 6c509c57 (ValidateOrClearTarget cleared only on `!IsAlive`). Follows the recorded owner decision in .bmad-loop/decisions.json exactly ("Instance-method ValidateOrClearTarget clearing on allied/same-faction id-recycle, alongside DW-444", effect: build, answered 2026-07-30): ValidateOrClearTarget is now an instance method (was private static) that drops a HELD auto-acquired AttackTarget when the occupant is same-faction (unconditional - that half of the class pre-dates alliances, as the force-fire guard's own comment acknowledges) or allied (`_alliances.AreAllied`, a no-op under a null/FFA mask). IsAlive is evaluated first and short-circuits so a stale id never indexes FactionOf. All four call sites (Idle / Stop+Hold / Patrol / AttackMove) inherit the guard, and a cleared target falls straight through to FindNearestEnemy in the same tick, so there is no acquisition stutter. A slot recycled into a DIFFERENT ENEMY faction is still silently inherited - deliberately preserved as the entry scopes it out, and pinned by HeldAutoTarget_RecycledIntoAnotherEnemy_KeepsFiring so a future change to it is a conscious one; filed as DW-775. Coverage, determinism and gate as recorded on DW-444 (9 shared tests, suite 5597/0/1, zero goldens moved).
decision: 2026-07-30 Build now with DW-444 — Instance-method ValidateOrClearTarget clearing on allied/same-faction id-recycle, alongside DW-444

### DW-454: The filename-safe charset check admits Windows reserved device basenames (`con`, `nul`, `aux`, `prn`, `com1`…
origin: migrated from flat appender bullet, 2026-07-30 (A1-E11)
source_spec: `spec-item-definition-validator-hardening.md`
location: ItemDefinitionValidator.cs:90
reason: The filename-safe charset check admits Windows reserved device basenames (`con`, `nul`, `aux`, `prn`, `com1`, `lpt1`) — all within `[a-z0-9_]` — so saving such an item makes `Persist()`'s `File.WriteAllText("con.json.tmp")` throw on Windows (the primary platform), surfacing as an opaque generic "Save failed" with no field badge and no way to save the item. — Evidence: `ItemDefinitionValidator.cs:90` / `:154` check only the `[a-z0-9_]` charset, which reserved device names satisfy; `Persist()` (`ItemCardPanel.Edit.cs:223`) then writes `<id>.json.tmp`, which the Win32 filesystem rejects for reserved basenames, caught only by the generic `catch (Exception ex)` → "Save failed". Pre-existing class orthogonal to DW-47's traversal fix and shared with the sibling `UnitDefinitionValidator` charset. Niche (requires a creator to name an item exactly a reserved word). Closure = add a reserved-basename reject (`con|prn|aux|nul|com[1-9]|lpt[1-9]`) alongside the charset check in both validators.
status: done 2026-08-03
resolution: Bundle unit-def-validator-strict-bounds (workflow burn-down 2026-08-03) — added `UnitDefinitionValidator.IsReservedDeviceName(string?)` as the single shared convention helper beside SanitizeId and wired it into all three surfaces this entry names: the item sim gate (ItemDefinitionValidator.Validate), the item editor gate (ValidateFields — the one that actually blocks ItemCardPanel.Persist via DoSave/Revalidate, confirmed at ItemCardPanel.Edit.cs:214-238 where `Path.Combine(absDir, id + ".json")` + the .tmp File.WriteAllText is the throwing call), and the sibling unit gate (which BuildingDefinitionValidator reuses kinded "building", so buildings are covered for free). Used `else if` after the charset check so an uppercase "CON" badges the id field once, not twice (the D-9 per-field-badge contract). Also closed a coherence gap the new reject created: MakeUniqueId now treats a reserved basename like a taken id, so the shared minter (editor New/Duplicate plus the Story-8.4 AI-draft landing) can no longer hand back an id its own validator refuses on Save. Authoring-time reject only — no golden/checksum/hash moved. Gate: build 0 errors, Tier-1 3777 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped (self-measured 3714 baseline + 63 new tests shared with DW-380). The faction-name wizard's free-text path is safe only INCIDENTALLY (via its `_faction` filename suffix) and was left outside scope → DW-528.

### DW-213: CS8632 nullable annotations without #nullable enable (2 files remain)
origin: migrated from legacy ledger ("From code review of story-1.1 (2026-06-22)"), 2026-07-28
location: godot/src/Economy/GatheringSystem.cs:34-36; godot/src/Navigation/FlowFieldSystem.cs:114
severity: low
reason: Of the original 6 warnings, SimulationLoop.cs got `#nullable enable` (3 cleared); GatheringSystem (`MatchStats?`) and FlowFieldSystem (`out FlowField?`) still lack the directive. Two-line fix. Verified 2026-07-28.
status: done 2026-08-04
resolution: workflow burn-down bundle nullable-directive-cleanup — the `location:` line above was stale in BOTH directions: godot/src/Economy/GatheringSystem.cs was ALREADY fixed (`#nullable enable` on line 1) and needed nothing, while the class had re-opened in three more files, so a clean build on the run base emitted 6 CS8632 warnings across 4 files: Navigation/FlowFieldSystem.cs (80, 115), Core/EntityWorld.cs (324, 983), Core/ResourceNodeStore.cs (103), Core/ResourceStore.cs (76). All four were fixed (the entry's goal is zero CS8632; fixing only the named file would have left the defect live). EntityWorld needed follow-through — three doc comments explicitly justified an opt-out — so the members they described were annotated: `_elevationGrid`/`SetElevationGrid(grid)` → `ElevationGrid?`, `FeedbackProfile` → `CombatFeedbackProfile?[]`, `SourceDefinition` → `UnitDefinition?[]`, `OnDestroy`/`OnUnitDefinitionApplied` → `Action<int>?`, and the comments rewritten to match; that surfaced exactly two consumer warnings (CS8600 at UI/SelectionSystem.cs:1243 and UI/SelectionSubgroupPanel.cs:492), both `UnitDefinition def = _world.SourceDefinition[id];` immediately followed by a null check, declared `UnitDefinition?`. Net godot.csproj warnings 11 → 5, with 0 CS8632. Determinism: annotation-only (nullable metadata + one preprocessor directive per file) — no runtime semantics, no folded field, no golden touched; `CombatFeedbackProfile?[]` and `CombatFeedbackProfile[]` are the same CLR type. Regression coverage: new Godot-free guard godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Meta/NullableContextHygieneTests.cs (2 tests, following Meta/DependencyHygieneTests' [CallerFilePath] pattern) — one pins the five ledger-named files, one walks godot/src/**.cs, skips files already in a nullable context, strips comments/strings/char literals with a state machine so line numbers stay accurate, and flags any nullable annotation on a PROVABLE reference type (array, string/object/dynamic, or a type this assembly compiles and knows to be a class); unknown names are deliberately never flagged so a struct from a Godot-coupled assembly cannot false-positive. Teeth proven by temporarily removing the directive from FlowFieldSystem.cs and ResourceNodeStore.cs (both tests fail and name the exact compiler sites) — an earlier casing-heuristic iteration false-positived on `Fixed?` in BuildingStore.cs, which drove the reflection-backed check. Gate: build 0 errors / 5 pre-existing warnings, suite 4843 passed / 1 skipped with the lone documented CanonicalModelHashPerfTests timing flake (passed 2/2 in isolation); ProjectChimera.Sim.Analysis also built clean (0 errors).
decision: 2026-07-28 correct-course — bundle nullable-directive-cleanup (Epic 15, Story 15.5)

### DW-233: PhaseOrderTest cannot catch concrete-phase Name drift or duplicate canonical names
origin: migrated from legacy ledger ("Deferred from: code review of story-1.8c (2026-06-24)"), 2026-07-28
location: godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Bootstrap/PhaseOrderTest.cs
severity: low
reason: Unchanged — no duplicate-name assert (≈3 lines, Tier-1) and no Tier-2 GdUnit4 companion instantiating the real phases; value rose with 40 phases. Verified 2026-07-28.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: 2026-08-05 resolved by burn-down bundle phaseorder-test-hardening (workflow burn-down run) - verified STILL OPEN against current code first (no duplicate-name assert existed and every one of the 5 existing tests drove StubPhase only, never a real phase). Test-only change to godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Bootstrap/PhaseOrderTest.cs (+241 lines, 3 new [Fact]s); no production code touched. Both named holes closed: (1) duplicate canonical names - ScenePhaseRunner.AssertOrder matches POSITIONALLY BY NAME, so a name at two positions makes those positions interchangeable and the elementwise pin cannot see it (a duplicate mirrored into ExpectedOrder matches happily); Canonical_HasNoDuplicateNames asserts uniqueness on BOTH arrays so 'silence the red order test by mirroring the duplicate' cannot launder one in, with Canonical_NamesAreNonBlank as the corollary (a blank name collides with every other blank and destroys the runner's drift diagnostic). (2) concrete-phase Name drift - Bootstrap/Phases/** is deliberately <Compile Remove>d by SimSources.props (those classes hold CanvasLayer/Node handles), so a SOURCE scan is the only Godot-free way to read the real literals; ConcretePhaseClasses_DeclareExactlyTheCanonicalNames locates the tree via [CallerFilePath] (the NullableContextHygieneTests / DependencyHygieneTests precedent), reads the Name literal from all 41 concrete ISetupPhase classes and asserts that set is EXACTLY ScenePhaseOrder.Canonical - catching drifted spelling, orphan classes, unbacked canonical entries and two classes claiming one name - and fails loudly rather than skipping when a phase file cannot be parsed (0 or >1 ISetupPhase classes, 0 or >1 readable Name literals, empty result set). PROVEN TO BITE by injection, each reverted: duplicating 'Hud' into both arrays left all 5 original tests GREEN and reddened only Canonical_HasNoDuplicateNames ('Hud' x2 at [8,9]); drifting HudPhase.Name to 'HUD' left all 5 GREEN and reddened only the concrete-name scan. The entry's optional Tier-2 GdUnit4 companion was deliberately NOT built - the Godot-free source scan closes the same hole at Tier-1 where it runs on every gate, while a GdUnit4 test is Godot-coupled and ungateable by `dotnet test` in a Godot-free burn-down; the residual gap (phases construct/run without throwing) stays on the in-engine gate and is filed as DW-721. DETERMINISM: no risk - test-only, ScenePhaseOrder is presentation bootstrap folded into nothing; zero goldens re-recorded, SimChecksum / CanonicalModelHash / StartStateHash untouched, no AlgoVersion change. GATE: `dotnet build godot/godot.csproj` succeeded, 0 errors (6 pre-existing warnings); suite raw 5256 passed / 1 failed / 1 skipped, the lone failure being CanonicalModelHashPerfTests.MaxCapsScenario_ColdCompute_StaysUnderTheRegressionCeiling (314.63 ms vs a 250 ms ceiling) - the documented CPU-contention timing flake, PASSED 2/2 in isolation - so the suite counts GREEN: 5254 baseline + 3 new = 5257 non-skipped, reconciling exactly. Follow-on filed as DW-720.
decision: 2026-07-28 correct-course — rides bundle scenecontext-producer-consumer-guards (Epic 15, Story 15.7)

### DW-237: N≥3 minority desync self-halt silently kills the surviving majority's desync guard
origin: migrated from legacy ledger ("Deferred from: code review of story-1.9a (2026-06-24)"), 2026-07-28
location: godot/src/Multiplayer/Server/ServerHost.cs:95-103; godot/src/Multiplayer/LockstepManager.cs:372,482-486
severity: critical
reason: ESCALATED from unreachable (N=2) to live (9.7/9.15 shipped 4-player MP: MpSeatCeiling=4). ProcessVerdict still sends DesyncAlert without Halted; the alerted minority halts, stops sending checksums while staying CONNECTED, so DropReporter never runs, _expected still counts it, no bucket completes → survivors' guard silently dead. status: done 2026-08-03
resolution: resolved by sweep bundle dw-minority-halt-quorum-rebase — ServerHost.ProcessVerdict now drops each alerted minority slot from the collector quorum immediately after sending its DesyncAlert, logs the rebase (slot + resulting quorum), and routes any window the reduced quorum now completes through the same clean/alert/HALT logic — the recorded decision's quorum-drop arm. Extracted RouteReTalliedWindows so the Story-9.6 disconnect path and the new rebase share one router; the drop is idempotent with the later disconnect-driven DropReporter so the quorum never double-decrements into a trivially-passing lone reporter, and recursion is bounded by MaxSlots. LockstepManager.cs needed no change — its terminal halt on DesyncAlert is the intended UX-DR64e behavior and the cause described here, not a fix site. Residual: the merged-tick command half is still starved by a halted-but-connected peer — filed as a seen-again escalation on DW-433.
decision: 2026-07-28 correct-course — bundle minority-halt-quorum-rebase (Epic 15, Story 15.7): drop an alerted minority from the quorum or force-disconnect/HALT it; pairs with the ledgered "drop-path HALT branch untested" 9.6 bullet. ### DW-242: Zero-damage units are locked out of Patrol/Follow/AttackBuilding by the pre-switch combat gate
origin: migrated from legacy ledger ("Deferred from: code review of story-1.12 (2026-06-25)" + "Deferred from: code review of story-2.9a (2026-07-01)" item 1 — merged), 2026-07-28
location: godot/src/Combat/CombatSystem.cs:121-126
severity: medium
reason: The `EffectiveAttackDamage == 0 → continue` gate still sits above the whole command switch (which now also carries AttackBuilding/PickupItem/Patrol/Follow), so zero-damage non-gatherers sit inert in those commands with no normalize-to-Idle. Fix = hoist pure-movement branches above the gate TOGETHER WITH DW-202's wave filter (else zero-damage units start auto-attacking). Verified 2026-07-28.
status: done 2026-08-04
resolution: workflow burn-down bundle noncombatant-command-gate - CombatSystem.cs:126's pre-switch `EffectiveAttackDamage == Fixed.Zero -> continue` blanket skip now routes through a new movement-only TickNonCombatant instead of skipping the entity, exactly the one-gate-hoist this entry prescribes. AttackMove and Patrol run their movement half only (ResumeAttackMove/ResumePatrol - AttackMove's arrival normalize-to-Idle is what also closes DW-202's pool leak at the combat end); Follow reuses TickFollowCombat verbatim because it is pure tracking for every unit; AttackTarget and AttackBuilding normalize to Idle with both target refs and both flags cleared, the same disposal the gatherer guard directly above applies to the same orders (this entry's reason line names no-normalize-to-Idle as the defect). Every acquisition/engagement path stays CLOSED to non-combatants - deliberately, since this entry warns that hoisting engagement would make zero-damage units auto-attack. Determinism: all 25 goldens byte-unchanged because every resting state (Idle/Move/Stop/HoldPosition/Build/PickupItem) stays a no-op byte-identical to the old blanket skip; every golden scenario carrying a zero-damage unit (FormationSeparation, CommandVocabulary, MultiFaction, MergedTickN2, MidMatchDrop) was audited and all sit in Idle or Move. Gate: build 0 errors, suite 4860/0/1, 16 of the 18 new tests proven RED against the run-base - the 2 that pass in both states are deliberate fences (a non-combatant at Idle or under Move must stay completely untouched, so a future edit that routes movement can never quietly start routing engagement). Residual filed separately as DW-643: the zero-damage predicate is spelled `== Fixed.Zero` here and `> Fixed.Zero` in the AI, complements only by ModifierSystem's clamp, which SaveGameState's restore path bypasses.
decision: 2026-07-28 correct-course — bundle noncombatant-command-gate (Epic 15, Story 15.4)

TFilter is struct-constrained so the per-candidate test is devirtualized with no delegate and no boxing, preserving the zero-alloc contract. The unfiltered QueryRadius is left byte-identical on purpose: MovementSystem's separation pass uses it and its output feeds Position, a SimChecksum input — that half is DW-512. No cap constant changed (RulesetHash untouched); no golden moved or was re-recorded.

### DW-250: SearchArea truncates the hit buffer BEFORE the faction filter — enemy fan-out under-selects
origin: migrated from legacy ledger ("Deferred from: code review of story-2.1 (2026-06-25)"), 2026-07-28
location: godot/src/Effects/SearchAreaEffect.cs:64-78
severity: medium

status: done 2026-08-03
resolution: resolved by sweep bundle dw-searcharea-target-selection-correctness — Root cause was ordering: the 64-slot buffer filled via the UNFILTERED QueryRadius, sorted, then compacted by TargetMatcher, so non-matching entities consumed slots before the filter ran (an Enemy-filtered nuke cast amid 64+ of the caster's own allies selected ZERO enemies while enemies stood in the radius). Fixed by evaluating the predicate BEFORE a candidate may occupy a slot, via the new SpatialHash.QueryRadiusLowestIds<TFilter>; the predicate is still the single TargetMatcher.Matches, wrapped as the new nested TargetMatcher.QueryFilter so no consumption site can drift. Proven RED without the fix (EnemyFanOut_IsNotStarved_ByACrowdOfLowerIdAllies and OverCap_MatchingEnemies_StillFillTheWholeFanOut_WhenAlliesCrowdTheRadius both fail on the pre-fix body).

### DW-266: StatusFlags are authorable and hashed but read by NOTHING — authored stuns are silent no-ops
origin: migrated from legacy ledger ("Deferred from: story 2.2b (2026-06-26)"), 2026-07-28
location: godot/src/Combat/CombatSystem.cs; godot/src/Navigation/MovementSystem.cs; godot/src/Effects/AbilityCastSystem.cs
severity: critical
reason: HEADLINE GAP — StatusFlagsOf is written/folded (EntityWorld, ModifierStore, SimChecksum) but whole-repo grep shows zero reads in CombatSystem/MovementSystem/AbilityCastSystem, while all five flags (Disarmed/Stunned/Rooted/Silenced/Invulnerable) are authorable through the 2.5 editor and JSON. An authored stun costs energy, shows in the HUD, and does nothing. Determinism-relevant fix (golden re-baseline). Verified 2026-07-28.
status: done 2026-08-04
resolution: Bundle status-flags-become-real (workflow burn-down 2026-08-04) — verified still open (written/folded/authorable/rendered, read by ZERO runtime consumers), then implemented exactly the recorded 2026-07-28 routing below. Stunned → a whole-unit gate at the top of CombatSystem.Tick (no cooldown tick, acquire, chase, attack or on-hit rider; drops AttackTarget, clears Attacking) + the MovementSystem anchor + the AbilityCastSystem refusal; Rooted → the MovementSystem anchor, exempt from seek AND separation (mirroring the Story 1.12 HoldPosition anchor) so neither its own order nor a neighbour shove displaces it; Disarmed → both CombatSystem damage choke points (TryDealDamage + TryDealBuildingDamage), checked BEFORE the cooldown is consumed so a disarm burns no attack timer and spawns no projectile; Silenced → an atomic TryCast refusal (nothing debited, no cooldown, no graph run) with a new DenialReason; Invulnerable → DamageResolver.Apply, the single entity-damage path covering melee hitscan, projectile primary + splash and every DamageEffect leaf. Every gate is a PAUSE not a cancel (CommandState/MoveTarget/Moving untouched) so the order resumes the tick the modifier expires. Two new DenialReason members (Silenced, Stunned) + DenialReasonText mappings. Determinism: no golden moved or was re-recorded — StatusFlagsOf is None for every entity in every recorded golden scenario, so no new branch is ever entered. CONTENT LANDMINE FIXED: godot/resources/data/abilities/aura_guard.json authored `"status": "Stunned"` on an Ally-filtered +5-armor aura — a no-op while the flag was unread, a permanent mass-stun of your own army the instant it became real; set to "None". Coverage: 13 tests in StatusFlagRuntimeTests.cs including an end-to-end authored-modifier install/expire (no test shortcut writes StatusFlagsOf); negative control against f93e678 fails 12 of 13, the 13th being the None no-op control that must pass on both sides. Gates: dotnet build 0 errors; Tier-1 4855/0/1 (baseline 4842 + 13 new), no flake.
decision: 2026-07-28 correct-course — Story 15.3 (status effects become real): Disarmed→CombatSystem gate, Rooted/Stunned→MovementSystem+combat, Silenced→AbilityCastSystem refuse, Invulnerable→DamageResolver

### DW-272: Stacked periodic Modifier doesn't scale its DoT/HoT per stack
origin: migrated from legacy ledger ("Deferred from: code review of story-2.2b (2026-06-26)"), 2026-07-28
location: godot/src/Effects/ModifierStore.cs:320-324,536-541
severity: low
reason: Unchanged — RunEffect executes the period graph once per slot with no _stackCount term while RemoveSlot multiplies stat deltas by it; a 3-stack DoT ticks 1×. Design decision + validator warning first; behavior change waits for stacking content. Verified 2026-07-28.
status: done 2026-08-07
resolution: Story 15.12 (behavior half; the DW-278 warning half was already done) — implemented Alec's CREATOR-AUTHORED-MODE decision exactly: a new authored PeriodicStackMode { None, Multiply, Repeat } on the Modifier model. Repeat re-runs the period graph min(stacks,cap) times (armor-per-hit); Multiply runs it once at ×min(stacks,cap) magnitude (armor-once) via a new identity-guarded EffectContext.PulseScale on the direct-magnitude leaves; the system-level runaway cap is EffectCaps.MaxPeriodicStackScale=8 (folded into RulesetHash, bumped 2→3). DEFAULT None preserves today's non-scaling pulse BYTE-FOR-BYTE — no shipped content changes, no per-tick SimChecksum golden moves. The new folded field moves CanonicalModelHash (14→15, hero-start-state.golden re-recorded) exactly as predicted. Surfaced in the ability editor alongside the StackRule split (in-engine gate PASS: Periodic-stacking dropdown 3 items None/Multiply/Repeat; the corrected footgun warning surfaces via DW-503). AbilityValidator warning narrowed to fire only when the pulse genuinely does not scale. Tier-1 green 6275/1/0.
goldens: none-by-default — the authored default must preserve today's non-scaling pulse byte-for-byte, so shipped content is unchanged and no existing golden moves; the new authored fields DO move CanonicalModelHash. Not batch material.
decision: 2026-07-28 correct-course — warning half in bundle modifier-period-semantics-and-authoring-warnings (Story 15.3); behavior half rides Story 15.12
decision: 2026-08-06 correct-course (Alec) — CREATOR-AUTHORED MODE + SYSTEM CAP. Asked to rule between multiply-the-pulse / run-it-N-times / cap-it, Alec rejected the premise that the engine should pick: "I want the creator to have the freedom of choosing this. We can create a cap to protect the system, but I want the user to be able to create a stackable debuff or buff in as many ways as they want." Build an authored periodic-stacking mode offering BOTH multiply and repeat, plus a system-level cap on the periodic contribution as a runaway protector, surfaced in the ability editor's existing stacking dropdown alongside the StackRule split. DEFAULT MUST PRESERVE TODAY'S NON-SCALING PULSE BYTE-FOR-BYTE (same principle as the StackRule grouped-variant split). This makes DW-272 a BUILD, not a bounded correction — it leaves the Phase C batch (Story 15.22) and lands entirely on Story 15.12, resolving its 15.3/15.12 double-homing.

### DW-283: Ability cost debits discard return values — negative CostEnergy would partial-spend
origin: migrated from legacy ledger ("From code review of story-2.4a (2026-06-28)"), 2026-07-28
location: godot/src/Effects/AbilityCastSystem.cs:193,215-217,240-252
severity: medium
reason: Unchanged, and the check-then-debit surface GREW: a 4th cost (CostHealth, debited after the graph) now relies on the same pre-check/debit lockstep; TryDebitEnergy returns false without mutating on cost<0 while the pre-check passes negatives. Gated only by the authoring validator today. Cheap fail-closed asserts on the debit returns. Verified 2026-07-28.
status: done 2026-08-04
resolution: workflow burn-down bundle ability-cast-path-hardening - verified still-open at AbilityCastSystem.cs:241-243 (all three cost debits discarded their return values). Root cause characterised: the affordability pre-checks are `have >= cost` comparisons that a NEGATIVE authored cost passes trivially, while the debits DISAGREE about it - ModifierStore.TryDebitEnergy refuses cost<0 without mutating, but ResourceStore.SpendOre/SpendCrystal subtract a negative and therefore GRANT resources, so a negative-cost ability printed ore/crystal, ran its effect graph and started its cooldown while its energy price silently never applied. Fix = a fail-closed negative-cost gate (energy/ore/crystal/health) BEFORE any mutation, plus checked + short-circuited debits that roll back exactly what landed on an unexpected refusal (AC6 refuse-atomic); the rollback arm is the documented fail-closed backstop and the gate is what makes it unreachable for validator-clean content. Determinism: CombatEventQueue is not a SimChecksum input and the gate/rollback are unreachable for clean content; no golden moved or was re-recorded. Covered by rows in the bundle's 24 new Tier-1 tests (godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Effects/AbilityCastPathHardeningTests.cs), proven RED by temporarily reverting the gate + checked debits in place (6 failures together with the DW-284 validator revert), then restored and re-verified. Gate: build 0 errors, suite 4866/0/1 run twice (baseline 4842 + 24), no flake. Residual filed separately as DW-642: ResourceStore.SpendOre/SpendCrystal still CREDIT on a negative cost for every OTHER caller (BuildingSystem, BuyItemCommand, ReviveHeroCommand, AiOpponentSystem) - the systemic primitive-level fix is out of this entry's scope.
decision: 2026-07-28 correct-course — bundle ability-cast-path-hardening (Epic 15, Story 15.9)

### DW-284: SecondsToTicks 16.16 overflow for cooldowns above ~1092s — no validator upper bound
origin: migrated from legacy ledger ("From code review of story-2.4a (2026-06-28)"), 2026-07-28
location: godot/src/Effects/AbilityCastSystem.cs:81,255; godot/src/Core/Definitions/AbilityValidator.cs:81-82
severity: low
reason: Unchanged — conversion unclamped, validator has only the lower bound. ScenarioDirector guards its own conversion with Math.Max(1, ...) — precedent for the one-line fix + validator upper bound. Verified 2026-07-28.
status: done 2026-08-04
resolution: workflow burn-down bundle ability-cast-path-hardening - verified still-open at AbilityCastSystem.cs:81 + AbilityValidator.cs:93-94. SecondsToTicks multiplied through Fixed.operator*, whose 16.16 product is cast back to int32, so any cooldown above ~1092.27 s wrapped to a NEGATIVE tick count - which the `> 0` countdown gate reads as ready, i.e. the longest authorable cooldown became NO cooldown at all (measured: 2000 s -> -5536 ticks). Fix = a 64-bit intermediate (`(long)seconds.Raw * TicksPerSecond >> 16`), algebraically identical below the bound, plus the missing validator UPPER bound referencing the new public AbilityCastSystem.MaxCooldownSeconds (raw int.MaxValue/TICKS_PER_SECOND) rather than a hand-copied number (DW-125 lesson). Determinism: AbilityCooldownTicks is folded (SimChecksum v7), so byte-identity below the bound is pinned by an explicit test over 0/3/6/10/12/15/20 s, the sub-tick 0.01 s case and the boundary value itself; all shipped ability cooldowns are 0-20 s. No golden moved and none was re-recorded. Proven RED by reverting SecondsToTicks in place (1 failure) and the validator bound (part of the 6-failure revert), both then restored and re-verified. Gate: build 0 errors, suite 4866/0/1 run twice.
decision: 2026-07-28 correct-course — bundle ability-cast-path-hardening (Epic 15, Story 15.9)

### DW-297: DraftNode.Depth()/SearchAreaDepth() are Tier-1-tested but unused by production
origin: migrated from legacy ledger ("Deferred from: code review of story-2.5b (2026-06-29)"), 2026-07-28
location: godot/src/CreationSuite/AbilityDraft.cs:277-309
severity: low
reason: Unchanged — only referenced from AbilityDraftTests; production re-derives via TreeCtx/CountNodes. Delete or pin semantics vs EffectCaps.MaxEffectDepth. Verified 2026-07-28.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: closed by workflow burn-down (bundle abilitydraft-deadcode) — verified STILL OPEN against current code first (`Depth()`/`SearchAreaDepth()` referenced by exactly one place in the repo, `AbilityDraftTests.Metrics_CountDepthSearchArea_AreCorrect:135-136`; production `AbilityEditorPanel.Advanced.cs` derives both depths TOP-DOWN via its `TreeCtx` struct and calls only `CountNodes()`), then closed by the DELETE arm of the entry's either/or. Note the location line above is STALE — the file actually lives at godot/src/Core/Definitions/AbilityDraft.cs (filed as DW-759). WHY DELETE, NOT PIN: (1) the bottom-up subtree metrics cannot answer the panel's actual question — "which kinds may I add IN THIS SLOT" depends on depth ABOVE the slot, which only the top-down TreeCtx has, and a freshly-added node is always a leaf so its own subtree depth is always 1; wiring them in would mean rewriting the panel to a worse design; (2) the panel is src/CreationSuite/**, which godot/CLAUDE.md puts behind a mandatory in-engine gate — out of scope for a Godot-free bundle. BONUS DEFECT FOUND: `Depth()` did not actually agree with the cap it claimed to mirror — it counted EVERY node on a path including the terminal leaf (self = 1) while `EffectCaps.MaxEffectDepth` counts COMPOSITION nodes only (`EffectBounds.Validate`: root frame = 0, leaves contribute nothing), so a legal chain of 8 nested compositions ending in a leaf measured 9 and any `Depth() <= MaxEffectDepth` guard built on it would have rejected content the loader accepts; that off-by-a-leaf is now documented in the code comment and pinned by test. CHANGES: both methods deleted; `CountNodes()` kept (production spends the 64-node budget against it) and its coverage upgraded from hand-counted literals to a semantic pin that must agree with `AbilityValidator.WalkGraph`'s `MaxTotalEffectNodes` tally at the cap boundary from BOTH sides (64 accepted / 65 rejected naming the cap), using the one shape the two walks could plausibly disagree on — an `ApplyModifier`'s period subtree, a structural leaf to `EffectBounds` but descended by the node tally; plus a guard that the two deleted metrics are not reintroduced unpinned, and a pin of the composition-depth semantics on `EffectBounds` itself so the new comment cannot go stale. TEETH VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY: temporarily stubbing the `Modifier.Period` descent in `CountNodes()` turned `CountNodes_AgreesWithTheValidatorTally_AtTheMaxTotalEffectNodesBoundary` RED (both drafts collapse to 56), then the probe was reverted and green confirmed. Net test delta +3 (one test replaced 1:1, three added). DETERMINISM: no risk — `DraftNode` is a mutable authoring/scratch model that never touches the load/deserialize path and is folded into none of SimChecksum, CanonicalModelHash, StartStateHash or RulesetHash (RulesetHash folds `EffectCaps` constants, untouched); no golden moved and no hash test failed. GATE: `dotnet build godot/godot.csproj` succeeded, 0 errors (6 pre-existing warnings in unrelated files); full suite 5449 passed / 1 failed / 1 skipped, the lone failure being CanonicalModelHashPerfTests.MaxCapsScenario_ColdCompute_StaysUnderTheRegressionCeiling at 254.63 ms vs a 250 ms ceiling — the documented CPU-contention timing flake, 2/2 PASSED when re-run in isolation — so the suite counts GREEN at 5449 = baseline 5446 + 3 new. Follow-on filed as DW-758.
decision: 2026-07-28 correct-course — bundle ability-editor-composer-cleanup (Epic 15, Story 15.9)

### DW-457: The skirmish map/faction catalog scans `res://` content via `System.IO.Directory` over…
origin: migrated from flat appender bullet, 2026-07-30 (A1-E11)
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-11-1-the-real-skirmish-setup-screen-loading-match-start-flow.md`
reason: The skirmish map/faction catalog scans `res://` content via `System.IO.Directory` over `ProjectSettings.GlobalizePath`, which resolves to a real OS directory only in the editor/unpacked runtime — in an exported PCK build those resources are packed and `System.IO` sees no directory, so `SkirmishCatalog.ScanMaps`/`ScanFactions` return empty and the skirmish screen shows "No maps found". — Evidence: `SkirmishCatalog` uses `Directory.GetFiles`; `SkirmishSetupOverlay.Initialize` passes `ProjectSettings.GlobalizePath(res://…)`. This is the same repo-wide pattern already used by `FactionDefinition.LoadSelectableFromDirectory` and the MainScene faction seeding, so it is not unique to this story — but it must migrate to PCK-aware `DirAccess` (or an editor-only gate) before any exported client build ships (Epic 10 release/export work, 10-5/10-8).
status: open

### DW-458: `SkirmishSetupToScenario.Build` drops Open/Closed player slots but leaves the base map's triggers, win-condition…
origin: migrated from flat appender bullet, 2026-07-30 (A1-E11)
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-11-1-the-real-skirmish-setup-screen-loading-match-start-flow.md`
reason: `SkirmishSetupToScenario.Build` drops Open/Closed player slots but leaves the base map's triggers, win-condition spec, and scenario entities byte-identical — so a shipped map authored with per-slot triggers or a per-player-elimination win condition referencing a now-dropped slot boots with dangling references the setup screen never warns about. — Evidence: `Build` rebuilds only `PlayerSlots` (per its own doc-comment) and the transform has no trigger/win-condition reconciliation; reachable if a 3–4-start shipped map with per-slot trigger/win-condition logic is launched as a 1v1 (2 active slots). Low probability today (win-condition presets are mostly last-team-standing), needs a design decision on prune-vs-reject, so deferred rather than patched.
status: done 2026-08-04
resolution: `skirmish-scenario-and-boot` bundle (d16d336) — per the recorded prune-and-reconcile decision, `SkirmishSetupToScenario.Build` now strips/rewrites every per-slot reference left dangling by a dropped-slot launch: trigger events stripped (trigger dropped when none remain), a condition on a dropped slot drops the whole trigger, actions stripped (trigger dropped when empty), kept refs renumbered; win-spec TimedSurvival slot and Assassination/Landmark placement indices remapped or the spec pruned to the built-in fallback; Income nodes owned by dropped slots dropped (their dangling owner_slot previously made the boot validator REJECT the whole built scenario and silently substitute the fallback map — now pinned by a new end-to-end validator test). Identity launches keep reference-identical triggers/win-spec/nodes. Residual scope limitation (trigger_graph IR + custom_events.allowed_raisers) filed as DW-609.
decision: 2026-07-30 Prune-and-reconcile — Strip/rewrite triggers and win-condition clauses referencing dropped slots during Build; add coverage test

The pure decisions (rawSlots from the in-memory scenario; the fail-safe state transition) could be extracted to Godot-free helpers and pinned, mirroring how the `ScenePhaseRunner` progress seam was extracted; live in-engine verification for Epic 11 is otherwise deferred to Epic 10 per project record.
status: done 2026-08-04
resolution: `skirmish-scenario-and-boot` bundle (d16d336) — the boot orchestration's pure decisions extracted to Godot-free `SkirmishBootFlow`/`SkirmishBootHandoff` (Arm/ConsumeStart/RawRegistrySlots/FailBoot/CommitSuccess/TakeReopen + ArmLoad/TakeLoad/DisarmLoad); MainScene and ScenarioLoadPhase.PendingGeneratedScenario delegate to the one handoff, and both named regressions (registry sized from the stale on-disk map; fail-safe not clearing PendingGeneratedScenario) are Tier-1 pinned. FailBoot additionally disarms a pending SP load, closing a pre-existing gap where a failed boot left a stale save armed for a later unrelated launch. The AI-map-generator boot path still peeks the on-disk map for registry sizing — pinned as-is and filed as DW-610; in-engine observation of the refactored path filed as DW-611.

### DW-460: The setup-screen slot swatch (`SkirmishSetupOverlay.SlotColorFor(i)` keyed by the map's start-position ROW index)…
origin: migrated from flat appender bullet, 2026-07-30 (A1-E11)
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-11-1-the-real-skirmish-setup-screen-loading-match-start-flow.md`
reason: The setup-screen slot swatch (`SkirmishSetupOverlay.SlotColorFor(i)` keyed by the map's start-position ROW index) drifts from the actual in-match team color whenever the active (Human/AI) slots are not row-0-contiguous — because `SkirmishSetupToScenario.Build` renumbers active slots to a CONTIGUOUS 0..k-1 span and the in-match color is keyed by that post-transform contiguous index, not the row index. — Evidence: After this follow-up pass's color/order patches, the human always renders Player1=blue in-match, but its setup swatch = `SlotColorAt(rowIndex)` — e.g. a human placed in row 2 (rows 0/1 Open) shows a green swatch while playing blue. This directly contradicts PATCH 7's stated invariant ("the setup swatch can never drift from the in-match team color"). Cosmetic only (a preview swatch), and the correct fix is to color each swatch by the slot's rank among currently-active slots (recomputed on Revalidate) — more than a trivial review patch, so deferred.
status: done 2026-08-03
resolution: workflow burn-down bundle team-color-slot-mapping (commit 5971848) - extracted Build's Human-first-then-row active-slot ordering into SkirmishSetupToScenario.ActiveSlotsInLaunchOrder + LaunchIndexBySlot, Build consumes the same helper so ordering drift is structurally impossible, and SkirmishSetupOverlay.RecolorSwatches now recolors every swatch on each Revalidate by launch RANK (Open/Closed rows render neutral InactiveSlotColor grey). Row-vs-rank keying, Human-first rank, inactive-row omission, and rank/Build renumbering agreement pinned by TeamColorSlotMappingTests; presentation-only so zero goldens moved. Live in-engine observation of the swatch reshuffle still owed - filed as DW-575.

### DW-463: A skirmish launch of `alpha_map_01` reaches Play with only 2 of the 3 units the map authors for start position 0…
origin: migrated from flat appender bullet, 2026-07-30 (A1-E11)
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-11-1-the-real-skirmish-setup-screen-loading-match-start-flow.md`
reason: A skirmish launch of `alpha_map_01` reaches Play with only 2 of the 3 units the map authors for start position 0 (the `mage` at x=-40,z=0 alongside the two workers), in BOTH a same-faction and a cross-faction launch. Not attributed to Story 11.1 — it survives the transform, so the loss is downstream in the applier/Play-entry path. — Evidence: In-engine gate 2026-07-28. Post-launch HUD at `Tick 0/1 [PLAY]` reads `P1: 2 units` for every skirmish launch of `alpha_map_01`, whose `units[]` authors 3 entries for slot 0 (worker, worker, mage) and 2 for slot 1. `SkirmishSetupToScenario.Build` keeps every unit whose slot maps and the slot-0 remap is the identity path (`Build_SameFactionLaunch_LeavesPrePlacedUnitIdsUntouched`), so all 3 are emitted into the built `ScenarioData` — the drop happens after the transform. The pre-launch boot HUD shows `P1: 3` but reads `[EDIT]` and carries a "Placing: P1 [Covenant Transmuter]" placement ghost, so it cannot be used as the control: the EDIT-vs-PLAY comparison may be counting a ghost rather than proving the mage spawns on the legacy path. Needs an applier-level check (does `ScenarioApplier` spawn all 3 slot-0 units, and does Play entry despawn one?) before it can be assigned to this story or confirmed pre-existing. Distinct from the cross-faction roster defect fixed in this story — that one is closed and regression-tested.
status: open

### DW-464: The ONLINE concede path has two unpolished robustness/UX gaps — (a) `LockstepManager.EnqueueConcede`'s online…
origin: migrated from flat appender bullet, 2026-07-30 (A1-E11)
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-11-2-in-match-menu-pause-game-speed-concede-surrender-leave-victory-defeat-score-screen.md`
reason: The ONLINE concede path has two unpolished robustness/UX gaps — (a) `LockstepManager.EnqueueConcede`'s online branch silently drops the concede order when `_pendingCount >= TickCommandPacket.MAX_ORDERS` (returns false, `MainScene.IssueConcede` ignores it, no retry/feedback), and (b) after a confirmed online concede the menu closes immediately with no "surrendering…" feedback while the verdict only latches a tick-round-trip later, so the player is dropped back into a still-live match as if nothing happened. — Evidence: Surfaced by the Story 11.2 adversarial + edge-case review. Both are online-only: the offline path applies the concede immediately (verified in the in-engine gate — P1→LOST resolves next tick), so neither is reachable in the currently-shippable offline skirmish. Live MP is explicitly deferred to Epic 9 (the spec scopes online as "not in-engine verifiable now"), so these are genuine but un-exercisable now. Fix when the MP shell lands: buffer/retry a dropped concede (a rare high-intent order must not be lost on a busy tick) and give the online player pending-surrender feedback (disable Concede / show "Surrendering…") until the verdict latches.
status: done 2026-08-04
resolution: `concede-buffer-retry` bundle (e959dd0) — both halves fixed. (a) New Godot-free `ConcedeBuffer` (godot/src/Multiplayer/ConcedeBuffer.cs, single-file-included in SimSources.props per the DelayMath/HandshakeGate precedent): EnqueueConcede latches a sticky queued flag, Flush's send branch claims a batch slot for it (retrying next send on a full batch), and EnqueueOrder/EnqueueDslEvent reserve the last slot while one is queued so order spam can never starve it; reset on GoOnline/GoSpectate/GoOffline. (b) `InMatchMenuOverlay.SetSurrenderPending` keeps the menu OPEN with Concede disabled and relabeled "Surrendering…", driven by MainScene.IssueConcede from the real EnqueueConcede result (guarded so a spectator's no-op press shows no false promise) and cleared at the three verdict/reset seams. Offline flow unchanged; all changes client-send-side or presentation-only, nothing folded into SimChecksum, zero goldens moved; Tier-1 4118/0/1. Spectator enabled-Concede quirk filed as DW-612; live two-client verification owed via DW-613.

### DW-466: SP saves are not portable across machines and the format cannot detect it; make AiOpponentSystem Fixed-point (or…
origin: migrated from flat appender bullet, 2026-07-30 (A1-E11)
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-11-3-sp-save-load-full-world-serializer-slots-autosave-format-stability.md`
reason: SP saves are not portable across machines and the format cannot detect it; make AiOpponentSystem Fixed-point (or fold a platform/runtime marker into the save header) before advertising cross-machine saves. — Evidence: AiOpponentSystem scoring runs on float (_aggressionWeight, ScoreLaunchAttack), which is not deterministic across CPU/JIT; the save header stamps only algo versions, so a save loaded on another machine can pick a different AI action on the first resumed tick and desync undetectably. 11.3 documents saves as same-machine for 1.0; this is the same float→Fixed dependency already noted for lockstep MP AI.
status: open
decision: 2026-07-30 Migrate AiOpponentSystem float→Fixed — Make saves genuinely portable; also unblocks lockstep MP AI (large effort)

### DW-469: The 256-entry `CombatEventQueue` ring silently drops events when full, and denial/completion cues now share that…
origin: migrated from flat appender bullet, 2026-07-30 (A1-E11)
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-11-4-under-attack-alerts-minimap-pings-event-cues-denial-acknowledgment-feedback.md`
reason: The 256-entry `CombatEventQueue` ring silently drops events when full, and denial/completion cues now share that lossy queue with no priority — a large single-tick battle (>256 hit pushes) can drop a denial or training-complete cue. — Evidence: `CombatEventQueue.MAX_EVENTS=256` with silent drop-when-full (pre-existing); 11.4 adds `OrderDenied`/`TrainingComplete`/`ResearchComplete` consumption to the same queue. Reserving headroom or prioritising non-hit events is a queue-design change beyond this story's scope; self-healing and low-likelihood.
status: done 2026-08-04
resolution: Bundle combat-event-queue-capacity (workflow burn-down 2026-08-04) — verified still open against current code, then fixed. Two-lane admission behind a single private `HasRoomFor(type)` gate both `Push` overloads and `PushDenied` route through: `MAX_AMBIENT_EVENTS = 256` (the old flat capacity, so battle-cue admission and drain-side worst case are unchanged) + `PRIORITY_RESERVE = 64` slots only low-volume notification cues can occupy, `MAX_EVENTS = 320`; `public static bool IsAmbient(CombatEventType)` is a closed list of spammy types with a fail-safe default (a new enum member is treated as a notification, over-protecting rather than starving a cue). Deliberately NOT a 4x ring: growing it multiplies per-frame drain work in exactly the huge-battle frame where budget is tightest, for zero perceptible gain. Determinism: no golden/checksum/replay can move — every `.Count`/`.Get(` read resolves only in AudioManager/CombatFeedbackBridge/MatchAlertBridge, no sim system reads the queue and SimChecksum references it only in comments; no new instance fields so the StoreClearCompleteness fixture needed no change. Mutant-verified: reverting `HasRoomFor` to the lane-blind `_count < MAX_EVENTS` fails 8 of the 26 new tests including DenialRaisedDuringABattleFlood_IsStillAdmittedWithItsReason. Gates: dotnet build 0 errors (11 pre-existing warnings); Tier-1 4868/0/1 (baseline 4842 + exactly 26 new); a repeat run produced only the documented CanonicalModelHashPerf flake, which passed 2/2 in isolation.

### DW-472: **RESOLVED 2026-07-30** — `MainScene.PendingLoadedSave` (static) survived an early-return launch-gate veto and…

source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-11-4-under-attack-alerts-minimap-pings-event-cues-denial-acknowledgment-feedback.md`

reason: **RESOLVED 2026-07-30** — `MainScene.PendingLoadedSave` (static) survived an early-return launch-gate veto and leaked into the next, unrelated skirmish. — Evidence: Found by the post-merge ultra-review of 11-3/11-4 (2026-07-29), `MainScene.cs:2288`. Fix shape: clear the static in a `finally` (or at entry, into a local) so no early-return path can leave it armed. Not reproduced live; reasoned from the control flow.
status: resolved
resolution: Split the body into `ResetToAuthoredStartCore` and wrapped it in a `try/finally` that disarms the statics (with a "Load discarded" notice) on any non-completing exit. Deliberately a FAILURE-path sweep, not consume-at-entry: `LaunchSkirmish` reaches this via `GetTree().ReloadCurrentScene()`, so the statics must survive the reload for whichever reset call actually enters Play — capturing at entry would let an earlier boot-sequence reset swallow the load. Success path unchanged, verified in-engine by a save/load round trip (loaded an autosave at tick 3599 from a live match at tick 2954; post-reload tick 3717 — it jumped UP past the pre-load tick, which a restart cannot do).

### DW-476: **RESOLVED 2026-07-30** — `SelectionSystem.ConfirmOrder` acked unconditionally, so a Shift-queued order onto full…
origin: migrated from flat appender bullet, 2026-07-30 (A1-E11)
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-11-4-under-attack-alerts-minimap-pings-event-cues-denial-acknowledgment-feedback.md`
location: SelectionSystem.cs:634
reason: **RESOLVED 2026-07-30** — `SelectionSystem.ConfirmOrder` acked unconditionally, so a Shift-queued order onto full order rings produced the confirmation AND the `QueueFull` refusal for one click. — Evidence: Found by the post-merge ultra-review (2026-07-29), `SelectionSystem.cs:634`. Note the issue-time-optimism itself is the deliberate GDD §6 design (and was rejected as a finding during 11.4's own review); the defect is only the contradictory DOUBLE feedback on the one guard that rejects synchronously at issue time. Cheapest fix: suppress the ack when the local ring-full precheck already knows the order cannot be queued.
status: resolved
resolution: `ConfirmOrder` takes a `queued` flag and, when set, acks only if some selected unit still has ring room — reading the same FOLDED `OrderQueueCount` the guard rejects on, so the two cannot disagree. Threaded through the four queued-capable issue paths (move, attack-move, attack-target, attack-building). Issue-time optimism is retained everywhere else; this covers only the guard that rejects synchronously at issue time.

### DW-477: **RESOLVED 2026-07-29** — Alt+LMB on the minimap dropped a ping AND panned the camera to the pinged point
origin: migrated from flat appender bullet, 2026-07-30 (A1-E11)
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-11-4-under-attack-alerts-minimap-pings-event-cues-denial-acknowledgment-feedback.md`
location: MinimapBridge.cs:248
reason: **RESOLVED 2026-07-29** — Alt+LMB on the minimap dropped a ping AND panned the camera to the pinged point. — Evidence: Found by the post-merge ultra-review (2026-07-29), `MinimapBridge.cs:248`, then CONFIRMED IN-ENGINE the same day: an Alt+LMB at minimap px (1750, 1030) moved the camera pivot to `(-79.36, 0, 74.24)`, the exact world point clicked. Root cause was wider than first described: the Alt branch consumed only the PRESS, so BOTH the matching release (the pan branch never tested `mb.Pressed`) and any drag leaked through. FIXED by a `_pingGesture` latch that swallows the remainder of the gesture, self-healing on a plain press so a release delivered outside the Control cannot strand it. Re-verified in-engine: Alt+click and Alt+drag both leave the pivot at `(0,0,0)`; a plain click still pans to `(-79.36, 0, 74.24)`.
status: resolved

### DW-478: Depth-5 production queue lets a player queue N units against unchanged live SupplyUsed (supply is consumed at…
origin: migrated from flat appender bullet, 2026-07-30 (A1-E11)
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-11-6-production-queue-depth-5-with-queue-display-and-cancel-refund.md`
location: godot/src/Economy/BuildingSystem.cs:422-427
reason: Depth-5 production queue lets a player queue N units against unchanged live SupplyUsed (supply is consumed at spawn, never reserved at enqueue), so queuing can overshoot the supply cap by up to 4. — Evidence: BuildingSystem.TrainUnit (godot/src/Economy/BuildingSystem.cs:422-427) gates each enqueue with resources.HasSupply against SupplyUsed, which is recomputed from LIVE units and never incremented by enqueue; five enqueues therefore all see the same headroom. At depth-1 (2.8) at most one order was ever in flight so overshoot was impossible — the depth-5 widening (this story) introduces it. Deferred, not fixed: reserving supply on enqueue (WC3-strict) vs consume-at-spawn (the existing model, kept deliberately) is a design decision the intent does not specify; consequence is a self-correcting balance overshoot (own-ore overspend, deterministic across peers), not a crash/desync/free-resource exploit.
status: done 2026-08-04
resolution: closed by workflow burn-down (bundle production-queue-correctness) - BuildingSystem.TrainUnit now gates on HasSupply(faction, cost + QueuedSupply(faction)) - a gate-time projection re-derived from the already-folded production queue, never written into the checksum-folded SupplyUsed. Per the recorded 2026-07-30 WC3-strict decision.
decision: 2026-07-30 Reserve supply at enqueue (WC3-strict) — Count queued supply against the cap to prevent overshoot
