### DW-485: FlowFieldSystem._cache is an unbounded Dictionary — every distinct destination cell holds a ~200 KB field until the next building/terrain change
origin: filed from the Epic-11 retrospective (action item A8-E11) and the A5-E11 map-size verdict, 2026-07-30
source_spec: `_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/map-size-brainstorm-brief.md` (V2 prerequisite / V5 item 2)
location: godot/src/Navigation/FlowFieldSystem.cs (`_cache`, Dictionary<int, FlowField> keyed by goal cell)
severity: medium
reason: `FlowFieldSystem._cache` has no eviction limit — a field is computed on demand per unique goal cell and lives until `RebuildObstacles` / `SetBuildingObstacle` / `SetStaticBlocked` / `InvalidateCache` clears the whole dictionary, so ~100 distinct move orders between building events holds ~20 MB. — Evidence: read during the 2026-07-30 map-size verdict work; the cache is cleared only on obstacle/terrain change, never bounded by size or age, and nothing evicts a stale goal cell. Not a determinism risk (the cache is a pure function of the grid and is rebuilt identically on every peer) and not a per-tick cost — this is a retained-memory issue. Worth fixing on its own merits, and a HARD PREREQUISITE for map-size Route B (`GRID_SIZE` 128→256), which would multiply each entry to ~800 KB / ~80 MB at the same order count. Fix: an LRU or size cap on the dictionary. Filed as a numbered entry so a sweep can actually pick it up — the retro action item A8-E11 had no ledger entry and was therefore invisible to triage.
status: done 2026-08-03
resolution: closed by workflow burn-down bundle `flowfield-cache-bound` (commit 71b585d) - FlowFieldSystem._cache bounded at MAX_CACHED_FIELDS = 32 with deterministic monotonic-stamp LRU eviction routed through one ClearCache helper; evicted fields are never pooled so in-flight FlowFieldBridge references stay valid and an evicted field recomputes byte-identical; 6 new Godot-free tests, zero goldens moved.

### DW-488: ModifierSystem.AccumulateBonus's `+=` accumulator stays unsaturated after the DW-28 recompute clamp — a large POSITIVE +MaxHealth stack that wraps the accumulator negative now KILLS the over-buffed unit via the new DW-325 trigger
origin: deferred by review of `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-dw-28-325-modifier-effective-stat-clamp-and-death.md`, 2026-08-01
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-dw-28-325-modifier-effective-stat-clamp-and-death.md`
location: godot/src/Effects/ModifierSystem.cs:152-155 (AccumulateBonus `_flat*Bonus[id] += delta`, wrapping)
severity: medium
reason: DW-28 saturated the `Base + bonus` READ in `RecomputeEntity` but not the per-modifier accumulator write, so a stack of large +MaxHealth modifiers can wrap `_flatMaxHealthBonus` negative BEFORE the read; `AddSaturating(Base, wrappedNegative)` then saturates to `MinValue` → `Max(0,…)==0` → the new DW-325 trigger now KILLS the over-buffed unit (previously it was a benign 0-ceiling zombie), a strictly worse divergent outcome. — Evidence: adversarial + edge-case + intent-alignment lenses independently landed on it; `AddSaturating`'s own docstring concedes "a widen-then-clamp cannot recover a value that has ALREADY wrapped in the int add." Not closable by saturating the accumulator itself — per-step saturation would break `AccumulateBonus`'s order-independence invariant at the boundary; DW-28's intent offered "or a Base+modifier authoring bound" as the alternative. Full closure = a content-authoring cap on `MaxStacks × delta` magnitude (a validator rule). Content-gated + requires an already-extreme base; deterministic (no desync).
status: done 2026-08-04
resolution: closed by workflow burn-down (bundle modifier-robustness-and-ceiling) - Closed on the authoring side as the entry prescribes: Modifier.MaxStatDeltaTotalRaw (int.MaxValue / EffectCaps.MaxModifiersPerEntity) + Modifier.MaxAuthorableStacks, exposed as Modifier.CheckAuthoringBounds() and enforced fail-closed by AbilityValidator on every ApplyModifierEffect across all four stat deltas, making the 8-slot accumulator un-wrappable by construction. Not added to EffectCaps (would move RulesetHash).

### DW-489: ModifierStore.Apply / RemoveByModifierId gained a "target may be destroyed on return" post-condition (DW-325); external callers were not audited and cannot distinguish "installed & alive" from "installed & host died"

severity: medium
reason: The DW-325 kill makes `Apply` and `RemoveByModifierId` able to `Destroy`+recycle the host, a post-condition they never had; only the 3 INTERNAL `ApplyStatDeltas` callers were guarded. `ItemSystem.ApplyItemStatModifier` returns `Apply`'s `true` ("installed") straight through as claim-success, and `RemoveByModifierId` is now lethal so a +MaxHealth item drop/consume can re-enter `DropAll`→`DropOne` on the in-flight slot and emit a duplicate `ItemDropped` event; a future creator-authored net-negative-MaxHealth ("cursed") item would equip onto/claim a corpse. — Evidence: adversarial + edge-case lenses; `ApplyItemStatModifier` verified to return the raw `Apply` bool with no post-`IsAlive` check, and the `DropOne`/`UseItem` re-entrancy paths reach the lethal `RemoveByModifierId` before their own event/Destroy writes. Content-gated (Block-If confirmed only `aura_guard.json`=0 and `ring_of_vigor.json`=+50 author MaxHealth). Closure = document the post-condition + audit/guard external `Apply`/`RemoveByModifierId` callers (or a tri-state result).

resolution: 2026-08-05 closed by the itemsystem-modifier-death-audit bundle (workflow burn-down run).

### DW-491: The DW-325 ceiling-collapse kill is gated on the ABSOLUTE `EffectiveMaxHealth == 0`, not on a collapse TRANSITION — a live entity legitimately at ceiling 0, or a positive heal applied to one, is lethal
origin: deferred by review of `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-dw-28-325-modifier-effective-stat-clamp-and-death.md`, 2026-08-01
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-dw-28-325-modifier-effective-stat-clamp-and-death.md`
location: godot/src/Effects/ModifierStore.cs:566-567 (`if (_world.IsAlive(id) && _world.EffectiveMaxHealth[id] == Fixed.Zero) KillEntity(...)`)
severity: low
reason: The kill fires whenever a MaxHealth-touching modifier leaves the host at ceiling 0 while alive, regardless of sign or prior ceiling — so an entity that legitimately sits at `EffectiveMaxHealth == 0` (e.g. a base-0 / item-sustained host) is killed by ANY MaxHealth modifier, and even a POSITIVE +MaxHealth heal applied to such a host satisfies the gate and is lethal, contradicting the "net-negative-MaxHealth only" wording in the same comment. — Evidence: adversarial + edge-case lenses; the gate has no sign check on `maxHealthChange` and no "ceiling WAS >0 and dropped to 0 this apply" transition test. Content-gated (no shipped content produces a base-0 live entity; the modifier-delta `!= 0` gate excludes the aura_guard=0 case). Closure = gate on a downward ceiling transition (or on `maxHealthChange < 0`) rather than the absolute value, if a legitimately-ceiling-0 live entity is ever introduced.
status: done 2026-08-04
resolution: closed by workflow burn-down (bundle modifier-robustness-and-ceiling) - The kill is now a downward COLLAPSE transition with three conjuncts - net-negative change, prior ceiling > 0 (snapshotted before the accumulate/recompute), new ceiling == 0 - so a legitimately-ceiling-0 host and any positive +MaxHealth grant are no longer lethal. Every real collapse still kills.

### DW-492: The DW-325 "no 0-HP zombie" invariant is enforced ONLY inside ApplyStatDeltas — RestoreSlot (SP load) and the Tick catch-all recompute can still reconstitute a living 0-ceiling unit
origin: deferred by review of `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-dw-28-325-modifier-effective-stat-clamp-and-death.md`, 2026-08-01
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-dw-28-325-modifier-effective-stat-clamp-and-death.md`
location: godot/src/Effects/ModifierStore.cs (RestoreSlot re-accumulation, no death check) + godot/src/Effects/ModifierSystem.cs (Tick dirty-recompute path, no death check)
severity: low
reason: The ceiling-collapse death only runs on the apply/stack/remove paths through `ApplyStatDeltas`; `RestoreSlot` (save-game load) re-accumulates bonuses and the Tick catch-all recompute both compute `EffectiveMaxHealth` WITHOUT the death check, so a save produced with (future) net-negative-MaxHealth content, or a bonus dirtied outside the store, can load/recompute a living unit at ceiling 0 — the exact zombie DW-325 advertises as impossible, leaving the fresh-apply and loaded states divergent. — Evidence: adversarial + edge-case lenses; verified neither `RestoreSlot` nor the dirty-recompute in `RecomputeEntity` invokes `KillEntity`. Content-gated (requires net-negative-MaxHealth content, none shipped). Closure = run the ceiling==0 death check after load/dirty-recompute, or document that pre-existing ceiling-0 entities are intentionally not retro-killed and prove none can be created.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: closed by workflow burn-down (bundle modifierstore-death-attribution) - New `ModifierStore.RaiseExternalCeilingCollapse`, called from `ModifierSystem.Tick`'s dirty-recompute loop with the ceiling snapshotted before each `RecomputeEntity`; it re-clamps Health under a moved ceiling and raises the death on the SAME DW-491 downward transition (>0 -> 0). One mechanism covers BOTH named paths - `RestoreSlot` accumulates without recomputing, so a loaded entity is dirty and is reconciled at the first resumed tick. SCOPE DEVIATION (deliberate): the worklist intent's absolute `EffectiveMaxHealth==0` check was written pre-DW-491 and would have regressed it, so the TRANSITION form was used, pinned by a test asserting a legitimately-ceiling-0 host survives the external recompute; the check is also deliberately NOT run per restored slot, so a host whose slot 0 restores a -150 MaxHealth debuff before slot 1 restores the offsetting +150 grant is not destroyed mid-restore (own test). This also closes the seen-again stale-snapshot note: the residual pre-tick window can only under-read the ceiling, i.e. fail safe (documented at the gate). No SimChecksum fold; zero goldens moved.

### DW-497: EntityPlacer unit create/undo legs `_world.Destroy(box[0])` with no identity re-check — a redo that fails at world capacity leaves a stale boxed id whose next undo destroys whatever unit recycled that slot
origin: deferred by review of `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-editor-placement-bounds-height-and-sync.md`, 2026-08-01
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-editor-placement-bounds-height-and-sync.md`
location: godot/src/UI/EntityPlacer.cs:~2545 (`BuildCreate` Unit/RestoreUnit undo leg) + :~2557 (combat-fallback undo) + `PlaceUnit` :~771/:~801 (single-place undo legs)
severity: low
reason: The unit create history closures box the created id and undo via `_world.Destroy(box[0])` with no aliveness/generation re-check. Their redo legs guard `if (r >= 0) box[0] = r`, so if a redo's `DoSpawnCombatUnit`/`RestoreUnit` fails at world capacity, `box[0]` retains a now-stale id and the following undo destroys whatever unit has since recycled that free-list slot — corrupting an unrelated live unit. The sibling ITEM path avoids exactly this by routing undo through the generation-checked `_items.TryResolveRef` before `Destroy`; `EntityWorld.Destroy` has no such guard. Pre-existing across `PlaceUnit`; DW-151 added another instance following the same pattern. Extreme trigger (world at capacity + slot recycle). — Evidence: edge-case + adversarial lenses. Closure = gate the unit undo `Destroy` on the boxed id still being Alive (mirror the item path's resolve-before-destroy), or make `EntityWorld.Destroy` generation-safe.
status: open

### DW-498: No automated regression coverage for the LiveMatchSeed plumbing — the offline reset wiring and the online reseed-to-DEFAULT invariant are guarded only by the manual in-engine gate
origin: deferred by review of `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-match-seed-plumbing.md`, 2026-08-03
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-match-seed-plumbing.md`
location: godot/src/Core/Bootstrap/Phases/MatchLifecycleController.cs:157 (online `_ctx.World.Rng.Seed(_ctx.LiveMatchSeed)`) + godot/src/Core/MainScene.cs:2478-2481 (offline mint/reseed/store wiring)
severity: medium
reason: The pure `MatchSeedProducer` is exhaustively unit-tested, but the two seams that APPLY it have no automated test — no test file references `MatchLifecycleController` and `SimResetTests` only covers the sim-layer `ClearForReset` in isolation. The genuinely-new, load-bearing line is the online reseed at :157: pinning `LiveMatchSeed=DEFAULT` is behavior-identical to the old literal, but reseeding `World.Rng` back to DEFAULT is the new desync-prevention invariant (the session `EntityWorld` is reused, so an offline F5 playtest leaves a per-match seed resident). If a future Godot-layer refactor drops or reorders :157, an online match started after an offline playtest in the same session runs this peer on the leftover per-match seed while other peers run DEFAULT — a silent lockstep desync — with a fully green `dotnet test`. The offline wiring is likewise regressible (reorder before `ClearForReset`, or drop the `Rng.Seed`/`LiveMatchSeed` assignment) with a green suite. The change is CORRECT today (re-verified in-engine 2026-08-03); this is durability of the invariant, not a live defect. — Evidence: verification-gap + adversarial lenses; the online arm is documented as "verified by inspection only" in the spec. Closure = a testable seam (extract the reseed step, or a headless harness for `OnMatchStart`) that pre-dirties `World.Rng` to a non-DEFAULT value and asserts the online entry pins it back to DEFAULT, plus an offline-reset assertion that `LiveMatchSeed == World.Rng.State != DEFAULT`.
status: open

### DW-499: Per-launch varying offline match seed removes cross-launch reproducibility for RNG-touching content, with no debug/env override to PIN the offline seed for repro or A/B verification runs
origin: deferred by review of `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-match-seed-plumbing.md`, 2026-08-03

location: godot/src/Core/MainScene.cs:2478 (`MatchSeedProducer.Produce(Time.GetTicksUsec())`)
severity: medium
reason: The offline Edit→Play reset now mints a fresh wall-clock-entropy seed every launch (the intended per-match behavior), so two runs of the same authored scenario diverge on any tick-time RNG (combat crits, DSL `random`). This is by design for the bundle's stated intent (a per-match seed), but it weakens the project's in-engine A/B verification methodology — the gate discipline relies on comparing arms of a choice, and RNG-touching content can no longer be reproduced run-to-run because there is no debug/env flag to pin the offline seed to a fixed value. Out of the bundle's intent (which asked for a per-match seed, not a repro pin), hence deferred rather than added. — Evidence: adversarial + verification-gap lenses. Closure = an opt-in override (env var or debug setting) read as the offline entropy when set, so a verification/repro run can fix the seed while normal play stays per-match.
status: open

### DW-504: Modifier period_ticks/period_effect mismatches are only warned about, never rejected, unlike their while_alive Persistent siblings

origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03
location: godot/src/Core/Definitions/AbilityValidator.cs — ValidatePassiveShape (hard rejects) vs CollectModifierWarnings (warnings)
severity: low
reason: A Persistent carrying a period_effect with period_ticks <= 0 is a HARD reject on a while_alive passive, but the same shape is only a warning for a Modifier, and only a warning for a Persistent on an ACTIVE ability. DW-278 made the asymmetry explicit and diagnosed rather than silent, which was its remit, but it is a deliberate scope boundary and not a finished rule: an author who ignores the warning still ships an inert period. Promoting any of these to errors is a potentially content-breaking gate change that wants its own decision — and it is currently FREE, because all shipped content is clean today (no shipped Modifier has a period_effect), so the cost only rises as content lands.
status: done 2026-08-05
decision: 2026-08-04 Promote the period mismatch to a hard reject now while content is clean — Move the CollectModifierWarnings period_ticks<=0 (and period_ticks>0 with no period_effect) cases into ValidatePassiveShape-style hard rejects for Modifiers and active-ability Persistents, matching the while_alive rule.
resolution: closed by bundle decision-dw-504 (workflow burn-down, 2026-08-05). Verified live first: CollectModifierWarnings emitted the mismatch as a non-fatal warning while ValidatePassiveShape hard-rejected the identical shape on a while_alive Persistent, so the rule depended on where the shape appeared. Implemented the recorded owner decision exactly and no wider — three cases are now hard rejects for EVERY ability: (a) a Modifier with a period_effect and period_ticks <= 0, (b) a Modifier with period_ticks > 0 and no period_effect, (c) a Persistent with a period_effect and period_ticks <= 0 (previously a reject only on while_alive). Mechanism: the renamed CollectModifierDiagnostics/CollectPersistentDiagnostics route those cases into a fatal list on the existing single walk; Validate reports it AFTER ValidatePassiveShape (so the while_alive message keeps precedence and the defect is never double-reported) and after WalkGraph's inline structural errors. Every other DW-278 warning with a live non-inert reading deliberately stays non-fatal. Coverage: new AbilityPeriodMismatchRejectTests.cs (14 tests), proven RED against the pre-fix validator (9/14 failed); the three AbilityInertContentWarningTests cases encoding the old warn-only behaviour were removed as future false-greens and MultipleFootgunsInOneGraph_AllSurface re-armed with shapes that are still warnings. Determinism: content-gate logic only, no data shape changed, nothing folded touched; no shipped ability carries the shape (aura_guard.json is the well-formed no-period shape; furnace_pour/furnace_trickle pair period_ticks 15 with a period_effect) so no content moves and no golden moved. Gate: build 0 errors; suite 5180/1/1 where the lone failure was the documented CanonicalModelHashPerf CPU-contention timing flake (passed 2/2 in isolation) = 5170 baseline +14 -3.

### DW-505: ValidateComplete's mesh_path error mis-routes the wizard: the `faction '<id>'.` prefix defeats StepForError, and the existing test asserts a message shape the validator never produces

origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03
location: godot/src/Core/Definitions/FactionValidator.cs (Located + ValidateComplete's mesh_path loop) vs godot/src/Core/Definitions/FactionDefinerWizardCore.cs StepForError vs godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Definitions/FactionDefinerWizardTests.cs:116-117
severity: medium
reason: ValidateComplete emits "faction 'x'.mesh_path: unit 'grunt' is missing mesh_path…", but StepForError only routes to the Roster step when the message STARTS WITH "unit '" — so in production a missing UNIT mesh_path sends the author to the Buildings & Tech step. The existing theory rows pass the un-prefixed message, so the test is green while the real path mis-routes: a false-green test hiding a live UX defect. Out of the mesh-path bundle's scope (wizard step routing is DW-114 territory, and re-shaping validator message prefixes could ripple through other error-shape assertions). Note the new MeshAssetLint messages deliberately use the un-prefixed "unit '…'"/"building '…'" shape and a test asserts they route correctly, so the two axes now disagree.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: 2026-08-05 resolved by the faction-wizard-mesh-path-routing bundle (workflow burn-down run) - verified LIVE against run-base 6c509c57 before any edit (the worktree was reset from the stale 024025e4 snapshot first). BOTH remedies the entry offered were taken so neither side alone can re-open it, after measuring the message-shape ripple as ZERO (the only literal matches repo-wide were the two false-green FactionDefinerWizardTests rows plus a reverted 2026-07-10 patch artifact; every other assertion is a loose .Contains). PRODUCER (root cause): a new FactionValidator.LocatedItem helper emits "unit '<id>'.mesh_path: must be authored (required for a complete/playable faction '<faction>')", adopting the leading-kind-label convention MeshAssetLint / UnitDefinitionValidator / BuildingDefinitionValidator / TechTreeValidator / ResourceCostValidator already share - so the two mesh_path axes now AGREE and this entry's "two axes disagree" note is closed. The faction id moved to the tail rather than being dropped, verified harmless against all four consumers (FactionLaunchGate wraps with its own "faction '<id>' is incomplete:", LoadSelectableFromDirectory passes the file name, SlotFactionResolver prints slot + abs path, the wizard handles one faction). CONSUMER (defense in depth): StepForError now strips a "faction '<id>'.<field>: " prefix before sniffing the reason; faction-level reasons carry no kind label and still fall through to Buildings & Tech unchanged. COVERAGE: 8 new cases, ALL proven red by reverting the two sources (backed up to scratchpad and restored; no git stash at any point) - the two false-green rows corrected to the real emitted message, two rows pinning the prefixed shape, a theory that re-derives the message from the LIVE validator so it can no longer drift onto a shape nothing produces, a shape-parity test against MeshAssetLint plus faction-id survival, an end-to-end TryFinish routing theory (the only surface where the real UX defect was observable), and a guard that faction-level structural/null/truncated messages still land on the Buildings & Tech fallback after stripping. DETERMINISM: authoring-time strings and wizard tab routing only - nothing folded into SimChecksum / ContentHash / StartStateHash / CanonicalModelHash; no golden re-recorded or moved; all four touched files stay Godot-free. GATE: dotnet build godot/godot.csproj = 0 errors / 6 pre-existing warnings; dotnet test = 5596 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped, exactly the 5588 baseline plus the 8 additions, no flake exception needed. Follow-on filed as DW-776.

### DW-508: ServerBootstrap never builds or injects a PathabilityGrid — the headless/server sim has NO blocked cells while every client does (MP divergence risk)

origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03
location: godot/src/Core/Sim/ServerBootstrap.cs (Build: validates then `new ScenarioApplier(...).Apply(r.Value)` with no SetElevationGrid/SetPathabilityGrid); the only SetPathabilityGrid callers in src/ are the Godot presentation paths ScenarioLoadPhase.cs:284 and MainScene.cs:2510
severity: high
reason: Verified by grep: on the headless path world.Pathability stays null, so MovementSystem's blocked-cell rejection is a no-op server-side while each client's ScenarioLoadPhase injects the real union grid. On any map with painted, prop, water or slope blocking, the arbitrating server's positions — and therefore its checksum — diverge from its peers from the first tick a unit touches a wall. Godot-free and fixable via the existing shared ScenarioApplier.BuildPathabilityGrid recipe, but it CHANGES the server's start state and tick behaviour, so it needs its own determinism-reviewed slice with an explicit golden decision — it could not ride the scenario-validator bundle, whose entire safety argument was that no checksum input moved.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: workflow burn-down bundle server-pathability-grid (2026-08-05) — verified STILL LIVE against current code first (ServerBootstrap.Build validated and applied the scenario at line 85 but called NEITHER SetPathabilityGrid NOR SetElevationGrid, so world.Pathability stayed null on the headless/server leg while every client's ScenarioLoadPhase injected the real union grid); DW-508 is absent from .bmad-loop/decisions.json and its block carries no `decision:` line, so the worklist intent governed scope. FIX: Build now constructs the ScenarioApplier explicitly and, before Apply, injects (a) the elevation grid and (b) the union blocked-cell grid resolved through the ONE shared Godot-free ScenarioApplier.BuildPathabilityGrid recipe the client and the Edit->Play re-apply already share, so the two legs structurally cannot disagree on the blocked-cell set; the grid is derived from the VALIDATED model (r.Value.Value), never the raw argument. A new optional trailing `ElevationGrid? elevationGrid = null` parameter carries the finalized-terrain grid down from the Godot edge (terrain sampling stays Godot-side; ServerBootstrap stays Godot-free, no `using Godot;`), and no existing call site changed. MainScene.cs was deliberately NOT touched — it sits behind the in-engine gate this Godot-free bundle cannot run, and the new parameter defaults to the prior behaviour. DETERMINISM (this entry's stated blocker): NO golden moved and no re-baseline was needed — PathabilityGrid.Resolve returns null when nothing is blocked and a null grid makes both setters exact no-ops (EntityWorld defaults both to null); every golden scenario's inputs were checked directly (the in-code GoldenApplierScenario.BuildModel mirror and the shipped map_02_iron_crossing.json / alpha_map_01.json carry no painted layer, no props, no water and no slope config), so the server path stays byte-identical there, confirmed empirically by a green full suite including the applier/server goldens, CanonicalModelHash and StartStateHash. COVERAGE: new godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Server/ServerPathabilityInjectionTests.cs (8 Godot-free cases), proven RED by temporarily disabling the two injection lines — 6 of 8 fail without the fix (painted layer not reaching the world; prop+water footprints not reaching it; slope arm + spawn elevation absent; server/client blocked masks differing; a server-ticked mover walking THROUGH the painted wall at tick 76; a per-tick server-vs-client SimChecksum comparison diverging on a walled map), the 2 that pass in both states being the deliberate flat/no-op guards that pin the "no golden can move" claim. GATE: `dotnet build godot/godot.csproj` succeeded, 0 errors; `dotnet test godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests.csproj` = 5885 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped (baseline 5877/0/1 plus exactly the 8 new tests), clean on the first run with no flake exception needed. Residual filed as DW-828: the headless server still has no source for an ElevationGrid, so the SLOPE arm and spawn elevation remain client-only on sculpted maps — the injection seam now exists, so the follow-up is a supplier, not a rewiring.

### DW-511: ServerChecksumCollector has no ACCEPT_WINDOW guard, so a client can evict honest in-flight comparison windows with far-future checksum ticks

origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03
location: godot/src/Multiplayer/Server/ServerChecksumCollector.cs:115-133 (Record) — compare the sibling guard at godot/src/Multiplayer/Server/MergedTickBuilder.cs:128-130
severity: high
reason: Record accepts any checksum tick a client claims and evicts the ring bucket it lands on, so a single misbehaving or malicious client can silently destroy the honest majority's in-flight comparison windows and blind the desync guard (a grief/starvation vector, sibling of DW-435/DW-436 on the command path). Pre-existing and unrelated to either entry the discovering bundle closed, and NOT fixable by copying MergedTickBuilder's ACCEPT_WINDOW: the collector's _resolvedThrough starts at -1 while real checksum ticks start at the checksum interval, so a naive window rejects the first legitimate report of every match. A correct fix must gate acceptance on a real frontier (e.g. MergedTickBuilder.EmittedThrough) and needs its own design + tests. DW-239's fix makes the symptom OBSERVABLE (each eviction now logs an ABANDONED line and increments AbandonedWindows) but does not reject the input.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: workflow burn-down bundle server-checksum-accept-window (2026-08-05) - verified STILL OPEN against current code first (ServerChecksumCollector.Record had the monotonic _resolvedThrough stale-past drop but no future bound, so any client-claimed tick was accepted), and the two-part harm confirmed by reading the path: a far-future tick (a) hits AbandonWindow on whatever live ring bucket its index collides with, destroying an honest in-flight comparison window, and (b) drags _resolvedThrough up to the fabricated value, after which every honest report is dropped by the cheap stale check for the rest of the match - the desync guard dies silently and the FR-39 trail flatlines, from ONE client, no majority needed. DW-511 is absent from .bmad-loop/decisions.json and its block carried no decision line, so the bundle intent governed scope. FIX (godot/src/Multiplayer/Server/ServerChecksumCollector.cs): a future bound mirroring the existing stale-past bound, measured against an injected server-authoritative frontier (Func<long>) rather than against _resolvedThrough - the trap this entry called out, since MergedTickBuilder's ACCEPT_WINDOW is measured from a frontier that advances every tick whereas this collector's _resolvedThrough starts at -1 while real checksum ticks start at the checksum interval (60), so a naive copy would reject the FIRST legitimate report of every match and deadlock the quorum it protects. Production (DedicatedServer.cs:728) wires `() => _builder?.EmittedThrough ?? -1L`: a merged tick is emitted only when ALL expected players submitted it, so no single client can move that frontier. ACCEPT_SLACK = DelayMath.MAX_DELAY, derived not guessed: a checksum tick is an EXECUTED tick and a lockstep client gates execution of tick T on merged-arrival for T (MergedArrivalRing.IsReady), so exec <= emitted EXCEPT on the ticks the client SELF-SEEDS empty (SeedBootstrap ticks 0..delay-1, which the server never emits, and the SeedDelayGap newDelay-oldDelay ticks a growing delay change opens), both bounded by the delay clamp - so MAX_DELAY is exactly the honest-client lead and no more, and aliasing the constant keeps the two from drifting. Observability follows the file's precedents: ServerChecksumCollector.FarFutureRejections (sibling of AbandonedWindows) counts every drop, ServerHost.FarFutureChecksumRejections mirrors it and warns ONCE per offending slot (an unbounded line would be exactly the client-drivable log-write DoS DW-392 had to fix on the command path) and appends the count to the MATCH SUMMARY only when non-zero, so an honest match's summary line stays byte-identical to the legacy format; a dropped report is neither a desync nor an abandoned window, so it never moves the PASS/FAIL/INCONCLUSIVE verdict. The frontier param is optional - omitting it preserves today's unbounded acceptance, documented as the trusted in-process-harness default (unit tests, the DEBUG loopback self-test), which is why the existing ServerChecksumCollector/AbandonedChecksumWindow/SingleReporterVerdict tests (deliberately using ring-colliding ticks like 4 and 12 with no frontier) stay untouched and still assert exactly what they always did. DETERMINISM: nothing here is folded into SimChecksum, CanonicalModelHash or StartStateHash - this is server-side networking and the class doc already declares it exempt from in-tick rules; no golden moved. COVERAGE: godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Server/FarFutureChecksumRejectionTests.cs, 11 Godot-free tests, proven to bite by temporarily neutralizing IsBeyondAcceptWindow - 8 of 11 FAIL without the fix, including the two that pin the actual defect (honest window not evicted; resolved floor not poisoned so windows 60/120/180 still compare) and the ServerHost-level starvation pin (WindowsCompared 1 vs 0-compared-1-abandoned pre-fix); the 3 that pass either way are the guard-rails against the naive-copy trap (first legitimate report at tick 60 accepted with _resolvedThrough still -1, clean-match summary format unchanged, unbounded no-frontier default preserved), which is correct - they exist to fail if a future edit makes the bound too tight. GATE: `dotnet build godot/godot.csproj` Build succeeded, 0 errors (6 warnings, all pre-existing and in unrelated files); `dotnet test godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests.csproj` 5265 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped in 1m43s against the 5254/0/1 baseline - exactly the 11 new tests, no flake and no CanonicalModelHashPerf exception needed. Follow-ons filed as DW-713, DW-714 and DW-715.

### DW-512: MovementSystem's separation query has the same over-cap arbitrariness DW-249 described — and unlike SearchArea its output DOES feed SimChecksum

origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03
location: godot/src/Navigation/MovementSystem.cs:46,100 (_neighborBuffer = new int[32], SEPARATION_QUERY_RADIUS = 2.0) -> godot/src/Navigation/SpatialHash.cs QueryRadius
severity: medium
reason: The unfiltered SpatialHash.QueryRadius keeps the first 32 neighbours in cell-scan order, so in a crowd denser than 32 units inside a 2.0 radius (the 500-2000-entity target is well past that) WHICH neighbours push a unit is decided by grid geometry rather than any defined rule. It is deterministic across peers (same grid, same positions) so it is NOT a desync — it is a steering-quality/fairness issue. Deliberately left byte-identical by the searcharea-target-selection-correctness bundle because separation output flows into Position, a SimChecksum input, so re-ruling the truncation or raising the buffer moves every movement golden (formation-separation, ai-active, the merged-N goldens) — that needs its own deliberate re-baseline story, which the burn-down brief forbids. The pure API to consume already exists: SpatialHash.QueryRadiusLowestIds<TFilter>, and both QueryRadius overloads now carry a doc note pointing callers at it.
status: done 2026-08-06
resolution: closed with NO CODE CHANGE by Story 15.22 (Phase C). The 2026-08-04 decision to keep the separation query byte-identical was RE-CONFIRMED by Alec on 2026-08-06 with the re-record window open — i.e. it was held on its merits, not deferred again because a re-baseline was expensive. The truncation is deterministic across peers so it is a crowd-fairness nicety rather than a desync, and re-ruling unit steering is a game-feel change wanting a playtest, not a correction batch. SpatialHash.QueryRadiusLowestIds<TFilter> remains available for a future caller that wants the defined rule.
goldens: none — decision held; behaviour is unchanged so no golden moves.
decision: 2026-08-04 Keep byte-identical (deterministic, not a desync — only a fairness nicety)

FIX: added godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Persistence/EntityWorldSaveCompletenessTests.cs (6 tests, test-only; no simulation source touched, no SimChecksum/CanonicalModelHash/StartStateHash input changed, no golden moved). DESIGN: the sweep keeps NO list of what is "supposed" to be persisted — every EntityWorld instance field must land in exactly one bucket, either a justified allowlist or (by default) the reflective round-trip sweep, which bumps every element of every swept lane on a scenario-applied source host, runs a real CaptureFrom -> Validate -> RestoreInto onto a second applied host, and requires every value to have arrived. `Bump()` derives its value from the current one rather than a constant, so a filler can never collide with what the scenario wrote (EntityFlags.Alive == 1 would have blinded a constant filler), and per lane/index the bumped value is first REQUIRED to differ from what the destination already held — the DW-19 per-field-divergence precondition applied to persistence. `Validate()` runs between capture and restore exactly as ReadBody does, so a lane wired with the wrong cardinality (a flat/strided lane declared before EA.PatrolWpX) fails there rather than only on a real player's save. Allowlists: TransientLanes (PrevPosition, DW-80 GateClosedTicks, DW-532 GatherWalkStallTicks, DW-634 RallyMovePending), each separately pinned as genuinely NOT arriving so the exemption cannot rot into a hiding place; DefDerivedRefLanes (SourceDefinition by def id, FeedbackProfile re-derived) with its own assertion; the allocator triple (hwm/alive/free-list LIFO order) and the RNG scalar, each proved by a dedicated test; and the re-applied sim-globals/grids/host delegates with reasons. origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03

severity: medium

### DW-521: `git stash` is SHARED across every burn-down worktree, so parallel bundle agents silently steal and drop each other's uncommitted work

origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03
location: .claude/workflows/dw-burndown.workflow.js + the per-agent bundle brief (agent instructions); .git/refs/stash (one stack for all ~80 worktrees)
severity: high
reason: `refs/stash` lives in the shared common .git directory, NOT per-worktree, so a `git stash push` from any one of the parallel bundle worktrees lands on ONE global stack and a `git stash pop` in a different worktree applies whatever another agent pushed last and DROPS that agent's entry. This fired live in a single chunk, in both directions: worktree wf_5d8656b5-2c0-21 popped wf_5d8656b5-2c0-19's validator WIP (ItemDefinitionValidator.cs / UnitDefinitionValidator.cs / DefinitionValidatorStrictBoundsTests.cs) into its own tree while -19 concurrently popped -21's, and both had to be hand-repaired. Both agents recovered with zero work lost, but the unnoticed failure modes are severe: an agent that commits after a bad pop silently ships ANOTHER bundle's code inside its own merge (with a green gate, because the foreign code compiles), and an agent whose entry was dropped loses its work to gc. The proximate cause is the baseline drift in DW-502 — agents stash precisely to measure the pristine Tier-1 baseline the brief states wrongly. Fix = an explicit prohibition in the agent brief (never `git stash` in a burn-down worktree; copy files to the scratchpad, or commit-then-reset, or measure the baseline in a throwaway clone) plus stating a correct per-base baseline so nobody needs to measure it. Recovery recipe worth putting in the brief too: `git stash list --format="%H %gd %gs"` to snapshot SHAs, `git stash store -m "<original message>" <sha>` to put a wrongly-dropped entry back, and `git diff <stash>^1 <stash>` plus `git show <stash>^3:<path>` to extract your own work without trusting the stash index again.
status: open

### DW-527: `UnitDefinitionValidator` still admits `hp = 0` for a unit while `BuildingDefinitionValidator` rejects it, and the two checks cannot both fire without doubling the badge

origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03
location: godot/src/Core/Definitions/UnitDefinitionValidator.cs:207 (the `CheckStat` call for "hp") vs godot/src/Core/Definitions/BuildingDefinitionValidator.cs (its own `HpAuthored` branch)
severity: medium
reason: `hp` is the fourth genuinely degenerate-at-zero stat alongside the three DW-380 just closed: a 0-HP unit spawns with a zero health ceiling, and per the DW-491/DW-489 decision text an EffectiveMaxHealth of literally zero is the one lethal ceiling case. Buildings are already protected (BuildingDefinitionValidator rejects hp <= 0) but the unit gate still accepts 0. Deliberately NOT fixed inside DW-380 for two reasons: that entry's reason line names only attack_speed / mesh_scale / collision_radius, and BuildingDefinitionValidator REUSES the unit gate on top of its own hp check — so a naive `hp` rule in the unit validator emits a SECOND error keyed "hp" on every building, i.e. exactly the doubled per-field badge (D-9) that DW-380's bundle had to fix for attack_speed. Closing this cleanly means reconciling the building-side and unit-side hp checks into one rule, which is a separate change with its own badge-contract test.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: closed by workflow burn-down bundle `definition-validator-degenerate-stats` (2026-08-05). Verified genuinely OPEN against current code before fixing: UnitDefinitionValidator.cs:238 still read `CheckStat(errors, kind, id, "hp", def.Hp)` — the generic [0, 32768) bound, INCLUSIVE of 0 — while BuildingDefinitionValidator carried its own `!IsFinite(Hp) || Hp <= 0f` branch. Not in .bmad-loop/decisions.json and no `decision:` line here, so the worklist intent governed. WHY hp=0 is degenerate, stated from the code rather than the ledger: EntityWorld.Create seeds Health/BaseMaxHealth/EffectiveMaxHealth from the authored value, so a 0-hp entity spawns ALIVE at 0 HP with a zero health ceiling; ModifierStore.ApplyStatDeltas re-clamps Health into [0, EffectiveMaxHealth] = [0, 0] so it can never be healed above zero; and per DW-491 the ceiling-collapse death cannot even fire on it (that gate needs a >0 -> 0 TRANSITION plus a net-negative change). It is a permanent 0-HP husk that dies to the first point of damage, not a frail unit. THE RECONCILIATION the entry asked for: a naive strictly-positive rule in the unit gate would double-badge every bad building, because BuildingDefinitionValidator reuses the whole unit gate on top of its own hp rule (D-9, one badge per control) — and that doubling was MEASURED to already exist for a negative or NaN building hp (both branches fired). So (1) the unit gate now routes hp through CheckStatPositive, kept in the stat's long-standing position so the reported error ORDER is unchanged; (2) the building validator's local VALUE branch is DELETED — the shared rule is a strict superset (non-positive, non-finite, AND at/above the 16.16 ceiling, which the local `<= 0f` branch never looked at; that half always came from the reused gate anyway); (3) only the HpAuthored PRESENCE check stays, since the unit gate cannot express a BuildingDefinition-only flag, and the error merge skips a shared "hp" verdict when the presence badge already fired — so "exactly one hp error" is a property of the merge rather than an accident of the 100f default. Determinism: authoring-time REJECT only. No stat value, quantization or SoA write changed; no SimChecksum / ContentHash / CanonicalModelHash / StartStateHash input moved; no golden touched or re-recorded. All shipped content authors positive hp (alpha_faction.json / beta_faction.json range 55..500; zero hits for `"hp": 0` anywhere in godot/resources), so nothing shipped is newly rejected. Coverage: +15 tests in DefinitionValidatorStrictBoundsTests.cs, verified RED without the fix by restoring both validators from 4c7a2259 via `git checkout <sha> -- <paths>` (no stash used) — 5 failures: ZeroHp_OnUnit_IsRejected; ZeroHp_BlocksTheBalanceApplyPath (hp IS in BalanceSuggestionApplier's tunable vocabulary and TryApply gates through this validator, so a suggested hp of 0 was one click from being committed); and all three NonPositiveOrNonFiniteBuildingHp rows (-5 / NaN / +Inf each produced 2 located "hp" errors — the exact doubled badge). Message routing was checked, not assumed: FactionDefinerWizardCore.StepForError sniffs with `reason.StartsWith("unit '")`, so the new reason text containing the words "a frail unit" mid-string cannot mis-route a building hp error — it still lands on Buildings & Tech. Follow-ons filed as DW-822 (Unit Card Editor HP copy still says "It dies at 0", and neither HP NumInput carries a floor) and DW-823 (a FactionDefinerWizardTests row now pins a building-hp message no producer emits). Gate: `dotnet build godot/godot.csproj` 0 errors; `dotnet test godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/...` 5892 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped, exactly baseline 5877 + 15, no flake, no CanonicalModelHashPerf failure.

### DW-528: The faction-name wizard's free-text path is safe from Windows reserved basenames only INCIDENTALLY, via its `_faction` filename suffix

origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03
location: godot/src/Core/Definitions/FactionDefinerWizardCore.cs:330
severity: low
reason: Found while scoping DW-454's reserved-device-name reject. This line builds `Path.Combine(factionsDirAbsolute, $"{id}_faction.json")` from free-text input, and DW-454's new `IsReservedDeviceName` gate was wired into the item and unit/building validators but NOT here. It is safe TODAY purely because the `_faction` suffix means the basename is never a bare `con`/`nul`/`aux`/`com1` (Win32 reservation matches the basename before the first dot, so `con_faction.json` is fine) — not because anything checks. Recorded so a future refactor that drops, shortens or parameterizes that suffix knows the safety was incidental and must add the explicit check; the file was outside DW-454's bundle scope.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: workflow burn-down bundle reserved-device-name-guard (merge 1fcde8d3) - verified genuinely open (TryFinish still built `Path.Combine(factionsDirAbsolute, $"{id}_faction.json")` from a free-text id with no reserved-basename check anywhere in the file). Two source files: (1) new `UnitDefinitionValidator.IsReservedDeviceFileName(string?)`, the filename-level companion to DW-454's whole-id `IsReservedDeviceName`, for callers that DECORATE an id before the write - it reduces a name to the Win32 device basename (last path component, segment before the FIRST '.', trailing dots/spaces stripped, per the documented "NUL.tar.gz is equivalent to NUL" rule) and defers to the existing helper, splitting on both '/' and '\' explicitly rather than Path.GetFileName whose separator set is platform-dependent, so the verdict is identical on Windows and Linux; ReservedPipeList made public so the message quotes the same list. (2) FactionDefinerWizardCore now names the suffix (FactionFileSuffix) and runs the ASSEMBLED file name through the guard before Path.Combine; TryFinishFromRawJson inherits it by delegation. Guarding the assembled name (not the bare id) is what makes it right in both directions and is exactly what "survives a future refactor that shortens or parameterizes that suffix" requires: a bare `con` stays authorable (`con_faction.json` is an ordinary file), while `con.x` / `nul.` / `com1.a` are rejected because they still assemble a reserved leading segment and sail past the existing separator/traversal guard. HONEST CORRECTION TO THE PREMISE, measured not assumed: on this dev machine (Win11 26200) File.WriteAllText creates `con.json`, `con.json.tmp`, `con.x_faction.json`, and so does cmd.exe - the DOS-device reservation is NOT enforced for file creation, and the without-the-fix RED run confirmed it (Finish reported SUCCESS and wrote the file). The guard is therefore documented in code as a PORTABILITY gate (authored content is shared; such a file stays unopenable wherever the reservation IS enforced), not a local crash fix. DW-454's own shipped message was deliberately left alone (closed entry, wording pinned by tests) and the premise correction is filed as DW-694. Coverage: +34 tests - 25 helper-level in DefinitionValidatorStrictBoundsTests (11 recognised shapes incl. `con.json.tmp`, `nul.x_faction.json`, `dir\con.json`; 13 non-flagged incl. the `con_faction.json` no-over-rejection control, `console`, `com0`, empty, null; 1 agreement test tying both helpers to one convention) and 9 wizard-level in FactionDefinerWizardTests (a 4-case reserved theory asserting exactly one located `id` error at step NameColor with zero files written, a 3-case positive control that a bare reserved word still saves, the raw-JSON pane inheriting the gate, and a test pinning FactionFileSuffix to the `*_faction.json` discovery glob). The 4 reserved wizard cases were verified RED by temporarily disabling the guard (5 failures incl. the raw-JSON one) before restoring it. Determinism: authoring-time reject only - no sim array, quantization or SoA write change, no SimChecksum/ContentHash/CanonicalModelHash/StartStateHash input movement, no golden touched. Gate: build 0 errors; 5288 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped (baseline 5254 + 34). Two uncovered siblings re-filed: DW-695 (AbilityEditorPanel, where the id IS the bare basename) and DW-696 (the unlinked `*_faction.json` convention sites).

severity: medium
reason: Emergent cross-bundle interaction, confirmed by reading both merged sides; neither bundle's agent could see it (DW-148 owned the confinement in scenario-validator-spawn-and-bounds, DW-80/DW-207 owned the release paths in gathering-worker-lifecycle, and the latter branched from 024025e before the former merged). `ScenarioApplier` deliberately only `_log.Warn()`s a spawn inside a blocked cell and applies the placement anyway (ScenarioApplier.cs:174-176: "silently refusing to spawn authored content would be strictly worse"), while `MovementSystem` now CONFINES such a unit via `IsBlockedOutside(fromCell, ...)`. Confinement still permits walking out into a CLEAR neighbour, so the trap needs a blocked region at least 3 cells across with the worker on an INTERIOR cell — then the step and both wall-slide axes all resolve to foreign blocked cells and line 173 hard-stops it in place every tick. `GatheringSystem.TickIdle` → `AssignToNode` (GatheringSystem.cs:366-374) has already incremented `_nodes.AssignedGatherers[node]` — a SimChecksum-folded value — and set `MovingToResource`. `TickMovingToResource` releases only on `node < 0 || !_nodes.Active[node]` (:129-134), so a worker that can never close to `ARRIVE_AT_NODE_SQR` holds the reservation for the whole match. None of the four release paths the bundle enumerates as exhaustive at GatheringSystem.cs:22-27 can fire: the tick loop never leaves `MovingToResource`, `EntityWorld.OnDestroy` needs a death, `BuildingSystem.QueueWorkerBuild` needs a Build order, and DW-80's `STREAMING_GATE_GRACE_TICKS` re-idle sits inside `TickGathering` (:182-190), reachable only AFTER arrival. `FindBestNode` skips a node at `AssignedGatherers >= MaxGatherers` (:434, shipped default 4), so enough stranded workers starve that node for EVERY faction — the precise starvation DW-207 was written to eliminate. Pre-DW-148 the same worker was exempt from blocking and simply walked out. Needs a real authored map to trigger (the validator only warns), which is why it is medium not high. Likely fix: bound the `MovingToResource` leg the way DW-80 bounded the gate park — a no-progress tick counter that releases the slot and re-idles — rather than weakening the confinement.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: 2026-08-05 resolved by the gathering-worker-lifecycle bundle, wave 2 (workflow burn-down run; branch dw/gathering-worker-lifecycle-wave2, commit 747311e3). Verified STILL LIVE against the run-base code first - TickMovingToResource released only on `node < 0 || !Active[node]` - and the DW-148 x DW-207 interaction reproduced. FIX: a new GatheringSystem.TickWalkStall counts CONSECUTIVE ticks on which the shared CheckedStep.Resolve hard-stops the worker's seek step toward its node, and after WALK_STALL_GRACE_TICKS (1s) hands the reserved slot back while leaving the worker en route. DESIGN CHOICE worth reviewing: this entry's suggested "release the slot and re-idle" does NOT actually fix the leak - nothing makes FindBestNode reachability-aware, so the next TickIdle re-picks the same node and re-reserves the slot for all but one tick of every window (a ~97% duty cycle, not a fix). Yielding is therefore TERMINAL for the leg, and self-heals: the worker re-claims a slot only on genuine arrival (re-idling if the node filled meanwhile), so a grid rebuilt mid-match frees it. State is one new UNFOLDED EntityWorld.GatherWalkStallTicks int array on the exact GateClosedTicks/RallyMovePending posture (ctor, Create() recycle-reset, Clear(), not folded, not persisted, no snapshot residue); ReleaseGatherSlot skips the decrement for a yielded worker so death or build-interrupt cannot double-decrement. DETERMINISM: the stall watch early-outs unless world.Pathability exists AND has a blocked cell; every recorded golden except PathabilityBlockScenario runs with a null grid, and that one has no worker (a single Inactive-gather unit), so the folded AssignedGatherers is untouched everywhere a golden looks. No golden moved, none re-recorded, no AlgoVersion / CanonicalModelHash / StartStateHash pin touched. RED-TEST PROOF: commenting out the single TickWalkStall call failed 6 of the 11 new confinement tests; the 5 that stay green either way are the deliberate must-NOT-fire pins (flat map, all-clear grid, unobstructed walk, recycle reset). GATE: dotnet build godot/godot.csproj = 0 errors / 6 pre-existing warnings; dotnet test = 5604 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped first attempt (5588 baseline + 16 new). Residuals filed as DW-777, DW-778 and DW-779.

### DW-533: Scenario enums went fail-closed (`allowIntegerValues:false`) while both production `LoadFromFile` callers still branch on `== null` for "parse-failed", so a numeric enum aborts boot instead of taking the fallback

origin: workflow burn-down post-merge review, 2026-08-03
location: godot/src/Core/Definitions/ContentJson.cs:119 (`BuildScenario`) vs godot/src/Core/Bootstrap/Phases/ScenarioLoadPhase.cs:88-94 and godot/src/Core/MainScene.cs:2796-2798
severity: low
reason: DW-274 replaced `ScenarioSerializer`'s deleted private `_options` — whose converter was the parameterless `new JsonStringEnumConverter()`, i.e. `allowIntegerValues: true` — with `new JsonStringEnumConverter(namingPolicy: null, allowIntegerValues: false)`. The tightening itself is correct and deliberate (name-only authoring, fail-closed) and the bundle correctly fixed `LoadFromFile`'s doc to admit that malformed input propagates. What was not updated is the two production callers, which still code to the OLD contract. `ScenarioSerializer.LoadFromFile` (:44-49) has no try/catch, so a scenario carrying `"win_condition": 0` (or a numeric `type`/`scope` on a scenario variable — ScenarioData.cs:534/538/596/714) now throws `JsonException` past `ScenarioLoadPhase.cs:88` and past `ScenePhaseRunner.Run` (no try/catch), so the client aborts `_Ready` mid-phase with a half-initialised scene instead of printing "Scenario not found or failed to parse … using defaults" and booting the fallback mirror; the dedicated server aborts instead of degrading to relay+quorum. `SkirmishCatalog.cs:106` is the only caller already wrapped. Low because every shipped map and the editor's own writer emit enum NAMES (verified: no numeric enum values under godot/resources/data/scenarios/), so this only fires on hand-edited or externally generated `user://` content — but that is exactly the content the located-fallback path exists to survive. Fix is to catch `JsonException` at the `LoadFromFile` boundary (or in both callers) and map it to the existing null/fallback contract, keeping the located error message.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: 2026-08-05 resolved by burn-down bundle scenario-load-fail-closed (workflow burn-down run) - verified STILL PRESENT at the run-base commit first (LoadFromFile had no try/catch around the Deserialize, while both production callers still branch on `== null`: ScenarioLoadPhase.LoadAndApplyScenario -> validated fallback mirror, MainScene.BuildHeadlessServerSimHost -> relay + quorum only). FIX, in godot/src/Core/Definitions/ScenarioSerializer.cs only (the bundle's single named file and the only Godot-free seam): the deserialize is wrapped in `try/catch (JsonException)` returning null, with the located reason surfaced on a new `LoadFromFile(string absolutePath, out string? parseError)` overload; the 1-arg form delegates via `out _` so all ~30 existing call sites are untouched. `parseError` is non-null ONLY when the file existed and its content failed to parse (null on success AND on a missing file), so 'this file is broken' stays distinguishable from 'no scenario here' - the reason for an out-overload rather than collapsing both nulls. The DW-366 `GuardScenarioInputSize` call is deliberately kept OUTSIDE the try so an over-cap file still throws (it bounds hostile input before any allocation; ScenarioInputSizeGuardTests pins that). Fail-closed is preserved in substance - a partial or numerically-miscoded model is never returned and never reaches the sim; only the CHANNEL changed from an escaping exception to the null/fallback contract the callers already implement. All other callers (SkirmishCatalog, SkirmishSetupOverlay, WinConditionPhase import, ContentBrowserPanel publish gate, SaveGameColdBoot) were read and already handle null with a located message or a fail-closed 0/skip, so no new silent-failure path was created. COVERAGE: new godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Definitions/ScenarioLoadFailClosedTests.cs (12 Godot-free cases): malformed syntax, numeric top-level enum, numeric nested enums (variable type/scope, win-condition-spec preset), a FixedJsonConverter rejection and a WidgetBaseJsonConverter closed-kind rejection (proving the whole malformed-CONTENT surface routes to the same contract, not just the enum spelling this entry was filed on), no-partial-model, plus two fences that must NOT move - missing-file returns null with no parseError, and the DW-366 over-cap file still throws (a fix that wrapped the whole method body fails that one). RED-TEST PROOF: replacing the catch body's `return null;` with `throw;` failed 10 tests (8 new + the 2 updated pins); reverted before commit and the committed file contains no `throw;`. Two DW-274 pins were updated (ContentJsonUnificationTests NumericEnum_InScenarioJson_FailsClosed / NumericEnum_InNestedScenarioSpec_FailsClosed): they used Assert.Throws<JsonException> on LoadFromFile, i.e. they pinned the exact behaviour this entry exists to change, and now assert the rejection through the new channel (null model + a located reason naming `win_condition`), which pins what DW-274 cares about more directly. That is the only pre-existing test behaviour altered. DETERMINISM: nothing folded into SimChecksum, CanonicalModelHash, StartStateHash or any golden is touched - only the error channel of a load that previously threw; valid content parses and serializes byte-identically, zero goldens moved, none re-recorded. ### DW-534: `QueryRadiusLowestIds` drops the `count < maxResults` scan bound with no authored radius cap anywhere, so a wide-radius SearchArea scans every entity in radius on a 30 Hz lockstep path

origin: workflow burn-down post-merge review, 2026-08-03
location: godot/src/Navigation/SpatialHash.cs:276-306 (bound deliberately absent; contrast `QueryRadius` at :208)
severity: low
reason: The missing bound is REQUIRED by the global-lowest-ids contract DW-249/250/252 established — a full buffer must not end the scan, because a later candidate may still be lower-id — and is correctly documented as such at :276-278. The gap is that it was also the only cost ceiling, and nothing else bounds the work: `cellRadius = (radius / CELL_SIZE).ToInt() + 1` is limited only by the `GRID_DIM` bounds checks (:265/:270), and no radius bound exists in `AbilityValidator` or `EffectBounds` (grepped both) — the authoring spin row is `AddSpinRow(card, "Radius", 0, FixedSpinMax, ...)` (AbilityEditorPanel.Advanced.cs:279) and `FixedJsonConverter` admits anything in the 16.16 range. With `GRID_DIM = 32` and `CELL_SIZE_F = 10`, an authored radius >= 320 visits all 1024 cells with no early exit, evaluating `filter.Accepts` (`DomainClassifier.Of` + `TagGate.Intersects` + `AllianceStore.AreAllied`, TargetMatcher.cs:37-78) for every alive entity up to `MAX_ENTITIES = 4096`, plus up to 64 insertion shifts per accepted match once the buffer fills. Nested one level (`MaxSearchAreaDepth = 2`) that is 64 outer targets × N candidates per cast versus roughly 64 candidates plus a cell walk before. Fully deterministic, so NOT a desync risk — but it is a 30 Hz lockstep hot path where a tick overrun stalls every peer through the adaptive-delay/stall machinery rather than degrading locally. Cheapest fix is an authored-radius cap validated at load (an `EffectCaps.MaxSearchRadius` folded into `RulesetHash`, since it is a structural bound), which bounds `cellRadius` without touching the selection contract.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: workflow burn-down bundle effect-radius-cap (2026-08-05) - verified STILL PRESENT against current code before fixing: SpatialHash.QueryRadiusLowestIds (SpatialHash.cs:279) still omitted the `count < maxResults` loop bound its sibling QueryRadius keeps (:208), and a grep of AbilityValidator.cs, EffectBounds.cs and EffectNodeJsonConverter.cs confirmed NO radius bound existed anywhere - the converter reads `radius` through FixedJsonConverter, which admits the whole 16.16 range. DW-534 carries no `decision:` line and is absent from .bmad-loop/decisions.json, so this entry's own closure guidance governed. FIX: added `EffectCaps.MaxSearchRadius = 64` (world units) and enforced it in `EffectBounds.Validate`'s SearchAreaEffect case, comparing against a `Fixed` built once from the named constant (no bare literal, CHM0004-clean). The gate lives in EffectBounds rather than in AbilityValidator deliberately: EffectBounds is the shared load-time gate all three authored effect sources already run - abilities (AbilityValidator:155), items (ItemDefinitionValidator:184/:266) and scenario run_effect embeds (ScenarioValidator:929) - so one check covers all three instead of three copies that drift. The exit-free scan itself is left UNTOUCHED: it is required by the global-lowest-ids contract DW-249/250/252 established, which is exactly why the ceiling has to come from authoring time. THE VALUE, derived not guessed: 64 holds `cellRadius = (radius/CELL_SIZE).ToInt()+1` at 7, so the cell walk spans at most 15x15 = 225 of the hash's 1024 cells however wide an author writes it, versus the pre-cap worst case of all 1024 plus a predicate evaluation per alive entity. It leaves an order of magnitude of headroom over real content (widest radius shipped today is 5, in aura_guard.json; fireball.json uses 4) and still covers a quarter of the largest supported map's 256-unit width. Both halves are pinned executably, recomputed from the live SpatialHash constants so a grid re-parameterization turns the test red rather than quietly restoring the whole-grid scan. DETERMINISM: load-time reject only - no sim array, no SimChecksum / CanonicalModelHash / StartStateHash input touched, no golden moved or re-recorded (all golden suites green). RulesetHash DOES move, by design and per EffectCaps' own documented rule ("ADDING a cap requires folding it into RulesetHash and bumping its AlgoVersion"): the cap is folded in file order and AlgoVersion goes 1 -> 2, so a build that bounds the radius and one that does not are handshake-rejected instead of running different per-cast work. That is a handshake fingerprint, not a sim value; no golden or recorded replay pins a concrete ruleset hash (SimRngChecksumReplayTests uses a synthetic 0x0F0F... fixture and otherwise self-gates against RulesetHash.Compute()). The two pins that hand-enumerate the fold moved with it in the same commit, as their own failure messages instruct: RulesetHashTests (both byte-stream folds, FoldedCapCount 10 -> 11, and the name set) and VersionStampConsistencyTests.ExpectedRulesetHashAlgoVersion 1 -> 2. COVERAGE: 11 new tests in godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Effects/EffectRadiusCapTests.cs - the gate itself (over-cap reject, inclusive boundary pinned in both directions so a `>=` typo cannot pass, over-cap nested below an in-cap search, over-cap inside a Sequence), each of the three authoring surfaces asserted one by one rather than assumed (AbilityValidator with a located error, AbilityLoader end-to-end from authored JSON, ItemDefinitionValidator, ScenarioValidator run_effect embed) each with an at-the-cap positive control, the cost-ceiling arithmetic made executable against SpatialHash's real geometry, an isolated teeth test for the RulesetHash fold term, and a shipped-content tripwire that scans the real ability files two ways with a vacuous-pass defense. COUNTERFACTUALS RUN, then restored: with the EffectBounds radius check disabled 8 of 11 fail (every gate test; the three that stay green are the fold test, the cell-walk arithmetic and the shipped-content scan, none of which depend on the gate); with the RulesetHash fold line removed MaxSearchRadius_IsActuallyFoldedIntoTheRulesetHash and RulesetHashTests.Compute_MatchesTheIndependentlyFoldedByteStream both fail. GATE: `dotnet build godot/godot.csproj` = Build succeeded, 0 errors, 6 pre-existing warnings; `dotnet test godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests.csproj` = 5888 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped - exactly the 5877 launch baseline plus the 11 new tests, on the first run, with no CanonicalModelHashPerf flake and so no use of the documented flake exception. The worktree was reset to run base 4c7a2259 first (it had been cut from a stale "chore(snapshot): date stamp 2026-08-01" snapshot at 024025e4). Follow-ons filed as DW-815 (a NEGATIVE authored radius is validated-but-inert, the lower-bound sibling of this cap) and DW-816 (the ability editor's Radius spin row still offers up to 32767 with no awareness of the cap).

resolution: 2026-08-05 resolved by the loader-duplicate-key-fail-closed bundle (workflow burn-down run). Verified STILL PRESENT against current code first: UnitDefinition.Cost (UnitDefinition.cs:80, inherited by BuildingDefinition) and ResearchLevel.Cost (ResearchDefinition.cs:77) are the only remaining Dictionary-shaped JSON DTO properties in src/ besides DW-227's already-fixed DamageTable.Multipliers, and neither loader ran any raw-document pass; a characterization test proves the premise on live code (`"cost": { "ore": 50, "ore": 5 }` deserializes through FactionDefinition.JsonOptions to a ONE-entry map holding 5, so the authored 50 is gone and ResourceCostValidator / ResearchValidator, which walk the deserialized dictionary, cannot see the collision at all). The guard mirrors the sibling validators' shape (pure C#, no logging, NO throw, list-all, located `{kind} '{id}'.cost` wording), walks only declared structural paths (faction units[] / buildings[] / research[].levels[] plus a bare single-definition root) and never blind name-recursion, reports a REPEATED `cost` property (the DW-227 duplicate-`multipliers` analogue), walks every occurrence of a repeated array key rather than a first-match lookup (fail closed), and labels an id-less entry by index. WIRING: both FactionDefinition entry points - LoadFromFile feeds results into the SAME aggregate errors list every content check throws with (file-prefixed, exactly like the DW-62 parse line) and is guarded to run only when the document actually parsed, so a malformed file still reports DW-62's single parse line; LoadSelectableFromDirectory runs the same pass and excludes the file with its reason, so discovery cannot list as SELECTABLE a faction the load gate now rejects (the split DW-327 closed for the signature-mechanic check). DETERMINISM: load-time only, pure C#, no float, no sim state, nothing folded into SimChecksum / CanonicalModelHash / StartStateHash; no golden moved or re-recorded; a test scans the real shipped faction files and asserts they carry no duplicate cost keys, pinning byte-identical parsing and acting as a tripwire. ### DW-543: Per-occurrence trigger dispatch keeps running after fuel exhaustion within one trigger, stretching the whole-trigger-boundary contract across N occurrences
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03
location: godot/src/Core/ScenarioDirector.cs — EvaluateTriggers, the param-reading occurrence loop
severity: low
reason: FuelExhausted is checked only at the sweep's per-trigger boundary, so a param-reading trigger that exhausts the budget mid-occurrence keeps dispatching its remaining matching occurrences that tick (each a full FireTrigger). Deterministic and arguably 'the in-flight trigger completes', but it stretches the documented whole-trigger-boundary contract across N occurrences of a single trigger, making the per-tick fuel ceiling less honest than it reads. Out of the dsl-runtime-fuel-hardening bundle's scope (named by none of its five entries); left unchanged to avoid altering established dispatch semantics without a recorded owner decision. Closure = an owner decision on whether the boundary is per-trigger or per-occurrence, then make the check match it.
status: done 2026-08-05
decision: 2026-08-04 Halt at occurrence granularity — Move the FuelExhausted check inside the occurrence loop so an exhausted budget stops dispatching further occurrences of the same trigger, tightening the per-tick ceiling to match the documented contract.
resolution: closed by bundle scenariodirector-fuel-requeue (workflow burn-down, 2026-08-05). Verified LIVE first, then implemented to the recorded ledger decision (DW-543 does not appear in .bmad-loop/decisions.json; the ledger `decision:` line was the authority and was followed literally). Confirmed: ScenarioDirector.EvaluateTriggers checked `_loopState.FuelExhausted` only at the sweep's per-TRIGGER boundary (top of the exec loop), so a param-reading trigger's per-occurrence loop kept dispatching every remaining matching occurrence after the budget was spent, each a full FireTrigger. Fix: the check now runs INSIDE the occurrence loop, after the run-once/cooldown gate (so a gate-blocked skip stays authored semantics) and before the batched-suppression check. On exhaustion it calls the existing DW-349 arm `RequeueEdgeEventsFor(idx, ex, fromEvent: e)`, so the unconsumed EDGE occurrences persist targeted at that trigger; the sweep's own top-of-loop check then persists the skipped tail from idx+1 — tightening the ceiling therefore loses nothing. Determinism: no golden, SimChecksum, CanonicalModelHash or StartStateHash value moved; every golden/hash/checksum test passed unchanged, including the DW-349 goldens-safety proof PolledThresholds_AreNeverPersisted_AndFuelSkipBehaviorIsUnchanged. Coverage: new Godot-free godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Dsl/DslFuelOccurrenceHaltTests.cs (3 tests) whose fixtures pre-burn 63 x 257 = 16191 of the 16384-op budget with whole-trigger burns keyed on a switchable P2 threshold, so the halt lands on a hand-computable dispatch; teeth proven by temporarily neutering the production code (file copy to scratchpad, then restored) — all 3 FAIL with both fixes neutered. Gate: build succeeded, 0 errors / 6 pre-existing warnings; suite 5172 passed / 1 failed / 1 skipped where the lone failure was the documented CanonicalModelHashPerf CPU-contention timing flake (338.73 ms vs the 250 ms ceiling; PASSED 2/2 in isolation) = 5170 baseline + 3 new. Follow-ons filed as DW-685 (the occurrence loop never re-checks the trigger-enabled mask) and DW-686 (RequeueEdgeEventsFor now has three callers all relying on an undocumented pre-checked-gate precondition).

### DW-545: DrainWorkList still abandons remaining same-tick custom occurrences on fuel exhaustion — a surviving loss class DW-349 did not close
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03
location: godot/src/Core/ScenarioDirector.cs — DrainWorkList
severity: medium
reason: Fuel exhaustion during the custom-event drain abandons the remaining same-tick work items (documented as an accepted-loss class in the method doc). DW-349's owner decision scoped the re-queue rail to base EDGE events, so custom occurrences are still silently dropped; extending persistence to them would change DrainWorkList semantics and the cascade-bound analysis and therefore needs its own decision. Filed so the ledger distinguishes this surviving loss class from the one DW-349 closed rather than reading the fuel-drop problem as fully solved. Closure = an owner decision on custom-occurrence persistence, then either extend the rail or record the loss as authored semantics in the DSL reference.
status: done 2026-08-05
decision: 2026-08-04 Extend re-queue rail to custom occurrences — Persist fuel-dropped same-tick custom occurrences through the DW-349 re-queue rail and re-validate the cascade-bound analysis so custom events get the same edge-parity as base events.
resolution: closed by bundle scenariodirector-fuel-requeue (workflow burn-down, 2026-08-05). Verified LIVE first, then implemented to the recorded ledger decision (DW-545 does not appear in .bmad-loop/decisions.json; the ledger `decision:` line was the authority and was followed literally). Confirmed: DrainWorkList's per-dispatch fuel check did a bare `return`, abandoning the rest of the same-tick work list (the method doc named it an accepted loss). Fix: the halt now persists everything. The occurrence caught mid-dispatch rides a NEW reserved rail, `EventBounds.CustomRequeueRailBase (0x100000) + resumeExec * MaxCustomEvents + eventIndex`, which packs the registry index and the RESUME exec into the queue's code lane so raiser and the full P0..P3 payload keep their own lanes — a max-param custom event persists losslessly, where the DW-349 rail's P3-as-target trick has no free slot on a custom occurrence. Items the halt never STARTED persist under their plain registry index, i.e. as ordinary next-tick occurrences, so the common case adds no new code shape to the folded queue. The tick-start dequeue decodes the rail into a work item carrying TargetExec as a resume floor; DrainWorkList starts its subscriber scan there, so subscribers already served on the drop tick can never double-fire. Cascade bound re-validated (the decision's second half) and written into the method doc: persistence DEFERS, never amplifies — at most one queue row per abandoned occurrence, redelivered as a root occurrence whose transitive same-tick cost the load-time MaxCascadeOps proof already bounds, with MaxNextTickEventQueue drop-newest capping how many roots can persist. Determinism: no golden, SimChecksum, CanonicalModelHash or StartStateHash value moved; the new rail rows can only exist on a tick that exhausts the 16384-op DSL budget, which no shipped content or golden fixture does, and the DW-349 proof PolledThresholds_AreNeverPersisted_AndFuelSkipBehaviorIsUnchanged still passes. Coverage: new Godot-free godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Dsl/DslFuelOccurrenceHaltTests.cs (3 tests); teeth proven by temporarily neutering the production code (file copy to scratchpad, then restored) — all 3 FAIL with both fixes neutered, and with ONLY the resume-exec neutered (persist untargeted) the two custom-drain tests FAIL with 448 and 512 instead of 384, proving the resume encoding is what prevents double-firing already-served subscribers. Gate: build succeeded, 0 errors / 6 pre-existing warnings; suite 5172 passed / 1 failed / 1 skipped where the lone failure was the documented CanonicalModelHashPerf CPU-contention timing flake (PASSED 2/2 in isolation) = 5170 baseline + 3 new. Follow-on filed as DW-684 (custom-occurrence re-queue parity is capped by the 64-row queue while the work list holds 1024).

Verifying the premise falsified half of this entry: "UpdateSnapshots has already wiped the log" holds only for scenarios that own at least one trigger, because ScenarioDirector.Tick's trigger-less early-out (ScenarioDirector.cs:1362) returns BEFORE UpdateSnapshots while clearing every OTHER transient rail, so a zero-trigger scenario accumulated one record per combat death up to CAPACITY and the assert alone would have shipped "save is impossible after any combat death on a trigger-less map" (GoldenApplierScenario declares no triggers).
