### DW-560: ContentPackager.Pack destroys a pre-existing output zip before writing the new one (non-atomic export output)
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03
location: godot/src/Core/Definitions/ContentPackager.cs - Pack, the File.Delete(outputZipPath) + ZipArchiveMode.Create write (~line 240)
reason: Same non-atomic-write family as DW-421 but on Pack's OUTPUT rather than RewriteManifest's in-place edit: an existing export at outputZipPath is deleted up front, so a throw mid-write leaves the creator's previous export destroyed and a partial zip on disk. Reachable in practice because the non-hashed sources (screenshot, faction files, thumbnail) are still re-read at write time, so one of them being deleted or locked between enumeration and the write loop throws after the old export is already gone. Out of the contentpackager-atomic-and-symmetry bundle's scope, which covered RewriteManifest atomicity, the hash TOCTOU, and pack/unpack gate symmetry - not Pack output staging. Closure = the same stage-to-temp-then-atomic-File.Move pattern RewriteManifest now uses, so a failed export leaves the prior export byte-identical.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: workflow burn-down bundle contentpackager-atomic-and-symmetry (2026-08-05) - verified STILL PRESENT against current code at the run base (godot/src/Core/Definitions/ContentPackager.cs:251 - `if (File.Exists(outputZipPath)) File.Delete(outputZipPath);` immediately followed by `using var archive = ZipFile.Open(outputZipPath, ZipArchiveMode.Create)`), then fixed exactly as this entry's closure line specifies; no decisions.json entry exists for DW-560, so the ledger reason/closure governed scope. FIX: Pack now writes the export into a temp SIBLING of the output (outputZipPath + ".pack.tmp") and File.Move-swaps it over outputZipPath (overwrite: true) only after the ZipArchive has fully committed on Dispose - the same stage-to-temp-then-atomic-rename pattern RewriteManifest adopted for DW-421, applied to Pack's OUTPUT. The `using var archive` was converted to an explicit `using (...) { }` block so the commit-on-Dispose provably precedes the rename; a throw anywhere in the write unwinds with any pre-existing export byte-identical and readable, and best-effort-deletes the staged partial. Sibling path means same volume, so the Move is an atomic rename. Public signature, success-path output and ZipArchiveMode.Create semantics (a re-export is a FRESH archive, never an Update over the old one) are unchanged, and the only production caller (WinConditionPhase.cs:430) is unaffected. Pre-existing failure modes are preserved or improved: a missing parent directory still throws from the same ZipFile.Open, and a locked output now fails AFTER staging (leaving the old export intact) instead of destroying it up front. COVERAGE: 3 new tests appended to godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Definitions/ContentPackagerAtomicityTests.cs (Godot-free, alongside the existing DW-421/DW-423 contracts) - Pack_ThrowMidWrite_LeavesPreviousExportIntact reproduces this entry's named real-world trigger with no new seam (it uses the existing PackTestHookAfterHash window to delete a NON-hashed screenshot source the write loop still re-reads, so File.ReadAllBytes throws mid-write); Pack_StagingFailure_LeavesPreviousExportIntact squats a directory on the .pack.tmp name to pin the staging MECHANISM (an in-place Pack succeeds there and fails the test); Pack_Success_ReplacesPreviousExportWholesaleAndLeavesNoResidue guards that staging did not silently become Update semantics (a v1 faction entry must not survive a v2 re-export) and that no .pack.tmp residue leaks. RED VERIFICATION: the fixed source was copied aside, `git checkout --` restored the pre-fix ContentPackager.cs, and the filtered run failed exactly 2 of the 3 new tests - Pack_ThrowMidWrite (previous export replaced by a partial zip: File.Exists true but bytes differed) and Pack_StagingFailure (no exception thrown, i.e. it wrote in place); the fix was then restored and rebuilt. The third passes both pre- and post-fix by design, being a semantics guard on the new staging path rather than a defect-pinner. No git stash was used at any point. DETERMINISM: nothing folded into SimChecksum, CanonicalModelHash or StartStateHash was touched - packaging paths are outside all three and no hash VALUE changed at all, only where the output file is written; zero goldens moved and none were re-recorded. GATE (on the committed tree, relative paths, this worktree only): `dotnet build godot/godot.csproj` succeeded with 0 errors and 6 warnings, all pre-existing in unrelated files (ScoreScreenOverlay, UnitCardPanel.Edit, MainMenuPhase, DedicatedServer) and none new; `dotnet test godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests.csproj` 5257 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped, exactly the 5254/0/1 baseline plus the 3 new tests, so the CanonicalModelHashPerf flake exception was not needed. BRANCH NOTE: `dw/contentpackager-atomic-and-symmetry` already existed from the earlier 2026-08-03 run of this same bundle name (commit d9047531, which closed DW-421/423/424); that tip is an ancestor of this run's base e221fa10 and the branch was checked out in no worktree, so `git checkout -B` fast-forwarded it onto the run base before committing - nothing was discarded and the stale commit remains reachable from master. New commit: 69f382bf. Follow-ons filed as DW-716 and DW-717.

### DW-561: ItemCardPanel.LoadItemsFromDir bypasses the fail-closed ItemLoader/Validate gate, admitting hostile or invalid hand-authored defs into the editable set
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03
location: godot/src/CreationSuite/ItemCardPanel.cs:184-185
reason: The panel deserializes item JSON raw with no Validate gate, so an invalid or hostile hand-authored def enters the editable set silently - asymmetric with ItemRegistry.LoadFromDirectory, which validates and reports drops via onSkipped (DW-455). Bind->Revalidate does badge the offending fields and Save stays disabled, and the one concrete filesystem sink this fed (the _originalId rename-cleanup File.Delete, reachable with an id like '../../evil') was closed under DW-456, so this is not currently fail-open. It is also plausibly deliberate: an ungated load is what lets a creator open and repair a broken file, which a fail-closed loader would make impossible. Closure = a ledger decision on the intended posture - either keep the raw load and document it as the repair path, or route through ItemLoader with a visible skipped-files warning like the registry - rather than a silent asymmetry between the two loaders.
status: open
decision: 2026-08-04 Gate the load fail-closed — Route LoadItemsFromDir through the ItemLoader/Validate gate with onSkipped reporting so invalid/hostile defs are dropped and reported at load, matching ItemRegistry.LoadFromDirectory.

### DW-570: Sim-side flow-field obstacle stamp is a fixed 3x3-cell block regardless of building footprint
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03
location: godot/src/Navigation/FlowFieldSystem.cs (BUILDING_HALF_CELLS = 1, MarkBuildingCells)
reason: The deterministic sim path layer stamps every building as a fixed 3x3 cells (~6x6 world units) no matter its real size, while the navmesh layer now derives footprints from the definition (DW-169). Built-in buildings already vary 4-7 units and custom footprints are now def-derived, so a large custom building routes NavigationServer paths around its true extent while flow-field units still only avoid 6x6 - units clip or crowd large buildings on the sim-steered path. Out of DW-169's scope (that entry targets NavObstacleManager only) and NOT safely fixable on the Godot-free burn-down track: changing the obstacle map alters MovementSystem trajectories -> Position -> SimChecksum, so it needs its own story with deliberate golden re-baseline consideration. No pre-existing ledger entry covers it. Closure = derive MarkBuildingCells' stamp from the same BuildingNavFootprint policy, with a planned SimChecksum fold / golden re-record.
status: done 2026-08-06
resolution: closed by workflow burn-down bundle `flowfield-building-footprint` (Phase C integration, branch rebaseline/phase-c) - verified still live at base 5b6021f5, then fixed per the recorded 2026-08-04 decision. FlowFieldSystem.MarkBuildingCells no longer stamps a fixed 3x3 cells for every building; per-building half-cell extents are derived from the SAME BuildingNavFootprint policy the navmesh carve uses. BuildingNavFootprint (src/UI, the DW-169 policy, Godot-free and already single-file-included by Sim.Tests) gained ToHalfCells / ResolveHalfCells / ObstacleExtentSource with halfCells = ceil((size/2)/cellSize), the exact conservative bound for an axis-aligned box whose centre may sit anywhere inside its centre cell: it reproduces the legacy stamp exactly for the 4x4 building the constant was sized for and grows from there (CommandCenter 6x4x6 -> 2 cells, ArcheryRange 4x3x5 -> 1 col x 2 rows, SiegeWorkshop 5x3x7 -> 2x2, un-authored custom -> guarded 5x3x5 default -> 2x2), with X driving COLUMNS and Z driving ROWS so a long-and-narrow building stamps a rectangle. ARCHITECTURE: FlowFieldSystem is globbed into both the Tier-1 harness and ProjectChimera.Sim.Analysis, and BuildingNavFootprint is deliberately float-based presentation policy, so a direct sim->UI reference would have failed the analyzer gate outright and put floats inside the CHM0001 ban; the sim therefore takes pure INTEGER extents through a new slot-keyed FlowFieldSystem.BuildingObstacleExtents delegate that NavigationPhase wires from the same ResolveBuildingDef closure NavObstacleManager uses, clamped into [1, MAX_BUILDING_HALF_CELLS=32] so absurd authored content can neither shrink the clearance floor nor unbound the marking loop. With no source wired the stamp is byte-identical to pre-DW-570. No mesh-AABB source is passed to the sim resolve, deliberately - a GLB's AABB is not state both lockstep peers provably share (residual filed as DW-845). GOLDENS MOVED: ZERO, and that is a real finding rather than an omission: FlowFieldSystem is driven only by FlowFieldBridge, a Godot Node in src/UI whose _Process polls BuildingStore, and SimulationHost/MovementSystem contain no FlowField reference at all (grepped across the whole sim set), so the Godot-free Tier-1 golden harness never exercises the obstacle map - the entry's "changing the obstacle map alters MovementSystem trajectories -> Position -> SimChecksum" is true of the LIVE game, not of the harness. 428 hash/golden guard tests green in isolation and in the full suite. FALSIFICATION-CHECKED BOTH WAYS: with the derivation short-circuited to the legacy floor 4 of the new tests go RED; NoFootprintSource_KeepsTheLegacyThreeByThreeStamp passes against old and new code by design (the opt-in back-compat pin). GATE (this worktree, relative paths): `dotnet build godot/godot.csproj` 0 errors / 6 pre-existing warnings; `dotnet test godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests --logger trx` 6073 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped (6050 baseline + exactly the 23 new tests incl. Theory rows). ProjectChimera.Sim.Analysis also built clean, confirming the sim layer stayed float-free.
goldens: moves — bounded sim correction. Rides Story 15.22 (Phase C batched re-baseline, AlgoVersion 23->24).
decision: 2026-08-04 Derive the flow-field stamp from the building footprint and re-record goldens — Change MarkBuildingCells to compute per-building half-cell extents from the definition footprint (mirroring the navmesh derivation), then re-record affected SimChecksum goldens on Windows.

### DW-578: `expr_call` renders operand ports a/b even for zero-arity state-read builtins
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03
location: godot/src/Dsl/NodePortCatalog.cs (ExprCallNode case)
reason: Pre-existing view behavior faithfully preserved by the DW-195 extraction: `NodePorts` admits operand ports 0/1 on EVERY `expr_call`, so an author can wire an operand into a zero-arity builtin (e.g. `unit_count_tag`) and only learn it is illegal at compile time via the located badge, not before drawing the wire. Not a correctness bug - the compiler still rejects it - but it is a discoverability wart in the visual editor, and the extraction has now made the rendered-port rule an explicit, easily-corrected seam. Left as-is because curating rendered ports per-fn arity is a separate polish item outside the node-editing bundle's scope. Closure = derive the rendered operand-port count from the per-fn arity table `NodeFieldCatalog` already consults, keeping `NodePorts` legality unchanged.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: workflow burn-down bundle dsl-node-port-arity - DW-578 verified still open against current code: NodePortCatalog's `case ExprBinaryNode: case ExprCallNode:` fell through to a single body that unconditionally added operand pins a AND b, so every expr_call rendered two wireable operand ports regardless of the builtin's arity. Note the entry's example is slightly off - `unit_count_tag` is arity 1 (its tag is a static Selector, not an operand); the true zero-arity read is `region_unit_count`. Both classes were mis-rendered. The fix is exactly the closure this entry asks for (ONE arity table, NodePorts legality untouched): (1) NodeKinds.ExprCallArity(string? fn) in godot/src/Dsl/NodeBase.cs is the per-fn operand-arity table, lifted verbatim out of ExprCompiler.VisitCall's local switch (same values, -1 for unknown) - the entry said the table NodeFieldCatalog already consults, but no arity table lived there, the closest analogue being NodeKinds.FnUsesSelector, so the table now sits beside it; (2) ExprCompiler.VisitCall consults it instead of its private copy, giving byte-identical compile behavior while making it impossible for the pins the editor RENDERS to drift from the edges the gate ACCEPTS - ExprParser.ParseCall deliberately keeps its own narrower 7.4-only table (routing it through the shared one would silently widen the TEXT grammar to the 7.13 state reads), now stated in the doc comment so a later author does not de-duplicate it into a language change; (3) NodePortCatalog's ExprCallNode case splits off ExprBinaryNode and emits exactly `arity` operand pins (clamped to the 0/1 legality pair), with an unknown fn - unreachable, since both parse and the inspector membership-check ExprCallFns - falling back to the full legal pair rather than hiding an already-drawn wire. Coverage: 5 new tests in godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Dsl/NodeEditingSeamTests.cs; the regression net was proven by restoring the pre-fix NodePortCatalog from 2a97c463 and re-running - 4 of the 5 FAIL without the fix (OperandPortsFollowBuiltinArity, ZeroArityStateRead_RendersNoOperandPin, RenderedOperandPins_AreExactlyTheOnesTheCompilerAccepts, FnEdit_ReshapesRenderedOperandPins), the 5th documents the unknown-fn fallback and passes both ways by design. The strongest test runs end to end against ExprCompiler.TryCompile: for every fn in ExprCallFns and both legal operand ports, a RENDERED pin is one the compiler accepts an edge into, and every withheld pin is one it rejects with its located takes-N-arguments-but-port-P error. The existing PortCatalog_DataPorts_SoundAndComplete_ExceptActionIndexCuration was renamed to ..._ExceptSanctionedCurations and its inline curation predicate extracted, since there are now two sanctioned rendered-port curations. Determinism: view-only seam - nothing folded into SimChecksum, CanonicalModelHash or StartStateHash changed (CanonicalModelHash folds ExprCallNode's Fn/Selector, never arity), no golden moved and no hash/AlgoVersion test failed; float-free (src/Dsl is inside the analyzer's globbed set). Gate: dotnet build godot/godot.csproj succeeded (6 pre-existing warnings, 0 errors); dotnet test godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests = 5451 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped in 1m39s - exactly the 5446 baseline plus the 5 new tests, first try, no flake. Follow-ups filed as DW-755 (an edge into a curated-away port is un-drawable AND un-deletable in the T3 editor) and DW-756 (the expr_call fn setter clears a stale Selector but cannot prune operand EDGES stranded by an arity-shrinking fn switch).

### DW-581: `EntityWorld.Generation` is not persisted by `SaveGameState` (unlike `BuildingStore.Generation`)
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03

reason: DW-184 added a per-slot recycle `Generation` array to `EntityWorld` but deliberately did NOT add a save lane for it, unlike the persisted `BuildingStore.Generation`. Safe today by construction: the only cross-tick holder of a packed ENTITY ref is `WinConditionSystem._leaderRef`, which the SP load path re-packs at generation 0 during its fresh apply-time re-configure (`ClearForReset` zeroes generations; apply-time spawns append at gen 0), and a resolved leader's death latches its FOLDED `WinStateStore` verdict on the same tick it dies - so no save boundary can separate a bumped generation from its persisted consequence. The trap is future work: the moment any story stores a packed ENTITY ref in persisted or folded state (the way packed BUILDING refs already live in the persisted `CommandTarget` lane), `EntityWorld.Generation` MUST join the `SaveGameState` entity lanes or a reload will resolve stale refs as live. Documented on the field; adding the lane now would churn the save format for zero present benefit. Closure = add the lane at that point, or add a gate test asserting no packed entity ref reaches persisted or folded state.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: closed by workflow burn-down bundle `savegame-generation-persistence` (merge 5a9ec109, dev 980fed30) - verified STILL OPEN at run-base 6c509c57 (EntityWorld.Generation carried a literal "NOT persisted by SaveGameState" comment and SaveGameState's EA enum had no Generation lane, while BuildingStore/HeroStore/ItemStore generations were all persisted). No `decision:` line here and DW-581 is absent from .bmad-loop/decisions.json, so the worklist intent picked the entry's FIRST closure option (add the lane) over its second (a gate test asserting no packed entity ref reaches persisted/folded state) - the lane retires the hazard rather than fencing it, so that second artifact deliberately does NOT exist and no reader should expect it. `EA.Generation` added as the LAST per-entity lane (before PatrolWpX, where the flat-stride half begins, so Validate's existing `length == EntHwm` loop covers it for free); RestoreEntities also ZEROES the tail past EntHwm because Generation is the one per-slot field Create() does not re-default on the fresh-append path, so it rests on the "generation == 0 past the high-water mark" invariant; Validate rejects a generation outside [0, new EntityWorld.MAX_PACKABLE_GENERATION] (the lane feeds a SHIFT, not an index, so a corrupt value silently stops PackRef round-tripping instead of crashing); SaveGameFile.FormatVersion bumped 1 -> 2 so an older save fails at the header with the accurate "made by an older game version" message instead of being reported CORRUPT for an entity-lane-count mismatch; the now-false EntityWorld.Generation doc block rewritten (DW-194 class). Generation stays UNFOLDED - EntityRefPackingTests.Generation_IsNotFoldedIntoSimChecksum still passes; no SimChecksum / CanonicalModelHash / StartStateHash moved and no golden was re-recorded (the restore change makes a resumed world CONVERGE on the uninterrupted reference run). 7 new SaveLoadTests, each proven RED first by reverting the matching half. ### DW-582: `NoHardcodedPlayerCountTests`' source scan false-positives on multiplicative const expressions with a leading small literal

origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03
location: godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Meta/NoHardcodedPlayerCountTests.cs:66-68
severity: low
reason: The scan's regex `= (2|4|8|9)\b` also matches `<capacity/slot/player-named const> = 2 * OTHER_CONST`, so a sized-buffer constant written with the literal first is flagged as a hardcoded player count — exactly the RingCapacity-class site the guard explicitly documents as a non-goal. Hit for real in the `dslsimeventfeed-capacity` bundle when raising `DslSimEventFeed.Capacity`, and worked around by ordering the literal last (`EntityWorld.MAX_ENTITIES * 2`), which is semantically identical but reads as an arbitrary style rule to the next author. Fix = teach the regex to reject a following `*` (or otherwise require the literal be the whole initializer) — a change to a Tier-1 meta-guard, so it was out of that bundle's scope. Adjacent to DW-513, which is the mirror-image defect in the same regex (an aliased-to-sanctioned-constant form the scan cannot see); the two want to land together.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: workflow burn-down bundle meta-test-regex (2026-08-05) — verified STILL OPEN against current code first (the literal regex at NoHardcodedPlayerCountTests.cs:80 ended at a bare `\b`, and the live workaround it forced was sitting in production at godot/src/Core/DslSimEventFeed.cs:42 with a comment spelling out the defect verbatim); no decisions.json entry and no `decision:` line, so no owner override applied. FIX (one line of real change): the player-count literal must now be the WHOLE initializer — terminated by `;`, or by `,` for the first declarator of a multi-declarator field — instead of by `\b`. Of the two closures this entry offered, the second ("require the literal be the whole initializer") was taken because it is strictly more general (it kills `<< + - /` and every other operator form, not just `*`) and because it makes the literal half SYMMETRIC with DW-513's alias half, which has always required `;` for exactly this reason: an initializer computed from something else is a derived size, not a restated count. The class doc gained a (1c) paragraph stating that contract and naming the accepted residual. DW-789's merge concern is discharged empirically: the entire test-file diff removes exactly ONE line (the literal pattern), DW-513's `PlayerCountAliasConst` regex and its separate match loop are byte-unchanged, a new real-tree test proves the two halves never double-classify one declaration, and no sibling guard carries a copy of the defective pattern. RED BEFORE GREEN, measured: the new tests were written and run FIRST against the unfixed regex — 9 failed (all 7 sized-buffer theory cases, the historical-pattern comparison, and the live-source anchor); after the one-line fix, 36/36 in that class. Coverage is +21 cases: sized-buffer expressions across `* << + - /`; a frozen verbatim copy of the pre-fix pattern that fails both on a revert AND on an over-tightening; the literal half still flagging `= 2/4/8/9;` in every real spelling (trailing comment, split across lines, first of a multi-declarator) and still ignoring `= 6/42/256` including the `42` near-miss; and a live-source test that reads the REAL DslSimEventFeed.Capacity declaration, re-spells it literal-first order-agnostically, and requires the scan to stay silent. The production operand order was deliberately NOT flipped back (the file's own prose says "the entity cap, doubled"), but the stale comment instructing the next author to obey a rule that no longer exists WAS rewritten — that comment is the only production change in the whole diff. DETERMINISM: zero executable code changed in godot/src (the `const int Capacity` expression is byte-identical), so no SimChecksum / CanonicalModelHash / StartStateHash value can move; no golden was re-recorded and none failed. GATE: `dotnet build godot/godot.csproj` succeeded — 0 errors, 6 warnings all pre-existing in src/UI, src/CreationSuite, src/Multiplayer and src/Core/Bootstrap; `dotnet test godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests.csproj` = 5898 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped against the 5877/0/1 baseline, delta exactly +21 with no pre-existing test moved, clean on the first run (no CanonicalModelHashPerf flake). One xUnit2008 analyzer warning introduced mid-work was removed before commit, so the test-project warning set is also unchanged from baseline. Accepted residuals filed as DW-829 (folded-literal blind spot, documented in the new (1c) paragraph), DW-830 (only the first declarator of a multi-declarator field is ever seen — pre-existing) and DW-831 (basename-keyed allowlist — pre-existing, latent).

origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03

severity: low
reason: The trailing comments on these pin assertions ('7.5 re-land merge: 9-10; Story 7.9: 10-11') read as a bump log that trails the current pinned value of 14. status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: 2026-08-05 resolved by burn-down bundle hash-pin-comment-cleanup (workflow burn-down run) - verified still open first; all three named files carried the stale bump log verbatim, but the entry UNDERCOUNTED the class, so all 8 code sites across 7 files were swept. CHOICE OF CLOSURE: took this entry's second option (delete the partial logs), not 'bring current' - the authoritative per-version rationale already lives ONCE on CanonicalModelHash.AlgoVersion's own XML doc (confirmed to carry the full v1..v14 history), and re-copying 14 entries to 8 sites would guarantee re-rot at the next bump, the opposite of DW-194's own lesson that version-neutral forms can never rot. Each pin now points at that doc; where a trailing comment carried a genuinely version-neutral clause ('pathability folds unchanged') the substance was kept and only the version numbers dropped. WORST SITE, in a named file, was not a bump log at all: CanonicalModelHashTests.cs:297 read `AppendInt(buf, CanonicalModelHash.AlgoVersion);  // AlgoVersion (= 11)` - a bare false claim about the CURRENT value inside the independently-computed FNV stream - now `// AlgoVersion, mixed FIRST (read from the constant - never a restated literal)`. SCOPE BEYOND THE NAMED FILES: HeroProfilePersistenceTests.cs, ScenarioDataMapPropertiesTests.cs, SimResetTests.cs and CustomBuildingDeterminismTests.cs held the identical stale log on a CanonicalModelHash pin; fixing 3 and leaving 4 would defeat the entry's stated goal, and the wave-2 worklist was checked first (no other bundle names any of those files, so the sweep is merge-safe). SimResetTests.cs also had a stale prose header above the pin ('v18 sim fold + v10 canonical fold'), made version-neutral in the same pass. REGRESSION COVERAGE: new AlgoVersionPinCommentHygieneTests.cs, the source-scanning sibling of the DW-194 pin-NAME guard (12 tests). Rule: on any line whose CODE references <Family>.AlgoVersion and carries a trailing comment, the highest version the comment claims must not fall below that family's live pin - a ratchet, not a one-shot, so a log whose newest entry IS the pin stays legal until the next bump and then turns red, forcing update-or-delete and stopping the partial history from re-accreting. Deliberate boundaries, all documented in the class doc: only the code half of a line matches, so prose that merely mentions the symbol is untouched (ProceduralMapGeneratorTests' golden re-record narrative legitimately records the version in force when it was recorded); dotted story numbers are stripped first so 'Story 7.9' / '11.6' is never misread as a version; only unambiguous notation counts (vN, N->M, = N). Includes extractor teeth over real historical comment text, a family-table-vs-live-constant check, and a vacuous-pass defeat (the scan must still observe version-claiming pin lines, so a wrong path or broken splitter cannot pass silently). The guard scans its own source like every other file - no self-exemption - and its one fixture line is built by concatenation so it is not itself an offender. VERIFIED RED BEFORE GREEN: restoring one stale comment fails the guard with a file:line pointer and the offending text; reverted after. DETERMINISM: nothing at risk - outside the new test file the entire diff is comments, zero executable code changed, so no SimChecksum / CanonicalModelHash / StartStateHash value and no golden can move; no re-baseline needed or performed. GATE: `dotnet build godot/godot.csproj` succeeded, 0 errors (6 pre-existing warnings in src/UI and src/Multiplayer); `dotnet test` = 5266 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped against the 5254/0/1 baseline, the +12 being exactly the new class, with no CanonicalModelHashPerf flake. Existing coverage only ever exercised the two ARMED cases the stale comment named (DuplicateVariableDeclarations_WithExpressions_FailClosed_AtLoadScenario; DuplicateArrayDeclaration_WithLoopConstructs_IsRejectedAtBothGates) - i.e. the untested hole was precisely the case the stale prose implied was admitted. The new tests cover it: duplicate scalars with no triggers at all (empty graph - cannot carry an expr or a loop), duplicate scalars in a legacy flat-trigger scenario, a duplicate ARRAY declaration with no for_each (DslLoopGate.CheckDeclarations validates array shape but never uniqueness, and runs AFTER BuildDeclMap, so line 580 is the only thing standing between two same-named arrays at different capacities and a clean load), plus a unique-name control so the rejects cannot be credited to the bare director or the empty/legacy graph. COVERAGE PROVEN, NOT ASSUMED: line 580 was temporarily flipped to `requireUnique: false` (an exact simulation of the pre-7.7 loop-conditional arming, which evaluates false for every loop-free scenario) - 3 of the 4 new tests failed with "No exception was thrown" and the control stayed green; the probe was reverted and the committed diff re-checked to contain only the comment change. GATE (run in the bundle worktree with relative paths): `dotnet build godot/godot.csproj` -> Build succeeded, 0 errors (6 pre-existing nullable/hiding warnings, untouched); `dotnet test godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests.csproj` -> Failed: 0, Passed: 5881, Skipped: 1 - the 5877/0/1 launch baseline plus exactly the 4 additions, no flake exception needed (CanonicalModelHashPerfTests passed in the full run). The worktree was reset --hard to run base 4c7a2259 before any work (it had been cut from the stale 024025e4 "chore(snapshot): date stamp 2026-08-01"); deferred-work.md, sprint-status.yaml and epics.md were not touched by the bundle. Follow-on filed as DW-817 (the same stale 7.6 arming prose survives in a TriggerValidationTests comment and section header).

### DW-590: Allied-KotH concede by the team REP orphans the rep-keyed hold accumulator

origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-03
location: godot/src/Core/WinConditionSystem.cs - UpdateKothCounters/TeamRep + KothWinningTeam
severity: medium
reason: Pre-existing Story 11.2 x 7.12 interaction, NOT introduced or worsened by the DW-188 bundle: if the lowest-slot (rep) faction of an allied team latches LOST via CONCEDE while a live ally keeps sole-holding the zone, `UpdateKothCounters` keeps accruing hold ticks on the LOST rep (`TeamRep` ignores verdicts) but `KothWinningTeam` only reads verdict-NONE factions, so the ally's hold can never reach the win and the match hangs. Fixing it means touching the hold-race WIN path (e.g. re-repping to the lowest verdict-NONE member, which moves folded `KothHoldTicks` values) - exactly what the DW-188 decision said not to perturb - and concede-with-teams semantics deserve their own decision. The DW-188 wipeout fallback deliberately avoids this class via its team-scoped guard. Closure = a design decision on allied-KotH concede semantics, then a hold-race-path change with an explicit golden/checksum review.
status: done 2026-08-05
decision: 2026-08-05 Re-rep KothHoldTicks to the lowest verdict-NONE team member — Make TeamRep/KothWinningTeam agree by re-keying the accumulator to the lowest verdict-NONE ally when the rep latches LOST (moving folded KothHoldTicks), then re-record affected goldens.
resolution: closed by bundle decision-dw-590 (workflow burn-down, 2026-08-05), commit 4ce6b8d4. Defect confirmed live: UpdateKothCounters keyed the contiguous sole-hold count on TeamRep = the lowest-slot member full stop, while KothWinningTeam reads only verdict-NONE factions, so when the rep latched LOST out-of-band (Story 11.2 CONCEDE via OrderApplier, or the DSL `defeat` leaf) the count kept accruing on the dead rep while the live sole-holding ally was zeroed every tick as a non-rep — and with 2 live teams ApplyLastTeamStanding no-ops, so the match hung forever. Fix (godot/src/Core/WinConditionSystem.cs, 2 methods + 1 helper): TeamRep now returns the lowest-slot UNRESOLVED member, falling back to the historic lowest-slot member when every member is resolved; new TeamHoldTicks reads the team's live count as the max over active members (at most one slot per team is ever non-zero) so a re-rep CARRIES the count rather than restarting at zero, while a contest that already zeroed the counter correctly restarts the ally at 1. Determinism: NO golden was re-recorded and none moved — the decision's "then re-record affected goldens" clause proved unnecessary, because folded KothHoldTicks values are byte-identical wherever the old rep was already correct (every all-unresolved team, and every FFA teams-of-1 slot, which is why the fallback keeps the historic slot); independently confirmed no golden scenario or shipped resource uses the KingOfTheHill preset and no golden mutates AllianceStore.TeamId. SimChecksum AlgoVersion, CanonicalModelHash and StartStateHash untouched. Scope held: the DW-188 team-scoped wipeout guard was NOT narrowed even though its orphan rationale is now moot (that is a different loss rule than DW-188 recorded); only its comment was updated to say why it stays. Tests: new Godot-free KothRepReKeyTests.cs (6 tests; concedes drive the REAL OrderApplier wire path, not a hand-poked verdict), red-verified 4 failed / 2 passed against the pre-fix file — the 4 red ones being the headline re-rep-and-win case, the two-successive-concedes lowest-unresolved ordering pin, the contest-before-concede live-carry pin, and the two-run determinism fold (which hangs pre-fix); the 2 that pass on both sides are the intentional fold-neutrality pins. Gate: build 0 errors; suite 5175/1/1 where the lone failure was the documented CanonicalModelHashPerf CPU-contention timing flake (passes in isolation) = 5170 baseline + 6 new.

### DW-604: ReplayRecorder.RecordTick silently clamps a sub-bundle with more than MAX_ORDERS orders
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-04

status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: workflow burn-down bundle replay-recorder-fail-loud (2026-08-05) — verified still live against current code first (ReplayRecorder.cs:159 still held the silent clamp `if (count > TickCommandPacket.MAX_ORDERS) count = TickCommandPacket.MAX_ORDERS;` immediately after the DW-432 sub-bundle-count throw). FIX: replaced it with an InvalidOperationException whose shape and message style mirror the adjacent DW-432 guard, so both frozen-envelope ceilings in the recorder now fail loud instead of one throwing and one truncating; DW-604 is absent from .bmad-loop/decisions.json so no recorded human decision overrode scope, and nothing beyond that line was touched. This entry's latency claim was confirmed against the code rather than trusted: MergedTickPacket.TryRead (NetworkCommand.cs:1387) rejects a sub-bundle with count > MAX_ORDERS outright, and MergedTickApplier.Apply only fires the onSubBundle record hook after a successful TryRead (MergedTickApplier.cs:101-110), which is the sole production feed via LockstepManager._recordHook (LockstepManager.cs:285-286) — so the new throw is a tripwire for a future non-merged-stream caller, never a live branch. All 18 existing RecordTick call sites (17 in tests, 1 in src) were audited; none passes a count above 32, so nothing pre-existing trips the new guard. DETERMINISM: no sim state touched — the change lives entirely in the replay writer, with no SoA array, no Fixed math and nothing folded into SimChecksum, CanonicalModelHash or StartStateHash; no goldens moved and none were re-recorded. COVERAGE added to godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Multiplayer/ReplayRecorderOverflowTests.cs (where DW-432's tests already live): SubBundleOverMaxOrders_ThrowsInsteadOfSilentlyClamping drives a 33-order sub-bundle and asserts the throw, and ExactlyMaxOrders_RecordsAndEveryOrderRoundTrips pins the boundary — 32 orders is still legal and all 32 Move orders reach their own unit through a real ReplayPlayer round-trip, so an off-by-one in the new guard or a silent trim would both be caught. The first test was proven genuinely red without the fix (clamp temporarily restored → "Assert.Throws() Failure: No exception was thrown", 1 failed / 3 passed), then the throw was restored. GATE: `dotnet build godot/godot.csproj` → 0 errors (6 pre-existing warnings, all in untouched UI/Bootstrap/DedicatedServer files); `dotnet test godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests.csproj` → 5879 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped, i.e. the 5877 baseline plus exactly the 2 new tests, the skip being the pre-existing TriggerValidationTests.RandomEffect_MustDrawFromSimRng_ReservedUntilStory2_3; no CanonicalModelHashPerf flake, so no isolation re-run was needed. Adjacent findings filed as DW-832 (TickCommandPacket.Write still silently clamps on the wire writer — same class, but a real behavioural decision about the live send path rather than a latent-tripwire cleanup) and DW-833 (RecordTick leaves the tick buffer half-initialised when either ceiling guard throws).

### DW-605: Online lockstep silently drops orders past 32 per tick, so large box-select commands truncate with no player feedback
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/Multiplayer/LockstepManager.cs:318-319 (EnqueueOrder: `if (_pendingCount < TickCommandPacket.MAX_ORDERS)` with no else branch and no denial cue)
severity: medium
reason: Found during the DW-429 analysis. Online, a command issued against more than 32 units in one tick (box-select 40 units + right-click = 40 per-unit orders) silently drops orders 33+: those units never move and the player gets no OrderDenied cue, while the offline apply-now path applies all 40. It is deterministic (the drop happens client-side before send) so it is not a desync, but it is a live/offline behavior divergence and a silent-drop UX gap on a very ordinary RTS input. Pre-existing and orthogonal to the replay bundle's scope, so not touched. Closure = either coalesce/queue the overflow into the next tick or surface an explicit denial cue, and pin the chosen behavior with a test.
status: open
decision: 2026-08-05 Coalesce/queue overflow across ticks — Coalesce or queue orders beyond 32 into subsequent ticks so all selected units eventually receive the command, matching offline apply-now completeness.
scoping-note (owner, 2026-08-05): FIRST establish whether `TickCommandPacket.MAX_ORDERS = 32` caps *orders* or *units* — it changes the implementation completely and the wrong reading builds the wrong thing. If one right-click over N selected units currently emits N separate order entries, the correct fix is NOT a cross-tick queue: it is emitting ONE order carrying a unit-ID list, which is how lockstep RTS engines normally do this, is smaller, and removes the cap pressure entirely rather than spreading it. Only if the 32 are genuinely distinct commands does cross-tick coalescing apply. Rejected option 1 (OrderDenied cue) deliberately: box-select-and-right-click is the core RTS interaction and 40 units is a small army against a 500-2000 entity target, so a denial cue would fire constantly in normal play — it labels the defect rather than fixing it, and is not a stable resting place at target scale.

resolution: 2026-08-05 resolved by burn-down bundle nakama-ci-esbuild-gate (workflow burn-down run) - verified genuinely OPEN against current code first: the `nakama-ts-validator-gate` job ran only `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm test`, none of which ever emit `build/index.js`, the esbuild bundle Nakama actually loads (docker-compose mounts ./nakama-modules/build into /nakama/data/modules), so a change that typechecked and passed vitest but broke bundling shipped with CI green and only surfaced at `docker compose up`, where a missing bundle fail-closes every player out of online play. FIX, two files: (1) .github/workflows/determinism-gate.yml gains `run: npm run build` after the vitest step (matching the README's documented dev order) plus a single-line `run: test -s build/index.js` backstop that catches an `--outfile` drift which still exits 0; the build output is gitignored and discarded with the runner, nothing is published, and it is deliberately a bare `npm run build` rather than inlined esbuild flags so the workflow and package.json cannot drift apart. (2) NakamaTsValidatorCiGateGuardTests.cs gains two Tier-1 guards following the existing 1.10a convention in that file (structure asserted on every `dotnet test`, never as CI-only shell steps): DeterminismGateWorkflow_RunsNpmRunBuild_SoTheDeployBundleIsProvenBuildable pins the workflow step, and NakamaPackage_BuildScript_StillBundlesForTheGojaTarget pins the half a bundling run cannot catch - esbuild exits 0 for an esm/es2022 bundle and the failure lands inside goja at module load - so --bundle / --platform=node / --format=cjs / --target=es2017 are asserted individually with their own failure messages and --outfile is cross-checked against package.json `main`. A shared ActiveLines()/PackageJsonPath() helper was extracted, removing duplicated inline filtering; the pre-existing tests are behaviourally unchanged. package.json was in the bundle's file list but needed NO change - its build script already carried the correct es2017/cjs/node flags, so the defect was the missing CI step, not the script, and the flags are now pinned by the new guard instead. RED-WITHOUT-FIX PROOF: `git show e221fa10:.github/workflows/determinism-gate.yml` filtered through the guard's own active-line + `run:`-prefix logic yields zero matches for `npm run build` (only `npm ci`, `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`), so the new workflow guard fails against the pre-fix file. DETERMINISM: no simulation code touched at all (one CI YAML + one Meta guard test); nothing folded into SimChecksum, CanonicalModelHash or StartStateHash is affected, no golden moved and none was re-recorded. GATE: `dotnet build godot/godot.csproj` succeeded, 0 errors, 6 pre-existing warnings (ScoreScreenOverlay/UnitCardPanel/DedicatedServer/MainMenuPhase, none from this change); `dotnet test` = 5256 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped, exactly the 5254 baseline plus the 2 new guards, no flake encountered. Additionally verified the new CI step will land GREEN rather than red by running the full job locally (Node 24 / npm 11): `npm ci` (49 packages), typecheck clean, `npm test` 44 passed across 3 files, `npm run build` produced build/index.js at 8.2kb opening with a correct CJS "use strict"; prologue, and `test -s build/index.js` succeeds; local node_modules/ and build/ were deleted afterwards (both gitignored) and the commit contains only the two intended files. status: done 2026-08-04
resolution: closed by the total-relabel fix in SkirmishSetupToScenario (ReconcileCustomEvents + ReconcileTriggerGraphJson). The renumber itself is load-bearing (FactionRegistry active span, LocalFactionPolicy's Player1-human hardwire, TeamColorPalette indexing) so it stays; what changes is that the relabel is now TOTAL across every per-slot channel, which yields exactly the WC3/modern-RTS guarantee -- a reference designates the player the author meant, or an empty seat, never a DIFFERENT player. Graph structure is untouched (no node/edge pruning): survivors remap through slotMap, dropped refs canonicalize to the vacant seat k. Note the precise scope: dropped ordinals were ALREADY inert (d >= k always, since pairing takes the k lowest), so the real corruption fixed here is the renumbered SURVIVOR. Class guard: SkirmishGraphReconcileTests.EveryNodeTypeWithAFactionField_IsCoveredByTheReconcile reflects over NodeBase subclasses and fails if a new Faction-carrying node kind is added without being handled -- the silence that let DW-458 ship incomplete cannot recur. 14 tests, 6 proven RED against the un-reconciled build; Tier-1 4858/0/1, no golden moved.
seen-again: 2026-08-04 (post-merge review sweep of merge 0a06b2d) — two lenses re-reported this gap, and verification sharpens it beyond the "inert" framing above: the validator accepts NON-contiguous unique slot ordinals (ScenarioValidator.cs:262-283) and the editor produces them as a first-class state (ScenarioData.RemoveStartSlot removes by Slot value with no renumber — its doc names "a non-contiguous {0,1,3} set"). On such a map Build's positional pairing renumbers the surviving slots (authored {0,2,5} → {0→0, 2→1, 5→2}); the flat Triggers channel is rewritten but TriggerGraphJson faction fields and CustomEvents[].AllowedRaisers are not, so a stale ref lands on a LIVE renumbered player instead of an empty seat: a graph trigger keyed to a surviving original ordinal fires for the wrong player, and event-raise authorization silently transfers — the author-intended raiser is dropped at TryEnqueueExternalDslEvent's Array.IndexOf auth check (ScenarioDirector.cs:487-491) with no error or log, while the player renumbered onto the stale ordinal inherits it. Only on contiguous-from-0 maps does the pairing stay prefix-identity and the inert framing hold. Treat as severity medium for triage (wrong-player dispatch/authorization is semantic corruption of creator content, not mere staleness); closure unchanged. No separate entry filed.

### DW-616: DeathFeed has the identical silent-drop-when-full ring with no priority lane, and its drops are checksum-visible
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/Combat/DeathFeed.cs:35
severity: medium
reason: `MAX_DEATHS = 256` with the same drop-when-full shape as the pre-DW-469 CombatEventQueue, and its own doc comment says the cap mirrors that queue. Unlike the event queue this one has a FOLDED consequence — a dropped DeathRecord awards no hero XP, and XP is in SimChecksum — so a >256-death tick is a (self-healing, low-likelihood) determinism-visible feedback loss. Out of the combat-event-queue-capacity bundle's scope and NOT changed there: any fix moves folded XP and needs its own deliberate golden analysis. Closure = a capacity/priority design for DeathFeed with the golden work costed in.
status: done 2026-08-05
decision: 2026-08-05 Design capacity/priority fix with golden work costed — Raise/priority-lane DeathFeed capacity (or make overflow deterministic-and-lossless) and run the deliberate SimChecksum/golden re-baseline analysis for the folded XP change.
resolution: closed by bundle decision-dw-616 (workflow burn-down, 2026-08-05). Verified still open: DeathFeed.cs:35 still carried `MAX_DEATHS = 256` with a bare drop-when-full Push and a doc comment still claiming the cap "mirrors CombatEventQueue" — a claim DW-469 had already invalidated on the queue side. Defect confirmed REAL, not cosmetic: DeathFeed itself is unfolded (HeroXpSystem drains + Clears it in-tick) but the XP a DeathRecord pays IS folded — HeroStore.Xp/Level and the permanent growth-modifier stacks flow into SimChecksum (SimChecksum.cs:335 folds world.XpBounty explicitly) — so a >256-death tick silently withheld folded feedback. Fix: chose LOSSLESS, not a priority lane — a DW-469-style reserve is inapplicable because every death carries the identical kind of folded consequence, so there is no low-value class to sacrifice. Push now grows the backing array by amortized doubling from INITIAL_CAPACITY = 256 and never drops; growth is a pure function of the push sequence, preserves order index-for-index (Array.Copy, matching the ProjectileStore/BuildingStore house pattern), and capacity is exposed only as a diagnostic `Capacity` property — never folded, serialized or replicated, so two peers that grew differently still credit identical XP. Retained capacity is bounded by peak deaths in one tick (bounded by KillEntity calls, <= EntityWorld.MAX_ENTITIES = 4096 plus in-tick churn). GOLDEN RE-BASELINE ANALYSIS (the half the decision costed in): ZERO goldens move, no re-record needed. Everything the sim can observe about the feed is Count and Get over [0,Count); for the first 256 pushes both come from the exact same append the fixed ring did with no reallocation in between, so any tick at or under the old cap yields a bit-identical HeroXpSystem credit pass and therefore a bit-identical SimChecksum — the change is observable ONLY on a tick that would previously have overflowed, which no recorded golden or replay scenario contains. Pinned permanently by Push_AtInitialCapacity_DoesNotGrow_SoSubCapTicksAreBitIdenticalToThePreFixRing (asserts Count==256 AND Capacity==256) and confirmed empirically: all 31 .golden.txt-backed test classes plus GoldenChecksumReplay, ReBaselineDifferentialGuard, StartStateHash and CanonicalModelHash passed untouched. Tests: new godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Combat/DeathFeedCapacityTests.cs, 6 Godot-free cases, proven to bite by temporarily restoring the drop-when-full Push — 4 of 6 FAIL pre-fix (no-silent-drop, order-preserved-across-the-growth-boundary, overflow-deaths-credit-folded-hero-XP, different-capacities-drain-identically); the other 2 are the deliberate no-golden-move / Clear-posture pins that must pass in both worlds. Also corrected DeathLog.cs's now-stale doc line claiming its CAPACITY is "the DeathFeed cap" (comment only — DeathLog behaviour is DW-367's and deliberately untouched, since changing it would move trigger-visible unit_dies events; filed as DW-674). Gate: build 0 errors; suite 5175/1/1 where the lone failure was the documented CanonicalModelHashPerf CPU-contention timing flake (passed 2/2 in isolation) = 5170 baseline + 6 new, no pre-existing test changed state.

### DW-618: No validator lint for a beneficial (Ally-filtered) modifier that grants a HARMFUL status — the class that shipped a self-stunning Guardian Aura
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/Core/Definitions/AbilityValidator.cs (content: godot/resources/data/abilities/aura_guard.json:25)
severity: high
reason: aura_guard.json shipped `status: "Stunned"` on a SearchArea(filter: Ally) → ApplyModifier(+5 armor) graph and passed every gate, because nothing cross-checks a modifier's StatusFlags against its target filter. The DW-266 bundle corrected that one content file, but the authoring hole that let it through is unfixed — and now has teeth, since the flags are live. ModifierPolarity already encodes exactly the needed classification (HarmfulStatus = Stunned|Rooted|Silenced|Disarmed, Invulnerable = buff). status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: workflow burn-down bundle ability-validator-polarity-lint (2026-08-05) - verified against current code first: the hole is real and still open. aura_guard.json's status field is now "None" (DW-266's content fix landed) and NO shipped ability carries a non-None status at all, but AbilityValidator had zero cross-checks between a granted modifier's StatusFlags and its enclosing SearchArea's target filter, so the same graph was re-authorable at any time - every existing rule (DW-278 warnings, DW-504 period rejects, DW-488 bounds, the 2.6 passive shape rules) reads ONE descriptor in isolation, which is exactly why the self-stunning Guardian Aura shipped (filter Ally is a fine filter, status Stunned is a fine status, only the pairing is wrong). FIX (3 source files): godot/src/Effects/Modifier.cs gained `StatusPolarity` beside the StatusFlags enum (`Harmful = Stunned|Rooted|Silenced|Disarmed`, `Beneficial = Invulnerable`), deliberately NOT as new StatusFlags members since the content loader parses the authored `status` string against that enum and a combined member would become authorable content and widen the wire vocabulary; godot/src/UI/ModifierPolarity.cs now ALIASES StatusPolarity.Harmful for its private HarmfulStatus const and reads StatusPolarity.Beneficial in the Invulnerable branch (behaviour byte-identical - the point is one classification, two consumers); godot/src/Core/Definitions/AbilityValidator.cs gained `WalkFrame.FriendlyOnlySearch` (the located description of the innermost enclosing friendly-only SearchArea, else null) and `CollectPolarityDiagnostics`, which emits a WARNING - never a reject, per this entry's explicit "WARNING-channel lint, not a hard error" closure note - when an ApplyModifier below it grants a StatusPolarity.Harmful status, at field path `<path>.modifier.status` in the same located `ability '<id>'.<path>: <reason>` shape as every other diagnostic. TWO DESIGN CALLS flagged for review: (1) the bundle intent said to use ModifierPolarity's classification directly and listed godot/SimSources.props among its files (presumably to pull src/UI/ModifierPolarity.cs into the shared sim source set so ProjectChimera.Sim.Analysis could compile a Core->UI reference) - NOT taken, because a sim-layer content gate reaching into ProjectChimera.UI is a layering inversion and ModifierPolarity's own docstring calls itself "purely presentation"; hosting the partition in Effects (already globbed by SimSources.props) satisfies the intent's substance - one shared classification, no hand-copied duplicate - with no props or analyzer-set change, and `TheLintAgreesWithTheBuffDebuffIconClassifier_ForEveryStatusFlag` pins the two consumers together flag-by-flag so the anti-drift guarantee is asserted rather than described. (2) "Friendly-only" = Ally bit SET and Enemy bit CLEAR, both halves load-bearing and both pinned by teeth (without the first, TargetFilter.None - every allegiance eligible - trips the lint; without the second, an Ally|Enemy friendly-fire AoE stun, a legitimate design, does); TargetFilter.Self is deliberately NOT friendly, since a self-imposed root/silence as a cost (siege-mode immobility, berserk self-silence) is well-established and warning on it would be noise; nested searches OVERRIDE rather than inherit, because EffectContext.WithTarget re-centres the search but keeps the ORIGINAL CasterFaction (verified at EffectExecutor.cs:108), so the innermost filter decides who a leaf reaches. COVERAGE: 21 new Godot-free tests in AbilityStatusPolarityLintTests; 9 test methods (12 cases counting Theory rows) were PROVEN RED by temporarily neutering the lint and re-running, then restored - including the exact pre-DW-266 aura_guard graph, all four harmful flags, Sequence/nested-search propagation and the anti-drift pin; the rest are anti-false-positive teeth (Enemy filter silent, Ally-filtered Invulnerable silent, Ally|Enemy silent, bare None silent, self-grant silent, rejected ability reports only its error) plus a construction guard that Harmful|Beneficial partitions the whole StatusFlags set with no overlap, so adding a sixth flag without classifying it fails loudly instead of leaving the lint silently blind. Shipped-content cleanliness stays pinned by the existing AbilityInertContentWarningTests.EveryShippedAbility_ValidatesWithZeroWarnings, which still passes. DETERMINISM: nothing re-recorded, no golden touched - this is load-time content diagnostics plus two compile-time constants and one presentation-side alias, with no SoA field, no fold and no runtime branch, so SimChecksum, CanonicalModelHash and StartStateHash are untouched and every golden test passes unchanged. GATE: `dotnet build godot/godot.csproj` succeeded, 0 errors / 6 warnings all pre-existing and none in the touched files; `dotnet test godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests.csproj` 5275 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped against the 5254/0/1 baseline - exactly +21, no flake and no CanonicalModelHashPerf exception needed. The worktree was reset --hard to e221fa10 before any work (it had been cut from the stale "chore(snapshot): date stamp 2026-08-01" snapshot). Follow-ons filed as DW-718 and DW-719.

### DW-619: Stunned/Rooted are invisible to GatheringSystem and BuildingSystem — a stunned worker parked on a node keeps mining
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/Economy/GatheringSystem.cs:199-234; godot/src/Economy/BuildingSystem.cs
severity: medium
reason: Gather progress accrues purely on ticks (CarryAmount += gathered) with no StatusFlagsOf read, and construction progress is the same shape. A stunned/rooted worker already AT its node or build site is anchored by the DW-266 MovementSystem gate but keeps accruing resources / build progress, so a stun only half-lands on the economy. Out of DW-266's scope: its location line and recorded decision name only CombatSystem/MovementSystem/AbilityCastSystem (+DamageResolver), and touching the gather loop would move the gather-state fold that the separate DW-78 bundle owns. Closure = extend the status gate to the economy loops, sequenced after DW-78 so the fold moves once.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: closed by workflow burn-down bundle `status-effect-action-gating` (2026-08-05). Verified against current code before touching it: the gathering half was real and open, the construction half was a MISDIAGNOSIS that needed a different (still real) fix. GATHERING (the filed defect, confirmed): GatheringSystem.TickGathering accrued purely on ticks with no StatusFlagsOf read, so a stunned worker anchored at its node by the DW-266 MovementSystem gate kept draining node supply, filling CarryAmount and — on a Streaming node — crediting its faction every tick at full rate. Fix: a new GATHER_BLOCKING mask (Stunned | Rooted, deliberately the same pair as MovementSystem.MOVE_BLOCKING, as the recorded intent asks) read at the very top of TickGathering. While either flag is live the worker takes NO gather action at all: no supply drain, no carry accrual, no Streaming credit, no depletion, no DW-80 closed-gate streak, no state transition. Placed at the loop-body top for the same reason DW-266's own gate is — the status is a PAUSE, not a cancel, so the node, the AssignedGatherers reservation and the carry all survive and the worker resumes the identical cycle the tick the modifier expires; every release path (death hook, Build interrupt, depletion) still fires, so no reservation can leak while a worker is held. CONSTRUCTION (premise corrected): the entry's claim that "construction progress is the same shape" is FALSE against current code — BuildingSystem.TickConstruction runs a per-BUILDING ConstructionTimer never linked to a builder (the worker only walks to the site to clear its own Build command in TickWorkerArrival, and construction completes whether or not any worker exists), and BuildingStore has no status channel of its own (already filed as DW-677). There is therefore no worker-status-gateable per-tick accrual, and inventing a builder link would have been the restructure this bundle forbids. The one moment a worker's status can reach construction at all is the ORDER: QueueWorkerBuild spends the cost and starts the self-ticking timer in a single atomic act, so a stunned worker could pay for and start a whole building that then finished on its own while it stood held. Fix: a BUILD_BLOCKING check above every debit — no ore/crystal spent, no building placed, no gather slot released, no Build command written — with a guard-sourced denial cue (DenialReason.Stunned when stunned, the existing generic "Order denied" otherwise). Determinism: read-only flag tests only. No SoA field, no fold, no SimChecksum / CanonicalModelHash / StartStateHash input changed, and no golden re-recorded or moved — every recorded golden leaves StatusFlagsOf at None for every entity (the same premise DW-266's existing MovementSystem/DamageResolver gates rely on), so neither new branch is ever entered in a golden; proven by the full suite staying green including the golden and determinism legs, and pinned by a dedicated bit-identity test showing the non-blocking flags (Invulnerable|Silenced|Disarmed) leave carry/supply/ore Raw-identical to StatusFlags.None. Coverage: new Godot-free godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Economy/WorkerStatusGateTests.cs, 9 cases — held-vs-identical-twin mining (exact Raw equality, both flags), Streaming credit-in-place suppression (both flags), the non-blocking-flag bit-identity invariant, an end-to-end AUTHORED stun through the real ModifierStore/ModifierSystem install-and-expire path, the atomic build refusal with its denial reason plus the same order succeeding once the flag clears (both flags), and a twin test proving the gate is on the ORDER and not on TickConstruction (a healthy worker's building still self-ticks). 8 of the 9 were proven RED by temporarily disabling both guards and re-running (then restored and rebuilt); the 9th is the no-op invariance test, which must pass either way by design. Follow-ons filed as DW-824 (including Rooted contradicts the codebase's own "Rooted = held in place, still able to act" semantics — wants an owner confirmation; left in per the recorded intent and isolated behind one named mask so it is a one-token revert), DW-825 (no DenialReason.Rooted, so a root-only refusal falls back to the generic "Order denied"; the fix needs src/UI/** which trips the in-engine gate) and DW-826 (this entry's construction-accrual premise does not hold — recorded so the close reflects what was actually true). Gate run in the burn-down worktree: dotnet build godot/godot.csproj 0 errors, 6 pre-existing warnings; dotnet test full Sim.Tests suite 5886 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped against the 5877/0/1 launch baseline — exactly the 9 added tests, no flake, no CanonicalModelHashPerf failure.

### DW-620: Invulnerable does not cover the ModifierStore ceiling-collapse kill or direct_hp_delta/cost_health self-costs
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/Effects/ModifierStore.cs:~575 (EffectiveMaxHealth==0 → DamageResolver.KillEntity); godot/src/Effects/DirectHpDeltaEffect.cs:34; godot/src/Effects/AbilityCastSystem.cs (cost_health debit)
severity: medium
reason: Recorded as an explicit DW-266 scope boundary rather than an oversight: the recorded decision routes Invulnerable to DamageResolver, so it now blocks all DAMAGE, but a -MaxHealth debuff that collapses the ceiling to 0 still kills an invulnerable unit (DW-325's zombie-kill path calls KillEntity directly, bypassing Apply), and self-costs still spend HP. Both are arguably correct (a self-cost is not damage), but the ceiling-collapse case is a genuine open question. Closure = a later balance/status story settles whether Invulnerable is damage-immunity or death-immunity, and pins it with a test either way.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: closed by bundle decision-dw-620 (workflow burn-down, 2026-08-05). Implemented the recorded owner decision verbatim: Invulnerable is DEATH-immunity, so the guard moved to the single death primitive rather than being duplicated at each direct-kill site. Verified against current code first — DW-266's gate really does sit only on DamageResolver.Apply (DamageResolver.cs:89), and two callers reach the death sequence without passing through it: ModifierStore.ApplyStatDeltas's DW-325 ceiling-collapse kill (ModifierStore.cs:760) and AbilityCastSystem's deferred self-lethal cost_health death (AbilityCastSystem.cs:442); both killed an invulnerable unit outright. The entry's third named location, DirectHpDeltaEffect.cs:34, was already correct (it clamps to [0, MaxHealth] and never fires a death sequence), so the decision's "leave self-costs spend-able" half needed no change there. Fix: DamageResolver.KillEntity now refuses the kill when StatusFlagsOf carries Invulnerable, placed ahead of every write in the sequence so a refused kill is a strict no-op — no killer attribution, no DeathLog record, no UnitKilled/HeroFell event, no RecordKill, no DeathFeed push, no Destroy. One home covers both current direct callers and any future one; unreachable from Apply (its own DW-266 guard returns first). One consequence had to be handled or the change would have introduced a new defect: AbilityCastSystem returned unconditionally after the self-lethal KillEntity, so a death-immune caster would have been left on NEGATIVE health with no cooldown started — free to re-cast every tick and walk Health toward the Fixed underflow. The tail now re-checks IsAlive and floors the pool at 0 (the DirectHpDeltaEffect self-cost convention), then falls through to the normal cooldown/feedback tail; byte-identical for a killable caster. Determinism: nothing re-recorded, no golden touched — the new branch is entered only when StatusFlagsOf carries Invulnerable, which no recorded golden sets (the pre-existing DW-266 damage-path guard already relies on and demonstrates that), and no SoA field or fold changed, so SimChecksum, CanonicalModelHash and StartStateHash are untouched. Coverage: new Godot-free InvulnerableDeathImmunityTests (4 cases), each proven RED by temporarily disabling the guard (4/4 failed, then restored) — the primitive's refused-kill-is-a-no-op plus kills-once-the-flag-drops; the ceiling collapse where the immune host survives at ceiling 0 while a non-immune twin in the same world dies (teeth against simply disabling DW-325); the collapse turning lethal again once an AUTHORED invulnerability modifier expires through the real store path; and the self-lethal cast spending its health, damaging its target, surviving at exactly 0, and starting its cooldown. Gate: build succeeded (6 pre-existing warnings, 0 errors); suite 5174 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped against the 5170/0/1 baseline — exactly the 4 new tests, no flake. Follow-ons filed as DW-675 (stale Invulnerable HUD tooltip), DW-676 (a death-immune host left permanently at 0 HP with no re-kill on flag expiry) and DW-677 (buildings have no status-flag channel to gate on).
decision: 2026-08-05 Invulnerable = death-immunity: also block the ceiling-collapse KillEntity path — Guard the ModifierStore EffectiveMaxHealth==0 -> KillEntity path (and any direct KillEntity) against StatusFlags.Invulnerable, leaving self-costs as spend-able, and pin with a test.

### DW-622: DropDirective applyAtTick is NOT the first idle tick when the dropped peer led the frontier — the doc contract and the UI marker both over-claim

severity: low
reason: applyAtTick is captured as EmittedThrough+1 and documented as naming "the first idle tick", justified by "the merge is stalled on the silent dropped slot until the freeze commits, so the marker cannot be overtaken". That justification only holds when the dropped peer was AT or BEHIND the merge frontier. When it was racing ahead (the DW-412 case), its real commands are already buffered for ticks well past the marker: the new DirectiveMarker_IsTheEmittedHighWater_NotTheRacersLead pins applyAtTick==3 while the peer's real orders still execute through tick 30. Not a desync — the client never hard-zeros at the marker, it only raises OnPlayerDropped for UI and echoes the value in its ACK, and the merged stream stays authoritative — so this is an observability/doc-accuracy gap ("Player2 frozen at tick 3" while Player2 acts until tick 30). Deliberately NOT fixed in the slot-faction-injective-assert bundle: a frontier-derived marker changes the DropDirective/DropAck wire contract (the survivor must ACK the exact pair it received) and moves the applyAtTick assertions in DropCoordinatorTests/DropControllerTests. ### DW-623: A research completion banks the level and keeps the spend even when EVERY living unit refuses its modifier — the player pays for an upgrade nobody receives
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/Economy/ResearchSystem.cs — CompleteResearch (the living-army application loop) vs StartResearchCommand's _resources.Spend
severity: medium
reason: Cost is spent at Start and CompletedLevels is incremented BEFORE the modifier-application loop runs, so a fully-starved army (every unit at the 8-slot EffectCaps.MaxModifiersPerEntity ceiling) leaves the faction poorer with no effect and no refund. Now VISIBLE — the DW-83 bundle's new aggregate warn names the refused count — but deliberately not corrected: choosing between refund / block-the-Start / partial-credit is a design ruling exactly like DW-85's heal ruling, and out of scope for a diagnostic-only bundle whose recorded decision explicitly chose "diagnostic on refusal" over the cap and eviction options. Closure = a human ruling on the economic semantics, then the corresponding Start-gate or refund path.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: closed by bundle decision-dw-623 (workflow burn-down, 2026-08-05). Verified live first: the defect was real and unfixed — CompleteResearch spent at Start and banked CompletedLevels before the living-army application loop, so an army where every unit sat at the 8-slot EffectCaps.MaxModifiersPerEntity ceiling paid for an upgrade nobody received. Implemented the ledger's recorded ruling ("refund the spend when zero units received the modifier"); DW-623 does not appear in .bmad-loop/decisions.json, so the ledger decision was the authority. Change (godot/src/Economy/ResearchSystem.cs only): the application loop now counts eligibleUnits alongside DW-83's refusedUnits, and when every eligible unit refused the completion is VOIDED — CompletedLevels rolls back to the pre-completion index, the four Cumulative*Delta totals restore from a snapshot taken BEFORE the accumulate (subtracting the level's delta back off is not an inverse, because SaturatingAdd clamps at the Fixed ceiling), and the level's cost is credited via _resources.Add. The faction still returns to idle so the same level can be re-started at its own cost/time; a voided completion pushes OrderDenied(InventoryFull) — the established modifier-cap denial reason, per ItemSystem's precedent — instead of the ResearchComplete cue, and DW-83's aggregate warn gets a VOIDED+refunded tail. Two guards were added beyond the literal decision text, both to stop the ruling creating a worse defect and both narrowing it: (1) eligibleUnits > 0 — an EMPTY army is not a refusal (the banked level is genuinely received by every future spawn via ApplyCompletedResearch, and a literal "refused == eligible" reading would refund 0 == 0 and make research permanently impossible for an army-less faction, also breaking FutureSpawn_ReceivesCumulativeModifier_ViaApplyCompletedResearch); (2) the cumulative modifier must carry a non-zero payload — a research with no (or net-zero) ResearchModifierDelta is a TECH GATE whose whole value is the banked level PrerequisitesMet reads, so voiding it would break tech unlocks for a starved army. Both have dedicated negative-control tests. Determinism: ResourceStore and ResearchStore are both SimChecksum (v14) inputs, but the new branch is reachable only from a fully-starved army, which no golden scenario builds (ResearchScenario runs one unit with an empty ring) — no golden moved, no re-record, no AlgoVersion/CanonicalModelHash/StartStateHash touch; the 487-test Golden|Checksum|StartStateHash|CanonicalModelHash filter passed 487/0. Pure sim C# (no using Godot;), Fixed-only (the payload test compares Fixed.Raw, never a float epsilon), ascending-id loop unchanged, no new SoA fields. Tests: 7 new in ResearchSystemTests (void+refund; re-start re-pays the SAME level's cost/time; partial-refusal control; empty-army control; tech-gate control; later-level cumulative rollback proven through a future spawn; saturated-add exact restore) + 1 new in ModifierInstallDiagnosticsTests for the voided warn text; verified red-then-green by reverting ResearchSystem.cs to the run-base version via git show (never git stash) — exactly the 5 positive tests failed, 46/51 — then restored, 51/51. DW-83's existing aggregate-warn test needed one edit (a third unit with ring room, because its two-of-two starved army is now voided rather than banked); it still asserts the same research id / level / "2 living unit(s)" and now also pins that it gets the DW-83 partial tail, not the DW-623 one. Gate: build succeeded, 0 errors; suite raw 5177 passed / 1 failed / 1 skipped where the lone failure was the documented CanonicalModelHashPerf CPU-contention timing flake (309.68 ms vs the 250 ms ceiling; passed 2/2 in isolation) = 5170 baseline + 8 new. Follow-ons filed as DW-678 (a zero-payload tech-gate research still burns a ring slot on every unit) and DW-679 (the future-spawn catch-up path still silently drops a banked, paid-for bonus with no refund available).
decision: 2026-08-05 Refund the spend when zero units received the modifier — In CompleteResearch, if the refused count equals the eligible army count (nobody received it), refund _resources.Spend and do not increment CompletedLevels.

### DW-634: A trained worker's rally point is silently overridden by auto-gather on the next tick
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/Economy/BuildingSystem.cs SpawnTrainedUnit rally branch, vs godot/src/Economy/GatheringSystem.cs TickIdle/AssignToNode
severity: low
reason: With the DW-205 residue written, a worker trained from a building that has a rally point still gets CommandState=Move + MoveTarget=rally, but GatheringSystem.TickIdle re-targets MoveTarget to the nearest eligible node on the very next tick, so the rally never takes effect for workers (combat units are unaffected). This matches how a scenario-placed worker behaves and is strictly better than the pre-fix "never gathers, auto-shoots" state, but "walk to the rally point, THEN start gathering" would need a rally-aware first leg or a new gather state. Design question rather than a defect; closure = decide whether worker rally should be honored and, if so, add the first-leg state.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: closed by bundle decision-dw-634 (workflow burn-down, 2026-08-05). Verified against current code as a LIVE defect first: BuildingSystem.SpawnTrainedUnit:360-372 still wrote CommandState=Move + MoveTarget=rally with a NOTE explicitly saying auto-gather wins, and GatheringSystem.TickIdle unconditionally called AssignToNode, overwriting MoveTarget on the next tick. Implemented to the recorded decision plus the owner's MINIMAL-shape scoping note, across 3 source files: (1) EntityWorld gains RallyMovePending — an UNFOLDED one-shot bool[] per-entity flag following the GateClosedTicks/CarryAmount posture (not folded, not persisted, not snapshot residue), with the mandatory Create() recycle-reset and a Clear() entry so the DW-19 reflection sweep stays green; (2) SpawnTrainedUnit's rally branch sets the flag AND EntityFlags.Moving; (3) GatheringSystem.TickIdle stands down while the flag is set, then clears it and runs the UNCHANGED nearest-node logic — so, standing at the rally, the worker picks the mine the player rallied to. No new gather state, no rally-to-resource targeting. Two deliberate scoping calls, both documented in code: (a) arrival uses the PURE-SIM goal test OrderQueueSystem already uses (SqrDistance to CommandGoal vs ArrivalTuning.GoalArriveRadiusSqr), never the presentation-written Moving flag, so headless and live agree, and the gate also releases when any other command state supersedes the rally Move, so an unreachable rally can never park a worker in Idle forever; (b) both new writes are WORKER-ONLY — the rally branch NEVER set EntityFlags.Moving, so no trained unit has ever physically walked to its rally in the sim, and without adding it the new gate would freeze the worker instead of gathering (strictly worse). Setting it for COMBAT units too is the wider correct fix but that path IS golden-covered (ShiftQueueScenario trains a Melee grunt from a rallied Barracks and its recorded checksums encode the grunt standing still), so it belongs in a deliberate re-baseline — filed as DW-680. Determinism: no SimChecksum input changed shape (the new array is unfolded), AlgoVersion untouched, no golden re-recorded, CanonicalModelHash/StartStateHash untouched; the only behaviour that moves is a trained WORKER's, a path no golden exercises (no golden trains a Worker-category unit; the only golden that sets a rally trains Melee). Gate: build succeeded, 0 errors; suite Passed 5178 / Failed 0 / Skipped 1 (5170 baseline + 8 new), no flake. Teeth proven: temporarily neutering the TickIdle gate turned 4 of the 7 new tests RED (WithARally_IsNotReTargeted, OnReachingTheRally_GathersFromTheNodeBesideIt, WalksTheWholeRallyLeg_ThenGathersAtTheRalliedMine, RallyPendingWorker_WhoseMoveIsSuperseded), then the gate was restored and the full suite re-ran green. Follow-ons filed as DW-680 (rallied combat units never raise EntityFlags.Moving — golden-blocked) and DW-681 (nothing in the sim layer owns the Move->Stop/Idle transition, which is why the fix needs the one-shot flag rather than reading CommandState).
decision: 2026-08-05 Honor the rally point first, then auto-gather — Add a rally-aware first-leg gather state so TickIdle/AssignToNode does not re-target a worker until it has reached its rally MoveTarget.
scoping-note (owner, 2026-08-05): implement the MINIMAL shape — do NOT build rally-to-resource targeting or a new gather state machine. It is sufficient that the idle-gather sweep stops re-targeting a worker while it still has an outstanding rally MoveTarget. On arrival the worker goes idle and the EXISTING nearest-node logic picks the node next to the rally point, which is the mine the player rallied to. The desired behaviour falls out of the current code once the sweep stops firing too early. Rationale for building at all: an explicit player order must beat automatic behaviour, and the current state means you cannot direct new workers to a specific resource at production time (rallying the town hall to a far mine or a new expansion is standard macro in WC3/SC2/AoE). Note this is sim code and may move Position/SimChecksum — if it does, it joins the golden re-baseline batch.
