### DW-636: ScoreBuildSecondBarracks is gated on the SUPPLY expansion, coupling AI production growth to a supply device
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/AI/AiOpponentSystem.cs — ScoreBuildSecondBarracks (`if (!s.HasCCExpansion) return 0f;`)
severity: medium
reason: The AI can only ever build a second Barracks after it has committed the supply-expansion CommandCenter, wiring an economic/production decision to a supply-pressure trigger. That coupling is what forced DW-63's fix to DEPRIORITIZE the ungated expansion (flat 0.25) rather than hard-skip it — a hard skip would permanently cost an ungated-scenario AI its second production building. Closure = decouple the second-Barracks gate onto ore/army demand instead of HasCCExpansion, then revisit whether ScoreExpandSupply can return 0 when gating is disabled. This is a real AI-tuning change with golden implications.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: closed by bundle decision-dw-636 (workflow burn-down, 2026-08-05), commit 9b89eeea on branch dw/decision-dw-636 atop run-base 01ea6764. Verified LIVE first: AiOpponentSystem.cs still carried `if (!s.HasCCExpansion) return 0f;` in ScoreBuildSecondBarracks, and ScoreExpandSupply still returned the DW-63 EXPAND_SUPPLY_UNGATED = 0.25f. DW-636 does NOT appear in .bmad-loop/decisions.json; the ledger decision line (mirrored verbatim in the worklist bundle intent) was the authority and was followed exactly. Changes, all in godot/src/AI/AiOpponentSystem.cs: (1) ScoreBuildSecondBarracks re-gated off HasCCExpansion onto ore/army demand — fewer than 2 LIVE Barracks, a COMPLETE first Barracks, an ore surplus past the new SECOND_BARRACKS_ORE_SURPLUS (derived as 2 x COST_BARRACKS so a cost retune moves it), and an available army below the decisive size ScoreLaunchAttack tops its ratio out at (_attackThreshold * 2); the 0.50 score value is UNCHANGED, since the decision replaces the gate, not the tuning weight. AiSnapshot loses HasSecondBarracks/HasCCExpansion and gains LiveBarracksCount + HasOreSurplusForSecondBarracks (the surplus read goes through the same Fixed CanAffordOre comparator as the existing affordability rows — no new float). (2) The "revisit" half of the decision, resolved YES: ScoreExpandSupply now returns a hard 0 when SupplyGatingEnabled is false — DW-63's own comment states it could only deprioritize rather than skip BECAUSE the expansion CC was the second-Barracks gate, and that constraint is gone; the ungated expansion's only remaining payoff is +10 to a cap nothing enforces (DW-637). (3) Collateral defect the decoupling would otherwise have widened: the old first gate read HasSecondBarracks (COMPLETE >= 2), which stays false for the whole time a second Barracks is a construction site, so the AI re-entered the action every tick and stacked duplicate Barracks on the single hardcoded POS_BARRACKS_2 tile for as long as it could afford them; the gate now counts LIVE Barracks. Determinism: NO GOLDEN MOVED AND NONE WAS RE-RECORDED — the recorded decision anticipated an AiActive re-record and it proved unnecessary. AiActiveGoldenTests.MatchesCommittedGolden_OnTheRecordingPlatform passes unmodified, because AiActiveScenario builds its first Barracks on tick 1 with a 10s construction timer and runs exactly 300 ticks = 10s, leaving HasCompleteBarracks false for the entire recording; GoldenScenario/MultiFactionScenario starve Player2 of ore so CanAffordBarracks is false; and the ungated ScoreExpandSupply branch is unreachable for every shipped scenario (none authors a `supply` block, so SupplyConfig.Resolve(null) yields enabled:true). CanonicalModelHash/StartStateHash untouched. Coverage: new godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/AI/AiSecondBarracksDemandTests.cs (7 tests) drives the real AiOpponentSystem.Tick — no reflection, no scorer stub — asserting on the buildings/orders actually committed; verified RED against the pre-fix scorer (4 fail: surplus-driven second Barracks, ungated second Barracks, the fixture-assumption pin, and the rewritten expansion-skip test), and a per-term mutation pass confirmed each of the four gate terms is load-bearing (neutering any one kills exactly one test). DW-63's UngatedSupply_StillCommitsTheExpansion_OnceNothingElseScores was rewritten to the new contract as UngatedSupply_SkipsTheExpansionEntirely (its own docstring already tied its expectation to the coupling this bundle removes), and the behaviour its 0.25 protected is re-pinned by UngatedSupply_StillReachesASecondBarracks_WithoutAnExpansion. Gate: build succeeded, 0 errors / 6 pre-existing warnings; suite 5176 passed / 1 failed / 1 skipped where the lone failure was the documented CanonicalModelHashPerf CPU-contention timing flake (278.06 ms vs the 250 ms ceiling; PASSED 2/2 in isolation) = 5170 baseline + 7 new - that 1 flake. Follow-ons filed as DW-682 (AI structure placement is five hardcoded tiles with no occupancy/pathability check, now load-bearing far more often) and DW-683 (the second Barracks at 0.50 now outranks the ArcheryRange tech step at 0.49 by a 0.01 float margin).
decision: 2026-08-05 Decouple second-Barracks gate onto ore/army demand — Replace the HasCCExpansion gate in ScoreBuildSecondBarracks with an ore/army-demand score, then revisit whether ScoreExpandSupply can return 0 when gating is disabled; re-record the AiActive golden.

### DW-637: The AI's expansion CommandCenter is neither a resource drop-off nor a production building
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/AI/AiOpponentSystem.cs — DoExpandSupplyCap; godot/src/Economy/GatheringSystem.cs:245,416
severity: low
reason: DoExpandSupplyCap creates a CommandCenter but never adds it to _productionBuildingIds, and gathering deposits route through the single per-faction ResourceStore.FactionBase rather than the nearest CC — so the expansion's only real payoffs are its +10 SupplyBonus and the second-Barracks unlock (see DW-636). A second base therefore does not behave like an expansion in any economic sense. Closure = make deposits resolve to the nearest owned drop-off and register the expansion for production; this is a design/feature change, not deferred-work repair, so it needs a scoping decision first.
status: open
decision: 2026-08-05 Leave the expansion as supply/unlock only — correct as a burn-down answer, but this entry is MIS-SCOPED and must not be closed here.
reclassify: NOT AI deferred work — this is a missing core mechanic affecting every player. The root cause is not in AiOpponentSystem: gathering deposits route through a single per-faction ResourceStore.FactionBase (GatheringSystem.cs:245,416), so the economy model assumes ONE base per faction. A HUMAN player who builds a second CommandCenter next to a far mine gets the same nothing — no local drop-off, no production. In RTS terms, expansions do not work. Severity 'low' reflects the AI framing and is wrong for the real scope.
gdd-check (2026-08-05): the GDD does NOT explicitly specify multi-base drop-off economy, so this is not a literal unimplemented requirement. BUT the GDD's AI section names `expand` as one of the core scored utility-AI actions ("build workers, expand, attack, research, defend"), which is incoherent if expanding yields only +10 supply — so expansion IS implied as a strategically real act. Treat as a design/roadmap gap requiring its own feature story (drop-off resolution to nearest owned structure, expansion registered for production, rally/control-group implications), NOT a deferred-work repair. Expect Epic 10 live play to surface this loudly on day one.

### DW-642: ResourceStore.SpendOre/SpendCrystal CREDIT resources on a negative cost - every caller other than the hardened ability path is still exposed
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/Core/ResourceStore.cs:126-131,145-150
severity: high
reason: This is the primitive behind DW-283: CanAffordOre(faction, -5) is `Ore >= -5`, trivially true, so SpendOre then subtracts a negative and ADDS 5 ore. DW-283 hardened only the ability-cast caller it named; BuildingSystem (train/build/shop), BuyItemCommand, ReviveHeroCommand and AiOpponentSystem share the same primitive and would print resources identically if any of their definitions ever carried a negative cost - and resources are SimChecksum-folded, so an authored negative cost is a money printer, not just a validation gap. The systemic fix is to reject cost < 0 inside SpendOre/SpendCrystal, mirroring ModifierStore.TryDebitEnergy which already refuses it; that is a cross-system change with its own regression surface, which is why it was left out of the ability-cast-path-hardening bundle.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: closed by workflow burn-down bundle resource-store-negative-cost (2026-08-05) - SpendOre/SpendCrystal now return false without mutating on a negative cost, mirroring ModifierStore.TryDebitEnergy, and CanAffordOre/CanAffordCrystal fail closed on a negative cost too. That second half is load-bearing, not belt-and-braces: nearly every caller is a check-then-debit pair that DISCARDS the spend's return (BuildingSystem:894-895 ReviveHeroCommand, :964-965 BuyItemCommand, :632 TrainUnit, ResearchSystem:222), so a debit-only guard would have turned the money printer into a silent FREE transaction, and inside the sparse-map Spend it would have broken check-all-then-spend-all atomicity outright. Zero cost stays affordable/spendable (only strictly negative is rejected). For every non-negative cost the path is byte-identical, so no SimChecksum-folded value moves; no golden re-recorded, all 30 goldens plus the frozen ReBaselineDifferentialGuard control green unchanged. Coverage: 12 new tests in godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Economy/ResourceStoreNegativeCostTests.cs, redness proven empirically (baseline file restored via `git checkout --`: 10 FAILED / 2 passed, the 2 being exactly the zero-cost over-reach guards), including caller-level proofs that TrainUnit minted 100 ore per enqueue, QueueWorkerBuild PAID 250 ore and BuyItemCommand paid the buyer 100 ore AND handed over the item pre-fix. One ledger claim did NOT hold: ReviveHeroCommand is protected upstream by RevivalRuleRuntime.LinearSat's Story-3.13 [0, ~32767) saturation, so no test was written around it. Gate: build 0 errors; suite 5600/0/1 = 5588 baseline + 12. The inverse exposure on AddOre/AddCrystal/Add is filed as DW-801.

### DW-643: The zero-damage predicate is spelled two different ways and they are complements only by a third system's clamp that the save-restore path bypasses
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/Combat/CombatSystem.cs:129 (`== Fixed.Zero`) vs godot/src/AI/AiOpponentSystem.cs:278,312 (`> Fixed.Zero`); clamp at godot/src/Effects/ModifierSystem.cs:90; unclamped restore at godot/src/Persistence/SaveGameState.cs:649
severity: medium
reason: CombatSystem asks `EffectiveAttackDamage == Fixed.Zero` for non-combatant and AiOpponentSystem asks `> Fixed.Zero` for conscriptable. Those partition the space only because ModifierSystem clamps EffectiveAttackDamage at Fixed.Max(Fixed.Zero, ...). Paths that write the SoA directly do not go through that clamp - notably SaveGameState's restore, which reconstructs EffectiveAttackDamage from raw ints with no re-clamp. A negative value loaded from a save would then be a COMBATANT to CombatSystem and a NON-combatant to the AI: the two systems would disagree about the same unit. The noncombatant-command-gate bundle deliberately kept both spellings (changing CombatSystem's test to `<=` alters the gate's semantics and risks moving goldens). Closure = one shared predicate, or a clamp on the restore path.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: workflow burn-down bundle effective-attack-damage-clamp (merge b62e3559) - verified STILL PRESENT against current code before fixing (SaveGameState.RestoreEntities copied EffectiveAttackDamage raw from the blob, CombatSystem spelled the non-combatant test `== Fixed.Zero`, AiOpponentSystem spelled the conscriptable test `> Fixed.Zero`), and no .bmad-loop/decisions.json entry overrode scope. BOTH closures this entry offered were implemented. (1) CLAMP - SaveGameState.cs:661 now writes `Fixed.Max(Fixed.Zero, Fixed.FromRaw(ead[i]))`. That overlay was the one writer of the field that skipped ModifierSystem.RecomputeEntity's zero-floor and nothing downstream would ever repair it: restore runs no tick, and a modifier-free entity is never recomputed. BaseAttackDamage is deliberately left raw - it is the authored source ModifierSystem re-derives Effective from, and UnitDefinitionValidator.CheckStat already bounds it to [0, 32768) at load, so flooring it would only mask a corrupt blob at a different field. (2) SHARED PREDICATE - new `CanDealDamage` / `IsNonCombatant` pair on EntityWorld beside `IsAlive`; CombatSystem and AiOpponentSystem both route through it, so the partition is structural rather than resting on a third system's clamp. Behaviour is unchanged for every non-negative value, which is all of them (the validator bars negative authored damage and every writer now floors at zero). Determinism: NO golden re-recorded, no SimChecksum fold, no AlgoVersion / CanonicalModelHash / StartStateHash change - the clamp is a provable no-op on a well-formed save (pinned by a test asserting the whole EffectiveAttackDamage lane round-trips bit-exact) and `<=` agrees with `==` everywhere the old spelling was reachable. Coverage: godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Combat/EffectiveAttackDamageClampTests.cs, 10 Godot-free Fixed-only tests; two VERIFIED RED against pre-fix behaviour by temporarily reverting each half (Restore_ClampsANegativeEffectiveAttackDamageToZero failed with raw -327680 surviving the restore; NegativeDamageUnit_IsANonCombatantToCombat_AndNeverAcquires failed with the negative-damage unit acquiring target id 1 instead of staying at -1), both reverts undone and the tree re-verified clean before commit. Gate: build 0 errors (6 pre-existing warnings in untouched UI/Multiplayer files); 5264 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped (baseline 5254 + 10), no flake. Two out-of-scope siblings re-filed: DW-692 (the three unclamped effective stats) and DW-693 (SelectionSystem's third spelling).

### DW-644: The AI can pin itself on a raze it is structurally unable to execute - ScoreRazeBuildings counts units DoRazeBuildings then skips for attack domain
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/AI/AiOpponentSystem.cs - ScoreRazeBuildings (~:390) vs DoRazeBuildings (~:515)
severity: medium
reason: Same stall family as DW-202 but the attack-domain half rather than the zero-damage half, and NOT closed by the noncombatant-command-gate bundle's shared IsConscriptable predicate. ScoreRazeBuildings only asks how MANY units are available; DoRazeBuildings then skips every unit whose AttackDomainOf lacks Structure. An AI whose free units are all air-only or anti-unit-only scores RazeBuildings 0.90 every tick and issues zero orders - an indefinite no-op that also starves BuildBarracks (0.85), BuildArcheryRange, BuildSiegeWorkshop and BuildSecondBarracks, all of which score below 0.90, so the AI stops producing entirely. Closure = give the scorer the same Structure-domain term the dispatcher applies, or a fallback when the raze set is empty. Out of that bundle's scope because it changes WHICH action the AI picks - a behaviour change deserving its own golden audit.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: 2026-08-05 resolved by the ai-opponent-scoring bundle (workflow burn-down run). Verified as a LIVE defect against current code first, and no decisions.json entry exists for DW-644 so the worklist intent governed scope. FIX (godot/src/AI/AiOpponentSystem.cs): added AiSnapshot.AvailableRazeCapableUnits, counted inside BuildSnapshot's existing ascending-id scan; extracted a single shared predicate CanRazeStructures(world, i) that BOTH the new count and DoRazeBuildings' dispatch filter now go through, so the strength the scorer measures is the strength the wave actually fields; and pointed BOTH of ScoreRazeBuildings' commit bars (the full-wave >= _attackThreshold bar and the Story 2.13 below-threshold stall-breaker's > 0 test) at the new count. ScoreLaunchAttack and ScoreBuildSecondBarracks deliberately keep reading the raw AvailableCombatUnits - an AttackMove wave conscripts every free unit regardless of domain, so those are correct as-is. DETERMINISM (the golden audit this entry asked for): no golden, CanonicalModelHash or StartStateHash moved, and none was re-recorded. AttackDomain is an authored, UNFOLDED field; no faction/scenario JSON in godot/resources/ authors attack_domains, so UnitDefinition.ParsedAttackDomains and EntityWorld.Create both yield AttackDomain.All and AvailableRazeCapableUnits is identically equal to AvailableCombatUnits everywhere a checksum is recorded. The remaining 4 rows are labelled in-file as controls / over-correction guards. status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: workflow burn-down bundle combat-command-switch-completeness (2026-08-05) - verified still-live against the run base before fixing: CombatSystem.Tick's command switch ended in `default: // Idle ...` -> TickIdleCombat, and nothing at compile time or test time asserted that every UnitCommand value which PERSISTS as a CommandState had an explicit arm. DW-206's instance (Build) was closed; the class was not. Not in .bmad-loop/decisions.json, so no recorded human decision overrode scope. Closed exactly as the bundle intent prescribed, with a red-test enumerating the persisting subset. (1) `UnitCommandTraits.PersistsAsCommandState` - new static class in godot/src/Core/EntityWorld.cs, placed immediately after `UnitOrderFlags` and the `UnitCommand` enum it describes (the existing precedent for a helper beside that enum, and the spot a dev appending a member is already looking). It makes the per-member doc prose executable, is total over the 24 members, and throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException on an unclassified value. Classification-only: no sim state, never called per tick, not a SimChecksum input. (2) godot/src/Combat/CombatSystem.cs - DW-645 BEGIN/END guard anchors around both command switches; an explicit `case UnitCommand.Idle:` arm (Idle was spelled `default:`, the very spelling that hid Build); and an explicit no-op case group (Idle/Move/Stop/HoldPosition/Build/PickupItem) in TickNonCombatant, whose switch has no `default:` at all so an un-cased command there is silently inert - the DW-242 half of the same class. `default:` is deliberately KEPT rather than made a throw: SaveGameState restores CommandState with a raw int cast, and resting a unit on a corrupt byte beats crashing the tick; the guard makes an un-cased PERSISTING command a loud test failure instead. (3) New godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Combat/CombatCommandSwitchCompletenessTests.cs (15 rows, Godot-free, Fixed-only, ascending-id), four layers: (a) every enum member is classified; (b) the persisting set {Idle, Move, AttackMove, Stop, HoldPosition, Build, AttackTarget, Patrol, Follow, AttackBuilding, PickupItem} is pinned, plus the complement from the other side; (c) the declaration is checked against OBSERVED behaviour - every command driven through a real OrderApplier.Apply on a live owned entity with all system handles null and left stored in CommandState must be declared persisting; this is the layer that needs no human action, since a new wire command that quietly persists goes red by itself; (d) every persisting command owns an explicit case label in BOTH switches, read from the shipping source between the anchors (the PositionWriterGuardTests source-scan recipe: [CallerFilePath] root, comments/literals stripped). Plus a dead-arm check (no arm for a command that cannot persist), an anchor-presence check, and a behavioural theory + positive control. NON-VACUITY proven three ways, not assumed: (i) the arm extractor run against a doctored copy of the LIVE switch with the Build arm removed reports exactly `Build` - the pre-DW-206 state, reconstructed from real source so the fixture cannot rot; (ii) temporarily deleting the PickupItem arm from the shipping file turned the structural guard red naming PickupItem AND turned the behavioural theory red (the unit inherited Idle's global chase and its MoveTarget was overwritten), then restored; (iii) temporarily appending an unclassified `ProbeNewCommand = 24` turned 7 of the 15 rows red, led by the layer-1 message naming it, then restored. DETERMINISM: no behavioural change whatsoever - Idle already reached TickIdleCombat through `default:` and still does through its own arm, `default:` is unchanged, and the added non-combatant cases replace a fall-through with an explicit `break`. No SimChecksum fold, no golden re-recorded, no CanonicalModelHash/StartStateHash touched; all golden and determinism tests pass, including the frozen ReBaselineDifferentialGuard control. GATE (run in the bundle worktree with relative paths): `dotnet build godot/godot.csproj` succeeded (0 errors, 6 pre-existing warnings); `dotnet test godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests.csproj` = 5892 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped in 1m52s against a 5877/0/1 baseline, so the delta is exactly the 15 new rows - no flake exception needed, CanonicalModelHashPerfTests passed in the full run. Follow-ons filed as DW-818 (OrderQueueSystem.CurrentOrderComplete is a third `default:`-swallowing CommandState switch), DW-819 (OrderApplier.ApplyActiveOrder blind-stores CommandState before its switch, so a wire-issued Build soft-locks a unit) and DW-820 (the UnitOrderFlags doc comment still says the enum uses values 0-13).

### DW-646: Slope derivation still under-reports slope at the outermost map edge - a clamped neighbour is nearer than the nominal run
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/Navigation/PathabilityGrid.cs - DeriveSlopeBlockedInto
severity: low
reason: After DW-149 the derivation takes the max rise over all four neighbours, but at the extreme edge cells one sampled neighbour can clamp to an elevation cell NEARER than the nominal 2-unit run, so the rise is divided by a run longer than the real one and the slope reads lower than it is. This is the CONSERVATIVE direction - it never fabricates a blocked cell, it can only miss one - and fixing it needs an ElevationGrid API that reports the clamped sample's true distance, i.e. new surface area beyond the swept-cell/4-neighbour intent of that bundle. Documented in the method's doc comment in the meantime.

### DW-650: The DW-488 authoring bound is enforced only on the ABILITY path - the three non-ability Modifier minters still bypass it
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/Combat/ItemSystem.cs:339 (ApplyItemStatModifier) + godot/src/Combat/HeroXpSystem.cs:338 (level-growth modifier) + godot/src/Economy/ResearchSystem.cs:368 (BuildCumulativeModifier)
severity: medium
reason: DW-488's closure put the MaxStacks x delta magnitude cap in AbilityValidator, which is where its recorded closure named it, but those three sites build Modifiers directly and never reach AbilityValidator - so an authored ItemDefinition stat bonus (or a pathological research/hero-growth curve) can still contribute an unbounded delta into the same 8-slot accumulator DW-488 set out to make un-wrappable. The rule is deliberately public and self-contained as Modifier.CheckAuthoringBounds() so ItemDefinitionValidator and the research/hero paths can adopt it verbatim in one line each. Not done in the bundle because ItemDefinitionValidator.cs was being edited by the parallel unit-def-validator-strict-bounds bundle (guaranteed merge conflict) and the other two are outside that bundle's intent.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: workflow burn-down bundle modifier-authoring-bounds - DW-488's |delta| x MaxStacks accumulator bound is now enforced at all three non-ability minters, each at its own path's gate rather than at the minter. ITEM (ItemDefinitionValidator.cs): a new private CarriedModifier(def) rebuilds the exact descriptor ItemSystem.ApplyItemStatModifier mints (permanent, StackRule.Ignore, 1 stack, the four authored deltas) and runs Modifier.CheckAuthoringBounds on BOTH the sim Validate and the editor ValidateFields; honest scope note - on today's constants this is a PASS-THROUGH (MAX_ITEM_STAT_DELTA 1000 and MAX_MOVE_SPEED_DELTA 50 already sit under MaxStatDeltaTotalRaw ~4096 stat units), so the item gap was latent, not open, and it is adopted anyway because that ordering is a coincidence of two independently-owned public knobs, now pinned by a test that goes red if a cap is raised past the bound. Placed AFTER the tighter per-stat caps so existing error messages and the D-9 one-badge-per-field contract stay byte-identical. HERO (UnitDefinitionValidator.cs): the genuinely open one - new CheckHeroGrowth + HeroGrowthStacks run the exact growth descriptor HeroXpSystem.ReconcileGrowth mints (StackRule.Stack) over hero.health/damage/armor_per_level; before this, health_per_level 200 on a max_level 100 hero was fully valid under the coarse HeroStatGrowthMax = 256 and contributed 99 x 200 = 19800 stat units (~1.66e9 raw) from a single modifier id, so a couple of ordinary neighbours in the same 8-slot accumulator wrap it negative and, since DW-325/DW-491, can collapse the hero's own ceiling to 0 and kill it. Bounded against the hero's OWN max_level-1 worst case rather than the descriptor's MaxStacks (99), so a low-max-level hero keeps its existing headroom - no false positives and no existing test's numbers moved. RESEARCH (ResearchSystem.cs): the only site with no authorable magnitude - the cumulative is a runtime running sum SaturatingAdd accumulates across a repeatable ladder, so the bound is applied where the modifier is built (new BoundedDelta on all four deltas of BuildCumulativeModifier). Deliberately NOT applied to the banked total: SaturatingAdd's full-Fixed-range semantics are persisted, folded into SimChecksum and load-bearing for DW-623's void/rollback snapshot, so clamping the stored value would move unrelated behaviour (pinned by a new test; the two existing ResearchSystemTests asserting Fixed.MaxValue pass unmodified). Determinism: no golden, CanonicalModelHash or StartStateHash moved and no AlgoVersion bump was needed - the only checksum-adjacent change is the research contribution clamp, which engages solely above ~4096 accumulated stat units, and no shipped content authors a research modifier delta at all (zero modifier_delta keys in godot/resources/data), so nothing reachable changed value. Coverage: godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Effects/ModifierMinterBoundsTests.cs, 12 tests, new file (kept out of the shared ResearchSystemTests/UnitDefinitionValidatorTests files to avoid parallel-bundle merge conflicts); 6 of the 12 were verified RED by temporarily reverting each fix, the other 6 are guards/non-vacuity controls that must stay green either way. The headline test drives DW-488's exact defect end to end through the research path: 8 saturated researches (one per ring slot) sum 8 x int.MaxValue in the wrapping `_flatArmorBonus +=` to -8 raw and the Zero-floor collapses EffectiveArmor to 0, so the unit ends up with LESS armor after eight paid-for upgrades; bounded, the same eight sum to exactly MaxModifiersPerEntity x MaxStatDeltaTotalRaw <= int.MaxValue. Gate: dotnet build godot/godot.csproj = 0 errors (6 pre-existing warnings, all in untouched Godot/UI files); dotnet test godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests = 5458 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped, run twice, against a 5446/0/1 baseline (+12 = exactly the new file). No CanonicalModelHashPerf flake. Follow-ups filed as DW-750 (HeroStatGrowthMax's stated derivation is now stale), DW-751 (clamped research cumulative is silently unreachable with no diagnostic) and DW-752 (ItemRegistry's in-memory ctor trusts its input).

### DW-654: The DSL `victory` leaf latches no verdict: the declared WINNER's own score screen reads DEFEAT with zero rows, and the leaf is a total no-op headless

severity: high
reason: The victory leaf only fires the OnVictory presentation delegate; it writes no WinStateStore.Verdict. So on a DSL-authored victory: (a) GameOverSummary.Build emits a row per faction WITH A LATCHED VERDICT, so the score screen is empty; (b) GameOverPresentation.BuildHeadline keys LocalWin off Verdict[local] == VERDICT_WON, so the player the author just declared the winner is shown the DEFEAT headline alongside a 'Player N Wins!' sub-line (the DW-448 contradiction class at a different surface); (c) OnVictory is bound only by ScenarioDelegateBinder in the Godot scene, so on the dedicated server / headless the leaf does literally nothing and the match never resolves. Latching VERDICT_WON there fixes all three and is the natural completion of the DW-189/DW-383 fix - but it makes ScenarioDelegateBinder's OnVictory->ShowGameOver AND MainScene._Process's DecideOutcome->ShowGameOver both fire in the same frame (see DW-655), and the guard can only live in MainScene / the binder, in-engine-gated presentation files outside the Godot-free burn-down track. Left unshipped rather than shipped unobserved.

### DW-658: BuildingStore.Destroy leaves the razed producer's ProductionQueue slots and ProductionTimer populated - no refund, and phantom orders stay in the checksum fold
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/Core/BuildingStore.cs:355-362 (Destroy) vs godot/src/Core/SimChecksum.cs:406-431 (the fold runs 0..Count with no Alive filter)
severity: medium
reason: Destroy only flips Alive[id] and pushes the free-list entry; the depth-5 queue and head timer are zeroed solely on the next Create of that slot. Two consequences. (1) A producer razed mid-training silently forfeits every paid-for queued order with no refund - WC3 refunds them, and the codebase already has the exact re-resolve-from-def refund machinery in CancelTrainCommand. (2) The dead slot's stale queue bytes and timer stay in the SimChecksum fold until the slot is recycled; deterministic on every peer (Destroy is deterministic and Create zeroes on recycle) so it is not a desync, but the folded state carries phantom orders. Out of the production-queue-correctness bundle's scope: it is a destroy-path refund POLICY decision, not one of the three queue-correctness defects that bundle named, and adding a refund on destroy would move ResourceStore.Ore (a folded value) on a path goldens can reach - it needs its own isolated story. ### DW-659: A live re-ApplyUnitDefinition silently wipes Effective* for every entity WITHOUT a self-passive
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/Core/EntityWorld.cs:1022-1034 (the Base*->Effective* re-mirror) + godot/src/Effects/ModifierSystem.cs:60-72 (Tick recomputes only DIRTIED entities)
severity: medium
reason: Same future trap as DW-300 but a different defect, and outside the passive-install-idempotence bundle's two named files. ApplyUnitDefinition re-mirrors BaseAttackDamage/BaseArmor into EffectiveAttackDamage/EffectiveArmor, discarding every installed modifier's contribution; ModifierSystem.Tick only recomputes entities something DIRTIED, so for a unit carrying a research/item/aura modifier and NO self-passive the bonus vanishes until an unrelated apply/remove happens to re-dirty it. DW-300 fixed only the guarded self-passive path (the new ModifierStore.RecomputeEffectiveStats, called from InstallSelfPassive) - provably zero blast radius. The general fix is one more line in SimulationHost.cs:252-259: wire Modifiers.RecomputeEffectiveStats as a third OnUnitDefinitionApplied subscriber. Deliberately NOT done in that bundle: it would run on every def-based spawn and a spawn path that sets Effective* before the mapper could not be ruled out, i.e. a possible golden move that needs its own story.
status: done 2026-08-06
resolution: closed by workflow burn-down bundle `modifier-effective-stat-remirror` (Phase C integration, branch rebaseline/phase-c) - verified live against current code, then fixed exactly as this entry's reason line prescribes. EntityWorld.ApplyUnitDefinition still re-mirrored BaseAttackDamage/BaseArmor into EffectiveAttackDamage/EffectiveArmor while ModifierSystem.Tick recomputes only DIRTIED entities, and the only two OnUnitDefinitionApplied subscribers (InstallSelfPassive, ApplyCompletedResearch) both no-op for exactly the affected population. FIX: SimulationHost now wires `World.OnUnitDefinitionApplied += id => Modifiers.RecomputeEffectiveStats(id);` as a THIRD subscriber, after both installers, so the seam always ends at Effective = max(0, Base + sum of bonuses), plus a doc paragraph on EntityWorld.OnUnitDefinitionApplied recording that the repair must stay LAST. No recorded human decision constrained scope (not in .bmad-loop/decisions.json, no `decision:` line). GOLDENS MOVED: ZERO, and that is the correct outcome rather than a missed re-record - this entry's `goldens: moves` prediction did not hold. The recompute is a strict no-op on every path any golden exercises: a fresh or recycled slot's ModifierSystem accumulators are zero (ClearEntity wipes them on destroy) so Effective = Base + 0, byte-identical to the mirror the mapper just wrote, and identical for EffectiveMaxHealth/EffectiveMoveSpeed which Create sets to Base; where an installer does apply a modifier it already eager-recomputes, so the third subscriber is idempotent. The re-baseline differential guard's control, FormationSeparationScenario, builds every unit with bare EntityWorld.Create and never calls ApplyUnitDefinition, so the new subscriber cannot reach it - checked specifically because this bundle was flagged as the one that could perturb it. Both ReBaselineDifferentialGuardTests assertions, FrozenControl_OwnBytes_ArePinned and SimChecksumCoverageGuardTest.KnownWorldState_ProducesPinnedV23Hash all pass; no *.golden.txt, no SimChecksum.AlgoVersion and no AlgoVersion pin touched (verified by `git diff --name-only 5b6021f5..HEAD | grep -iE "golden|AlgoVersion"` returning nothing). COVERAGE (godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Effects/ModifierRemirrorOnReApplyTests.cs, Godot-free, drives the real SimulationHost wiring): LiveReApply_KeepsAnExternalModifiersEffectiveStats_OnAUnitWithNoSelfPassive confirmed RED pre-fix and GREEN after; GenuineSpawn_WithNoModifiers_IsUnperturbedByTheSeamRecompute pins the no-perturbation property directly; SeamRecompute_RunsAfterTheInstallers_SoASelfPassiveSpawnStillLandsExactlyOneStack is ordering teeth. ### DW-660: ResearchSystem.ApplyCompletedResearch is state-idempotent but NOT heal-idempotent on a re-fired seam

severity: medium
reason: The OTHER OnUnitDefinitionApplied subscriber named in DW-300's reason line. Its stat state IS idempotent (RemoveByModifierId then Apply per research id), so DW-300 left it alone. ### DW-664: TickNonCombatant DESTROYS the attack order of a unit whose damage is only TEMPORARILY debuffed to zero
origin: post-merge review of the workflow burn-down, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/Combat/CombatSystem.cs:253-262 (TickNonCombatant's AttackTarget/AttackBuilding arm), entered from the :155 gate
severity: medium
reason: DW-242 replaced the blanket `if (world.EffectiveAttackDamage[i] == Fixed.Zero) continue;` skip with a route into TickNonCombatant, whose AttackTarget/AttackBuilding arm writes CommandState=Idle, CommandTarget=-1, AttackTarget=-1 and clears Moving|Attacking. Its comment assumes the condition is a permanent authoring property, but the gate reads the EFFECTIVE stat, which ModifierSystem.RecomputeEntity zero-FLOORS (`Fixed.Max(Fixed.Zero, Fixed.AddSaturating(BaseAttackDamage, _flatAttackDamageBonus))`, ModifierSystem.cs:90) - so any modifier with attack_damage_delta <= -BaseAttackDamage lands a live combatant in that arm. Such content is authorable: Modifier.CheckDelta takes |delta| (Modifier.cs:161) so negative deltas validate, and DW-488 bounds only |delta| x max_stacks. Trigger: force-attack an enemy, then take a temporary attack-damage debuff of at least your base damage; next CombatSystem tick the order is wiped, and on expiry the unit stands Idle instead of resuming - TickIdleCombat re-acquires the NEAREST enemy, not the one the player picked. Pre-DW-242 the bare `continue` mutated nothing, so the order survived the debuff window intact. This also contradicts the disposition the status-flags bundle landed in the same merge range: DW-266 models "cannot attack" as StatusFlags.Disarmed, which CombatSystem.cs:29-31 documents as "still acquires and chases but can never land a hit" (order preserved), and MovementSystem.cs:71-73 states the general rule that a debuff must PAUSE a queued order, not CANCEL it. Two bundles disagree about one situation and the zero-damage path wins because it is tested first. Fix direction: gate the Idle normalization on a PERMANENT non-combatant (BaseAttackDamage == Fixed.Zero) rather than the effective value, so a debuffed combatant keeps its order and resumes on expiry. Not fixed here: it moves live combat behaviour and needs its own golden/checksum judgement, which is a bundle, not a review edit.
status: done 2026-08-06
resolution: workflow burn-down bundle combat-order-preservation (2026-08-06, Phase C batch) - verified UNFIXED against the run base first, then fixed in the intent's direction: a new `EntityWorld.IsPermanentNonCombatant(id)` (`BaseAttackDamage[id] <= Fixed.Zero`, bounds-guarded, out-of-range answers true) sits beside the DW-643 `CanDealDamage`/`IsNonCombatant` pair, and CombatSystem.TickNonCombatant's order-destroying arm now asks IT instead of the effective stat. A permanent non-combatant still normalizes to Idle exactly as DW-242 built it; a combatant whose damage is only TEMPORARILY debuffed to the zero-floor is PAUSED - AttackTarget and the Attacking flag drop (the DW-266 stun-gate disposition; dropping the transient acquisition slot avoids holding a stale id across a window nothing re-validates, DW-184's ABA trap) while CommandState / CommandTarget / MoveTarget / Moving are left untouched, so the same player-picked target resumes on expiry instead of TickIdleCombat re-acquiring the nearest enemy. The :160 entry gate was deliberately NOT changed (routing a zero-damage unit into the full engagement path would spawn zero-damage projectiles, run the on-hit rider and break DW-643's AiOpponentSystem complement); ModifierSystem's zero-floor is behaviourally untouched and only gained a doc note that the floor is a clamp, not a classification. COVERAGE: 13 new tests in godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Combat/DebuffedCombatantOrderPreservationTests.cs - order/flag/chase preservation on both arms, resume-on-expiry proving the FORCED target takes the blow while a NEARER enemy does not, a positive control proving a cancelled order really does hit the wrong victim, the DW-242 permanent-non-combatant fences, an "Idle debuffed combatant still never acquires" fence, predicate bounds/negative-base edges, and an end-to-end pass driving a real expiring authorable ModifierStore debuff through the real ModifierSystem->CombatSystem tick order; reverting ONLY CombatSystem.cs to the run base failed 7 of the 13, the 6 survivors being precisely the fences, the control and the predicate tests. DETERMINISM: fold set UNCHANGED (no field added, removed or reordered), AlgoVersion stays 23, no golden payload re-recorded or edited, ZERO goldens moved - explained, not assumed: the new branch is reachable only with BaseAttackDamage > 0 AND EffectiveAttackDamage == 0, a separation only a live modifier can create, and no recorded scenario carries a damage-nulling debuff; all 466 golden/checksum/hash tests passed including SimChecksumCoverageGuardTest, ReBaselineDifferentialGuardTests (frozen control untouched) and the CanonicalModelHash / StartStateHash pins. The `goldens: moves` prediction below is therefore empirically wrong for this entry - filed as DW-858 rather than rewritten here. GATE (in the phase-c worktree): `dotnet build godot/godot.csproj` 0 errors / 6 pre-existing warnings, none in a touched file; `dotnet test --logger trx` = 6063 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped (6050 baseline + 13 new), no CanonicalModelHashPerf flake, build + suite re-run after commit and reproduced. New findings filed as DW-858 and DW-859.

### DW-665: DW-240's fail-closed spawn_unit gate rejects the WHOLE map on a cross-faction skirmish launch
origin: post-merge review of the workflow burn-down, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/Core/Definitions/ScenarioValidator.cs:840 (flat trigger channel) and :941-944 (graph channel); the un-remapped source is godot/src/Core/Skirmish/SkirmishSetupToScenario.cs:359
severity: medium
reason: SkirmishSetupToScenario remaps PRE-PLACED unit ids across factions (SkirmishRosterMap.MapUnitId at :143 - alpha's "worker" becomes beta's "forgehand") but copies trigger action unit ids VERBATIM (`UnitId = a.UnitId` at :359), and on the identity-remap path (SkirmishSetupToScenario.cs:161-165) the base triggers are not rewritten at all. DW-240 now hard-fails validation on an unresolvable spawn_unit unit_id. So an authored map whose slot 0 is alpha and which carries a trigger action {"type":"spawn_unit","unit_id":"worker","faction":0}, launched as a skirmish with beta picked for slot 0, resolves IsKnownUnitId("worker", betaDef) = false; ScenarioLoadPhase.cs:65-66 has already written beta into SlotFactionDefs, so Validate fails and :74-76 discards the ENTIRE scenario and boots the flat fallback map. Pre-DW-240 the map loaded and only that one trigger's spawn was skipped with a runtime log warning - a whole-map reject is a much larger blast radius than the defect DW-240 closed. Latent on shipped content today (no scenario JSON under godot/resources/data uses a spawn_unit trigger action), so this is an authoring hazard the first such map will hit, not a live break. Fix direction: remap the trigger spawn_unit unit_id through SkirmishRosterMap in ReconcileTriggers AND on the identity path (the root cause - the ids are simply wrong for the chosen faction, validator or not); only if that proves impossible should this arm be demoted to a warning.
status: done 2026-08-05
resolution: workflow burn-down bundle skirmish-scenario-remap (2026-08-05) - verified UNFIXED against the run-base code first (`SkirmishSetupToScenario.ReconcileTriggers` still carried `UnitId = a.UnitId` verbatim, and the identity-slot path (`if (!identityRemap)`) never rewrote the base triggers at all); DW-665 is absent from .bmad-loop/decisions.json, so no recorded human decision applied and the bundle intent governed scope. FIX: a trigger's `spawn_unit` unit_id is as faction-specific as a pre-placed unit's, so it now goes through the same `SkirmishRosterMap.MapUnitId` role remap (Category, ordinal-within-category) the pre-placed loop uses - `ReconcileTriggers` (the DW-458 renumbering path) translates a kept spawn_unit's id, reading it in the AUTHORED slot's frame BEFORE the faction rewrite; a new `RemapTriggerSpawnUnitIds` covers the identity-slot path (an identity SLOT remap but not an identity FACTION remap); and `ReconcileTriggerGraphJson` gets the same translation plus a `redirectSlots` flag so the identity path reuses it for the unit-id half only (the graph channel hits the identical DW-240 gate at ScenarioValidator:941-944). Unmappable role (a selectable faction fielding no unit of that category): the flat channel STRIPS the action and drops an emptied trigger, mirroring the pre-placed-unit drop and the DW-458 action-strip - i.e. the pre-DW-240 blast radius - while the graph channel leaves it verbatim for the validator, because DW-609's rule forbids removing a node. Gated by a new `AnyFactionSwap`, so a same-faction launch skips the remap entirely and stays reference-identical and parse-free, preserving the DW-458 byte-identity contract (test-pinned). `CloneAction` is now the ONE field-complete TriggerAction copy both rewrite passes share, so a newly added TriggerAction field cannot be dropped by one of them. DETERMINISM: nothing folded into SimChecksum, CanonicalModelHash or StartStateHash changed - this transform runs pre-load on the skirmish launch path and only alters the model on a CROSS-FACTION launch; no golden moved and none was re-recorded. COVERAGE: 17 new tests in godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Skirmish/SkirmishTriggerUnitIdRemapTests.cs covering both channels on both paths, role-not-position translation, renumbered-survivor keying, field-completeness of the clone, unmappable strip/drop/verbatim and the byte-identity guards, plus an end-to-end pass over the REAL shipped alpha_map_01 + beta faction proving the built scenario clears the boot validator and a CONTROL test forcing the id back to "worker" proving DW-240's gate still rejects the whole scenario, so the green assertion is load-bearing; reverting the source to HEAD (via `git checkout HEAD -- <file>`, no stash) failed 12 of 17, the 5 survivors being precisely the invariant/control tests. GATE: `dotnet build godot/godot.csproj` succeeded, 0 errors / 6 warnings all pre-existing and none in the touched files; suite raw 5270 passed / 1 failed / 1 skipped (5272 total = 5254 baseline + 17 new + 1 skipped), the lone failure being CanonicalModelHashPerfTests.MaxCapsScenario_ColdCompute_StaysUnderTheRegressionCeiling at 290.16 ms vs a 250 ms ceiling - the documented CPU-contention timing flake, Passed 2/2 when re-run in isolation - so the suite counts as GREEN (5271 passing / 0 real failures / 1 skipped). Follow-ons filed as DW-711 and DW-712; the new test file's missing `.cs.uid` companion is recorded as a seen-again on DW-576.

### DW-666: G is still double-bound after the hotkey-restore pass - grid snap AND the Item Card Editor both fire on one press
origin: post-merge review of the workflow burn-down, 2026-08-04
location: godot/src/UI/EntityPlacer.cs:537-541 (the `case Key.G:` with no SetInputAsHandled) vs godot/src/Core/MainScene.cs:1249-1254; the stale advertisement is MainScene.cs:2032/2037
severity: medium
reason: EntityPlacer._Input's `case Key.G:` toggles grid snap and falls out of the switch WITHOUT calling GetViewport().SetInputAsHandled() - unlike every other branch in that method (Escape :462, Ctrl+Z :483, Delete :499). The event therefore continues to MainScene._UnhandledInput, whose `else if (key.Keycode == Key.G)` calls _ctx.ItemCardPanel.Toggle(). Both handlers are Edit-mode gated, so ONE press of G flips grid snap and simultaneously opens/closes the Item Card Editor. Commit 50f643c was specifically the double-bound-hotkey repair (it rebound K->Ctrl+K and N->Ctrl+N after a58efb4 fixed R) but it missed this pair and then rewrote the hotkey strip to advertise BOTH claimants two lines apart - `G=Snap({snap})` at MainScene.cs:2032 and `G=Item` at MainScene.cs:2037 - so the collision now reads as intended. The same strip line also still advertises `N=Lobby`, which no longer exists: Story 9.7 removed the plain-N lobby bind (see the comment at MainScene.cs:1208-1210) and WaterTool.cs owns plain N, so pressing N toggles the water tool. Every letter A-Z is already claimed in Edit mode, so the fix needs the same modifier treatment 50f643c used (e.g. Ctrl+G for the Item editor, leaving plain G to snap) plus a strip correction - a UI bundle with an in-engine gate, not a review edit.
status: done 2026-08-04
resolution: closed by the Ctrl-tier keymap policy (7b7713e), NOT by the fix this entry proposes -- and that distinction matters. The entry recommends adding the missing GetViewport().SetInputAsHandled() to EntityPlacer's `case Key.G:`, which would be actively HARMFUL: G is a deliberate BROADCAST key that RegionTool and WaterTool also observe for their own grid-snap (see WaterTool's own status print, 'G grid-snap'), so consuming it in the placer would silently break grid snap in both tools -- trading a double-fire for two dead toggles. The real defect was only that MainScene ALSO opened the Item Card editor on bare G; with every editor moved to Ctrl+<letter> no editor sits on a bare letter at all, so the second consumer is gone by construction and the broadcast stays intact. Verified in-engine from a clean boot: one bare G takes Snap(OFF) -> Snap(ON) with neither the Item nor the DSL Graph editor opening.

### DW-667: Opening the Item Card editor in-engine REWRITES the shipped item JSON — reformats it, reorders keys, drops a zero-valued field and strips the trailing newline
origin: live in-engine sweep, 2026-08-04
location: godot/resources/data/items/potion_of_healing.json (observed), godot/src/CreationSuite/ItemCardPanel*.cs (writer)
severity: medium
reason: Driving the Item Card editor during the 2026-08-04 sweep left `potion_of_healing.json` modified in the working tree with NO explicit Save pressed by the operator. The rewrite is not benign reformatting: `"cost_crystal": 0` is DELETED (consistent with a serializer using WhenWritingDefault), the key order changes (`effect` moves ahead of `cost_ore`), the compact one-line `effect` object is expanded, and the trailing newline is removed. Losing an explicitly-authored zero is a real semantic change for a field a creator may have set deliberately, and the reformat makes every future diff of shipped content noisy. It was caught only because `git status` was checked before committing — an AutoSave or an `git add -A` would have committed corrupted shipped content silently, which is the same class as the Epic-6 AutoSave incident that produced a red baseline for a whole epic. Closure: (a) find why merely opening/binding the panel triggers a write at all (a Save-on-bind or Revalidate-then-persist path); (b) make the writer preserve absent-vs-zero and key order, or make it a targeted JsonNode patch like the FactionWriter precedent (see DW-64's whole-object-replace finding) rather than a full re-serialize; (c) add a Tier-1 round-trip test asserting a shipped item file is byte-identical after a load->save with no edits.
status: open

### DW-678: A zero-payload tech-gate research still installs an EMPTY modifier into every unit's ring, burning 1 of the 8 slots for nothing
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/Economy/ResearchSystem.cs — CompleteResearch's application loop / BuildCumulativeModifier / ApplyCompletedResearch
severity: medium
reason: Surfaced while writing DW-623's payload guard. A pure tech-gate research (the harness's 'gated' entry, and any authored research whose levels omit modifier_delta, or whose deltas net to zero) builds an all-zero Modifier and consumes a ring slot on every living unit AND every future spawn — so it actively worsens the very EffectCaps.MaxModifiersPerEntity starvation DW-83/DW-623/DW-625 are about, for zero effect. NOT fixed in the DW-623 bundle: skipping the install would change ModifierStore contents for already-shipped content, and ModifierStore state feeds entity effective stats, so it is a checksum/golden-moving change that needs its own isolated re-baseline decision. Closure = rule on skipping the empty install, then take the re-baseline deliberately.
status: done 2026-08-06
resolution: workflow burn-down bundle research-empty-modifier-skip (2026-08-06, Phase C batch) - verified still live at run base 5b6021f5, then fixed. ResearchSystem.ApplyCumulativeModifier unconditionally did RemoveByModifierId then Apply(BuildCumulativeModifier(...)), so a pure tech-gate research (levels with no modifier_delta) or a ladder netting to zero installed an all-zero permanent Modifier into every living faction unit's ring AND every future spawn via ApplyCompletedResearch, burning 1 of the 8 EffectCaps.MaxModifiersPerEntity slots for nothing. FIX: build the descriptor first, keep RemoveByModifierId unconditional and ABOVE the guard (a net-to-zero ladder has a live non-zero instance from the earlier level that must come off - skipping the remove too would strand it forever), and call Apply only when the built descriptor carries something. The predicate is `Modifier.HasNoEffect()` - four stat deltas raw-zero, Status None, PeriodEffect null - and it is a METHOD, not a property: the first draft used a property and EffectFoldCompletenessTests.EveryModifierField_IsConsciouslyClassified correctly rejected it, because that guard pins the effect vocabulary to public-readonly-FIELD shape so no state can hide behind a property and escape CanonicalFold.MixModifier's handshake hash (same shape Modifier.CheckAuthoringBounds() already uses). ModifierStore.Apply deliberately does NOT consult the predicate - authored modifiers are observable via the 11.5 buff bar, SelectionSubgroupPanel's ring digest and the save round-trip, and a zero-stat MARKER modifier may exist purely so a later RemoveByModifierId finds it; only ResearchSystem's MINTED cumulative is safe to skip (that scoping is filed as DW-854). Correct side effect: a skipped install is no longer counted as a ring REFUSAL, so DW-83's warn, DW-623's void guard and DW-624's per-match tally stop claiming a tech gate's non-existent bonus was "dropped". DETERMINISM: fold set UNCHANGED - no folded field added, removed or reordered, only ModifierStore's folded per-slot VALUES could change; SimChecksumCoverageGuardTest green with its pinned known-state hash unmoved. GOLDENS MOVED: ZERO, and that is a genuine finding rather than a miss - (1) no shipped faction JSON authors any research at all (godot/resources/data/factions/{alpha,beta}_faction.json have no research key; `grep -rn '"research"' godot/resources/data` is empty), and (2) the only golden scenario carrying research, Golden/ResearchScenario, authors "armor_up" with a real +2/+3 ArmorDelta so its install path is byte-identical. All 605 golden/guard tests passed including ReBaselineDifferentialGuardTests, CanonicalModelHash and StartStateHash; nothing was re-recorded, no *.golden.txt edited, no AlgoVersion or pin touched. The `goldens: moves` prediction below is empirically wrong for this entry - filed as DW-853 rather than rewritten here, so the serial re-record phase does not read "no golden moved for DW-678" as a missing fix. COVERAGE: 8 new tests; with the guard temporarily short-circuited to `if (true || ...)` 6 of the 8 fail (the 2 that pass are the payload control and the predicate table, correctly), guard then restored and re-verified. GATE (in the phase-c worktree): `dotnet build godot/godot.csproj` succeeded, 0 errors / 6 pre-existing warnings in untouched UI/Multiplayer/CreationSuite files; `dotnet test godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests.csproj --logger trx` = 6058 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped, TRX parsed not eyeballed ({Passed: 6058, NotExecuted: 1}, the NotExecuted being the pre-existing TriggerValidationTests.RandomEffect_MustDrawFromSimRng_ReservedUntilStory2_3 skip); baseline 6050/0/1, +8 is exactly the new tests, no CanonicalModelHashPerf flake. Committed 9ac4fb39 on dw/research-empty-modifier-skip with the new test file's .cs.uid sidecar. New findings filed as DW-853, DW-854 and DW-855.
goldens: moves — bounded sim correction. Rides Story 15.22 (Phase C batched re-baseline, AlgoVersion 23->24).

Combat units therefore park at the spawn point in CommandState=Move forever, and CombatSystem's "case Move: continue" means they do not even fight back. status: done 2026-08-06
resolution: resolved by the Phase B batch - the dead guard is DELETED. EntityFlags.Moving is what actually makes MovementSystem walk a unit, and DW-634 had fenced it inside `if (isWorker)` to keep ShiftQueueScenario's golden byte-identical; DW-634's own comment recorded that the wider fix 'belongs in a deliberate re-baseline, not here', and this batch IS that re-baseline. ### DW-687: The DW-620 Invulnerable guard reads a STALE status union on BOTH ModifierStore paths — a collapse during removal is wrongly refused, and a collapse during install is wrongly allowed
origin: post-merge review of the DW-620/DW-623/DW-634/DW-636 burn-down merge, 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/Effects/ModifierStore.cs:443-452 (RemoveSlot runs ApplyStatDeltas BEFORE RecomputeStatusUnion) and :186-190 (Apply runs ApplyStatDeltas BEFORE the `StatusFlagsOf |= mod.Status` write), read against the guard at godot/src/Combat/DamageResolver.cs:144
severity: medium
reason: The DW-620 guard puts the flag check inside KillEntity, but both ModifierStore paths mutate stats on one side of the status-union write and therefore hand the guard a flag that does not describe the post-operation host. REMOVE arm (wrongly refused): base MaxHealth 100; install B {id 910, status Invulnerable, max_health_delta +40, duration 60} then A {id 911, max_health_delta -100, permanent} — ceiling 140 then 40, Health clamped to 40. At tick 60 B expires: RemoveSlot -> ApplyStatDeltas(-40) drives the ceiling 40 -> 0, the DW-491 collapse gate is satisfied, KillEntity is REFUSED because StatusFlagsOf still carries the Invulnerable that this very removal is about to clear, and :452 then recomputes the union to None. Final state: alive, EffectiveMaxHealth 0, Health 0, StatusFlags None — the live 0-ceiling zombie DW-325 exists to eliminate, and unreachable by the DW-620 comment's own recovery ("a FRESH collapse once the flag drops") because `ceilingBefore > Fixed.Zero` can never hold again while permanent A is installed; only incoming damage can still kill it, so an unattacked one keeps its faction alive for elimination win conditions indefinitely. APPLY arm (wrongly allowed, the mirror image): a modifier granting Invulnerable together with a net-negative max_health_delta collapses the ceiling at :186 while StatusFlagsOf has not yet been OR-ed at :190, so the modifier KILLS the host it was authored to make death-immune. Distinct from DW-676, which is the definitional pause-vs-cancel question for a host that is GENUINELY immune at collapse time; here the immunity is stale (remove) or not yet installed (apply), and DW-676's deferred-death re-check would not touch the apply arm at all. Uncovered: InvulnerableDeathImmunityTests.CeilingCollapse_KillsTheFormerlyImmuneHost_OnceTheInvulnerabilityExpires expires the -MaxHealth debuff FIRST (duration 1 vs 3), so the hazardous ordering never runs. Latent today — no shipped ability authors a status, so every golden leaves StatusFlagsOf at None — and reachable the moment creator content pairs Invulnerable with a MaxHealth delta. Closure = recompute the status union (or evaluate the guard against the post-operation union) BEFORE the stat revert in RemoveSlot and before the collapse test in Apply, with a two-arm test pinning both orderings.
status: open

### DW-688: The DW-634 rally-arrival test wraps int32 past ~181 units — a long rally reports "arrived" on tick 1 and is silently discarded
origin: post-merge review of the DW-620/DW-623/DW-634/DW-636 burn-down merge, 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/Economy/GatheringSystem.cs:138 (`FixedVec3.SqrDistance(Position, CommandGoal) <= ArrivalTuning.GoalArriveRadiusSqr`)
severity: medium
reason: Fixed `*` truncates to int32 (`new Fixed((int)(((long)a.Raw * b.Raw) >> 16))`, FixedPoint.cs:69-70), so SqrDistance = Dot(d,d) WRAPS once the squared distance passes 32768, i.e. a separation past ~181 units. At a 250-unit rally leg: Raw 16,384,000 -> ((long)Raw*Raw)>>16 = 4,096,000,000 -> (int) = -198,967,296, and GoalArriveRadiusSqr.Raw is 262,144, so the `<=` compare is TRUE and `arrived` is set on the worker's FIRST idle tick. RallyMovePending clears at :145 and FindBestNode/AssignToNode immediately re-target the worker to the node nearest its SPAWN — exactly the pre-DW-634 behaviour the bundle was chartered to remove, so the fix is a no-op for precisely the long rallies ("rally the hall to a far expansion mine") its own comment cites as motivating. A mid-flight worker walking in from beyond the band is worse than a no-op: at 200u the product is negative too, so it spuriously "arrives" partway and is assigned to whatever node is nearest at that intermediate position. Reachable on every shipped map (ScenarioData.MapBounds defaults to 120, MapSize.Large is a 128 half-extent = a 256-unit span). Int32 wrap is well-defined in C# so every peer computes the same wrong answer (no lockstep divergence), but the state it drives — GatherTarget, MoveTarget, and ResourceNodeStore.AssignedGatherers, which IS folded into SimChecksum — is sim truth, so this is a wrong-but-deterministic sim outcome, not a cosmetic one. HeroXpSystem.cs:96-109 documents this exact overflow and works around it with long-widened raws; the new call site does not. Unpinned: TrainedWorkerRallyFirstLegTests rallies to (22,0), a 22-unit leg. Same unwidened pattern is pre-existing at OrderQueueSystem.cs:74 and CombatSystem.cs:514/:622 against the same 2u radius, so a fix should cover the shared arrival predicate rather than this one line. Closure = a long-widened squared-distance helper (the HeroXpSystem pattern) used by every ArrivalTuning goal test, with a test at a >181-unit leg.
status: done 2026-08-06
resolution: resolved by the FixedVec3.SqrMagnitude root fix (Phase B batch). Fixed ONE helper rather than the filed call site: SqrMagnitude now accumulates each squared term in a long, shifts individually (matching Fixed operator* exactly, so every non-overflowing result is BIT-IDENTICAL to before) and saturates at Fixed.MaxValue instead of wrapping negative. SqrDistance, Magnitude and Normalized all route through it. A read-only audit found 47 call sites, 29 of them genuinely able to see spans past ~181u - so per-site patching would have guaranteed a 30th. Sites reached well beyond the filed instance: ProjectileSystem (a shell resolved its hit on the spawn tick), ExprProgram.Eval's DSL distance() (read 0 for anything 181-256u apart), GatheringSystem x5, MovementSystem, FlowField.HasArrived, OrderQueueSystem, SpatialHash.FindNearestEnemyGlobal.
### DW-689: An UNREACHABLE rally point parks a trained worker in Idle permanently — the DW-634 gate's "superseded" escape cannot fire in the sim layer
origin: post-merge review of the DW-620/DW-623/DW-634/DW-636 burn-down merge, 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/Economy/GatheringSystem.cs:133-146 (the RallyMovePending stand-down; the escape at :144 is `CommandState != UnitCommand.Move`)
severity: medium
reason: The stand-down clears RallyMovePending only on arrival within GoalArriveRadiusSqr, or when CommandState leaves Move — and nothing in the SIMULATION layer ever takes a rallied worker out of Move. CombatSystem.cs:136-147's gatherer normalization rewrites AttackMove/Stop/HoldPosition/AttackTarget/Patrol/Follow/PatrolAppend/AttackBuilding to Idle but NOT Move, then `continue`s past every other Idle write in that file; OrderQueueSystem skips an entity with an empty queue (a freshly trained worker has one); BuildingSystem.ClearWorkerBuild fires only from CommandState=Build; the only Move->Stop writers are PathRequestSystem.cs:190/:234 and FlowFieldBridge.cs:172, all under src/UI (presentation, absent headless) and all gated on WAYPOINT_REACH_SQR (1.5u), strictly tighter than the 2u arrival test on :138, so they can never fire where :144 has not already passed. Trigger: an authored Custom building with produces_category "Worker" (the only worker producer TrainUnit accepts) rallied to a point inside a PathabilityGrid-blocked region — MovementSystem.cs:195-206 hard-stops the worker at the blocked-cell boundary, so SqrDistance(Position, CommandGoal) never falls inside the radius and TickIdle returns at :144 on every tick forever. FindBestNode/AssignToNode are never reached: the worker never gathers again, a silent permanent loss of its economic function, where pre-DW-634 it was re-targeted to the nearest node on the very next tick. The bundle's own comment at :140-143 claims to prevent exactly this, and its escape test (TrainedWorkerRallyFirstLegTests.RallyPendingWorker_WhoseMoveIsSuperseded_ResumesAutoGatherWithoutReachingTheRally) hand-writes CommandState = Idle, a value the simulation never assigns to this unit on its own. Related but NOT covered by DW-681 (which records the layering gap; its closure — move goal-arrival resolution into a sim system — still only fires ON arrival) or DW-682 (AI placement). Closure = a bounded stand-down (a tick budget or a reachability/no-progress test) that releases the worker to auto-gather when the rally leg provably cannot complete.
status: open

### DW-690: RallyMovePending is the one input to its own gate that SaveGameState drops, so a save/load mid-rally reverts the DW-634 fix — and the comment justifying the omission is factually wrong
origin: post-merge review of the DW-620/DW-623/DW-634/DW-636 burn-down merge, 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/Core/EntityWorld.cs:681-687 (the "not persisted" rationale) vs godot/src/Core/Persistence/SaveGameState.cs:167 (the EA enum), :266-267/:290-291 (capture), :636/:664-665 (restore)
severity: low
reason: SaveGameState round-trips Flags, CommandState, MoveTarget, CommandGoal, GatherState, GatherTarget, CarryAmount, CarryResType, CarryCapacity and BuildTarget, but RallyMovePending is not in the EA enum and comes back false from EntityWorld.Create. A worker autosaved mid-leg therefore reloads looking exactly like it is still walking the rally (Flags/CommandState/MoveTarget all restored) while its gate is off, so the first GatheringSystem tick runs FindBestNode/AssignToNode and overwrites MoveTarget with whatever node is nearest its mid-leg position — the player's explicit rally discarded, the precise defect DW-634 was chartered to fix. The EntityWorld doc defends the omission as "the exact posture of every other field of this worker state machine (GatherState/GatherTarget/CarryAmount/GateClosedTicks are all unfolded)", which conflates UNFOLDED with UNPERSISTED: three of those four ARE persisted and only GateClosedTicks is genuinely absent from EA, so the stated rationale does not hold even though the omission may still be the right call. Closure = either add RallyMovePending to the EA enum/capture/restore (a save-format addition, no fold and no golden movement) or correct the comment to state the real reason for dropping an in-flight rally leg across a load.
status: open

### DW-691: The DeathFeed is unthreaded on every EFFECT-GRAPH EffectContext — a hero that lands the last hit through a modifier period or an on-hit rider gains no XP
origin: post-merge review of the DW-620/DW-623/DW-634/DW-636 burn-down merge, 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/Effects/ModifierStore.cs:839 (RunEffect builds its EffectContext with the `deaths` parameter omitted; the store has no DeathFeed field at all — fields :76-86, ctor :100-108) and godot/src/Combat/CombatSystem.cs:830-833 (RunOnHit, same omission); godot/src/Combat/ItemSystem.cs:236-237 likewise
severity: medium
reason: EffectContext defaults `deaths` to null (EffectContext.cs:71-75), so a DamageEffect leaf reached through a modifier's period_effect, through an on-hit rider, or through a consumable's graph calls DamageResolver.Apply with ctx.Deaths null and the `deaths?.Push(...)` at DamageResolver.cs:161 no-ops. HeroXpSystem.Tick reads only that feed (:83-86), so a hero whose poison DoT or whose on-hit rider lands the killing blow banks 0 XP, while the identical last hit from its auto-attack credits world.XpBounty in full — the three cast contexts in AbilityCastSystem (:200-202, :269-271, :417-419) and ScenarioDirector (:2824-2826) all DO pass `deaths`, so this is an inconsistency between sibling effect paths, not a design stance. Shipped content already reaches one arm: onhit_searing.json carries a damage leaf and runs through the CombatSystem context. HeroStore Xp/Level are folded into SimChecksum, so the withheld credit is folded state, which makes DW-616's new DeathFeed class doc ("a death is NEVER dropped", DeathFeed.cs:37-40) true only of the feed's CAPACITY, not of the channel — DW-616 closed a loss needing >256 deaths in one tick while these paths withhold XP in ordinary play. Scoped to the effect-graph contexts: DW-490 already covers the sibling omission on the DW-325 ceiling-collapse KillEntity call (ModifierStore.cs:766), which also needs a caster-attribution decision this entry does not. Closure = thread the DeathFeed into ModifierStore (a ctor dep, like _events/_stats) and into RunOnHit/UseItemCommand, then re-check the DW-616 invariant statement.

### DW-697: DW-356's proposed streaming-Utf8JsonReader closure is measurably SLOWER — whole-document parse costs 3x the per-node transient JsonDocuments

### DW-698: DW-356's proposed "share LoadScenario's parsed TriggerGraph with the hash fold" closure is a DETERMINISM hazard as written — Merge mutates the graph in place
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/Dsl/TriggerGraph.cs:253-256 (Merge) vs godot/src/Core/ScenarioDirector.cs:570 (LoadScenario feeding it FromJson output directly)
severity: medium
reason: TriggerGraph.Merge MUTATES the graph passed to it — it rewrites every node's Id (`n.Id += offset`) and offsets EnableTrigger/DisableTrigger/RunTrigger TargetTriggerId in place, because the merged graph reuses the same node object references. LoadScenario feeds it TriggerGraph.FromJson(scenario.TriggerGraphJson) directly, so any cache handing that SAME instance to CanonicalModelHash.MixTriggerGraph would see node ids shifted after the merge and fold a DIFFERENT hash on a later Compute — a silent MP-handshake divergence, the most expensive failure class in the project, arising from a pure performance change. Making it safe requires a non-mutating Merge, i.e. Clone() on all ~36 NodeBase subclasses, whose own failure mode is a silently dropped field. Judged out of scope for DW-356's bundle and not worth the risk given that entry states the cold hash is not a live stall; DW-356 was instead closed by optimizing the parse itself. Recorded as a code comment on CanonicalModelHashPerfTests. Closure (if ever wanted) = a non-mutating Merge with per-kind Clone coverage pinned by a field-completeness test, THEN the shared-graph cache.
status: open

Traced failure: host id 0 holds [slot0 = periodic modifier A, slot1 = modifier B], n=2. If A's period pulse removes A's own slot (RemoveSlot → CompactSlot swaps B into slot0, _count → 1), the walk — still standing on slot0 with a stale n=2 — overwrites _ticksUntilPeriod/_periodsRemaining onto B's swapped-in fields, then at s=1 walks a CLEARED slot whose _remainingTicks decrements 0 → −1, reads as expired, and RemoveSlot/CompactSlot it: B vanishes and _count goes 2 → 0. Latent, not live: unreachable with the shipped vocabulary (no node calls RemoveByModifierId/ClearEntity) and the Story 2.3 validator fences period-nested installs. Not fixed in the modifier-store-hardening bundle because (a) it is outside DW-662's recorded intent, which is specifically the target-alive guard, and (b) it cannot be given teeth without a test-only LeafEffect that calls RemoveByModifierId mid-pulse, which requires editing the hardcoded probes allowlist in godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Validation/EffectFoldCompletenessTests.cs:89 — a cross-bundle edit. Closure = capture the slot's descriptor refs before RunEffect and, after it, clamp n DOWN to _count[i] (never grow — a re-entrant install must still wait for the next tick, or the fold moves) and break when the slot no longer holds the instance that was pulsed; the same twin belongs after RemoveSlot's expire-effect.
status: open

### DW-727: A stale `.pack.tmp` takes the NEXT export down with it - Pack's staged open is CreateNew, so it cannot tolerate the residue its own catch block admits it may leave
origin: post-merge review of the DW-560 burn-down merge (1be256fd), 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/Core/Definitions/ContentPackager.cs:258-261 (`string stagePath = outputZipPath + ".pack.tmp";` then `ZipFile.Open(stagePath, ZipArchiveMode.Create)` with no pre-delete), read against the sibling pattern at :627 (`File.Copy(zipPath, tmpPath, overwrite: true)`) and the best-effort cleanup at :308
severity: low
reason: ZipArchiveMode.Create maps to FileMode.CreateNew, which throws when anything already occupies the path - verified empirically on this box (.NET 8 SDK 8.0.419): pre-creating `map.chimera.zip.pack.tmp` and calling `ZipFile.Open(stage, ZipArchiveMode.Create)` yields `IOException: The file '...map.chimera.zip.pack.tmp' already exists.` The pre-DW-560 shape had no such state (delete the output, then write straight into it), and RewriteManifest - the DW-421 pattern DW-560's own comment says it mirrors - is immune precisely because it stages via `File.Copy(..., overwrite: true)` at :627. Trigger = anything that leaves the staged partial behind: the editor is killed or loses power mid-write, or the catch block's best-effort `File.Delete(stagePath)` at :308 is defeated by an AV/indexer handle (it swallows its own failure by design, so as not to mask the real error). Consequence for the realistic FILE case is bounded, not permanent: the failing Pack() runs that same catch, deletes the stale file and rethrows, so attempt #2 succeeds - the creator eats one confusing IOException naming a temp file they never created, on an export whose inputs and destination are both fine. The DIRECTORY case IS permanent, also verified: `ZipFile.Open` throws UnauthorizedAccessException, `File.Exists(dir)` is false so the cleanup is skipped entirely, and `File.Delete` on a directory would throw and be swallowed anyway - every later export to that path fails forever with no in-app remedy. Adjacent to DW-717 but distinct in substance, and it contradicts that entry's "harmless to correctness" line: leaked staging residue is not inert disk clutter, it is a tripwire under the next export. Not pinned by the bundle's own Pack_StagingFailure_LeavesPreviousExportIntact, which squats a DIRECTORY on the temp name and asserts only that something throws while the previous export stays byte-identical - a stale FILE at that path is never exercised, so the suite stays green either way. Closure = make the stage open symmetric with RewriteManifest (delete or overwrite stagePath immediately before :261), plus a test that leaves a stale `.pack.tmp` FILE and asserts the next Pack succeeds.
status: open

### DW-728: DW-533 flipped the editor's Import-Map flow from a loud failure to a reported SUCCESS on an unparseable bundled scenario.json
origin: post-merge review of the DW-533 burn-down merge (37fe897d), 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/Core/Bootstrap/Phases/WinConditionPhase.cs:616 (DoImport's TerrainRef rewrite calls the 1-arg `ScenarioSerializer.LoadFromFile(destScenario)`), null branch at :622-626, success report at :629-632, the catch that used to fire at :636
severity: medium
reason: DW-533's doc justifies the throw-to-null change against "both production callers", but there are eight production call sites and the map-import flow is one where the observable outcome INVERTS rather than degrades. Trigger: import a `.chimera.zip` that bundles at least one terrain file (so `result.TerrainFiles.Count > 0` at :611 and the scenario is actually re-parsed) and whose `scenario.json` fails under ContentJson.ScenarioOptions - a package authored by a newer build carrying an unknown custom-UI widget `kind` (WidgetBaseJsonConverter rejects it), a hand-edited zip, or any numeric enum since DW-274. ContentPackager.Unpack passes, because the manifest hash covers the packaged bytes and Pack never parses the scenario. BEFORE: :616 threw, the enclosing `catch (Exception ex)` at :636 set `statusLabel.Text = "Import failed: <located json error>"`, and the creator knew the package was bad. AFTER: :616 returns null, the else at :622-626 only `GD.PrintErr`s "imported map will load flat", execution falls through and :629 tells the user `Imported: <DisplayName>` with a matching `GD.Print`. The unparseable scenario stays written at `res://resources/data/scenarios/{id}.json` (the File.Copy above it already ran), where SkirmishCatalog.ScanMaps:106 now silently skips it (`map == null -> continue`) and ScenarioLoadPhase boots the fallback - so the map is reported imported, then simply never appears in the picker, with no error anywhere the user looks. The zero-terrain path never parses the scenario at all and so was always silent, which makes this uniformly-silent rather than uniformly-loud; that is the wrong direction for a creator-facing import of third-party content. Distinct from DW-722 (the two FALLBACK callers discard the new located parseError - a log-detail gap on paths that were always null-tolerant) and from DW-145/DW-235 (TerrainRef / one-path import legs). Closure = adopt the `LoadFromFile(path, out string? parseError)` overload in DoImport and treat a non-null parseError as an import FAILURE (report the located reason, and decide whether to roll back the already-copied `{id}.json`), rather than reporting success on a scenario the app has just proven it cannot read.
status: open

### DW-729: NodeScan.TryGet is first-wins where JsonElement.TryGetProperty is LAST-wins, so DW-356's stated parity invariant is false and a duplicated `kind` now reports a different located error
origin: post-merge review of the DW-356 burn-down merge (8a72f0c2), 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/Dsl/NodeBaseJsonConverter.cs:1044-1047 (the doc claim + TryGet's first-match loop), consumed by ReadKind at :717-725; the same false claim at :948 and in the sibling godot/src/Core/Definitions/EffectNodeJsonConverter.cs:411
severity: low
reason: The NodeScan doc asserts first-occurrence resolution is "exactly what JsonElement.TryGetProperty returns when a name is duplicated". It is not: JsonDocument.TryGetNamedPropertyValue walks the row table BACKWARD from EndObject, so TryGetProperty returns the LAST occurrence. Verified empirically (.NET 8) - for `{"kind":"first","name":"x","kind":"second"}` TryGetProperty("kind") returns "second" while EnumerateObject yields first, name, second. The divergence is observable only through ReadKind, the one read that runs BEFORE RejectUnknownProperties, and it selects a different branch's allow-list. Concrete: `{ "id":0, "kind":"display_message", "name":"T", "kind":"trigger" }` - pre-DW-356 `kind` resolved to "trigger", whose allow-list admits `name`, and the second `kind` threw `node.kind: duplicate property (each field may appear at most once, AR-22).`; post-DW-356 it resolves to "display_message" and the walk throws first on index 2 - `node.name: unknown property (graph nodes are closed - no scripting/extension escape hatch, AR-22).` - pointing the author at a field that is perfectly valid on the node they wrote instead of at the duplicate that is the actual fault. Accept/reject is NOT affected (every kind branch calls RejectUnknownProperties and the fall-through throws "unknown node kind", so a duplicated key is rejected either way) and no hash, golden or AlgoVersion moves - the harm is the misleading diagnostic plus a stated invariant that is wrong for anyone who later adds a read ahead of the allow-list pass. Two aggravations: the sibling EffectNodeJsonConverter still resolves via `el.TryGetProperty` and therefore really is last-wins, so the two closed-node converters now disagree about which duplicate `kind` wins while their docs assert the same (wrong) shared rule; and NodeBaseJsonConverterScanTests.DuplicatedKind_ResolvesToTheFirstOccurrence_NotTheLast pins the NEW message as if it were parity with the old one, so the divergence is now test-frozen. DW-356's commit message and this ledger's own DW-356 resolution line repeat the claim (append-only, so they stand as written). Closure = either correct all three doc sites (and the test's rationale comment) to state that TryGetProperty is last-wins and that NodeScan deliberately differs, or make TryGet scan backward so the pre-DW-356 located message is restored and the two converters agree.
status: open

origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/Navigation/MovementSystem.cs (Velocity is written before the CheckedStep resolution, so a hard-stopped unit keeps its seek velocity)
