reason: MovementSystem writes world.Velocity[i] = velocity and only then resolves the step, so a unit pressed against a wall reports a non-zero Velocity forever while its Position never changes. It would become a real defect the moment anything reads Velocity for presentation (walk-animation blending, a movement-based audio cue) or for AI/trigger conditions. Closure = zero (or resolve) Velocity when CheckedStep hard-stops or slides, with its own determinism argument, since it is a behaviour change outside a golden-neutral bundle's remit.

### DW-747: DW-535's own rationale misstates the direction of the MaxHitsPerSearch trap - do not copy it forward
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-05

severity: low
reason: DW-535 says a future story that WIDENS MaxHitsPerSearch "would in fact widen the fan-out selection window". Widening is actually inert today: SearchAreaEffect.FindTargets:75-76 truncates the result back to MaxSearchTargets, and truncating an ascending lowest-128 prefix to 64 yields exactly the lowest-64 - the same set. The real hazard is the OPPOSITE direction, since LOWERING MaxHitsPerSearch below MaxSearchTargets narrows which entities the effect hits. The precise rule is that effective fan-out = min(MaxHitsPerSearch, MaxSearchTargets). The effect-caps-doc bundle wrote the accurate version into the code doc rather than the ledger's wording, and could not amend DW-535's reason line because the ledger is append-only. This entry exists so nobody re-imports the inverted rationale into a future story or resolution note. Closure = documentation-only cross-reference; close it once the accurate rule has been read into whatever story next touches the SearchArea caps.

### DW-753: Vector3Fixed.GetHashCode still uses process-seed-randomized HashCode.Combine - the same DW-337 defect class but in the SIMULATION layer

severity: medium
reason: Identical defect class to DW-337 (ExecEdge/DataEdge), but potentially worse because Vector3Fixed is a simulation-layer type: HashCode.Combine is re-seeded every process, so the same position hashes differently on every launch and any code that places Vector3Fixed values in a HashSet/Dictionary and ENUMERATES it gets a per-run iteration order - a lockstep desync source rather than an editor wart. After the triggergraph-determinism-hardening bundle replaced the two edge structs' hashes with a seed-free FNV-1a-32 fold, this is the LAST remaining HashCode.Combine anywhere in godot/src (those three were the only ones). Closure = audit the call sites, then apply the same GraphEdgeHash-style seed-free fold over X.Raw/Y.Raw/Z.Raw in a fixed field order, with a cross-process stability test.

### DW-754: DataEdge.CompareTo is not a total order (it ignores Wire), so ToCanonicalJson's data-edge sort falls back to LINQ stability - i.e. to authoring order
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/Dsl/GraphEdge.cs:86 (CompareTo) and godot/src/Dsl/TriggerGraph.cs:1028 (ToCanonicalJson)
severity: medium
reason: Two data edges sharing a (Src,SrcPort,Dst,DstPort) topology tuple but differing in Wire compare EQUAL, so ToCanonicalJson's `DataEdges.OrderBy(e => e)` leaves their relative order to sort stability, which means authoring order - and two structurally-equal graphs built in different orders could therefore serialize to DIFFERENT bytes, directly weakening the documented byte-identity claim. CanonicalModelHash.MixTriggerGraph already guards itself with an explicit `.ThenBy(x => x.Wire)`; ToCanonicalJson does not, so the hash is safe and only the serialization is exposed. Whether such a pair is actually reachable depends on GraphStructureGate's forked-data-edge rules, which the DW-337 bundle did not fully audit, so this may be unreachable in practice - that audit is part of the work. The caveat was documented on the DataEdges property but the sort was NOT changed: altering canonical emission order is a serialization-format change needing its own scoped entry, not a drive-by inside a hashing bundle. Closure = audit reachability, then either add the `.ThenBy(e => e.Wire)` tiebreak to ToCanonicalJson or make CompareTo itself a total order, and pin it with a build-order-independence test.
status: open

### DW-762: ClearCompletenessSweep has no guard that a fixture's NormalizeFresh cannot silently neuter the comparison
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-05
location: godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Sim/ClearCompletenessSweep.cs (AssertClearRestoresFreshState, step 2 - the NormalizeFresh hook)
severity: medium
reason: NormalizeFresh runs on the FRESH instance after dirtying, and the machinery only re-checks per-field divergence afterwards. A fixture that normalized fresh INTO the dirty state - e.g. by replaying the store's own Clear() on the fresh side, which looks like the obvious way to match a retained buffer - would still satisfy the divergence precondition on some other field (Count) while making the field it was actually written for vacuous, and nothing would flag it. The sweep is the load-bearing guard for reset completeness across 25 store cases, so a hook that can quietly disarm one field per fixture is a real hole in a test-of-tests. The DW-584 bundle avoided the hazard by hand (its fresh buffer is Poked directly, never routed through Reset()/Clear()) but nothing enforces that on the next fixture. Closure = have the machinery verify each normalized field still diverges pre-Clear, or forbid NormalizeFresh from invoking the store's own reset path. Out of DW-584's recorded scope (removal of one exemption) and it is a machinery-level change to a shared sweep used by 25 cases, so recorded rather than attempted in-bundle.
status: open

### DW-764: DW-439's new FindNearestEnemyUnit ranks targets with the int32-overflowing FixedVec3.SqrDistance, so past ~181 units the FARTHEST enemy wins
origin: post-merge review sweep (wave 2), 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/AI/AiOpponentSystem.cs:728 (FindNearestEnemyUnit, called from TryResolveWaveDestination:707); the sibling FindNearestEnemyBuilding:788 shares the flaw (pre-existing)
severity: medium
reason: The scan ranks with `Fixed sqrDist = FixedVec3.SqrDistance(from, world.Position[i])` and keeps `sqrDist < bestSqr`. SqrDistance = (b-a).SqrMagnitude() = Dot(v,v), built from `Fixed.operator*` (FixedPoint.cs:69, `new Fixed((int)(((long)a.Raw*b.Raw) >> 16))` - a TRUNCATING cast) and `Fixed.operator+` (FixedPoint.cs:60, a wrapping int add). A single-axis gap past ~181 world units overflows: at dx=240 the term is 240^2 * 65536 = 3,774,873,600, which truncates to int32 as -520,093,696, and a negative value always satisfies the `<` test. This is not hypothetical geometry - MapSizes.ToBounds is 120 for Medium (a 240-unit span) and 128 for Large (256), so an anchor at one corner and a hostile at the opposite corner wraps both terms. HeroXpSystem.cs:97-107 documents this exact hazard by name and works around it with long-widened raw math (`((dxr*dxr) >> 16)` summed in long); the new scan does not. Consequence: the wave marches at the far-corner enemy instead of the adjacent one. Latent today because the branch is only reached when `!IsHostile(Faction.Player1)`, which needs a non-FFA AllianceStore - it arms the moment lobby team seeding lands (see DW-740), so it is a dormant defect on an unshipped path rather than a live one, which is why it is filed rather than fixed here. Closure = compute the ranking distance in long-widened raw units, exactly as HeroXpSystem does, and do the same for FindNearestEnemyBuilding in the same pass since it is the identical shape; golden-neutral because the FFA path never enters either branch's overflow regime today, but confirm before merging.
status: done 2026-08-06
resolution: resolved by the same FixedVec3.SqrMagnitude root fix as DW-688 (Phase B batch) - FindNearestEnemyUnit's argmin no longer inverts past ~181u, so the wave picks the nearest hostile rather than the farthest. See DW-688's resolution for the mechanism and the 47-site/29-reachable audit.
### DW-765: DW-490's collapse attribution makes the victim its own killer at the three self-cast Modifier minters, crediting the victim's faction with a kill
origin: post-merge review sweep (wave 2), 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/Effects/ModifierStore.cs:855 (ApplyStatDeltas -> `DamageResolver.KillEntity(_world, id, casterFaction, _events, _stats, _deaths, casterId)`), fed by the caster recorded at :212 (fresh install) and :236 (stack branch); minters at godot/src/Combat/ItemSystem.cs:470, godot/src/Combat/HeroXpSystem.cs:359, godot/src/Economy/ResearchSystem.cs:481
severity: medium
reason: DW-490 replaced the DW-325 ceiling-collapse kill's hardcoded `Faction.Neutral` / attacker -1 with the installing instance's recorded caster, and justified it in the doc block above the call: "When the caster is genuinely unknown the recorded pair IS (-1, Faction.Neutral) ... so a rules-driven collapse is byte-identical to the pre-DW-490 behaviour apart from the DeathFeed push". That premise holds for the ability/EffectExecutor path DW-490 was tested against, but it is FALSE for the three non-ability Modifier minters - each passes the VICTIM as the caster: ItemSystem `modifiers.Apply(entityId, mod, entityId, world.FactionOf[entityId])`, HeroXpSystem's ReconcileGrowth `_modifiers.Apply(entityId, growthMod, entityId, faction)`, and ResearchSystem `_modifiers.Apply(id, BuildCumulativeModifier(...), casterId: id, casterFaction: faction)`. Reachable with VALID content: ItemDefinitionValidator.CheckDelta (ItemDefinitionValidator.cs:322-333) bounds only |delta| against MAX_ITEM_STAT_DELTA=1000, so `max_health_delta: -500` on a hero whose EffectiveMaxHealth is 500 is authorable; ItemSystem.Tick -> ResolvePickup -> ApplyItemStatModifier -> Apply -> ApplyStatDeltas drives the ceiling 500 -> 0, the DW-491 collapse gate fires, and KillEntity is called with killer = the hero's OWN faction and attackerId = the hero's own entity id. Three shipped consequences: (1) DamageResolver.cs:158 `stats?.RecordKill(world.FactionOf[id], killer)` now increments `_kills[ownFaction]` as well as `_losses[ownFaction]` (MatchStats.cs:51-52), where the pre-DW-490 Neutral was deliberately skipped by the `killer > 0` guard - the score screen reads this; (2) DamageResolver.cs:149-150 write `world.KillerOf[id] = id` and `world.KillerFactionOf[id]` = the victim's own slot; (3) DamageResolver.cs:156 pushes the same pair into the DeathLog, which ScenarioDirector.cs:1651-1652 emits as the `unit_dies` payload `p1: deathLog.KillerAt(rec), p2: deathLog.KillerSlotAt(rec)`, exposed to creator triggers as the `killer` / `killer_faction` event params (EventDispatchPlan.cs:44-45) - so a scenario branching on "who killed this unit" sees the unit as its own killer instead of the -1/-1 it saw before, and that branch can move folded sim state. The same path is reachable via a net-negative research modifier; ResearchSystem.cs:472 already documents that "the remove step can collapse a MaxHealth ceiling and kill the host". Distinct from DW-744 (the REMOVAL arm crediting the buff granter) and DW-745 (the recompute seam bypassing the check): this is the APPLY arm with a self-recorded caster. Neither wave agent could see it - DW-490 inspected only the ability caster convention and DW-650 only the descriptors' magnitude bounds, and no test in the wave asserts the killer identity of a minter-driven collapse. Closure = a decision on whether a self-cast, non-ability Modifier collapse should attribute to the victim's faction at all (a WC3-shaped alternative is to fall back to Neutral when casterId == victimId), then implement it with a test pinning the killer identity for all three minters; sequence it with DW-744 since the two are the same design question on the two arms.
status: open

### DW-766: DW-490 makes ItemSystem (index 10) a DeathFeed producer that runs AFTER HeroXpSystem (index 9) drains and clears it
origin: post-merge review sweep (wave 2), 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/Core/Sim/SimulationHost.cs:238 (`Modifiers = new ModifierStore(..., _deathFeed)`) vs the system order at :314 (HeroXpSystem [9]) and :318 (ItemSys [10])
severity: low
reason: Threading the shared DeathFeed into ModifierStore means the ceiling-collapse kill now calls `deaths?.Push(...)` in DamageResolver.KillEntity (DamageResolver.cs:161). ModifierStore.Apply is reachable from ItemSystem, registered at [10] - AFTER HeroXpSystem at [9], whose Tick drains `_deaths` (HeroXpSystem.cs:83-86) and then `_deaths.Clear()`s it (HeroXpSystem.cs:167). Same trigger as DW-765: a hero picks up an item whose negative max_health_delta collapses its ceiling during ItemSystem.Tick, so the DeathRecord is pushed at index 10 and the feed holds Count == 1 at the end-of-tick checksum boundary, with the XP credit landing one tick late. That falsifies a premise two files state as load-bearing: DeathFeed.cs's type doc ("Drained + cleared every tick, so it is EMPTY at the checksum boundary -> NOT folded into SimChecksum") and SimChecksum.cs:198 and :601, which both cite CombatEventQueue/DeathFeed being "provably drained" as the reason they are excluded from the fold. The residue feeds HeroStore.Xp/Level, which ARE folded, so it is mutable state outside the desync detector. Rated low because it WIDENS a pre-existing hole rather than opening a class: ScenarioDirector at index [15] already holds `_deaths` (ScenarioDirector.cs:2835 passes `deaths: _deaths` into its EffectContext), so a director-run effect graph could already leave the feed non-empty. Closure = either re-order/drain (a second HeroXpSystem drain pass, or move the item tick ahead of it), or - probably better, since the director instance cannot be re-ordered - drop the "provably drained" claim and state the real invariant, then decide whether the feed needs an end-of-tick assert or a fold. Any change here moves folded XP timing, so it needs its own golden analysis.
status: done 2026-08-06
resolution: workflow burn-down bundle deathfeed-drain-invariant (2026-08-06, Phase C batch) - verified live against current code, then fixed per the spec §Rulings ("make the invariant TRUE, do not weaken the claim"). Repro confirmed before fixing: a Player1 hero picking up a -100 max_health_delta item collapses its ceiling inside ModifierStore.Apply during ItemSystem at index [10] - after HeroXpSystem at [9] already drained and Clear()ed - leaving DeathFeed.Count == 1 at the checksum boundary with the XP credit landing a tick late on the FOLDED HeroStore.Xp. FIX, three parts: (1) HeroXpSystem.DrainResidue, a second CREDIT-ONLY pass sharing the single extracted CreditRecordedDeaths implementation (no second copy of the rule); (2) a new DeathFeedDrainSystem registered LAST at index [16], past ScenarioDirector [15] (the last producer), so the tick order is now 17 systems; (3) SimulationLoop.EnableTickBoundaryInvariants, asserting DeathFeed.Count == 0 after the whole system array and before the checksum, so a future producer registered past the drain throws with a DW-766 diagnosis instead of silently re-opening the hole. Level/growth deliberately stay at [9] on the next tick rather than running in the residue pass: reconciling growth there would re-enter ModifierStore.Apply AFTER the clear (its own ceiling-collapse kill would push a new record and re-open the very hole being closed) and would raise hero_level into the transient DslSimEventFeed after ScenarioDirector already drained and cleared it, breaking that feed's identical empty-at-the-boundary posture (filed as DW-850). Banking the XP in the same tick is exactly what the ruling requires; the level advance lands when it always did. The "provably drained" prose in DeathFeed.cs and both SimChecksum sites (:198 and the DslEventQueue fold-site comment) now states what enforces it. FOLD SET UNCHANGED: no new folded state, SimChecksum.AlgoVersion untouched at 23, DeathFeed still not hashed - only the premise for excluding it now holds. ZERO GOLDENS MOVED, expected rather than a miss: DrainResidue early-returns on Count == 0 so every tick whose deaths were all recorded before index [9] is bit-identical to the pre-fix runtime, and the residue path is content-gated (no shipped item authors a negative max_health_delta and no golden's director graph kills); verified explicitly with a 428-test filtered run over all Golden/CanonicalModelHash/StartStateHash/SimChecksumCoverageGuard/ReBaselineDifferentialGuard tests, all green - the coverage guard's pinned known-state hash did not move, the differential guard passes on the UNMODIFIED frozen Phase-B control, and CanonicalModelHash/StartStateHash did not move. RED-without-fix proven by temporarily no-oping DeathFeedDrainSystem.Tick: the three host-level tests failed, two via the new boundary assertion firing with "1 DeathFeed record(s) survived to the tick boundary" - the tripwire reproduces the ledger defect directly. One forced test-side edit, not scope creep: StoreClearCompletenessTests' reflection sweep fails any new SimulationLoop field the ResetTick fixture leaves at its fresh value, so `_boundaryDeaths` was added to that case's allowlist alongside the fourteen existing `_checksum*` host-lifetime wiring refs, justified because its CONTENT is per-match state already swept by the `_deathFeed.Clear()` case and re-nulling the reference would disarm the invariant for the host's life. GATE (in the phase-c worktree, relative paths): `dotnet build godot/godot.csproj` clean - 0 errors, 6 warnings all pre-existing in untouched Godot presentation files (ScoreScreenOverlay, DedicatedServer, UnitCardPanel, MainMenuPhase); `dotnet test --logger trx` = 6062 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped (6050 baseline + 12 new tests). Worktree D:\Projects\Project_Chimera\.claude\worktrees\wf_99fe7442-e52-10, commit c6ce3c7f on run base 5b6021f5. New findings filed as DW-850, DW-851 and DW-852.
goldens: moves — bounded sim correction. Rides Story 15.22 (Phase C batched re-baseline, AlgoVersion 23->24).

### DW-767: DW-542's LLM placement-slot gate skips resource_nodes[].owner_slot, so the "two gates agree" invariant it installs is still violated
origin: post-merge review sweep (wave 2), 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/AI/LLMService.cs:665-677 (the DW-542 block) and :714-720 (the resource-node pass) vs godot/src/Core/Definitions/ScenarioValidator.cs:351-354
severity: low
reason: The DW-542 block gates `buildings[i].slot` and `units[i].slot` against `declaredSlots` and its comment claims it exists "so the two gates agree", but ScenarioValidator.Validate has a THIRD check with the identical `references no declared player_slot` shape: `if (n.CollectionModel == "Income" && !declared.Contains(n.OwnerSlot))`. The LLM gate's resource-node pass checks only bounds/supply/rate and never looks at `collection_model` or `owner_slot` - LLMService.cs contains no occurrence of either identifier. `ScenarioResourceNode.OwnerSlot` defaults to -1 (ScenarioData.cs:274) while `CollectionModel` defaults to "Gather" (:242), so the invalid combination is reachable purely by the model naming the collection model and omitting the slot. Concrete trigger: the model emits `"resource_nodes": [{ "x": 0, "z": 0, "supply": 400, "rate": 5, "collection_model": "Income" }]` - deserializable even though the prompt schema at LLMService.cs:775-781 omits the field, because ContentJson.ModelOutputOptions is deliberately lenient (DW-526). ValidateScenario returns success, the creator is told the map validated, and ScenarioLoadPhase's `_validator.Validate` then refuses it with `scenario.resource_nodes[0].owner_slot=-1 references no declared player_slot` - exactly the promise-then-refuse UX defect DW-542 names, on the one slot-reference field the fix did not cover. DW-542's entry files DW-743 for the unit_id half but nothing for this one. Closure = extend the DW-542 block (or the node pass) with the Income/owner_slot pair, mirroring ScenarioValidator's condition and located error shape verbatim; cheap, and it belongs with DW-743 in the same gate-agreement pass.

goldens: moves — but NOT in Phase C. Re-homed to Story 15.23; the fix adds folded state, so it re-records at the end of its own story per the 2026-08-06 batch rule.
decision: 2026-08-06 (Alec) — OUT of the Story 15.22 Phase C batch, re-homed to its own story 15.23. The batch rule takes bounded corrections only, and this is not one: even the narrow version (a generation stamp stored beside the two held ids) adds NEW FOLDED SIM STATE, which would turn Phase C from a value-only re-record into a genuine fold change and invalidate the SimChecksumCoverageGuardTest known-state pin that window relies on as its proof. The full close-out — a PackRef/TryResolveRef pair over entity space, closing AttackTarget, CommandTarget, ProjectileStore.TargetId and every other cross-tick raw entity id at once — is a build with real checksum and persistence blast radius, exactly what this entry's own text says needs its own bundle. Behaviour stays pinned meanwhile by HeldAutoTarget_RecycledIntoAnotherEnemy_KeepsFiring and Projectile_PrimaryTargetRecycledIntoAnotherEnemy_StillDetonates.

### DW-778: A worker walled off in a CLEAR pocket can still hold a gather slot indefinitely - only the hard stop is counted, not a wall-slide that never closes distance
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/Economy/GatheringSystem.cs - TickWalkStall (the `CheckedStep.Resolve != pos` test)
severity: low
reason: Chosen deliberately for zero false positives when DW-532 was closed. The stall test counts only the CheckedStep HARD stop (full step plus both wall-slide axes rejected), which is provably conservative - a step hard-stopped at this length is hard-stopped at every length in that direction, so a worker legitimately rounding a corner is never stripped of its reservation. The uncovered case is a worker enclosed in a CLEAR pocket whose node is outside: it slides around the pocket perimeter and each sliding tick resets the streak, so it can hold the slot for the whole match. Closing it needs a progress-based test (distance-to-node must decrease), which produces false yields for any worker legitimately walking around a long wall - a trade worth its own deliberate decision.

### DW-783: AI attack waves march to a hardcoded P1_BASE in every FFA match, ignoring where Player1's base actually is
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/AI/AiOpponentSystem.cs:741 (TryResolveWaveDestination) / P1_BASE at :80
severity: high
reason: TryResolveWaveDestination short-circuits with `if (IsHostile(Faction.Player1)) { dest = P1_BASE; return true; }`, i.e. every FFA match (the overwhelmingly common case) sends DoLaunchAttack's wave to the literal (-45, 0, 0) regardless of the map, so on any map whose Player1 start is not at that point the AI's waves march to empty ground. DW-439 already built the correct logic - nearest hostile building, then nearest hostile unit - but wired it ONLY to the teamed branch that no shipped scenario reaches; ResourceStore.FactionBase[(int)Faction.Player1] is already populated and would be the honest destination. Pre-existing and unrelated to the DW-644 raze-scoring defect, and it changes WHICH ground the wave marches on, so it would move the AI-active golden - a behaviour change deserving its own bundle plus a deliberate isolated re-baseline, which the ai-opponent-scoring bundle was explicitly forbidden from doing.
status: done 2026-08-06
resolution: resolved by the Phase B batch - the dead guard is DELETED, not worked around. TryResolveWaveDestination short-circuited with `if (IsHostile(Faction.Player1)) { dest = P1_BASE; return true; }`, which is EVERY free-for-all match, so the correct nearest-hostile-structure-then-unit resolution below it was unreachable in every shipped scenario. The method's own doc comment recorded that the short-circuit was kept deliberately so no checksum sequence would move; this batch IS that deliberate re-baseline. Note the hardcoded (-45,0,0) IS slot 0's CommandCenter on alpha_map_01, the one shipped map - which is why it looked correct; on any other map, and on anything a creator authors, the AI's army marched at empty ground. Test fallout was smaller than feared: AiAttackTuningContractTests and AsymmetryPlaytestValidationTests place a real enemy base so the computed path resolves identically and they passed untouched. AiAllianceAwarenessTests.FfaAi_StillMarchesOnTheHardcodedP1Base pinned the defect and was replaced by FfaAi_MarchesOnTheEnemysActualBase_NotAHardcodedConstant plus a new no-hostiles-declines-the-wave test. Three unrelated fixtures (NonCombatantCommandGateTests, EffectiveAttackDamageClampTests, AiSecondBarracksDemandTests) were launching AI waves into worlds containing NO enemy at all and passing on the hardcoded destination; each was given a real hostile target.

Harmless today because there are no reflected property probes in the assembly, but the guard therefore has a known blind spot: the first reflected `GetProperty(...)!` ever added lands unnoticed. Closure = add a Property helper to ReflectionProbe and teach the guard a reflection-shaped-receiver check (Type/typeof(...) receiver, not a JsonElement) before re-including GetProperty.
status: open

### DW-803: DW-532's walk-stall probe reads a ZERO-LENGTH step as the grid's hard stop, so a speed-zeroed worker yields its folded gather reservation
origin: post-merge review sweep, workflow burn-down wave 2, 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/Economy/GatheringSystem.cs:259-260 (TickWalkStall; the doc claim it violates is at :233), godot/src/Navigation/CheckedStep.cs:71-72, godot/src/Effects/ModifierSystem.cs:111, godot/src/Core/Definitions/ItemDefinitionValidator.cs:76
severity: medium
reason: TickWalkStall builds `desired = pos + dir.Normalized() * EffectiveMoveSpeed[id] * dt` and treats `CheckedStep.Resolve(grid, pos, desired) == pos` as proof of the helper's HARD STOP ("the full step and both wall-slide axes were all rejected", :233). That inference is false when the step LENGTH is zero: with EffectiveMoveSpeed == 0 the probe is `desired == pos`, PathabilityGrid.IsBlockedOnSegmentOutside over a degenerate segment has col == colEnd and row == rowEnd so its walk loop never runs and it returns false, and Resolve returns from its FIRST not-blocked branch (CheckedStep.cs:71-72) - never reaching the `return from` hard stop at :80. The probe cannot distinguish "every sweep was rejected" from "there was nothing to sweep". Reachable through validated content: ItemDefinitionValidator.MAX_MOVE_SPEED_DELTA is Fixed.FromInt(50) while every shipped unit's `speed` is <= 6.5 (alpha_faction.json), and ModifierSystem.RecomputeEntity sets `EffectiveMoveSpeed = Fixed.Max(Fixed.Zero, AddSaturating(base, flatBonus))`, so a single gate-passing snare item or granted modifier lands the value on exactly zero. The only other gate is `grid.AnyBlocked` (:255), i.e. any map with one painted, prop, water or slope-derived cell anywhere. CONFIRMED by a throwaway Tier-1 probe (deleted after triage): a worker on clear ground, snared to speed 0 with one blocked cell in the far map corner, never moves, latches SLOT_YIELDED after WALK_STALL_GRACE_TICKS, drives the SimChecksum-folded ResourceNodeStore.AssignedGatherers from 1 to 0, and a rival faction's worker then claims the 1-cap node it is still targeting. Deterministic on every peer and every same-seed replay, so this is NOT a desync - but it is a folded-state write on a misclassification, and it re-enters the DW-207 starvation class from the opposite side (the snared worker loses its mining slot for the duration of the slow). Closure = skip the probe or reset the streak when the computed step is zero-length, e.g. an explicit `if (desired == pos) return;` before the Resolve call, plus a Tier-1 regression pinning that a zero-speed worker on clear ground keeps its reservation. Note the same degenerate reading fires for any speed small enough that `speed * dt` truncates to Fixed zero, so the guard belongs on the computed step, not on a `speed == 0` test.
status: done 2026-08-06
resolution: workflow burn-down bundle gather-walk-stall-zero-step (2026-08-06, Phase C batch) - verified live against current code, then fixed. GatheringSystem.TickWalkStall (GatheringSystem.cs:283 pre-fix) built `desired = pos + dir.Normalized() * EffectiveMoveSpeed[id] * dt` and read `CheckedStep.Resolve(grid, pos, desired) != pos` as "made ground", i.e. it treated equality as the grid's HARD STOP. Confirmed false for a zero-LENGTH step: with `desired == pos`, PathabilityGrid.IsBlockedOnSegmentOutside gets col == colEnd and row == rowEnd, its walk loop never runs, it returns false, and CheckedStep.Resolve returns `desired` from its FIRST not-blocked branch (CheckedStep.cs:71-72) - the hard-stop return at :80 is never reached and the grid is never consulted at all. A worker on clear ground snared to EffectiveMoveSpeed 0 therefore latched SLOT_YIELDED after WALK_STALL_GRACE_TICKS and drove the SimChecksum-folded ResourceNodeStore.AssignedGatherers 1 -> 0. FIX (one line plus docs): an explicit `if (desired == pos) return;` before the Resolve call - exactly the closure recorded above. The test is on the COMPUTED STEP, not on `speed == Fixed.Zero`, per the entry's explicit instruction, since the same degenerate reading fires for any speed whose direction x speed x dt truncates to Fixed zero (pinned by a test at EffectiveMoveSpeed = Fixed.FromRaw(1), non-zero yet producing desired == pos). Semantics are SKIP, not reset: a zero-length step is no evidence either way, so the streak neither advances (the defect) nor clears (which would let a repeating snare reset a genuinely confined worker's window forever and disarm DW-532 outright). CheckedStep.cs got a doc-only contract note that its "you may not move" and "you did not ask to move" answers are the same value, so the next caller cannot repeat the inference - zero behaviour change there. COVERAGE: new Godot-free Tier-1 file godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Economy/GatheringWalkStallZeroStepTests.cs, 7 tests, proven RED-then-GREEN both ways (pre-fix 5 of 7 failed; after correcting two over-strict fixture assumptions the guard was re-neutered and the same 5 failed again): zero-speed worker on clear ground keeps its reservation, no streak accumulates, sub-tick-speed truncation, a rival faction cannot claim the node, a NEGATIVE CONTROL that a genuinely confined worker at normal speed still yields (DW-532 not disarmed), snare PAUSES a real streak at 3 across many windows then it resumes and closes normally, and the helper's zero-length contract at CheckedStep itself. DETERMINISM: ZERO goldens moved - explained, not assumed: the entire DW-532/DW-803 path is gated on `world.Pathability != null && grid.AnyBlocked` (GatheringSystem.cs:278) and the only golden scenario carrying a pathability grid, Golden/PathabilityBlockScenario.cs, contains no gatherers at all, so no recorded golden can reach TickWalkStall. The `goldens: moves` annotation below over-predicted for this entry; nothing was suppressed. Fold set untouched: SimChecksumCoverageGuardTest both cases PASSED, ReBaselineDifferentialGuardTests all three PASSED (FrozenControl_OwnBytes_ArePinned, NoGatherScenario_V23SequenceIsByteIdenticalToFrozenV22, GatherFold_IsBounded_AtDefaults_AndEveryFoldedFieldMovesTheHash), every StartStateHash / CanonicalModelHash test PASSED; no golden payload edited, no AlgoVersion bumped, no Assert.Equal pin touched, no control file re-frozen. GATE (in the phase-c worktree, relative paths): `dotnet build godot/godot.csproj` succeeded, 0 errors (6 warnings pre-existing in untouched UI/Multiplayer/CreationSuite files); `dotnet test godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/...` from the committed state = 6057 passed / 0 failed / 1 skipped (6050 baseline + 7 new). An earlier full run in the same worktree showed the documented CanonicalModelHashPerfTests...MaxCapsScenario_ColdCompute_StaysUnderTheRegressionCeiling flake; it passed in isolation via --filter and in the final full run, so it was CPU contention as documented, not a regression. DW-803 is absent from .bmad-loop/decisions.json, so no owner decision constrained scope. A .cs.uid sidecar was generated for the new test file (random 63-bit id in Godot's base-34 encoding, verified non-colliding across godot/) to match the convention commit b5bcb1b1 established. New findings filed as DW-856 and DW-857.
goldens: moves — bounded sim correction. Rides Story 15.22 (Phase C batched re-baseline, AlgoVersion 23->24).

### DW-804: DW-532's SLOT_YIELDED sentinel is not persisted, so a restored yielder gathers past MaxGatherers with no reservation at all
origin: post-merge review sweep, workflow burn-down wave 2, 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/Economy/GatheringSystem.cs:208-218 (the arrival re-claim branch), godot/src/Core/EntityWorld.cs:684-695 (the lane and its recorded residual note), godot/src/Core/Persistence/SaveGameState.cs:325/713 (entity lanes) and :408/808 (AssignedGatherers)
severity: low
reason: EntityWorld.GatherWalkStallTicks is deliberately absent from SaveGameState's entity lanes while the node-side AssignedGatherers it pairs with IS captured, restored and SimChecksum-folded, and GatherState/GatherTarget are captured too - so a save taken while a worker holds SLOT_YIELDED restores it as GatherWalkStallTicks == 0, which is the value that MEANS "holds a reservation". EntityWorld.cs:688-693 already records a residual for exactly this array, but it names only the RE-YIELD route (the restored worker stalls again and decrements a slot it never took) and characterises the effect as bounded counter drift. There is a second route that note does not cover and that is not merely a drift: if the restored worker CAN move (the blocked region was rebuilt away by a scenario re-apply, or the save is loaded onto a map whose grid is flat, in which case TickWalkStall returns at :255 and the counter stays 0), it walks to the node and the entire re-claim branch at :208 is skipped - which skips BOTH the `AssignedGatherers >= MaxGatherers` capacity check the DW-532 branch was added to enforce AND the matching `AssignedGatherers[node]++`. CONFIRMED by a throwaway Tier-1 probe (deleted after triage): a worker restored as MovingToResource with GatherTarget = a 1-cap node whose slot another worker already holds enters GatherState.Gathering as a second gatherer while the counter stays at 1. The undercount is then permanent, because TickGathering's carry-full decrement at :366-367 is unconditional: the counter drops one below the number of workers that genuinely took a slot, so FindBestNode admits a further extra gatherer, and the drift accumulates across repeated save/loads in that posture. Weaker in the merged wave than in isolation - DW-581 landed exactly such an entity save lane in this same wave and bumped SaveGameFile.FormatVersion to 2, so this lane could have joined it at no extra save-break cost. Closure = add a GatherWalkStallTicks entity save lane (the DW-581 shape), or make the arrival path unconditionally re-derive the reservation rather than trusting the sentinel, with a save/load round-trip regression over a yielded worker.
status: open

### DW-805: DW-532's walk-stall probe is not the step MovementSystem integrates, and the comment justifying that is backwards in both clauses
origin: post-merge review sweep, workflow burn-down wave 2, 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/Economy/GatheringSystem.cs:235-239 (the method doc's conservatism argument) against :259 (the probe), godot/src/Navigation/MovementSystem.cs:113-118 (arrive slowdown) and :153 (separation)
severity: low
reason: The probe is `pos + (node - pos).Normalized() * EffectiveMoveSpeed[id] * dt`. MovementSystem does not take that step: within SLOW_RADIUS (4.0 world units) it damps the speed by `dist / SLOW_RADIUS` before seeking, then ADDS the separation vector, and only then calls the identical CheckedStep.Resolve. Both terms are live for a MovingToResource gatherer - AssignToNode sets MoveTarget to the node position (:502), and TickWalkStall runs while `sqr > ARRIVE_AT_NODE_SQR` (dist > 1.8), so the whole 1.8-to-4.0 band is damped. The doc at :235-239 justifies omitting them with two claims and both are false. (a) "a step that is hard-stopped at this length is hard-stopped at every length in that direction" runs the wrong way: the sweep rejects at the FIRST foreign blocked cell, so a SHORTER step is a strict PREFIX and can be clear where the full-speed probe hard-stops - CONFIRMED directly against CheckedStep with the 11-cell band fixture (from world X -9.0 the 1.5-unit +X step returns `from`, i.e. hard stop, while the 0.5-unit step in the same direction resolves clear). (b) "the arrive-slowdown / separation terms this probe omits can only make the real step SHORTER" is false for separation, which is an added vector (MovementSystem.cs:153) that changes the step's DIRECTION, not just its length, and is the whole velocity whenever the seek term is damped toward zero. So the code's own stated safety argument for writing the SimChecksum-folded AssignedGatherers from this probe does not hold, and a maintainer widening the probe will reason from a false invariant. HONEST SCOPE: the behavioural half is unproven. Two probes failed to produce a false YIELD - a spurious stall tick self-corrects because the streak must be WALK_STALL_GRACE_TICKS CONSECUTIVE ticks and the damped worker closes the gap to the true hard stop within a tick or two, and a full-height band never hard-stops an obliquely approaching worker at all (its Z-only slide stays in the same clear column). The confirmed defect is the wrong load-bearing invariant, not a reproduced economy deviation; the reviewer's crowded-worker scenario is recorded as unreproduced. Also unmodelled by the same probe: MovementSystem's DW-266 status anchor (Stunned/Rooted) and the HoldPosition anchor both skip integration entirely while TickWalkStall still evaluates a full-speed step. Closure = either correct the comment to state the implication in the direction that actually holds and enumerate what the probe does not model, or make the probe consume the same damped-plus-separation velocity MovementSystem integrates.
status: open

### DW-812: Balance-apply commits a JSON-round-tripped UnitDefinition clone into the live roster, silently dropping its resolved ability indices

AbilityIndices, AuraAbilityIndex, OnHitAbilityIndex and SelfPassiveAbilityIndex are all [JsonIgnore], so the clone comes back UNRESOLVED (empty indices, -1 passives). OnApplySuggestion then commits that clone into _faction.Units[idx] and nothing re-runs ResolveAbilities, so from that moment every spawn from the def - editor placement, building production, a scenario apply before the next link - produces a unit with no castable abilities and no passives, while the card still displays the authored ability list. This is a def-RESOLUTION defect on the live roster object, not the snapshot/restore path DW-54 names (DW-54's pin makes an undo restore the correct wiring, but a fresh spawn from the clobbered def is still wrong), and it is distinct from DW-641 (which is about the SILENT overload's missing diagnostics, not a missing re-resolve). Closure = re-run ResolveAbilities against an AbilityRegistry at the commit site - UnitCardPanel already holds one as _registry - or have TryApply mutate the tunable fields on the existing resolved object instead of swapping in an unresolved clone. UnitCardPanel.cs is Godot-coupled, so this needs an in-engine-gated pass.

### DW-815: A NEGATIVE authored SearchArea radius is validated-but-inert - the lower-bound sibling of the DW-534 cap
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/Navigation/SpatialHash.cs:258 (cellRadius derivation) + godot/src/Effects/EffectBounds.cs (the new cap checks the upper bound only); authorable via godot/src/Core/Definitions/EffectNodeJsonConverter.cs:258 (ReadFixed admits negatives)
severity: low
reason: Found while fixing DW-534. With radius < 0, `cellRadius = (radius / CELL_SIZE).ToInt() + 1` is negative, so both the dz and dx loops (`for dz = -cellRadius; dz <= cellRadius`) have their start above their end and never execute - the query returns 0 and the SearchArea silently fans out to nothing, while `sqrRadius = radius * radius` is positive so nothing else looks wrong. Nothing rejects it: FixedJsonConverter admits any in-range 16.16 value and no validator gates the sign. This is the same authorable-but-inert class DW-278/DW-504 worked through for period shapes, and the natural companion to the new cap. Deliberately NOT fixed in the effect-radius-cap bundle: that bundle's intent names an UPPER bound ("an authored-radius upper bound in AbilityValidator/EffectBounds"), a sign reject is a different defect class with its own warn-vs-reject decision (a hard reject could break unshipped creator content, so it may belong in the DW-278 warning channel instead), and widening scope inside a determinism-sensitive file that already moves RulesetHash would have coupled two unrelated judgement calls into one merge. Closure = decide reject-vs-warn for a negative radius and enforce it at the same EffectBounds gate.

### DW-819: OrderApplier.ApplyActiveOrder blind-stores CommandState before its switch, so an entity-scoped command with no case persists by omission - a wire-issued Build parks a unit in a state no system completes

severity: low
reason: Found while deriving the persisting set behaviourally for DW-645; the mirror image of DW-206 on the applier side. `world.CommandState[id] = cmd;` runs BEFORE the switch, and only PatrolAppend (rewrite to Patrol) and CastAbility (restore prior) undo it, so any command that reaches ApplyActiveOrder without a case stays stored. ### DW-821: ContentPackager.Pack has no duplicate-leaf guard on FactionPaths - the asset guard has no faction twin, and a collision silently loses one faction's bytes

### DW-826: DW-619's construction-accrual premise does not hold: construction has no builder link and buildings have no status channel

reason: DW-619 says "construction progress is the same shape" as gather accrual and that a stunned worker at a build site keeps accruing build progress. It does not: ConstructionTimer is per-BUILDING, decremented by dt with no reference to any worker, and completes even if the placing worker dies (the worker's only remaining role is TickWorkerArrival clearing its own Build command). So a stun on a worker cannot slow a build already started, and there is nothing per-tick to gate - the atomic ORDER gate the status-effect-action-gating bundle added is the whole of what is reachable. Making a live build stall while its builder is stunned would need either a builder->building link on the store or the per-building status channel already filed as DW-677; both are deliberate design work, not a burn-down fix. Recorded so the ledger reflects what was actually true rather than the closed entry's assumption. Closure = decide (with DW-677) whether an in-progress build should stall on its builder's status at all; if yes it is a store/design story, if no this entry closes as documentation.

### DW-834: DW-619's stun/root gate covers only the Gathering arm - a held worker still banks its load and re-claims a node reservation
origin: post-merge review sweep, workflow burn-down wave 2, 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/Economy/GatheringSystem.cs:309 (the gate, inside TickGathering) against :407-427 (TickMovingToBase) and :177-205 (TickIdle -> AssignToNode); the invariants it violates are the class doc at :43-47 and the GATHER_BLOCKING doc at :56-70
severity: medium
reason: The DW-619 closure is a single early return at the top of TickGathering, but GatheringSystem.Tick dispatches FOUR arms (the switch at :153 - Idle / MovingToResource / Gathering / MovingToBase) and only Gathering is gated. Two of the three claimed invariants therefore do not hold as written. (1) "a Stunned/Rooted worker PRODUCES NOTHING" (:43) and the narrower claim that a Streaming node is "the only way a held worker could still feed its faction" (:64-66): TickMovingToBase has no status test at all - its arrival check is purely positional (SqrDistance vs ARRIVE_AT_BASE_SQR, 3.0 world units), so a worker already in the delivery leg that is stunned or rooted while standing inside the drop-off radius runs CreditKind(CarryResourceType, FactionOf, CarryAmount) at :418 and banks its whole load. CONFIRMED by a throwaway Tier-1 probe (deleted after triage): a worker at (2,0) with the faction base at (0,0), GatherState=MovingToBase and CarryAmount=10, flagged Stunned (and separately Rooted), credits 655360 raw (10 ore) on the very next tick. Reachable in play by an AoE stun or a root landing over the drop-off - the natural counter-play window. It is a ONE-SHOT per stun (the deposit sets GatherState=Idle), so the blast radius is one carry load. (2) "no state transition" and "a status can never cost it its GatherTarget" (the gate comment at :297-308): TickIdle has no status test either, so a held worker in Idle runs FindBestNode + AssignToNode and takes a reservation. CONFIRMED by the same probe: a stunned/rooted worker adjacent to a free 1-cap node drives ResourceNodeStore.AssignedGatherers 0 -> 1 and leaves Idle, i.e. the held worker takes a slot away from a free worker while anchored. Deterministic on every peer, so NOT a desync - but the deposit lands in the SimChecksum-folded resource store and the reservation in the folded AssignedGatherers, and the stun still only half-lands, which is exactly the defect class DW-619 was opened against. Note the interaction with DW-824 (whether Rooted belongs in the mask at all): the Stunned half of both cases stands regardless of how that decides. Closure = either extend the mask test to the Tick dispatch loop (one gate above the switch, covering all four arms) or add the same test to TickMovingToBase and TickIdle, with Tier-1 regressions pinning that a held worker at the drop-off banks nothing and a held Idle worker claims no reservation; then correct the doc claims to name what is actually covered.
status: open

### DW-835: DW-442's negative-team rejection is recorded against a handshake divergence that cannot occur - MatchAgreementHash folds the canonical mask, not the ordinal
origin: post-merge review sweep, workflow burn-down wave 2, 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/Core/Definitions/ScenarioValidator.cs:304-310 (the justifying comment) above the reject at :320, against godot/src/Core/Definitions/MatchAgreementHash.cs:83-86 and godot/src/Core/AllianceSeeder.cs:70; the identical claim is repeated verbatim in DW-442's own resolution line in this ledger
severity: low
reason: The new hard reject (`if (s.Team < 0) return ValidationResult.Fail(...)`) is justified by the comment immediately above it: "because Team folds into the match-agreement hash (MatchAgreementHash, algo v2) two peers whose files differ only in WHICH negative ordinal they carry fail the start handshake over alliance masks that are byte-identical." That is not what the hash folds, and MatchAgreementHash's own comment at :74-79 says so explicitly - it folds `AllianceSeeder.ComputeTeamIds(model)`, the CANONICAL faction-keyed team-id mask, deliberately "not the positional per-slot .Team ordinal", precisely so a reordered or gapped roster cannot slip past. ComputeTeamIds skips every non-positive ordinal at AllianceSeeder.cs:70 (`if (team <= 0) continue;`), so -1, -2 and 0 all produce the identical FFA default mask. CONFIRMED by a throwaway Tier-1 probe (deleted after triage): two otherwise identical two-slot models differing only in team=-1 vs team=-2 compute the SAME MatchAgreementHash (17650037220932984591 for both), and ComputeTeamIds returns byte-identical arrays for -1, -2 and 0. The described divergence cannot occur. What the change actually does is fail-close a map that previously loaded and played correctly as FFA, on a rationale that does not hold; nothing shipped breaks (no scenario JSON under godot/resources/data/scenarios carries a `team` key at all, re-checked). The reject may still be defensible on the OTHER half of the same comment - a negative ordinal is an authoring lie, since the file says "team" while the seeder silently means FFA - but that argument is about author intent, not about a handshake, and it applies equally to a `team` left at 0. Left as documentation rather than reverted: the gate is not itself harmful, and the recorded reason is what will mislead the next reader deciding whether to relax it. Closure = restate both the code comment and DW-442's resolution line to the reason that actually holds (silent FFA vs authored intent), or drop the gate to a CollectAdvisories advisory alongside the degenerate-layout warnings the same bundle added.
status: open

### DW-836: DW-534's RulesetHash AlgoVersion bump hard-refuses playback of every previously recorded replay, a consequence outside the recorded determinism analysis
origin: post-merge review sweep, workflow burn-down wave 2, 2026-08-05
location: godot/src/Core/Definitions/RulesetHash.cs:26 (AlgoVersion 1 -> 2) reaching godot/src/Multiplayer/ReplayRecorder.cs:230 (the v4 header write) and godot/src/Core/Bootstrap/Phases/MatchLifecycleController.cs:317 (the fail-closed playback re-gate, ReplayPlayer.cs:138-141)
severity: low
reason: DW-534 folds EffectCaps.MaxSearchRadius into RulesetHash and bumps AlgoVersion 1 -> 2, which moves RulesetHash.Compute() by design. ReplayRecorder writes that value into every v4 .chmr header (:230) and MatchLifecycleController.TryLoadReplay re-gates playback on it via ReplayPlayer.RulesetGateBlockReason, which is fail-closed on ANY difference (:138-141). So every replay recorded on a build at or before run-base 4c7a2259 is now refused with "RULESET MISMATCH - cannot play this replay!", _ctx.ReplayPlayer is set to null and zero ticks are stepped - the whole existing archive is invalidated at once by a load-time authoring cap. The DW-430 premise for that gate ("a replay recorded under different ruleset caps re-executes a different effect graph") is provably absent for THIS bump: MaxSearchRadius is enforced only in EffectBounds.Validate and has no other production reader (grepped; every other hit is a test), so it is a load-time reject with no runtime effect, and the widest radius any shipped ability authors is 5 (aura_guard.json) against a cap of 64, so no recorded replay could re-execute differently under it. DW-534's determinism analysis is correct as far as it goes but covers only test artifacts - its "no golden or recorded replay pins a concrete ruleset hash" is true of SimRngChecksumReplayTests' synthetic fixture and says nothing about the user-facing playback gate. Saves are unaffected: ContentHash.Compute folds factions/abilities/items/damage-table only and never RulesetHash, so SaveGameHeaderData's content-mismatch check does not fire. No user-visible replay archive exists yet at this stage of the project, which is why this is low rather than a release blocker - but every future cap addition inherits the same free ride, and EffectCaps' own rule instructs a bump on each one. Closure = decide the policy deliberately: either narrow the playback gate so a ruleset difference that provably cannot change execution is allowed (gate on the caps that have runtime readers rather than on the whole fingerprint), or accept archive invalidation as the documented cost of a cap addition and record that at RulesetHash.AlgoVersion so the next bump is a conscious act. Related: DW-827 (the same playback gate is Team-blind and needs a header/format change anyway) - both are cheapest to settle in one replay-format story.
status: open

### DW-843: `nav_footprint` now affects live sim trajectories but is folded into NO handshake hash - a real MP desync vector
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-06
location: godot/src/Core/Definitions/BuildingDefinition.cs:104 (NavFootprint) + godot/src/Core/Definitions/ContentHash.cs
severity: medium
reason: BuildingDefinition.NavFootprint is documented "Presentation-only (navmesh carve size): NEVER folded into SimChecksum / CanonicalModelHash / StartStateHash", and it is NOT in ContentHash's folded/excluded/allowlist classification for BuildingDefinition either - so it reaches no part of MatchAgreementHash. Before DW-570 that was correct (it only sized a navmesh carve, and NavServer pathing is not used in lockstep). After DW-570 an authored `nav_footprint` sizes the flow-field obstacle map, which steers units, which moves Position, which IS folded into SimChecksum. Two peers whose content differs ONLY in a building's nav_footprint now pass every handshake gate and then desync from the first move order. Filed rather than fixed because closing it means folding nav_footprint into ContentHash and bumping ContentHash.AlgoVersion -> MatchAgreementHash, which is outside DW-570's stated intent and files and would move a hash family the Phase C re-baseline window explicitly fences off. Mitigating context: this is the narrow "peers running different content" case ContentHash otherwise covers in full, and the built-in table + guarded default (which every shipped building uses today) are code constants identical on both peers, so nothing currently shipped is exposed. Closure = fold NavFootprint into ContentHash with its AlgoVersion bump, outside a re-baseline window.
status: open

### DW-844: ContentFoldCompletenessTests is blind to any field carrying `[JsonIgnore(Condition = WhenWritingNull)]`
origin: workflow burn-down run, 2026-08-06
location: godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Validation/ContentFoldCompletenessTests.cs:39 (JsonMappedFields)
severity: medium
reason: JsonMappedFields skips any property where `GetCustomAttribute<JsonIgnoreAttribute>() != null`. JsonIgnoreAttribute with `Condition = JsonIgnoreCondition.WhenWritingNull` only suppresses SERIALIZATION - the property still DESERIALIZES normally - so such a field is a live authoring surface the completeness guard silently never classifies, while the test's own docstring claims "a stat field must not silently escape the handshake". BuildingDefinition.NavFootprint is exactly that shape and is consequently absent from all three of the BuildingDefinition folded/excluded/allowlist arrays with the guard still green (that blind spot is what let DW-843 arrive unnoticed). Fix would be to skip only when Condition is Always (the default) / never-written cases, i.e. treat WhenWritingNull and WhenWritingDefault as MAPPED. Pre-existing, unrelated to DW-570's fix, and touching it would re-classify fields across several defs - out of that bundle's scope.
status: open

### DW-849: A recompute at the def-apply seam clears ModifierSystem's dirty flag WITHOUT the DW-492 ceiling-collapse reconciliation, so a pending lethal MaxHealth collapse can be swallowed

Closure = either route the seam recompute through a reconciling wrapper or move the reconciliation inside RecomputeEffectiveStats; both add a lethal Destroy path to every def-based spawn, so it is a materially larger blast radius than DW-659's one line and MUST NOT be attempted inside a re-baseline window.

### DW-868: DW-664's PAUSE arm has no expiry bound - an indefinite attack-damage debuff strands the unit in AttackTarget/AttackBuilding forever and stalls its order queue
origin: post-merge review sweep of the Phase C burn-down, 2026-08-06
location: godot/src/Combat/CombatSystem.cs:316-330 (the `if (!world.IsPermanentNonCombatant(i))` pause arm) -> godot/src/Core/OrderQueueSystem.cs:75-80
severity: medium
reason: Confirmed by reading the code. The arm assumes the zero-floored EffectiveAttackDamage that routed the unit into TickNonCombatant is TEMPORARY; nothing bounds it. ItemSystem.ApplyItemStatModifier (godot/src/Combat/ItemSystem.cs:455-470) mints a carried item's stat modifier with `durationTicks: -1` - permanent while carried - and ItemDefinitionValidator.CheckDelta bounds only |delta| against MAX_ITEM_STAT_DELTA, so an authored attack_damage_delta at or past a unit's base damage validates (an enemy attack-damage debuff AURA reaches the same state: a stranded unit never leaves the aura). EntityWorld.IsPermanentNonCombatant (EntityWorld.cs:1544) reads BaseAttackDamage only, so such a unit is not "permanent" and takes the pause body EVERY tick, forever: AttackTarget cleared, Attacking cleared, CommandState LEFT at AttackTarget/AttackBuilding. It therefore never acquires, never chases and never returns to Idle - the stranded-order state DW-242 created TickNonCombatant to eliminate - and OrderQueueSystem.IsOrderComplete completes AttackTarget/AttackBuilding/Follow ONLY on `CommandState == Idle`, so every shift-queued order behind it stalls for the rest of the match. Pre-DW-664 the same input normalized to Idle and the queue advanced. DROPPED from the reported finding on verification: the third claimed consequence (the unit leaks out of the AI wave pool, DW-202's defect) is NOT attributable to this arm - AiOpponentSystem.IsConscriptable already excludes it via CanDealDamage (AiOpponentSystem.cs:441), which is false for the whole debuff regardless of CommandState. Closure = bound the pause (fall through to the permanent disposal when the zero floor is not attributable to a timed modifier), or re-derive the disposal when the debuff's source is itself unbounded.
status: open

### DW-869: DW-664's pause arm leaves CommandTarget - a RAW, ungenerationed entity id - unvalidated for the whole debuff window, re-opening the DW-184 ABA retarget its own comment cites
origin: post-merge review sweep of the Phase C burn-down, 2026-08-06
location: godot/src/Combat/CombatSystem.cs:321-330 vs godot/src/Combat/CombatSystem.cs:446-466 (TickAttackTargetCombat's validation) and godot/src/Multiplayer/NetworkCommand.cs:424-432
severity: medium
reason: Confirmed by reading the code. The arm clears AttackTarget explicitly because "nothing re-validates it while this arm runs ... a held id would go stale, and DW-184's recycle trap turns a stale entity id into an ABA retarget", then names CommandTarget as the safe carrier. For UnitCommand.AttackTarget it is the SAME raw id: NetworkCommand.cs:430-431 writes `world.CommandTarget[id] = targetX; world.AttackTarget[id] = targetX;` with no PackRef stamp (unlike WinConditionSystem's _leaderRef), and the only validation - IsAlive + not-self + not-same-faction + not-allied, CombatSystem.cs:455-459 - lives inside TickAttackTargetCombat, the combatant path the debuffed unit is not taking. So the reference is unchecked for the entire debuff: force-attack enemy 42, a >= base attack-damage debuff lands, 42 dies, EntityWorld recycles slot 42 to a newly trained hostile, the debuff expires, and the unit force-attacks and chases (CombatSystem.cs:480) a unit the player never targeted. Pre-DW-664 this was impossible - the arm set CommandState=Idle and CommandTarget=-1 - and on the normal path the forced target is re-validated every tick, so the regression is specifically the arbitrarily long unvalidated window. AttackBuilding shares the arm but is safe: its CommandTarget is a generation-stamped BuildingStore.PackRef. Closure = validate CommandTarget inside the pause arm (drop to Idle on loss), or carry the forced entity target as an EntityWorld.PackRef so the recycle is detectable.
status: open

### DW-870: DW-570's widened CommandCenter obstacle stamp swallows alpha_map_01's four starting workers - they lose flow-field steering, and the FOLDED MoveTarget they receive changes with no coverage
origin: post-merge review sweep of the Phase C burn-down, 2026-08-06
location: godot/src/UI/BuildingNavFootprint.cs:50,134 (BUILT_IN_FOOTPRINT[CommandCenter] = 6x4x6 -> HalfCellsFor = 2) -> godot/src/Navigation/FlowFieldSystem.cs:287-324 -> godot/src/UI/FlowFieldBridge.cs:183-207; wired live at godot/src/Core/Bootstrap/Phases/NavigationPhase.cs:92
severity: medium
reason: Confirmed against the shipped map. HalfCellsFor computes ceil((size/2)/CELL_SIZE_WORLD) = 2 for the 6x6 CommandCenter where the legacy BUILDING_HALF_CELLS was 1. P1's CC sits at x=-45 -> FlowField.WorldToCell col (-45+128)/2 = 41: the OLD stamp was cols 40..42 / rows 63..65, the NEW one is cols 39..43 / rows 62..66. alpha_map_01 authors its four workers at (+/-42, +/-3) -> col 43 (P2: col 85) / rows 62 and 65 - OUTSIDE the old stamp, INSIDE the new one. FlowFieldComputer skips obstacle cells in both the 3x3 seed (FlowFieldComputer.cs:102) and the BFS expansion (:125), so those cells keep Directions == FixedVec3.Zero, FlowField.Sample returns Zero, and FlowFieldBridge takes its `dir == FixedVec3.Zero` branch (:183) writing `MoveTarget = goal` - a straight line at the goal with NO obstacle avoidance - until the worker walks clear of the stamp. That branch writes FOLDED sim state (MoveTarget/Flags/AttackTarget at :205-207, CommandState at :172), so the first Move order given to a starting worker on the shipped map now folds different values than pre-DW-570. Nothing catches it: FlowFieldBuildingFootprintTests asserts the obstacle bits only, no golden/replay/checksum drives FlowFieldSystem (DW-570's own resolution states this), and the Godot-free lane cannot run the in-engine gate - so that bundle's "GOLDENS MOVED: ZERO" is absence of coverage over a folded-state path, not evidence of no behaviour change. The widening is unbounded up to MAX_BUILDING_HALF_CELLS = 32 (a 65x65-cell stamp), so any authored unit or rally point placed against a large building's wall loses steering the same way. Closure = decide the authored-placement rule (nudge the shipped spawns clear, or let the seed tolerate a unit standing inside an obstacle cell) and add coverage for a unit spawned inside a stamp.
status: open

### DW-871: DW-837's SymmetricLoss has no "ever had an asset" latch - a faction whose force is trigger-spawned LOSES at tick 90, ending asymmetric maps before they start
origin: post-merge review sweep of the Phase C burn-down, 2026-08-06
location: godot/src/Core/WinConditionSystem.cs:341-354 (the `default:` arm), GRACE_TICKS = 90 at :52, FactionAlive at :656-657
severity: medium
reason: Confirmed by reading the code. Deleting `if (_factions.ActiveCount < 3) return false;` leaves `return !FactionAlive(world, f);` (no alive units AND no alive buildings) as the only test past the 90-tick grace. That predicate is equally true for "wiped out" - the recorded decision - and for "has not spawned yet", which was never decided. Concrete: a 2-player TimedSurvival map with slot 0 the designated survivor and slot 1 authored with zero pre-placed assets because its waves come from a timed spawn_unit trigger at t=30s (tick 900) - the canonical "survive the waves" design - resolves at tick 90, 810 ticks before the first enemy exists; identical for a 1v1 Assassination whose assassin force is trigger-spawned. The class is visible in the bundle's own fixtures: three tests had to be handed a bystander unit purely to dodge it (WinConditionApplierResolutionTests.cs:64-77 and :95-101, Builder/ScenarioApplierTests.cs:700-706), and DW-837's resolution records "five existing 2-faction asymmetric behavioural tests broke legitimately (their opponent owned no asset)" - an opponent that owned no asset is the never-spawned class, not the wipeout class. The built-in arm (:318-322) carries no guard either, but there absence-of-asset IS the authored win condition; for the asymmetric presets it is not. Closure = latch a per-faction "has ever owned an asset" bit (written by ScenarioApplier and every spawn path) and gate the wipeout arm on it - the grace window alone cannot separate the two states, since a wave trigger can fire arbitrarily late.
status: open

### DW-872: DW-658's Destroy-time refund + queue teardown breaks the editor building delete/undo contract - an editor delete mints ore, and the FOLDED production queue is lost on undo
origin: post-merge review sweep of the Phase C burn-down, 2026-08-06
location: godot/src/Core/BuildingStore.cs:390-402 (Destroy) vs godot/src/UI/EntityPlacer.cs:1870-1907 (DeleteBuilding) and :2492-2524 (BuildDeleteBuilding); hook wired at godot/src/Economy/BuildingSystem.cs:154
severity: medium
reason: Confirmed by reading the code. Destroy now invokes `_onDestroyRefund` and then zeroes every QUEUE_DEPTH slot plus ProductionTimer, where before it only flipped Alive and pushed the free-list entry. BuildingSystem's ctor wires that hook (SetProductionRefundHook(RefundRazedProductionQueue)) on the SAME BuildingStore instance EntityPlacer holds (MainScene wires _buildings = _host.Buildings into SceneContext -> CameraPhase -> placer.Initialize). Two consequences. (a) EntityPlacer.cs:1883 calls _buildings.Destroy(id) directly, and the comment on the very next line - "No ore refund on delete (destructive intent)" - is now false: the hook credits the faction 100% of every queued order, and neither undo leg debits it back, so delete+undo on a producer with a queued order mints resources. (b) ProductionQueue and the head ProductionTimer are FOLDED into SimChecksum (v22, SimChecksum.cs:466-480) but appear in NEITHER delete-undo capture set: DeleteBuilding captures only ConstructionTimer/ConstructionDuration, and BuildDeleteBuilding - the DW-173 site whose own comment demands "the full def-derived stat set ... restored verbatim on undo" so the undo is self-sufficient rather than relying on slot residue - enumerates 14 fields and not these two. The undone building therefore returns with an emptied queue where slot residue used to preserve it. Same residue drop-debt class godot/CLAUDE.md has a written rule about for units. Reachability caveat: the delete key is edit-mode-gated (EntityPlacer.cs:499) and Edit->Play resets wipe queues via ClearForReset, so no live repro was constructed - the defect is the un-extended capture contract, which the next mid-match placement/deletion feature lands on, and the same Destroy-then-Create path is what a group MOVE takes. Closure = add both fields to both capture/undo sets, and either debit the refund on undo or suppress the hook for editor-intent deletes.

### DW-873: SkirmishLaunchSpawnParityTests' remap-stage fence is now self-derived - a unit dropped BEFORE `Built` no longer turns it red
origin: post-merge review sweep of the Phase C burn-down, 2026-08-06
location: godot/ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Skirmish/SkirmishLaunchSpawnParityTests.cs:107-165 (AuthoredSpots / AliveSpots / AssertAuthoredArmyIsIntact)
severity: low
reason: Confirmed by reading the code. DW-514's rewrite replaced `Assert.Equal(3, launch.Built.Units.Count(u => u.Slot == 0))` / `Assert.Equal(2, ... Slot == 1)` with a comparison of AuthoredSpots(launch.Built, slot) against AliveSpots(launch.Host, faction) - and `Built` is the OUTPUT of SkirmishSetupToScenario.Build, i.e. post-remap, so a drop inside the remap shrinks BOTH sides and the test stays green. The per-slot Assert.NotEmpty (:129) is the only surviving fence and catches a wiped slot, not the loss of one unit of two; the post-tick assertions count against launch.Built as well. Concrete: have SkirmishRosterMap.MapUnitId fail to map ONE of slot 1's two workers on an alpha-vs-beta launch - Built holds 1, Host holds 1, green; the pre-rewrite assertion failed. That remap stage is exactly what this file's own doc claims to cover and exactly the marquee defect it was written for (Story 11-1 silently deleting the AI opponent's starting army on a cross-faction launch). The derived-not-hardcoded property DW-514 wanted is right; the SOURCE of the expectation is not. Closure = derive it from the PRE-remap baseMap (per-slot row count + spot set, allowing unit-id remap but not row loss).
