### DW-874: SimChecksum.AlgoVersion's "NO consumer anywhere in godot/src" is false - SaveGameFile stamps and hard-rejects on it, so the v24 bump invalidates every pre-Phase-C save
origin: post-merge review sweep of the Phase C burn-down, 2026-08-06
location: godot/src/Core/SimChecksum.cs:296-298 (the v24 doc note, repeated verbatim in commit ad6eceb1) vs godot/src/Core/Persistence/SaveGameFile.cs:64 and :114-118
severity: medium
reason: Confirmed by reading the code. SaveGameFile.Write stamps SimChecksum.AlgoVersion into every .chsav header, and Read compares it before the body is parsed, throwing InvalidDataException ("made by a different game version (simulation format changed) - it can no longer be loaded") on any mismatch. A save written by a pre-Phase-C build stamps 23 and is therefore permanently unloadable on this build. Because v24 is by design a pure RE-RECORD GENERATION MARKER - the fold is byte-for-byte v23, SimChecksumCoverageGuardTest's known-state hash 0x32911831 did not move, and the sim state in those saves is still structurally readable - this is precisely the gratuitous break the note's own reasoning says cannot happen. No shipped saves exist, so the practical cost today is zero; the note is wrong in the one respect that matters, and it is the standing reference for what a future AlgoVersion bump costs. (Separately: the post-merge DW-548 fix bumped SaveGameFile.FormatVersion 2 -> 3, which invalidates those same saves at the header for a genuine body-format reason.) Closure = correct the note to name SaveGameFile as the consumer and state that an AlgoVersion bump is a save-break, and decide whether a pure re-record marker should be a constant separate from the one saves gate on.
status: done 2026-08-06
decision: 2026-08-06 Alec — KEEP ONE CONSTANT, stay fail-closed. A pure re-record generation marker does NOT get a separate save-only world-format version; every AlgoVersion bump remains a save-break. Rationale: while the sim still changes every epic, a save that silently RESUMES under corrected combat/AI rules is a worse and much harder-to-diagnose failure than one that cleanly refuses to open — the v23-on-v24 case would continue a live match under twelve changed behaviours. The split is a one-way door in the safe direction: it can be introduced later, once re-records stop being routine, but a save that feels subtly broken cannot be un-shipped. REVISIT CONDITION: before 1.0 ships to players. The valid half of the objection — the gate's message claiming "simulation format changed" when a value-only re-record changed no format — is fixed rather than argued: SaveGameFile.Read now names the three actual version pairs instead.
progress: 2026-08-06 - the FALSE DOC HALF IS CORRECTED in SimChecksum.cs's v24 entry: it now names SaveGameFile as the consumer and states that any bump, re-record marker included, invalidates every older save. The claim originated in spec-15-22's brief and was traced to a grep truncated by `head -20`, which cut the godot/src hits off after the test-assembly ones - the spec and the worklist brief both carry the correction and the root cause. WHAT REMAINS OPEN is only the design question, which is Alec's call and NOT a dev-session decision: should a pure re-record generation marker share a constant with the one save loading gates on, or should the save header stamp a separate world-format version that a value-only re-record leaves alone? Note the two are genuinely different questions - a v23 save resumed on v24 code is structurally readable but its world would continue under twelve corrected behaviours, so fail-closed is defensible; the objection is that the gate's own message says 'simulation format changed', which is not what happened here.

### DW-875: Sculpted-map elevation read still routes the deterministic texel index through get_pixel's float world→texel path, and no end-to-end sculpted-map determinism test exists
origin: deferred by review of `spec-15-2-map-size-determinism-unification-raw-heightmap-read-dw-160-dw-146-dw-162.md`, 2026-08-06
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-15-2-map-size-determinism-unification-raw-heightmap-read-dw-160-dw-146-dw-162.md`
location: godot/src/Core/Bootstrap/Phases/ScenarioLoadPhase.cs:226-262 (BuildAndInjectElevationGrid) + godot/src/Core/HeightmapCellMapping.cs
severity: low
reason: DW-146's core intent (kill the get_height BILINEAR blend) is delivered — the read is now get_pixel nearest — but the review found three residual, forward-looking gaps on a path NO shipped/golden map reaches (every scenario is terrain_ref:"" flat, so the method early-returns before get_pixel). (1) The Godot-free HeightmapCellMapping.CellToTexel index is reconstructed back into a float world coord `wx = -half + (texel+0.5)*texelSize` and handed to get_pixel, which re-derives the texel from that float via Terrain3D's own float→texel mapping — so the sampled texel is not strictly chosen by the tested integer helper; the +0.5 centring avoids boundary landings but the guarantee is weaker than "pure integer index". (2) The sampler hardcodes half=128 / texelSize=256/regionSize, assuming every region spans exactly ±128 world units regardless of region_size × vertex_spacing; a region with non-256 size or non-unit spacing samples the wrong world coordinates. (3) No test samples a real non-flat heightmap through both get_height and the new get_pixel path to prove the "byte-identical, moves no golden" claim on sculpted terrain; TYPE_HEIGHT=0 is a bare magic constant and region_size is read assuming a plain Int variant. Evidence: Blind-Hunter F1/F2/F7/F8/F11 + Verification-Gap V2, all confirmed against the diff; zero reachability today. Closure (when sculpted terrain content and its own golden are first authored): read the region's raw TYPE_HEIGHT image indexed directly by integer texel (no world-coord round-trip), derive world coverage from region_size × vertex_spacing, and add an end-to-end sculpted-map determinism fixture.
status: open

### DW-876: Route C's visual border renders only on the fallback PlaneMesh — a bordered map on real Terrain3D pans the camera into void beyond the ±128 terrain edge
origin: deferred by review of `spec-15-2-map-size-determinism-unification-raw-heightmap-read-dw-160-dw-146-dw-162.md`, 2026-08-06
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-15-2-map-size-determinism-unification-raw-heightmap-read-dw-160-dw-146-dw-162.md`
location: godot/src/Core/Bootstrap/Phases/TerrainPhase.cs:22-42 (border sizing lives only in the terrain==null branch)
severity: low
reason: Confirmed by review (Blind-Hunter F3, corroborated by the in-engine gate auditor). Route C item 3 promises "terrain, water and scenery render across map_bounds + border_extent", and the camera pan-clamp + validator message + MapSize.cs doc all state "camera AND terrain". The implementation sizes only the fallback PlaneMesh (terrain==null branch); when a real Terrain3D node is present the region stays fixed at ±128 while the camera still pans to map_bounds+border_extent, so a bordered Terrain3D map would show empty void from ±128 to the visual edge. Unreachable on shipped content: both migrated bordered maps (map_10_mirror_lake +2, map_12_the_frontier +32) use terrain_ref:"" → the flat fallback plane, which IS border-sized correctly (verified in-engine, ±160). Deliberately narrowed by the 15.2 spec, whose determinism scope excluded Terrain3D region management. Closure (content-dependent): when a bordered map ships on real Terrain3D, extend the rendered terrain/scenery region — or the camera's terrain-edge treatment — to cover the border zone so the camera never reveals void.
status: open

### DW-877: Route C's fallback ground plane now SHRINKS below the ±128 sim extent on sub-128 maps, rendering void where forced movement can push entities
origin: deferred by review of `spec-15-2-map-size-determinism-unification-raw-heightmap-read-dw-160-dw-146-dw-162.md`, 2026-08-06
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-15-2-map-size-determinism-unification-raw-heightmap-read-dw-160-dw-146-dw-162.md`
location: godot/src/Core/Bootstrap/Phases/TerrainPhase.cs:22-42 (fallback PlaneMesh span = 2*(map_bounds+border_extent))
severity: low
reason: Confirmed by review (Blind-Hunter F7). Route C sizes the fallback PlaneMesh to the VISUAL extent `span = 2*(map_bounds + border_extent)`, replacing the former fixed 256×256. For a sub-128 map with no border this is now SMALLER than the old plane: Small (80) → 160×160, Medium (120) → 240×240, both under the 256 the fixed plane always provided. The four sim grids stay at ±128 (flow/fog/pathability) and placement is bounded to map_bounds, but forced movement (knockback, projectiles, forced-move triggers) can legitimately push an entity from ±map_bounds out toward ±128 — where it now renders over empty void instead of the old full 256 plane. Distinct from DW-876 (which is the real-Terrain3D branch not rendering the border): this is the terrain==null fallback branch shrinking below the sim extent on the LOW side. Unreachable/benign on shipped content: shipped maps load a real Terrain3D node (verified in-engine — the fallback branch is not taken), and where it is taken the visual glitch only appears at the sub-128 edge under forced displacement. Closure: floor the span to at least the sim-grid extent, `span = Max(2*(map_bounds + border_extent), 2*MapSizes.MaxHalfExtent)`, so the fallback plane can grow with a border but never shrink below ±128. NOTE: TerrainPhase is an in-engine-gate coupled surface — the fix requires the in-engine gate, and the fallback-plane path is not observable while a real Terrain3D node is present in the editor, so plan the gate environment accordingly.
status: open

### DW-878: map_bounds = NaN / non-finite bypasses the ScenarioValidator ceiling guard and now propagates into the camera's VisualHalfExtent
origin: deferred by review of `spec-15-2-map-size-determinism-unification-raw-heightmap-read-dw-160-dw-146-dw-162.md`, 2026-08-06
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-15-2-map-size-determinism-unification-raw-heightmap-read-dw-160-dw-146-dw-162.md`
location: godot/src/Core/Definitions/ScenarioValidator.cs:149-152 (map_bounds ceiling guard) + godot/src/Core/Bootstrap/Phases/ScenarioLoadPhase.cs (VisualHalfExtentOf)
severity: low
reason: Confirmed by review (Edge-Case-Hunter F3). The map_bounds ceiling guard tests only `m.MapBounds > MaxHalfExtent`; `NaN > 128` is false, so a NaN / non-finite map_bounds slips validation (pre-existing DW-158-era gap — this story did not touch the predicate). Story 15.2 newly makes map_bounds load-bearing for presentation: `VisualHalfExtentOf(s) = MapBounds + max(border,0)` runs post-validation (boot position 12) and sets the live camera pan clamp, so a NaN map_bounds now yields a NaN VisualHalfExtent / NaN pan clamp where the old fixed 128f could not. `PeekVisualHalfExtent` (position 5, sizes the fallback plane) already clamps non-finite map_bounds, so only the live camera-clamp path is exposed, and no authoring path emits NaN (it requires a hand-corrupted JSON). Border_extent IS finiteness-checked by this story; map_bounds is the sibling that still is not. Closure: add `if (!Finite(m.MapBounds) || m.MapBounds <= 0f) return Fail(...)` beside the existing ceiling guard so map_bounds is fail-closed on non-finite/degenerate values the same way border_extent now is.
status: open

### DW-879: No automated two-peer reconnect verification harness exists, so MP reconnect cannot prove its own acceptance criterion
origin: 15.1 dev-auto HALT (`bmad-dev-auto-result-15-1-mp-reconnect-v1-command-log-rejoin-fast-forward-catch-up-fr-79-dw-2.md`), 2026-08-06
location: godot/tests (no reconnect harness) + `LoopbackPeerSim` (lobby/desync self-tests only) + tools/verify-in-engine-gate.ps1
severity: medium
reason: Story 15.1's AC — "2-player LAN rejoin mid-match with post-catch-up checksum agreement; a failed content gate rejects the rejoin without disturbing the live match" — is inherently a TWO-PEER assertion, and nothing in the project can assert it. `LoopbackPeerSim` exercises lobby handshake and desync self-tests but never download-log -> fast-forward -> checksum-agrees; the DW-447 headless N-sim desync test that would have enabled it was scoped to 15-15 and did not land as a reconnect harness. Separately, the in-engine half is unobservable unattended: 15.1's wiring touches `MainScene.cs`, `godot/src/UI/LoadingScreenOverlay` and `Core/Bootstrap/MatchLifecycleController`, all coupled surfaces, so `tools/verify-in-engine-gate.ps1` demands an in-engine artifact — and a two-peer rejoin cannot be driven through the SINGLE-CLIENT godot-mcp bridge in one session. Consequence: 15.1 is mechanically unable to reach `done` in an unattended run regardless of implementation quality, which is why it HALTed in planning on 2026-08-06 rather than shipping an unverifiable MP diff. Closure = build a Godot-free loopback reconnect harness (DW-447-style, two in-process peers) asserting post-catch-up checksum agreement AND clean-reject-on-failed-content-gate; that harness is prerequisite work for DW-2 / FR-79, not part of it. The in-engine "Rejoining..." presentation half stays a human-present verification either way.
status: open

### DW-880: Scenario settings are spread across three surfaces with no standalone panel, and OnboardingPanel's win-condition control exposes only 2 of the 6 available conditions
origin: 15-10 dev-auto HALT (`bmad-dev-auto-result-15-10-scenario-settings-panel-new-scenario-empty-canvas-flow-dw-126-dw-127.md`), 2026-08-06 — the explicitly-re-filed residual of DW-126/DW-127, both closed the same day as delivered by Story 6.7.
location: `godot/src/Core/Bootstrap/Phases/WinConditionPhase.cs` (the always-on Edit-mode corner panel: all 6 win conditions at :45-187, `BuildPropertiesEditor` hosted live at :206-207, "New Map…" at :199, and the F5 Edit⇄Play authored-start reset at :252-289) + `godot/src/CreationSuite/EntityPlacer.cs:102-103, 250-251, 312-346` (per-slot StartOre/StartCrystal spinners) + `godot/src/UI/OnboardingPanel.cs:346-386` (`BuildWinConditionStep`/`AddWinConditionButton`).
severity: low
reason: Cosmetic/organizational only — nothing is unreachable and nothing is out of sync. Two distinct residuals. (1) There is no single standalone `ScenarioSettingsPanel` on a `Ctrl+<letter>` hotkey; the settings a creator needs live in three places (corner panel for win condition + map properties, placement-palette spinners for per-slot economy). (2) `OnboardingPanel`'s embedded win-condition control is a strict SUBSET of the corner panel's: it offers only `DestroyAllBuildings` and `EliminateAllUnits` (`OnboardingPanel.cs:366-368`) while the corner panel offers all six (2 built-in + 4 T1 presets with inline params). The two surfaces stay visually consistent — `AddWinConditionButton` calls `MainScene.RefreshWinConditionUi` → `SceneContext.WinConditionUiRefresh` (the DW-126 partial fix) — so this is a discoverability gap, not a divergence: a creator who sets a T1 preset in the corner panel then opens onboarding sees a picker that cannot represent their current selection's siblings. Also carried here from DW-127: onboarding step 4's instructional copy still coaches editing the boot-time scenario and does not OFFER the now-shipped blank-canvas New-Map flow as an alternative.
closure: low priority, and deliberately NOT an unattended-loop candidate. If built, a consolidated panel must not break the surfaces the corner panel is entangled with — it owns the F5 Edit⇄Play authored-start reset, and the move touches `EditorHotkeys` + its duplicate-chord red test, the `ISetupPhase[]` phase array + `ScenePhaseOrder.Canonical` + `PhaseOrderTest`, `SceneContext`, and `MainScene.ToggleEditorPanel`. Cheaper partial closures that stand alone: widen `AddWinConditionButton` to cover all six conditions (or point that onboarding step at the corner panel instead of duplicating it), and update step 4's copy to mention "New Map…". Either is worth doing on the next story that touches onboarding or `WinConditionPhase` for another reason.

severity: low
reason: Story 15.11's GroundPoint cast relies entirely on the UI's `RaycastGround` to keep the clicked point on-map; the sim applies NO bounds/finiteness check on the wire ground coords before debiting cost and starting cooldown. A non-UI issuer (AI, DSL/trigger, a hand-built or replayed order, or modded content) supplying an arbitrary/off-map point still spends energy and cools down while hitting nothing, and a far center feeds the already-tracked systemic `FixedVec3.SqrDistance` int32 overflow (DW-688/DW-764, ~181u wrap) so a SearchArea radius test can read true across the map — Evidence: both adversarial and edge-case review lenses flagged the missing guard; there is no non-UI ground-cast issuer in the codebase today (AI/DSL do not issue ground casts), so it is latent, and it compounds an overflow already queued for the golden re-baseline batch rather than being independently exploitable now.

### DW-882: In-engine gate for Story 15.11's cast gameplay is not drivable over the GDScript-only godot-mcp bridge
origin: deferred by review of `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-15-11-ability-targeting-increments-ground-target-cast-ally-heal-other.md`, 2026-08-06
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-15-11-ability-targeting-increments-ground-target-cast-ally-heal-other.md`
location: godot/src/Core/MainScene.cs (_world/_host are private C# fields, no marshallable sim seam) + godot/src/UI/SelectionSystem.cs (IssueCastAbilityGroundCommand takes non-marshallable Fixed) + godot/resources/data/abilities/{ground_nuke,mend_ally}.json (on no faction roster)
severity: medium
reason: The literal player-facing gameplay of 15.11 — press a GroundPoint card, click ground, watch the AoE land; press an Ally heal, click a friendly unit, watch it heal — could NOT be driven or observed in the running game. Empirically established 2026-08-06: the godot-mcp bridge executes GDScript only; it CAN call marshallable C# methods (proved `MainScene.CountFaction(1)=2`) but cannot reach the pure-C# `EntityWorld` SoA (not a GodotObject; `_world`/`_host` private), cannot construct `Fixed` to call `IssueCastAbilityGroundCommand`, and neither new ability is on any roster so no command card ever renders them. Consequence: the cast gameplay's IN-ENGINE verification is a standing gap — the sim path is instead proven through the real engine by the byte-identical ground-cast golden and the discriminating Tier-1 tests (SearchArea damages at the point not the caster; CastTargetPicker Ally excludes caster), and the reachable coupled surfaces (CreationSuite affinity dropdown, boot wiring, strict JSON load, "coming soon" removal) were driven and passed — but the card->arm->click->issue UI glue and the reticle-follow were not observed. Evidence: intent-alignment, verification-gap, and both hunter lenses converged on this gap; the gate-drive attempt hit a hard C#/GDScript-marshalling wall, not laziness. Closure = add a small debug-gated marshallable seam on MainScene (e.g. `int DebugSpawn(int faction,float x,float z,string unitId)`, `void DebugGrantAbility(int id,int slot,string abilityId)`, `void DebugSetHealth(int id,float hp)`, `float DebugHealth(int id)`) so the bridge can construct + read the real running sim, OR place the two abilities on a sandbox roster and drive the command card; note even then the mouse-pixel->RaycastGround sliver stays human-verify (the bridge has no absolute-mouse click). Best folded into the Epic-10 live-verify batch (A5-E9) alongside the other in-engine-observability debt.
resolution: BUILT 2026-08-07 (Alec: "land the DW-882 debug seam first", chosen over waiving Story 15.13's gate). `godot/src/Core/MainSceneDebugSeam.cs` — a debug-gated partial of MainScene exposing only marshallable primitives: READ (`_mcp_state()` godot-mcp digest hook, `DebugSimJson`, `DebugEntityJson` incl. RAW Fixed values, `DebugAliveCount`, `DebugFindUnit`), DRIVE (`DebugCastGround` — the seam's whole reason to exist, since GDScript cannot construct the two `Fixed` args — and `DebugCastTarget`, both issuing REAL orders through `SelectionSystem` → `OrderApplier`, never a test double), and SETUP (`DebugSpawnUnit`, `DebugGrantAbility`, `DebugSetHealth`, `DebugSetEnergy`). Mutators are gated on `OS.IsDebugBuild()` AND refuse while `Lockstep.IsOnline` (a direct SoA write outside the command stream is a guaranteed desync). Paired presentation taps: `CombatFeedbackBridge._mcp_state()` (per-`CombatEventType` cumulative drain tally, flash spawns/active, shake applies + last authored duration/strength) and `AudioManager._mcp_state()` (profile-first route count, last sound id/type, and `missing_streams` so "routed but the clip is not authored yet" is distinguishable from "never routed"). Both nodes are now explicitly Named so a gate artifact can cite a stable path instead of an auto-name (`@Node3D@494`) that changes every run. Excluded from the Godot-free Tier-1 assembly beside MainScene.cs in `SimSources.props`. PROVEN by driving Story 15.13's gate end-to-end: caster relocated to the cast point with exact Fixed raws, all three cue leaves tallied with their authored numbers. Residual (unchanged, still open as noted above): the mouse-pixel→RaycastGround sliver stays human-verify — the bridge has no absolute-mouse click. LESSON: freeze game time (`godot_game_time freeze` → cast → `step frames=3`) before asserting sim state — in a free-running match the caster walks off the blink point within a few hundred ms and a correct cast reads as a failed one.
status: done 2026-08-07

location: godot/src/Effects/EffectCaps.cs (`MaxPeriodicStackScale = 8` doc block) + godot/src/Effects/ModifierStore.cs (`RunScaledPulse` effective-scale calc) + godot/src/Core/Definitions/AbilityValidator.cs (no warning for this shape)
severity: low
reason: `MaxPeriodicStackScale = 8` bounds the pulse scale as `min(_stackCount, 8)`, but grouped `StackRule.Stack` allows `MaxStacks` up to `MaxAuthorableStacks = int.MaxValue >> 16 = 32767` (one slot, `_stackCount` up to MaxStacks) — so a `Stack` + `Multiply`/`Repeat` modifier with `max_stacks>8` reaches `_stackCount>8`, its flat stat deltas scale to the true count, but its pulse silently saturates at x8, with no author warning. The EffectCaps doc block justifies the value as "8 == the per-entity ring cap … the most independent stacks that can coexist, so it never truncates a legitimately-reachable stack count" — that reasoning holds only for `StackIndependent` (ring-capped at 8); it is FALSE for grouped `Stack`, whose reachable stack count is 32767. Evidence: adversarial lens; verified `MaxAuthorableStacks=32767` in `Modifier.cs:224`, `MaxPeriodicStackScale=8` in `EffectCaps.cs`, and that `CheckAuthoringBounds` caps `Stack.MaxStacks` only at 32767. No shipped content authors a non-None periodic mode, so nothing ships broken today — this is a balance footgun + a false load-bearing comment. Fix is a design call (warn when `Stack && MaxStacks>MaxPeriodicStackScale && PeriodicStacking!=None`, and/or correct the comment), so deferred rather than auto-patched (EffectCaps.cs is `EffectCapsDocHygieneTests`-guarded).
status: open

### DW-887: PeriodicStackMode.Multiply is a silent no-op on a period_effect whose leaf does not read PulseScale (e.g. ApplyModifier), with no validator warning
origin: deferred by review of `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-15-12-energy-stack-mechanics.md`, 2026-08-07
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-15-12-energy-stack-mechanics.md`
location: godot/src/Effects/ModifierStore.cs (`RunScaledPulse` Multiply branch) + godot/src/Effects/EffectContext.cs (`PulseScale`) consumed only in DamageEffect/HealEffect/DirectHpDeltaEffect; godot/src/Core/Definitions/AbilityValidator.cs (inert-mode warning does not cover this)
severity: low
reason: `Multiply` scales a pulse only via `EffectContext.PulseScale`, which is read exclusively by the three direct-magnitude leaves (Damage/Heal/DirectHpDelta). `AbilityValidator` explicitly permits an `ApplyModifierEffect` inside a `period_effect` subtree (it descends `am.Modifier?.PeriodEffect` and treats ApplyModifier as a leaf — verified at `AbilityValidator.cs:262-274`), so a `Stack` + `Multiply` modifier whose period leaf is an ApplyModifier (or spawn) runs the pulse ONCE unscaled — identical to `None` — with no warning. The story's inert-mode warning only fires for non-scaling Stack shapes, not for a scaling stack whose leaf cannot be scaled. This contradicts the prior review pass's rejection basis ("period is always direct-magnitude leaves — unreachable"), which is false for ApplyModifier. Evidence: adversarial + edge-case + verification-gap lenses independently; confirmed against the validator walk. Low severity (deterministic, arguably-correct since scaling a modifier-install is undefined) but exactly the inert-authoring footgun class this story set out to surface. Fix is a design call (warn when Multiply sits over a period subtree with no PulseScale-reading leaf).
status: open

### DW-888: Period-leaf magnitude × PulseScale (up to x8 under Multiply) has no authoring bound → Fixed int32 overflow at large authored period amounts
origin: deferred by review of `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-15-12-energy-stack-mechanics.md`, 2026-08-07
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-15-12-energy-stack-mechanics.md`
location: godot/src/Effects/DamageEffect.cs + godot/src/Effects/HealEffect.cs + godot/src/Effects/DirectHpDeltaEffect.cs (`Amount * ctx.PulseScale`) with no magnitude cap in godot/src/Core/Definitions/AbilityValidator.cs
severity: low
reason: `PeriodicStackMode.Multiply` multiplies a period leaf's authored magnitude by `PulseScale` (up to x8). `Modifier.MaxStatDeltaTotalRaw` bounds modifier STAT DELTAS only — there is no authoring ceiling on a `DamageEffect`/`HealEffect`/`DirectHpDeltaEffect` `Amount`. Fixed is Q16.16 in a 32-bit int, so an authored period amount above ~`int.MaxValue/8` raw (approx 4096 in Fixed value units) times 8 wraps the product negative — a Multiply DoT would heal / a HoT would damage. Evidence: adversarial + edge-case lenses; `FixedPoint` multiply is `(int)(((long)a.Raw*b.Raw)>>16)` with no saturation, and no validator bound on period-leaf magnitude was found. Requires an extreme (but authorable) magnitude, so low severity and unreached by shipped content; fix is either a load-time bound on `period-leaf magnitude x MaxPeriodicStackScale` or a saturating multiply in the leaf.
status: open

### DW-889: regen_rate has no authoring validation — a negative rate silently drains energy every tick, and regen_rate>0 with max_energy=0 is silently inert
origin: deferred by review of `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-15-12-energy-stack-mechanics.md`, 2026-08-07

severity: low
reason: `EnergyRegenSystem.Tick` early-outs only when the seam returns exactly `Raw == 0`, so a negative authored `regen_rate` passes the guard and does `Energy = clamp(Energy + negative, 0, MaxEnergy)` — a silent per-tick energy DRAIN presenting as "abilities randomly unavailable," with no load-time rejection, documentation, or test. Symmetrically, `regen_rate>0` on a unit with `max_energy=0` is silently inert (clamp pins Energy to [0,0]). Neither is validated or warned — inconsistent with this story's own theme of surfacing inert/footgun authoring. Evidence: adversarial + edge-case lenses; confirmed the guard and the absence of any `regen_rate` check in the unit-definition validators. Low severity (no shipped unit authors a non-zero regen_rate; the drain is only reachable by an authoring typo). Fix is a design call (reject/clamp negatives, or document them as intentional decay; warn on `regen_rate>0 && max_energy<=0`).

### DW-893: Placement ghost renders a box/rectangle instead of the object's own silhouette + shadow
origin: reported by Alec 2026-08-07 from live editor use (session that landed the DW-882 seam)
source_spec: — (live-use field report, no spec)
location: godot/src/CreationSuite/** (the placement preview/ghost path shared by doodad/prop, building and hero placement)
severity: medium
reason: When placing doodads, buildings or heroes the ghost is drawn as a generic rectangle/box for EVERY object rather than the object's real mesh, so its cast shadow is a slab and the author cannot judge footprint, facing or silhouette before committing the placement. This is the same defect class as the shipped-unit "cast-shadow SLAB" already recorded for the asset pipeline, but here it is a PRESENTATION choice in the placer, not a mesh defect: the GLBs exist and render correctly once placed. Fix: have the placement ghost instance the target's actual mesh (team-tinted/translucent) and cast a real shadow, falling back to the box only when no mesh resolves. Wanted by Alec for authoring feel.
resolution: FIXED 2026-08-07. The `location:` above was WRONG — this lives in `godot/src/UI/EntityPlacer.cs`, not CreationSuite. `RefreshGhostVisuals` assigned `_ghost.Mesh` from a hardcoded `_mode switch` of Godot primitives (a 0.6×1.2×0.6 box for units AND heroes, 4×2×4 for buildings, 1×1×1 for props), never touching `UnitDefinition.MeshPath` / `BuildingDefinition.MeshPath`; `CreateGhostMesh` also set `CastShadow = Off`, so the ghost cast NO shadow at all. Fix: `ResolveGhostMesh()` resolves through `MeshLoader.LoadFromGlb` — the SAME seam MultiMeshBridge (units/heroes) and BuildingBridge (buildings) already render from, whose box fallback means this can never be worse than before — cached by mode+id because the loader does a PackedScene load + Instantiate + Free and must never run per frame. Props share `PropRenderer.MeshForProp` (made internal); resource nodes, start positions and items keep their stand-ins because no authored mesh exists for them. Ground lift now comes from `-mesh.GetAabb().Position.Y * scale` (the `MultiMeshBridge.GroundOffsetFor` formula) for authored meshes, with the hand-tuned half-height constants kept for the primitives, and the authored `MeshScale` is applied. Shadow: NOT a CastShadow flip — in Godot 4 an alpha-BLEND material casts no shadow, and the translucent ghost look is deliberate, so an opaque `ShadowsOnly` twin shares the ghost's mesh and transform and contributes the silhouette shadow. ORDERING TRAP handled: CameraPhase builds the placer BEFORE FactionVisualsPhase resolves the real slot factions, so `SetFactionDefs` clears the cache and re-resolves — without that the ghost would be pinned to the pre-scenario default factions forever. The in-game worker-build ghost (`MainScene.EnterBuildPlacementMode`, a fixed 4×3×4 box) got the same treatment, so this is closed for the player as well as the editor. IN-ENGINE VERIFIED via the DW-882 seam: with the palette on P1 Unit and again on Building, the ghost node reports `ArrayMesh` (a real GLB) rather than BoxMesh, with a sibling at `cast_shadow = ShadowsOnly`.
status: done 2026-08-07

### DW-894: Dragging a placed building/unit does not follow the cursor — it teleports on mouse release
origin: reported by Alec 2026-08-07 from live editor use
source_spec: — (live-use field report, no spec)
location: godot/src/CreationSuite/** (editor select+drag path) + the placement preview shared with DW-893
severity: medium
reason: Alec: "I hold mouse click, drag, and release and then the building jumps to that location." The drag is committed as a single move at mouse-UP with no live preview during the drag, so the author gets no continuous feedback about where the object will land and must place-check-undo to iterate. Fix: drive the ghost/target transform from the motion events during the drag (the same preview DW-893 fixes), committing only on release. The two should be fixed together — they share the preview.
root cause CONFIRMED 2026-08-07 (read, not guessed): `EntityPlacer.HandleSelectMouse`. On left-press over a selection it sets `_groupMoving = true` and records `_groupMoveStartWorld`; the MOTION branch then updates only `_marqueeCurrent` and does nothing at all for `_groupMoving`; the release branch calls `MoveSelection(gp - _groupMoveStartWorld)` once. So the object provably cannot follow the cursor — there is no code that would move it before mouse-up. The reason this is not a two-line fix: `MoveSelection` is not a transform nudge, it is an atomic DELETE + RECREATE of every selected entity that also pushes an undo/redo pair and re-validates map bounds. Calling it per motion event would flood the undo stack and churn entity ids every frame. The correct shape is a PREVIEW: offset the visual (ghost/marker) transforms during the drag and call `MoveSelection` exactly once on release — which is the same preview DW-893 needs, hence "fix them together".
resolution: FIXED 2026-08-07 (with DW-893, as predicted). The motion branch of `HandleSelectMouse` now computes a live `_groupMovePreviewDelta` using the SAME `SnapDelta` the commit applies, so what the author sees during the drag is byte-equal to where the objects land. The preview carrier is `_markerRoot`: it sits at the origin with an identity transform and its children are written in ABSOLUTE world coordinates, so ONE assignment (`_markerRoot.Position = _groupMoving ? delta : Vector3.Zero`) translates the whole selection overlay, and zeroing it on release restores truth with no cleanup pass. On drag start a translucent copy of each selected object's REAL mesh (resolved through the same `MeshLoader` seam as DW-893) is parented under that root, so what follows the cursor is the building, not a floating pad. `MoveSelection` is still called EXACTLY ONCE on release with the raw delta — it is a delete+recreate that pushes an undo/redo pair, so it must never run per motion event. Also fixed a pre-existing latent bug the preview would have made visible: the right-click branch returns BEFORE the Select-mode dispatch, so a right-click mid-drag left `_groupMoving` true with a stale start point and the next left-release committed a bogus move; `CancelPlacement` now clears the drag state. The mesh-resolution half was verified in-engine via the DW-882 seam; the drag itself needed a human click. VERIFIED BY ALEC in live use 2026-08-07 (he tested the whole batch and confirmed it works) — the agent-side limit was only that the bridge has no absolute-mouse click, not that the fix was unproven.
status: done 2026-08-07

### DW-895: Ctrl+B and Ctrl+U both toggle their editor AND cycle the upper-right tab on every press
origin: reported by Alec 2026-08-07 from live editor use
source_spec: — (live-use field report, no spec)
location: godot/src/Core/Definitions/EditorHotkeys.cs (the binding table) + the editor dock/tab strip handler + MainScene input routing
severity: medium
reason: One chord is being consumed by TWO handlers: the EditorHotkeys panel toggle AND the upper-right tab strip's cycle action. Reported for Ctrl+B (building editor) and Ctrl+U (unit card), and the shape suggests the tab strip cycles on the BARE letter while the modifier is not being tested, so Ctrl+letter matches both. This is the same class the EditorHotkeys tier policy and its duplicate-chord red test were built to prevent — but that test only covers duplicates WITHIN the table, so a collision with a handler outside the table (the tab strip) is still silent. Fix: make the tab-strip handler require the modifier state it actually wants (and mark the event handled), then extend the hotkey guard to cover non-table consumers of the same chords.
resolution: FIXED 2026-08-07 (together with DW-897). Confirmed: the key ladder at the tail of `EntityPlacer._Input` had THREE defects — (1) it never tested `key.CtrlPressed`, and Godot's `Keycode` is modifier-independent, so Ctrl+B IS `Key.B` there (the Ctrl+Z/Y block above falls through without returning); (2) no case called `SetInputAsHandled`, unique among the branches of that method, so the event travelled on to MainScene's EditorHotkeys dispatch; (3) it was not gated on `editMode`, so the hidden palette also ran during Play. One Ctrl+B therefore cycled the palette AND opened the Building editor. Ctrl+U identical; Ctrl+G was an unreported THIRD instance (grid snap + DslGraph). Fix: the established Ctrl bail (`if (key.CtrlPressed && Keycode >= Key.A && <= Key.Z) return;` — the idiom the 2026-08-04 re-tier retrofitted into TerrainBrush/RegionTool/PathabilityTool/WaterTool and skipped here), an `editMode` gate, and consume-only-what-was-handled. The same bail was added to `WaterTool._Input`, which claimed bare G while its own `_UnhandledInput` already carried the bail. NEW STRUCTURAL GUARD: `ProjectChimera.Sim.Tests/Meta/HotkeyTierGuardTests.cs` source-scans the tree and fails when a listed bare-letter tool lacks the Ctrl bail — precisely what `EditorHotkeyTableTests` structurally cannot see, since it only detects duplicates WITHIN the table.
status: done 2026-08-07

### DW-896: Stale/deprecated key hints in the HUD (e.g. "N = Lobby" lower-left) — the whole hint set needs an audit
origin: reported by Alec 2026-08-07 from live editor use
source_spec: — (live-use field report, no spec)
location: godot/src/Core/Bootstrap/Phases/HudPhase.cs (hint strip) + per-panel close-button labels (e.g. godot/src/UI/ReplayBrowserPanel.cs "Close  [N]")
severity: low
reason: The lower-left hint strip still advertises bindings that no longer do what they say ("N = Lobby" called out by name), and panel close buttons carry hard-coded bracket hints (Close [N], Close [K], Close [J], Close [C], Close [R], Close [V], Close [X], Close [O]) that are strings, not reads of the binding table — so they cannot follow a rebind and were never re-checked after the 2026-08-04 keymap re-tier. Fix: audit every advertised chord against EditorHotkeys/the input map, delete the dead ones, and source the remaining hint text from the table so the two cannot drift again.
resolution: FIXED 2026-08-07. Full audit done — every advertised chord in the tree was cross-checked against `EditorHotkeys`, the (empty) project.godot input map, and the actual `Key.X` handlers. Findings: (a) `N=Lobby` was DEAD — Story 9.7 removed the dev-only lobby toggle, and bare N had since been re-taken by the Water tool, so the strip pointed at a different tool entirely; (b) `O=Maps` was DEAD *and* duplicated — no `Key.O` handler exists anywhere, and the Content Browser's real Ctrl+O was already advertised on the generated Editors line; (c) ALL EIGHT panel close captions were wrong (`[N] [O] [K] [J] [R] [V] [C] [X]`) — four naming a dead key, four naming a key another tool had taken; (d) twelve bootstrap `GD.Print` boot-log lines and the boot banner still advertised pre-re-map bare letters; (e) three OnboardingPanel `[J]` hints were dead. Fixes: added `EditorHotkeys.ChordFor(EditorPanelId)` and `CloseLabel(EditorPanelId)` (still Godot-free, Tier-1 testable) and routed all eight close captions, the three onboarding hints and all twelve boot-log lines through them, so a caption now CANNOT disagree with its binding; deleted the two dead claims from the Edit hint strip and the dead lobby claim from the banner, and replaced them with the tools that actually own those bare letters (N=Water, V=Cameras, I=Regions). Three new guards in `HotkeyTierGuardTests`: no file may hard-code a single-letter close hint, the retired advertisements may not reappear, and ChordFor/CloseLabel render the table's own chord. NOT fixed and filed as [[DW-902]]: the TOOL tier still has no table behind it (the Edit strip's bare-letter half and the whole Play strip are hand-written literals — the reason this line has now drifted twice), and the Play strip under-advertises seven live bindings.
status: done 2026-08-07

### DW-897: Tab cycles the upper-right Palette instead of its intended action
origin: reported by Alec 2026-08-07 from live editor use
source_spec: — (live-use field report, no spec)
location: the upper-right palette/tab strip handler (same consumer as DW-895) + MainScene `_UnhandledInput`
severity: low
reason: Pressing Tab cycles the upper-right Palette menu. Historically Tab was the edit-mode placement-mode cycler (documented in MainScene's own header: "Tab cycles mode"), so either the binding moved and the palette inherited it, or both consumers are live and the palette wins. Same root shape as DW-895 (an unclaimed/duplicated chord with no table entry and no red test). Fix alongside DW-895 — decide who owns Tab, mark the event handled, and add it to the guarded set.
resolution: FIXED 2026-08-07 (together with DW-895). The palette IS the legitimate Edit-mode owner of Tab (MainScene's own header documents "Tab cycles mode", and Play-mode Tab belongs to SelectionSystem's subgroup cycle — the two are mode-disjoint and never actually conflicted). The real conflict was with Godot's built-in `ui_focus_next`: the palette never consumed Tab, so one press both cycled placement mode AND walked GUI focus across every focusable Control on screen — the "Tab cycles the Palette" feel. Fix: Tab is now consumed in Edit mode, but only when nothing holds GUI focus (`GuiGetFocusOwner() != null` yields), so the palette owns Tab while the user drives the map and loses it to focus traversal inside an open editor panel. `TextFocusGuard` alone was insufficient — it bails only for LineEdit/TextEdit, so consuming Tab unconditionally would have broken tabbing between Buttons/OptionButtons in a panel.
status: done 2026-08-07

### DW-898: Esc does not open Settings in Create mode until a Play-mode round-trip has happened
origin: reported by Alec 2026-08-07 from live editor use
source_spec: — (live-use field report, no spec)
location: the pause/settings overlay wiring (godot/src/Core/Bootstrap/Phases/** settings/pause phase) + MainScene mode transitions
severity: medium
reason: Alec: "Esc isn't working to get to settings in create mode, only when I enter test mode by pressing F5 and then Esc. After going into the game and pressing Esc, now when I am in Create mode again, Esc works for settings." That ordering is diagnostic: the Esc-to-settings handler is armed LAZILY by the Play-mode entry path (or the overlay node is created/connected there) rather than at scene setup, so it is dead on the boot path into Create until a Play transition initialises it. Fix: arm the binding/overlay at setup for both modes, and add an in-engine check that Esc opens Settings from a COLD Create-mode boot (the state that is broken) — the warm path masks it.
resolution: FIXED 2026-08-07 — and the "armed lazily by the Play-mode entry path" premise above is FALSE. Nothing about Esc→Settings is Play-armed; `SettingsPhase` builds and publishes `SettingsPanel` eagerly at boot. The real cause: `EntityPlacer._Input` claimed Esc and called `SetInputAsHandled()` whenever `_placementActive` — and `_placementActive` is initialised TRUE ("Starts armed so placement works immediately on entering Edit mode"). `_Input` runs before the GUI phase and before every `_UnhandledInput`, so the cold-boot FIRST Esc was always eaten and never reached MainScene's Esc→Settings toggle. The Play round-trip was CORRELATION, not cause: that swallowed first press had already set `_placementActive = false`, so the second press fell through and Settings opened — and any palette click re-arms, so it went dead again for exactly one press each time. Fix: the Esc branch still cancels an armed ghost but no longer consumes the event (right-click remains the documented pure cancel per UX-DR56, and the Edit hint strip already promised "Esc=Settings" unconditionally). Guarded by `HotkeyTierGuardTests.ThePlacerDoesNotSwallowEscape`. VERIFIED BY ALEC in live use 2026-08-07 (he tested the whole batch and confirmed it works) — the agent-side limit was only that the bridge has no absolute-mouse click, not that the fix was unproven.
status: done 2026-08-07

### DW-899: Map Gen close button is dead after a failed generation (only Ctrl+M dismisses the panel)
origin: reported by Alec 2026-08-07 from live editor use
source_spec: — (live-use field report, no spec)
location: godot/src/Core/Bootstrap/Phases/MapGeneratorPhase.cs + the map-gen panel's close handler / busy-state flag
severity: medium
reason: After a generation FAILS, the panel's close button stops responding and the panel can only be dismissed with the Ctrl+M toggle. The failure path evidently leaves the panel in its "generating/busy" state — a guard that disables or early-returns the close handler while a job is in flight — because the error branch never clears the flag the success branch clears. A user with no knowledge of the hotkey is trapped in the panel. Fix: clear the busy/in-flight state in the failure branch (or a finally), and make close unconditional; regression-test the FAILED-generation path specifically, since the happy path already works.
resolution: FIXED 2026-08-07 — and the busy-flag hypothesis above is REFUTED. MapGeneratorPanel has no busy flag and `Close()` is unconditional. The real mechanism is a LAYOUT BLOW-OUT: `_statusLabel` is the one label in the panel with no `AutowrapMode`, so its minimum width equals its full single-line text width. A failed generation writes a 250-350 char error there (LLMService quotes up to 160 chars of the offending JSON line); that minimum propagates genRow → root → `_panel`, and because `_panel` is anchored CenterLeft with a pinned left edge, ALL the growth goes RIGHTWARD until the header ✕ — flush against the right content edge — renders outside the 1920px viewport and can no longer be clicked. Ctrl+M still worked because that path is keyboard-only and geometry-independent. Nothing about the button, its handler, or any visibility flag differs before/after the failure — only the text does, which is what forced the diagnosis. Fix: `AutowrapMode.Word` + `SizeFlags.ExpandFill`. Fill is LOAD-BEARING: an autowrapping Label reports a minimum width of ~1, and under Expand-WITHOUT-Fill an HBoxContainer lays a child out at its MINIMUM, so autowrap alone would collapse it to a 1px column wrapping one character per line. Same one-line defect fixed at its second site (TriggerEditorPanel — no ✕ there, so nothing became unreachable, but the panel still swallowed the screen). Also fixed an adjacent defect found while tracing: `LLMService.GenerateScenarioAsync` swallowed `OperationCanceledException` without enqueueing any callback, so a cancelled generation never ran `OnGenerationComplete` and left the Generate button disabled for the rest of the session — that IS the "flag set, never cleared" shape this entry was reaching for, applied to the button rather than to close. VERIFIED BY ALEC in live use 2026-08-07 (he tested the whole batch and confirmed it works) — the agent-side limit was only that the bridge has no absolute-mouse click, not that the fix was unproven.
status: done 2026-08-07

### DW-900: Ability editor AI generation always rewrites the ability — no "add more" / append affordance
origin: requested by Alec 2026-08-07 from live editor use
source_spec: — (live-use feature request, no spec)
location: the Ability editor panel's AI generate flow (godot/src/CreationSuite/** ability panel) + godot/src/AI/LLMService.cs
severity: low
reason: Alec: "Ability editor AI gen works pretty good, but I want it to have a generate or 'Add more' button so that the AI knows to add onto the ability instead of writing a new one." Today the single Generate button always drafts a fresh ability from the prompt, discarding the authored graph, so iterating means re-describing everything. Fix: a second action that sends the CURRENT ability draft as context with an append/extend instruction and MERGES the returned nodes into the existing graph rather than replacing it. Note this is the concrete next step of the recorded ability-authoring AI-transparency direction (creator types plain language, the AI shows the field swaps) — the append mode is what makes that conversational rather than one-shot.
resolution: BUILT 2026-08-07. Confirmed the destructive path first: `OnAiGeneratePressed` sent only the prompt (`AbilityDraftContext` carried nothing but existing ids) and `OnAiDraftComplete` called `LoadFromRegistry(def)`, which overwrites the header, the costs, the raw-JSON pane AND the whole graph — there was no merge code anywhere. Shipped: (1) `godot/src/Core/Definitions/AbilityGraphMerge.cs` — Godot-free `CanAppend` (a pre-flight that refuses BEFORE a provider call is spent: no graph yet, a passive whose root shape is pinned by the validator, a full sequence, or the node cap) and `Append` (root already a Sequence ⇒ extend its children, else wrap old-root + additions in one Sequence; every other field carried across). The merge runs on the IMMUTABLE `EffectNode` side and never through `AbilityDraft` — load-bearing, because the draft layer has no `RequireTag` and would silently strip tag gates off the author's EXISTING nodes, which would look exactly like the AI rewriting effects it was never asked to touch. (2) `LLMService.ExtendAbilityDraftAsync` + `BuildAbilityExtendPrompt` + `ValidateAbilityAddition`, sharing `_abilityCts` with Generate so only one call is ever in flight. The prompt shows the current ability and asks for a bare JSON ARRAY of NEW nodes — chosen over "return a rewritten whole ability and diff it" precisely because an additions array is STRUCTURALLY incapable of touching what already exists, whereas a whole-ability reply can always quietly reword it (the complaint this feature answers). (3) An "Add more ✦" button beside Generate, gated identically for availability and busy. The merged result runs the real `AbilityValidator`; on reject the draft on screen is left untouched and the located error is shown. 12 Tier-1 tests in `AbilityGraphMergeTests` pin the append shapes, the by-reference survival of the author's nodes incl. RequireTag, non-mutation of the source, every CanAppend refusal, and that a merged ability still passes the authoritative validator. VERIFIED BY ALEC in live use 2026-08-07 (he tested the whole batch and confirmed it works) — the agent-side limit was only that the bridge has no absolute-mouse click, not that the fix was unproven. PREREQUISITE FOUND AND FIXED IN THE SAME CHANGE — see [[DW-903]]: the composer would have CRASHED on any ability using Story 15.13's leaves.
status: done 2026-08-07

### DW-903: The ability composer crashed on Story 15.13's four new leaves (shipped content could not be opened)
origin: found 2026-08-07 while building DW-900 (its root-cause investigation flagged it as a prerequisite)
source_spec: `_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-15-13-effect-vocabulary-completion-teleport-presentation-leaves.md`
location: godot/src/Core/Definitions/AbilityDraft.cs (DraftNode.FromEffectNode / ToEffectNode / DraftKind) + godot/src/CreationSuite/AbilityEditorPanel.Advanced.cs (RenderNode)
severity: medium
reason: Story 15.13 added `teleport`/`play_vfx`/`play_sound`/`shake_screen` to the closed effect vocabulary and shipped `blink_strike.json` using all four, but did not teach the structured composer about them. `DraftNode.FromEffectNode`'s default arm THROWS `InvalidOperationException`, and nothing on the `LoadFromRegistry → ReflectModelIntoForm → SeedDraftFromDef` path catches it — so opening any ability that uses one of the four in the Ability Editor took the editor down. Latent from the moment 15.13's content landed, and it would also have fired the first time an AI draft named one of the new kinds. THE GENERAL LESSON: a closed-vocabulary addition is not complete when the sim, the JSON converter, the canonical fold and the validator know about it — the AUTHORING composer is a fifth consumer with its own exhaustive switch, and it fails at RUNTIME rather than at compile time, so no build or Tier-1 run catches the omission.
resolution: FIXED 2026-08-07. Added `DraftKind.Opaque` — a node the composer cannot EDIT but carries through unchanged, holding the original immutable `EffectNode`. `FromEffectNode` matches the four types EXPLICITLY rather than folding them into the default arm, so a genuinely unknown type still throws loudly (that throw is the signal the vocabulary grew again); `ToEffectNode` hands the carried node straight back (safe and byte-identical, since EffectNodes are immutable); `RenderNode` gives it a read-only header with working reorder/remove instead of the kind dropdown — which would otherwise render blank AND, if touched, call `ResetKind` and destroy the carried node. `Opaque` is deliberately ABSENT from `DraftVocabulary.Kinds`, so the composer can never offer it. 12 Tier-1 tests in `AbilityDraftOpaqueLeafTests`. NOT built: rich authoring widgets for the four (a colour/scale editor for `hit_flash`, a sound-id picker, a shake duration/strength pair) — the Raw JSON pane remains the way to edit those payloads. File a follow-up if that authoring is wanted.
status: done 2026-08-07

### DW-901: Paint-paths tool — "Erase mode" cannot be selected and "Slope auto-block" cannot be unchecked
origin: reported by Alec 2026-08-07 from live editor use
source_spec: — (live-use field report, no spec)
location: godot/src/CreationSuite/PathabilityTool.cs (the "Erase mode" CheckButton and "Slope auto-block" CheckBox and their toggled handlers)
severity: medium
reason: Both controls in the pathability/paint-paths panel are unresponsive: Erase mode never engages and Slope auto-block cannot be turned OFF, so the author can only ADD pathability blocking and cannot correct a mistake or hand-author a walkable slope. Two failure shapes fit: the toggled signal is never connected (the control renders but drives nothing), or a per-frame refresh re-asserts the backing value and overwrites the user's toggle. Both controls confirmed present in the live tree at .../PathabilityTool/.../@CheckButton@736 and @CheckBox@740 during the 2026-08-07 session, so this is handler wiring, not a missing widget. Paint-write at GDExtension was already recorded as broken once (set_control fix path) — check whether this is the same underlying write seam before treating it as pure UI.
resolution: FIXED 2026-08-07. Root cause was NOT in PathabilityTool — both controls were confirmed in-engine to be correctly wired (`Toggled` handlers connected), enabled, `MouseFilter.Stop`, and laid out INSIDE their panel rect (`Erase mode` at (1620,224) 296x31 and `Slope auto-block` at (1620,271) 296x31, both enclosed by the panel at (1620,200) 296x161). The clicks never arrived: `EntityPlacer.HandleSelectMouse` runs in `_Input` — which fires BEFORE Godot's GUI phase — and on a left-press starts a marquee and calls `SetInputAsHandled()`, guarded only by `IsOverPalette` (the placer's OWN upper-right palette). Every other editor panel was outside that guard, so with Select mode armed a click on any tool-panel control was consumed as a marquee start and the Control never saw it. Fix: `EntityPlacer.IsOverUi` = the palette rect check OR `GetViewport().GuiGetHoveredControl() != null` — the general form of "is the cursor over UI", which unlike a hand-rolled rect already honours MouseFilter, visibility and z-order. Failure mode of the change is safe (at worst a marquee does not start while hovering a control). Static fix at the time of writing (the bridge has no absolute-mouse click). VERIFIED BY ALEC in live use 2026-08-07 (he tested the whole batch and confirmed it works) — the agent-side limit was only that the bridge has no absolute-mouse click, not that the fix was unproven. SIBLING RISK (deliberately NOT changed): `PathabilityTool`, `RegionTool`, `TerrainBrush` and `WaterTool` each guard only their OWN panel the same way, so each still swallows clicks destined for the OTHER tools' panels. Widening those guards was left undone on purpose — there the failure mode is UNSAFE (a wrong guard silently stops terrain/path painting) and it cannot be click-verified over the bridge today.
status: done 2026-08-07

### DW-902: The TOOL-tier hint strip is a hand-written literal with no table and no test
origin: filed 2026-08-07 while closing DW-896 (the third drift of the same line)
source_spec: — (follow-up from the DW-896 audit)
location: godot/src/Core/MainScene.cs (UpdateHud — the Edit-mode and Play-mode ControlsLabel.Text literals)
severity: low
reason: The 2026-08-04 re-tier gave the EDITOR tier a table (`EditorHotkeys`), a generated hint line, a generated dock and a duplicate-chord red test. The TOOL tier got none of that: the bare-letter half of the Edit strip and the whole Play strip are hand-written interpolated literals, which is why they drifted into advertising two bindings that did not exist (DW-896) and why the Play strip under-advertises seven live bindings (P=Patrol, F=Follow, T=UseItem, Tab=CycleSubgroup, F1=QuestLog, F2=TriggerDebug, E=EdgeScroll). DW-896 deleted the dead claims and added a retired-advertisement deny-list test, but the structural fix — a `ToolHotkeys` (and `PlayHotkeys`) table beside `EditorHotkeys`, rendered by string.Join the way the Editors line already is, plus a cross-table test that no bare letter appears in both tiers — was deliberately deferred: it touches `UpdateHud`, a per-frame Godot-coupled path, so it needs the in-engine gate, whereas everything DW-896 shipped was mechanical. Fix: add the table(s), render both strips from them, and add (a) DuplicateChords on the new table, (b) a cross-tier collision test, (c) a source scan asserting every bare-letter row has a real `Keycode == Key.<L>` handler in the tree — that last one is what would have caught the dead N and O at the moment they died.
status: open

### DW-904: Placement ghost did not sit where the object actually lands (prop scale + rotation + ground lift)
origin: reported by Alec 2026-08-07 from live use, immediately after the DW-893 ghost shipped
source_spec: — (live-use field report, no spec)
location: godot/src/UI/EntityPlacer.cs (UpdateGhostPosition / RefreshGhostVisuals / BuildDragPreview)
severity: medium
reason: Alec: "there is a glitch where it isn't actually placing where the shadow shows it will. Example: when I scale the tree down and place it, it places it where my mouse click is and not where the shadow shows it will. It makes it hard for the user placing it because I can't tell EXACTLY where it will go." The HORIZONTAL position was never wrong — `TrySpawnAt` applies the identical `SnapValue(hit.X/Z)` the ghost does. The error was VERTICAL, and the new shadow converted it into an apparent horizontal one: a mesh floating above the ground throws its shadow sideways under the directional light, so the shadow pointed at a spot the object could never land on. Three distinct mismatches between the ghost transform and what the renderer that draws the placed object actually does: (1) GROUND LIFT — DW-893 classified props as "authored" so the ghost was lifted by `-aabb.min.Y * scale`, but `PropRenderer` places a prop at literally `new Vector3(p.X, 0f, p.Z)` with NO lift; for the default tree (CylinderMesh, height 2.5) that is a 1.25-unit float. (2) SCALE — the lift was precomputed once in `RefreshGhostVisuals` using the definition's `MeshScale` (1 for props), but the ghost RENDERS at `_propScale`, and the scale spinner does not call `RefreshGhostVisuals` at all — so scaling a prop down left the lift computed for the old size, which is why Alec hit it by scaling. (3) ROTATION — a placed prop gets `Basis(Up, p.Rot)`, but the ghost never rotated, so an R-rotated prop previewed one orientation and placed another. Note (1) predates DW-893 in kind: the prop ghost used a hard-coded 0.5 lift while the prop places at 0, so it was always half a unit off — there was simply no shadow to reveal it. THE GENERAL RULE this establishes: a placement ghost is a PROMISE about where the object will land, so its full transform (position, ground lift, scale, rotation) must be derived from the same rule as the renderer that will draw it — a ghost that merely looks plausible is worse than a crude one, because the author trusts it.
resolution: FIXED 2026-08-07. Replaced the precomputed `_ghostGroundLift` with `GhostGroundLift(scale)`, evaluated per frame against the scale actually applied that frame, with per-renderer rules documented at the method: props → Y = 0 (matching `PropRenderer`), units/heroes/buildings → `-aabb.min.Y * scale` (matching the shared `MultiMeshBridge.GroundOffsetFor` / `BuildingBridge` rule), remaining stand-ins → their hand-tuned constants. The ghost now also carries `_placementRot` in Prop mode, and the shadow twin copies rotation as well as position and scale. The DW-894 drag preview got the same treatment (per-kind lift; a placed prop's own authored `Scale` is mirrored so the preview is the right size). IN-ENGINE VERIFIED via the DW-882 seam: with Prop mode armed and the scale driven to 0.5, the ghost reports `pos_y = 0.0`, `scale = 0.5`, and the ShadowsOnly twin reports an identical position/scale/rotation — where before the tree ghost floated 1.25 units up. The mouse-to-placement sliver needed a human click (no absolute-mouse click over the bridge). VERIFIED BY ALEC in live use 2026-08-07 (he tested the whole batch and confirmed it works) — the agent-side limit was only that the bridge has no absolute-mouse click, not that the fix was unproven.
status: done 2026-08-07
